LABEL: monoatomic cation transmembrane transporter activity
IAO_0000115: Enables the transfer of cation from one side of a membrane to the other.

LABEL: alpha-N-acetylgalactosaminidase activity
IAO_0000115: Catalysis of the hydrolysis of terminal non-reducing N-acetyl-D-galactosamine residues in N-acetyl-alpha-D-galactosaminides.

LABEL: sarcosine dehydrogenase activity
IAO_0000115: Catalysis of the reaction: sarcosine + H2O + electron-transfer flavoprotein = glycine + formaldehyde + reduced electron-transfer flavoprotein.

LABEL: sulfite oxidase activity
hasExactSynonym: sulphite oxidase activity
IAO_0000115: Catalysis of the reaction: H2O + O2 + sulfite = H2O2 + H+ + sulfate.

LABEL: monoatomic anion transmembrane transporter activity
IAO_0000115: Enables the transfer of a negatively charged ion from one side of a membrane to the other.

LABEL: folic acid transmembrane transporter activity
hasExactSynonym: folate transmembrane transporter activity|folate transporter activity|vitamin B9 transporter activity|vitamin M transporter activity
IAO_0000115: Enables the transfer of folic acid (pteroylglutamic acid) from one side of a membrane to the other. Folic acid is widely distributed as a member of the vitamin B complex and is essential for the synthesis of purine and pyrimidines.

LABEL: ether lipid biosynthetic process
hasExactSynonym: ether lipid anabolism|ether lipid biosynthesis|ether lipid formation|ether lipid synthesis
IAO_0000115: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of ether lipids, lipids that contain (normally) one lipid alcohol in ether linkage to one of the carbon atoms (normally C-1) of glycerol.

LABEL: pyridoxine metabolic process
hasExactSynonym: pyridoxine metabolism
IAO_0000115: The chemical reactions and pathways involving pyridoxine, 2-methyl-3-hydroxy-4,5-bis(hydroxymethyl)pyridine, one of the vitamin B6 compounds. Pyridoxal, pyridoxamine and pyridoxine are collectively known as vitamin B6, and are efficiently converted to the biologically active form of vitamin B6, pyridoxal phosphate.

LABEL: carbohydrate transport
IAO_0000115: The directed movement of carbohydrate into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. Carbohydrates are a group of organic compounds based of the general formula Cx(H2O)y.

LABEL: biosynthetic process
hasExactSynonym: anabolism|biosynthesis|synthesis
IAO_0000115: A cellular process consisting of the biochemical pathways by which a living organism synthesizes chemical substances. This typically represents the energy-requiring part of metabolism in which simpler substances are transformed into more complex ones.

LABEL: obsolete aspartate family amino acid metabolic process
hasExactSynonym: aspartate family amino acid metabolism
IAO_0000115: OBSOLETE. The chemical reactions and pathways involving amino acids of the aspartate family, comprising asparagine, aspartate, lysine, methionine and threonine.

LABEL: obsolete serine family amino acid metabolic process
hasExactSynonym: serine family amino acid metabolism
IAO_0000115: OBSOLETE. The chemical reactions and pathways involving amino acids of the serine family, comprising cysteine, glycine, homoserine, selenocysteine and serine.

LABEL: branched-chain amino acid metabolic process
hasExactSynonym: branched chain family amino acid metabolism
IAO_0000115: The chemical reactions and pathways involving amino acids containing a branched carbon skeleton, comprising isoleucine, leucine and valine.

LABEL: L-methionine catabolic process
hasExactSynonym: methionine breakdown|methionine catabolism|methionine degradation
IAO_0000115: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of L-methionine.

LABEL: glycoprotein metabolic process
hasExactSynonym: glycoprotein metabolism
IAO_0000115: The chemical reactions and pathways involving glycoproteins, a protein that contains covalently bound glycose (i.e. monosaccharide) residues; the glycose occurs most commonly as oligosaccharide or fairly small polysaccharide but occasionally as monosaccharide.

LABEL: glycoprotein biosynthetic process
hasExactSynonym: glycoprotein anabolism|glycoprotein biosynthesis|glycoprotein formation|glycoprotein synthesis
IAO_0000115: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of glycoproteins, a protein that contains covalently bound glycose (i.e. monosaccharide) residues; the glycose occurs most commonly as oligosaccharide or fairly small polysaccharide but occasionally as monosaccharide.

LABEL: lipoate biosynthetic process
hasExactSynonym: lipoate anabolism|lipoate biosynthesis|lipoate formation|lipoate synthesis|lipoic acid anabolism|lipoic acid biosynthesis|lipoic acid biosynthetic process|lipoic acid formation|lipoic acid synthesis
IAO_0000115: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of lipoate, 1,2-dithiolane-3-pentanoate, the anion derived from lipoic acid.

LABEL: nucleoside metabolic process
hasExactSynonym: nucleoside metabolism
IAO_0000115: The chemical reactions and pathways involving a nucleoside, a nucleobase linked to either beta-D-ribofuranose (a ribonucleoside) or 2-deoxy-beta-D-ribofuranose, (a deoxyribonucleoside), e.g. adenosine, guanosine, inosine, cytidine, uridine and deoxyadenosine, deoxyguanosine, deoxycytidine and thymidine (= deoxythymidine).

LABEL: nucleotide metabolic process
hasExactSynonym: nucleotide metabolism
IAO_0000115: The chemical reactions and pathways involving a nucleotide, a nucleoside that is esterified with (ortho)phosphate or an oligophosphate at any hydroxyl group on the glycose moiety; may be mono-, di- or triphosphate; this definition includes cyclic nucleotides (nucleoside cyclic phosphates).

LABEL: ribonucleoside metabolic process
hasExactSynonym: ribonucleoside metabolism
IAO_0000115: The chemical reactions and pathways involving any ribonucleoside, a nucleoside in which purine or pyrimidine base is linked to a ribose (beta-D-ribofuranose) molecule.

LABEL: nucleoside monophosphate metabolic process
hasExactSynonym: nucleoside monophosphate metabolism
IAO_0000115: The chemical reactions and pathways involving a nucleoside monophosphate, a compound consisting of a nucleobase linked to a deoxyribose or ribose sugar esterified with phosphate on the sugar.

LABEL: nucleoside monophosphate biosynthetic process
hasExactSynonym: nucleoside monophosphate anabolism|nucleoside monophosphate biosynthesis|nucleoside monophosphate formation|nucleoside monophosphate synthesis
IAO_0000115: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of a nucleoside monophosphate, a compound consisting of a nucleobase linked to a deoxyribose or ribose sugar esterified with phosphate on the sugar.

LABEL: purine nucleoside monophosphate metabolic process
hasExactSynonym: purine nucleoside monophosphate metabolism
IAO_0000115: The chemical reactions and pathways involving purine nucleoside monophosphate, a compound consisting of a purine base linked to a ribose or deoxyribose sugar esterified with phosphate on the sugar.

LABEL: purine nucleoside monophosphate biosynthetic process
hasExactSynonym: purine nucleoside monophosphate anabolism|purine nucleoside monophosphate biosynthesis|purine nucleoside monophosphate formation|purine nucleoside monophosphate synthesis
IAO_0000115: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of purine nucleoside monophosphate, a compound consisting of a purine base linked to a ribose or deoxyribose sugar esterified with phosphate on the sugar.

LABEL: nucleoside triphosphate metabolic process
hasExactSynonym: nucleoside triphosphate metabolism
IAO_0000115: The chemical reactions and pathways involving a nucleoside triphosphate, a compound consisting of a nucleobase linked to a deoxyribose or ribose sugar esterified with triphosphate on the sugar.

LABEL: nucleoside triphosphate biosynthetic process
hasExactSynonym: nucleoside triphosphate anabolism|nucleoside triphosphate biosynthesis|nucleoside triphosphate formation|nucleoside triphosphate synthesis
IAO_0000115: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of a nucleoside triphosphate, a compound consisting of a nucleobase linked to a deoxyribose or ribose sugar esterified with triphosphate on the sugar.

LABEL: purine nucleoside triphosphate metabolic process
hasExactSynonym: purine nucleoside triphosphate metabolism
IAO_0000115: The chemical reactions and pathways involving purine nucleoside triphosphate, a compound consisting of a purine base linked to a ribose or deoxyribose sugar esterified with triphosphate on the sugar.

LABEL: fungal-type cell wall
IAO_0000115: A rigid yet dynamic structure surrounding the plasma membrane that affords protection from stresses and contributes to cell morphogenesis, consisting of extensively cross-linked glycoproteins and carbohydrates. The glycoproteins may be modified with N- or O-linked carbohydrates, or glycosylphosphatidylinositol (GPI) anchors; the polysaccharides are primarily branched glucans, including beta-linked and alpha-linked glucans, and may also include chitin and other carbohydrate polymers, but not cellulose or pectin. Enzymes involved in cell wall biosynthesis are also found in the cell wall. Note that some forms of fungi develop a capsule outside of the cell wall under certain circumstances; this is considered a separate structure.

LABEL: cell outer membrane
hasExactSynonym: outer membrane of cell
IAO_0000115: A lipid bilayer that forms the outermost membrane of the cell envelope; enriched in polysaccharide and protein; the outer leaflet of the membrane contains specific lipopolysaccharide structures.

LABEL: protein secretion
IAO_0000115: The controlled release of proteins from a cell.

LABEL: oligosaccharide metabolic process
hasExactSynonym: oligosaccharide metabolism
IAO_0000115: The chemical reactions and pathways involving oligosaccharides, molecules with between two and (about) 20 monosaccharide residues connected by glycosidic linkages.

LABEL: response to radiation
hasExactSynonym: response to electromagnetic radiation stimulus|response to radiation stimulus
IAO_0000115: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of an electromagnetic radiation stimulus. Electromagnetic radiation is a propagating wave in space with electric and magnetic components. These components oscillate at right angles to each other and to the direction of propagation.

LABEL: response to heat
IAO_0000115: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a heat stimulus, a temperature stimulus above the optimal temperature for that organism.

LABEL: response to cold
IAO_0000115: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a cold stimulus, a temperature stimulus below the optimal temperature for that organism.

LABEL: response to xenobiotic stimulus
IAO_0000115: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a stimulus from a xenobiotic, a compound foreign to the organism exposed to it. It may be synthesized by another organism (like ampicilin) or it can be a synthetic chemical.

LABEL: response to water deprivation
hasExactSynonym: response to dehydration|response to drought|response to thirst
IAO_0000115: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a water deprivation stimulus, prolonged deprivation of water.

LABEL: response to water
hasExactSynonym: response to water stimulus
IAO_0000115: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a stimulus reflecting the presence, absence, or concentration of water.

IAO_0000115: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA).

LABEL: chloroplast
IAO_0000115: A chlorophyll-containing plastid with thylakoids organized into grana and frets, or stroma thylakoids, and embedded in a stroma.

LABEL: plastid envelope
IAO_0000115: The double lipid bilayer enclosing a plastid and separating its contents from the rest of the cytoplasm; includes the intermembrane space.

LABEL: plastid
IAO_0000115: Any member of a family of organelles found in the cytoplasm of plants and some protists, which are membrane-bounded and contain DNA. Plant plastids develop from a common type, the proplastid.

LABEL: proplastid
IAO_0000115: The precursor of other plastids.

LABEL: response to wounding
hasExactSynonym: physiological response to wounding
IAO_0000115: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a stimulus indicating damage to the organism.

LABEL: response to virus
hasExactSynonym: response to viruses
IAO_0000115: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a stimulus from a virus.

LABEL: response to abiotic stimulus
IAO_0000115: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of an abiotic (not derived from living organisms) stimulus.

LABEL: hormone-mediated signaling pathway
hasExactSynonym: hormone mediated signalling
IAO_0000115: The series of molecular signals mediated by the detection of a hormone.

LABEL: pollination
IAO_0000115: The cascade of biological processes occurring in plants beginning when the pollen lands on the female reproductive organs of a plant and continuing up to, but not including, fertilization, as defined by sperm-egg cell fusion.

LABEL: chloroplast envelope
IAO_0000115: The double lipid bilayer enclosing the chloroplast and separating its contents from the rest of the cytoplasm; includes the intermembrane space.

LABEL: cellular process
hasExactSynonym: cell physiology|cellular physiological process
IAO_0000115: Any process that is carried out at the cellular level, but not necessarily restricted to a single cell. For example, cell communication occurs among more than one cell, but occurs at the cellular level.

LABEL: response to zinc ion
hasExactSynonym: response to zinc
IAO_0000115: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a zinc ion stimulus.

LABEL: response to lithium ion
IAO_0000115: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a lithium (Li+) ion stimulus.

LABEL: obsolete multicellular organism aging
IAO_0000115: OBSOLETE. An aging process that has as participant a whole multicellular organism. Multicellular organism aging includes loss of functions such as resistance to disease, homeostasis, and fertility, as well as wear and tear. Multicellular organisms aging includes processes like cellular senescence and organ senescence, but is more inclusive. May precede death (GO:0016265) of an organism and may succeed developmental maturation (GO:0021700).

LABEL: regulation of gene expression
IAO_0000115: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of gene expression. Gene expression is the process in which a gene's coding sequence is converted into a mature gene product (protein or RNA).

LABEL: regulation of platelet activation
IAO_0000115: Any process that modulates the rate or frequency of platelet activation. Platelet activation is a series of progressive, overlapping events triggered by exposure of the platelets to subendothelial tissue.

LABEL: lipid localization
hasExactSynonym: lipid localisation
IAO_0000115: Any process in which a lipid is transported to, or maintained in, a specific location.

LABEL: magnesium ion homeostasis
IAO_0000115: Any process involved in the maintenance of an internal steady state of magnesium ions within an organism or cell.

LABEL: endomembrane system
IAO_0000115: A collection of membranous structures involved in transport within the cell. The main components of the endomembrane system are endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi bodies, vesicles, cell membrane and nuclear envelope. Members of the endomembrane system pass materials through each other or though the use of vesicles.

LABEL: vesicle membrane
IAO_0000115: The lipid bilayer surrounding any membrane-bounded vesicle in the cell.

LABEL: ER to Golgi transport vesicle membrane
hasExactSynonym: COPII coated vesicle membrane|ER to Golgi constitutive secretory pathway transport vesicle membrane|ER-Golgi transport vesicle membrane|endoplasmic reticulum to Golgi transport vesicle membrane|endoplasmic reticulum-Golgi transport vesicle membrane
IAO_0000115: The lipid bilayer surrounding a vesicle transporting substances from the endoplasmic reticulum to the Golgi.

LABEL: monolayer-surrounded lipid storage body
hasExactSynonym: oil body|oilbody|oleosome|spherosome
IAO_0000115: A subcellular organelle of plant cells surrounded by 'half-unit' or a monolayer membrane instead of the more usual bilayer. The storage body has a droplet of triglyceride surrounded by a monolayer of phospholipids, interacting with the triglycerides and the hydrophilic head groups facing the cytosol, and containing major protein components called oleosins.

LABEL: neural crest cell development
IAO_0000115: The process aimed at the progression of a neural crest cell over time, from initial commitment of the cell to its specific fate, to the fully functional differentiated cell.

LABEL: postsynaptic density
hasExactSynonym: neuronal postsynaptic density|post synaptic density|post-synaptic density
IAO_0000115: An electron dense network of proteins within and adjacent to the postsynaptic membrane of an asymmetric, neuron-neuron synapse. Its major components include neurotransmitter receptors and the proteins that spatially and functionally organize them such as anchoring and scaffolding molecules, signaling enzymes and cytoskeletal components.

LABEL: response to isoquinoline alkaloid
IAO_0000115: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of an isoquinoline alkaloid stimulus. An isoquinoline alkaloid is any member of a group of compounds with the heterocyclic ring structure of benzo(c)pyridine which is a structure characteristic of the group of opium alkaloids.

LABEL: gastro-intestinal system smooth muscle contraction
IAO_0000115: A process in which force is generated within smooth muscle tissue, resulting in a change in muscle geometry. This process occurs in the gastro-intestinal system. Force generation involves a chemo-mechanical energy conversion step that is carried out by the actin/myosin complex activity, which generates force through ATP hydrolysis. The gastro-intestinal system generally refers to the digestive structures stretching from the mouth to anus, but does not include the accessory glandular organs (liver, pancreas and biliary tract).

LABEL: urinary tract smooth muscle contraction
IAO_0000115: A process in which force is generated within smooth muscle tissue, resulting in a change in muscle geometry. This process occurs in the urinary tract. Force generation involves a chemo-mechanical energy conversion step that is carried out by the actin/myosin complex activity, which generates force through ATP hydrolysis. The urinary tract consists of organs of the body that produce and discharge urine. These include the kidneys, ureters, bladder, and urethra.

LABEL: protein transport
IAO_0000115: The directed movement of proteins into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

LABEL: glycine amidinotransferase activity
IAO_0000115: Catalysis of the reaction: L-arginine + glycine = L-ornithine + guanidinoacetate.

LABEL: monoatomic ion transmembrane transporter activity
IAO_0000115: Enables the transfer of an ion from one side of a membrane to the other.

LABEL: chloride transmembrane transporter activity
hasExactSynonym: chloride ion transmembrane transporter activity
IAO_0000115: Enables the transfer of chloride ions from one side of a membrane to the other.

LABEL: sialic acid transmembrane transporter activity
IAO_0000115: Enables the transfer of sialic acid from one side of a membrane to the other.

LABEL: glucose-6-phosphate transmembrane transporter activity
IAO_0000115: Enables the transfer of glucose-6-phosphate from one side of a membrane to the other. Glucose-6-phosphate is a monophosphorylated derivative of glucose with the phosphate group attached to C-6.

LABEL: amino acid transmembrane transporter activity
hasExactSynonym: amino acid permease activity
IAO_0000115: Enables the transfer of amino acids from one side of a membrane to the other. Amino acids are organic molecules that contain an amino group and a carboxyl group.

LABEL: water channel activity
IAO_0000115: Enables the energy-independent facilitated diffusion of water through a transmembrane aqueous pore or channel.

LABEL: channel activity
IAO_0000115: Enables the energy-independent facilitated diffusion of a solute through a transmembrane aqueous pore or channel. Stereospecificity is not exhibited but this transport may be specific for a particular molecular species or class of molecules.

LABEL: calcium-activated potassium channel activity
IAO_0000115: Enables the transmembrane transfer of a potassium cation by a channel that opens when a calcium cation has been bound by the channel complex or one of its constituent parts.

LABEL: ligand-gated monoatomic ion channel activity
IAO_0000115: Enables the transmembrane transfer of an ion by a channel that opens when a specific ligand has been bound by the channel complex or one of its constituent parts.

LABEL: microtubule cytoskeleton
IAO_0000115: The part of the cytoskeleton (the internal framework of a cell) composed of microtubules and associated proteins.

LABEL: magnesium ion transport
IAO_0000115: The directed movement of magnesium (Mg) ions into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

LABEL: bilirubin transport
IAO_0000115: The directed movement of bilirubin into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

LABEL: neutral amino acid transport
IAO_0000115: The directed movement of neutral amino acids, amino acids with no net charge, into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

LABEL: folic acid transport
hasExactSynonym: folate transport|vitamin B9 transport|vitamin M transport
IAO_0000115: The directed movement of folic acid (pteroylglutamic acid) into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. Folic acid is widely distributed as a member of the vitamin B complex and is essential for the synthesis of purine and pyrimidines.

LABEL: thiamine transport
hasExactSynonym: thiamin transport|vitamin B1 transport
IAO_0000115: The directed movement of thiamine into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. Thiamine is vitamin B1, a water soluble vitamin present in fresh vegetables and meats, especially liver.

LABEL: cobalamin transport
hasExactSynonym: vitamin B12 transport
IAO_0000115: The directed movement of cobalamin (vitamin B12), a water-soluble vitamin characterized by possession of a corrin nucleus containing a cobalt atom, into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

LABEL: pantothenate metabolic process
hasExactSynonym: pantothenate metabolism|vitamin B5 metabolic process|vitamin B5 metabolism
IAO_0000115: The chemical reactions and pathways involving pantothenate, the anion of pantothenic acid, the amide of beta-alanine and pantoic acid. It is a B complex vitamin that is a constituent of coenzyme A and is distributed ubiquitously in foods.

LABEL: sarcoglycan complex
hasExactSynonym: sarcoglycan-sarcospan complex
IAO_0000115: A protein complex formed of four sarcoglycans plus sarcospan; there are six known sarcoglycans: alpha-, beta-, gamma-, delta-, epsilon- and zeta-sarcoglycan; all are N-glycosylated single-pass transmembrane proteins. The sarcoglycan-sarcospan complex is a subcomplex of the dystrophin glycoprotein complex, and is fixed to the dystrophin axis by a lateral association with the dystroglycan complex.

LABEL: membrane
IAO_0000115: A lipid bilayer along with all the proteins and protein complexes embedded in it and attached to it.

LABEL: lipid catabolic process
hasExactSynonym: lipid breakdown|lipid catabolism|lipid degradation|lipolysis
IAO_0000115: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of lipids, compounds soluble in an organic solvent but not, or sparingly, in an aqueous solvent.

LABEL: cellular component organization
hasExactSynonym: cell organisation|cellular component organisation at cellular level|cellular component organisation in other organism|cellular component organization at cellular level|cellular component organization in other organism
IAO_0000115: A process that results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of a cellular component.

LABEL: type I hypersensitivity
hasExactSynonym: immediate hypersensitivity response
IAO_0000115: An inflammatory response driven by antigen recognition by antibodies bound to Fc receptors on mast cells or basophils, occurring within minutes after exposure of a sensitized individual to the antigen, and leading to the release of a variety of inflammatory mediators such as histamines.

LABEL: carotene metabolic process
hasExactSynonym: carotene metabolism
IAO_0000115: The chemical reactions and pathways involving carotenes, hydrocarbon carotenoids.

LABEL: sterol metabolic process
hasExactSynonym: sterol metabolism
IAO_0000115: The chemical reactions and pathways involving sterols, steroids with one or more hydroxyl groups and a hydrocarbon side-chain in the molecule.

LABEL: sterol biosynthetic process
hasExactSynonym: sterol anabolism|sterol biosynthesis|sterol formation|sterol synthesis
IAO_0000115: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of sterols, steroids with one or more hydroxyl groups and a hydrocarbon side-chain in the molecule.

LABEL: superoxide-generating NAD(P)H oxidase activity
IAO_0000115: Catalysis of the reaction: NAD(P)H + O2 = NAD(P)H + O2-.

LABEL: N-sulfoglucosamine sulfohydrolase activity
hasExactSynonym: N-sulphoglucosamine sulphohydrolase activity
IAO_0000115: Catalysis of the reaction: N-sulfo-D-glucosamine + H2O = D-glucosamine + sulfate.

LABEL: protein processing
IAO_0000115: Any protein maturation process achieved by the cleavage of a peptide bond or bonds within a protein. Protein maturation is the process leading to the attainment of the full functional capacity of a protein.

LABEL: transferase activity
IAO_0000115: Catalysis of the transfer of a group, e.g. a methyl group, glycosyl group, acyl group, phosphorus-containing, or other groups, from one compound (generally regarded as the donor) to another compound (generally regarded as the acceptor). Transferase is the systematic name for any enzyme of EC class 2.

LABEL: short-chain fatty acyl-CoA dehydrogenase activity
hasExactSynonym: short-chain acyl CoA dehydrogenase|short-chain-acyl-CoA dehydrogenase activity
IAO_0000115: Catalysis of the reaction: a short-chain 2,3-saturated fatty acyl-CoA + H+ + oxidized [electron-transfer flavoprotein] = a short-chain (2E)-enoyl-CoA + reduced [electron-transfer flavoprotein]. A short-chain fatty acid has an aliphatic tail containing fewer than 6 carbons.

LABEL: very-long-chain fatty acyl-CoA dehydrogenase activity
hasExactSynonym: very long-chain-acyl-CoA dehydrogenase activity|very-long-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase activity
IAO_0000115: Catalysis of the reaction: a very-long-chain 2,3-saturated fatty acyl-CoA + H+ + oxidized [electron-transfer flavoprotein] = a very-long-chain (2E)-enoyl-CoA + reduced [electron-transfer flavoprotein]. A very long-chain fatty acid has an aliphatic tail containing more than 22 carbons.

LABEL: COG complex
hasExactSynonym: Golgi transport complex|conserved oligomeric Golgi complex
IAO_0000115: A multisubunit tethering complex of the CATCHR family (complexes associated with tethering containing helical rods) that has a role in tethering vesicles to the Golgi prior to fusion. Composed of 8 subunits COG1-8.

LABEL: 5-oxoprolinase (ATP-hydrolyzing) activity
IAO_0000115: Catalysis of the reaction: 5-oxo-L-proline + ATP + 2 H2O = L-glutamate + ADP + 2 H+ + phosphate.

LABEL: obsolete heterocycle biosynthetic process
IAO_0000115: OBSOLETE. The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of heterocyclic compounds, those with a cyclic molecular structure and at least two different atoms in the ring (or rings).

LABEL: obsolete biotin-protein ligase activity

IAO_0000115: OBSOLETE. Catalysis of the reaction: ATP + biotin + protein = AMP + diphosphate + biotin-protein.

LABEL: methanethiol oxidase activity
IAO_0000115: Catalysis of the reaction: methanethiol + O2 + H2O = hydrogen sulfide + formaldehyde + H2O2 + H+.

LABEL: regulation of vasoconstriction
IAO_0000115: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of reductions in the diameter of blood vessels.

LABEL: sensory perception of pain
IAO_0000115: The series of events required for an organism to receive a painful stimulus, convert it to a molecular signal, and recognize and characterize the signal. A painful stimulus is any physical or chemical event that has the potential to cause tissue damage (actual or perceived) and activates the nociceptive system.

LABEL: fatty acid oxidation
IAO_0000115: The removal of one or more electrons from a fatty acid, with or without the concomitant removal of a proton or protons, by reaction with an electron-accepting substance, by addition of oxygen or by removal of hydrogen.

LABEL: obsolete aromatic compound biosynthetic process
IAO_0000115: OBSOLETE. The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of aromatic compounds, any substance containing an aromatic carbon ring.

LABEL: protein metabolic process
hasExactSynonym: cellular protein metabolic process|cellular protein metabolism|protein metabolic process and modification|protein metabolism|protein metabolism and modification
IAO_0000115: The chemical reactions and pathways involving a protein. Includes protein modification.

LABEL: organophosphate metabolic process
hasExactSynonym: organophosphate metabolism
IAO_0000115: The chemical reactions and pathways involving organophosphates, any phosphate-containing organic compound.

LABEL: ribose phosphate metabolic process
hasExactSynonym: ribose phosphate metabolism
IAO_0000115: The chemical reactions and pathways involving ribose phosphate, any phosphorylated ribose sugar.

LABEL: immunoglobulin complex
IAO_0000115: A protein complex that in its canonical form is composed of two identical immunoglobulin heavy chains and two identical immunoglobulin light chains, held together by disulfide bonds and sometimes complexed with additional proteins. An immunoglobulin complex may be embedded in the plasma membrane or present in the extracellular space, in mucosal areas or other tissues, or circulating in the blood or lymph.

LABEL: L-ascorbic acid biosynthetic process
