LABEL: pharyngeal system development
IAO_0000115: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the pharyngeal system over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The pharyngeal system is a transient embryonic complex that is specific to vertebrates. It comprises the pharyngeal arches, bulges of tissues of mesoderm and neural crest derivation through which pass nerves and pharyngeal arch arteries. The arches are separated internally by pharyngeal pouches, evaginations of foregut endoderm, and externally by pharyngeal clefts, invaginations of surface ectoderm. The development of the system ends when the structure it contributes to are forming: the thymus, thyroid, parathyroids, maxilla, mandible, aortic arch, cardiac outflow tract, external and middle ear.

LABEL: heart contraction
hasExactSynonym: heart beating
IAO_0000115: The multicellular organismal process in which the heart decreases in volume in a characteristic way to propel blood through the body.

LABEL: micturition
hasExactSynonym: urination|urine voiding
IAO_0000115: The regulation of body fluids process in which parasympathetic nerves stimulate the bladder wall muscle to contract and expel urine from the body.

LABEL: relaxation of vascular associated smooth muscle
hasExactSynonym: relaxation of vascular smooth muscle|vascular smooth muscle relaxation
IAO_0000115: A negative regulation of smooth muscle contraction resulting in relaxation of vascular smooth muscle. The relaxation is mediated by a decrease in the phosphorylation state of myosin light chain. This can be achieved by removal of calcium from the cytoplasm to the sarcoplasmic reticulum lumen through the action of Ca2+ ATPases leading to a decrease myosin light chain kinase activity, and through calcium-independent pathways leading to a increase in myosin light chain phosphatase activity.

LABEL: regulation of ovulation
IAO_0000115: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of ovulation, the release of a mature ovum/oocyte from an ovary.

LABEL: positive regulation of ovulation
IAO_0000115: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of ovulation, the release of a mature ovum/oocyte from an ovary.

LABEL: bone development
IAO_0000115: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of bone over time, from its formation to the mature structure. Bone is the hard skeletal connective tissue consisting of both mineral and cellular components.

LABEL: regulation of gastric acid secretion
IAO_0000115: Any process that modulates the rate frequency or extent of gastric secretion. Gastric secretion is the regulated release of gastric acid (hydrochloric acid) by parietal or oxyntic cells during digestion.

LABEL: positive regulation of gastric acid secretion
IAO_0000115: Any process that increases the rate frequency or extent of gastric secretion. Gastric secretion is the regulated release of gastric acid (hydrochloric acid) by parietal or oxyntic cells during digestion.

LABEL: negative regulation of gastric acid secretion
IAO_0000115: Any process that decreases the rate frequency or extent of gastric secretion. Gastric secretion is the regulated release of gastric acid (hydrochloric acid) by parietal or oxyntic cells during digestion.

LABEL: regulation of wound healing
IAO_0000115: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency, or extent of the series of events that restore integrity to a damaged tissue, following an injury.

LABEL: vascular wound healing
IAO_0000115: Blood vessel formation when new vessels emerge from the proliferation of pre-existing blood vessels and contribute to the series of events that restore integrity to damaged vasculature.

LABEL: negative regulation of wound healing
IAO_0000115: Any process that decreases the rate, frequency, or extent of the series of events that restore integrity to a damaged tissue, following an injury.

LABEL: cardiac conduction
IAO_0000115: Transfer of an organized electrical impulse across the heart to coordinate the contraction of cardiac muscles. The process begins with generation of an action potential (in the sinoatrial node (SA) in humans) and ends with a change in the rate, frequency, or extent of the contraction of the heart muscles.

LABEL: response to anticoagulant
IAO_0000115: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of an anticoagulant stimulus.

LABEL: response to aromatase inhibitor
IAO_0000115: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of an aromatase inhibitor stimulus.

IAO_0000115: The regulated release of norepinephrine by a cell, in which the norepinephrine acts as a neurotransmitter.

LABEL: pharyngeal arch artery morphogenesis
IAO_0000115: The process in which the anatomical structures of a pharyngeal arch artery is generated and organized. The pharyngeal arch arteries are a series of six paired embryological vascular structures, the development of which give rise to several major arteries, such as the stapedial artery, the middle meningeal artery, the internal carotid artery and the pulmonary artery.

LABEL: canonical inflammasome complex
IAO_0000115: A cytosolic protein complex that is capable of activating caspase-1.

LABEL: extracellular membrane-bounded organelle
hasExactSynonym: extracellular membrane-enclosed organelle
IAO_0000115: Organized structure of distinctive morphology and function, bounded by a lipid bilayer membrane and occurring outside the cell.

LABEL: extracellular exosome

IAO_0000115: A vesicle that is released into the extracellular region by fusion of the limiting endosomal membrane of a multivesicular body with the plasma membrane. Extracellular exosomes, also simply called exosomes, have a diameter of about 40-100 nm.

LABEL: tear secretion
IAO_0000115: The regulated release of the aqueous layer of the tear film from the lacrimal glands. Tears are the liquid product of a process of lacrimation to clean and lubricate the eyes. Tear fluid contains water, mucin, lipids, lysozyme, lactoferrin, lipocalin, lacritin, immunoglobulins, glucose, urea, sodium, and potassium.

IAO_0000115: OBSOLETE. The covalent attachment and further modification of carbohydrate residues to a substrate molecule.

IAO_0000115: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the regulated release of glucagon.

IAO_0000115: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of the regulated release of glucagon.

IAO_0000115: Catalysis of the reaction: H2S (hydrogen sulfide) + a quinone = S0 (sulfane sulfur) + a hydroquinone.

hasExactSynonym: nephron absorption|renal reabsorption
IAO_0000115: A renal system process in which water, ions, glucose and proteins are taken up from the collecting ducts, glomerulus and proximal and distal loops of the nephron. IAO_0000115: A nuclear receptor-mediated signaling pathway initiated by vitamin D binding to an intracellular receptor of the nuclear receptor protein family, and ending with regulation of a downstream cellular process, e.g. transcription.

IAO_0000115: Catalysis of the reaction: (S)-2-(5-amino-1-(5-phospho-D-ribosyl)imidazole-4-carboxamido)succinate = fumarate + 5-amino-1-(5-phospho-D-ribosyl)imidazole-4-carboxamide.

hasExactSynonym: UV-damaged DNA endonuclease-dependent excision repair|UVDE-dependent excision repair|UVER
IAO_0000115: A DNA repair process that is initiated by an endonuclease that introduces a single-strand incision immediately 5' of a UV-induced damage site. UV-damage excision repair acts on both cyclobutane pyrimidine dimers (CPDs) and pyrimidine-pyrimidone 6-4 photoproducts (6-4PPs).

hasExactSynonym: MCAD activity
IAO_0000115: Catalysis of the reaction: a medium-chain 2,3-saturated fatty acyl-CoA + H+ + oxidized [electron-transfer flavoprotein] = a medium-chain trans-(2E)-enoyl-CoA + reduced [electron-transfer flavoprotein]. A medium-chain fatty acid has an aliphatic tail containing 6 to 12 carbons.

LABEL: cellular response to abiotic stimulus
IAO_0000115: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of an abiotic (non-living) stimulus.

LABEL: cellular response to pH
IAO_0000115: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a pH stimulus. pH is a measure of the acidity or basicity of an aqueous solution.

LABEL: vocalization behavior
hasExactSynonym: vocalisation behaviour
IAO_0000115: The behavior in which an organism produces sounds by a mechanism involving its respiratory system.

LABEL: ectodermal placode development
IAO_0000115: The progression of an ectodermal placode over time from its initial formation until its mature state. An ectodermal placode is a thickening of the ectoderm that is the primordium of many structures derived from the ectoderm.

LABEL: obsolete organic substance metabolic process
hasExactSynonym: organic molecular entity metabolic process|organic molecular entity metabolism|organic substance metabolism
IAO_0000115: OBSOLETE. The chemical reactions and pathways involving an organic substance, any molecular entity containing carbon.

LABEL: triglyceride-rich lipoprotein particle clearance
IAO_0000115: The process in which a triglyceride-rich lipoprotein particle is removed from the blood via receptor-mediated endocytosis and its constituent parts degraded.

LABEL: cell periphery
IAO_0000115: The broad region around and including the plasma membrane of a cell, encompassing the cell cortex (inside the cell), the plasma membrane, and any external encapsulating structures.

LABEL: elastic fiber
hasExactSynonym: elastic fibre|elastin fiber
IAO_0000115: An supramolecular fiber that consists of an insoluble core of polymerized tropoelastin monomers and a surrounding mantle of microfibrils. Elastic fibers provide elasticity and recoiling to tissues and organs, and maintain structural integrity against mechanical strain.

LABEL: circulatory system development
IAO_0000115: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the circulatory system over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The circulatory system is the organ system that passes nutrients (such as amino acids and electrolytes), gases, hormones, blood cells, etc. to and from cells in the body to help fight diseases and help stabilize body temperature and pH to maintain homeostasis.

LABEL: purine-containing compound metabolic process
hasExactSynonym: purine and derivative metabolic process|purine-containing compound metabolism
IAO_0000115: The chemical reactions and pathways involving a purine-containing compound, i.e. any compound that contains purine or a formal derivative thereof.

LABEL: response to hydroxyurea
hasExactSynonym: response to HU
IAO_0000115: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a hydroxyurea stimulus.

LABEL: negative regulation of platelet aggregation
IAO_0000115: Any process that decreases the rate, frequency or extent of platelet aggregation. Platelet aggregation is the adhesion of one platelet to one or more other platelets via adhesion molecules.

IAO_0000115: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a carboplatin stimulus.

IAO_0000115: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of an antimetabolite stimulus. LABEL: response to cytarabine
IAO_0000115: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a cytarabine stimulus.

LABEL: response to olanzapine
IAO_0000115: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of an olanzapine stimulus.

IAO_0000115: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a perphenazine stimulus. LABEL: response to quetiapine
IAO_0000115: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a quetiapine stimulus.

IAO_0000115: An abnormality of refraction characterized by the ability to see objects nearby clearly, while objects in the distance appear blurry.

LABEL: Abnormal conjugate eye movement
hasExactSynonym: Disconjugate eye movements
IAO_0000115: Any deviation from the normal motor coordination of the eyes that allows for bilateral fixation on a single object.

LABEL: Color vision defect
hasExactSynonym: Abnormal color vision|Abnormal colour vision|Abnormality of color vision|Abnormality of colour vision|Colour vision defect|Disturbed color vision|Disturbed colour vision
IAO_0000115: An anomaly in the ability to discriminate between or recognize colors.

LABEL: Uveitis
IAO_0000115: Inflammation of one or all portions of the uveal tract.

LABEL: Retinal dystrophy
hasExactSynonym: Breakdown of light-sensitive cells in back of eye
IAO_0000115: Retinal dystrophy is an abnormality of the retina associated with a hereditary process. Retinal dystrophies are defined by their predominantly monogenic inheritance and they are frequently associated with loss or dysfunction of photoreceptor cells as a primary or secondary event.

LABEL: Esotropia
hasExactSynonym: Inward turning cross eyed
IAO_0000115: A form of strabismus with one or both eyes turned inward ('crossed') to a relatively severe degree, usually defined as 10 diopters or more.

LABEL: Chorioretinal coloboma
hasExactSynonym: Birth defect that causes a hole in the innermost layer at the back of the eye|Choroidoretinal coloboma
IAO_0000115: Absence of a region of the retina, retinal pigment epithelium, and choroid.

LABEL: Visual loss
hasExactSynonym: Loss of vision|Vision loss|Visual loss
IAO_0000115: Loss of visual acuity (implying that vision was better at a certain time point in life). Otherwise the term reduced visual acuity should be used (or a subclass of that).

LABEL: Retinal hemorrhage
hasExactSynonym: Retinal bleeding|Retinal haemorrhage|Retinal haemorrhages|Retinal hemorrhages
IAO_0000115: Bleeding located within the retina. Retinal hemorrhages range from the smallest dot and blot hemorrhage to massive sub-hyaloid hemorrhage.

LABEL: Thick eyebrow
hasExactSynonym: Bushy eyebrows|Dense eyebrow|Heavy eyebrows|Hypertrichosis of the eyebrow|Prominent eyebrows|Thick eyebrow|Thick eyebrows
IAO_0000115: Increased density/number and/or increased diameter of eyebrow hairs.

LABEL: Exotropia
hasExactSynonym: Outward facing eye ball
IAO_0000115: A form of strabismus with one or both eyes deviated outward.

LABEL: Nasolacrimal duct obstruction
hasExactSynonym: Blocked tear duct|Lacrimal duct obstruction
IAO_0000115: Blockage of the lacrimal duct.

LABEL: Pigmentary retinopathy
hasExactSynonym: Pigmentary retinal deposits|Retinal pigment clumping|Retinal pigmentary clumping|Retinal pigmentary degeneration
IAO_0000115: An abnormality of the retina characterized by pigment deposition. It is typically associated with migration and proliferation of macrophages or retinal pigment epithelial cells into the retina; melanin from these cells causes the pigmentary changes. Pigmentary retinopathy is a common final pathway of many retinal conditions and is often associated with visual loss.

LABEL: Blepharophimosis
hasExactSynonym: Decreased width of palpebral fissure|Narrow opening between the eyelids
IAO_0000115: A fixed reduction in the vertical distance between the upper and lower eyelids with short palpebral fissures.

LABEL: Upslanted palpebral fissure
hasExactSynonym: Mongoloid slant|Upslanting palpebral fissures|Upward slanted palpebral fissures|Upward slanting of palpebral fissures|Upward slanting of the opening between the eyelids|Upward slanting palpebral fissures
IAO_0000115: The palpebral fissure inclination is more than two standard deviations above the mean for age (objective); or, the inclination of the palpebral fissure is greater than typical for age.

LABEL: Shallow orbits
hasExactSynonym: Decreased depth of eye sockets|Decreased depth of orbits|Shallow eye sockets|Small shallow orbits
IAO_0000115: Reduced depth of the orbits associated with prominent-appearing ocular globes.

LABEL: Abnormal optic nerve morphology
hasExactSynonym: Abnormality of the optic nerve|Optic nerve issue|optic nerve abnormalities
IAO_0000115: Abnormality of the optic nerve.

LABEL: Abnormal anterior chamber morphology
hasExactSynonym: Abnormality of the anterior chamber|Anterior chamber anomalies|Ocular anterior chamber abnormality
IAO_0000115: Abnormality of the anterior chamber, which is the space in the eye that is behind the cornea and in front of the iris.

LABEL: Abnormality of the ear
hasExactSynonym: Abnormality of the ear|Ear anomaly
IAO_0000115: An abnormality of the ear.

LABEL: Hypotelorism
hasExactSynonym: Abnormally close eyes|Closely spaced eyes|Decreased distance between eye sockets|Decreased distance between eyes|Decreased interpupillary distance|Decreased orbital separation|Ocular hypotelorism
IAO_0000115: Interpupillary distance less than 2 SD below the mean (alternatively, the appearance of an decreased interpupillary distance or closely spaced eyes).

LABEL: Central scotoma
hasExactSynonym: Central blind spot|Central scotomata
IAO_0000115: An area of depressed vision located at the point of fixation and that interferes with central vision.

LABEL: Macular degeneration
IAO_0000115: A nonspecific term denoting degeneration of the retinal pigment epithelium and/or retinal photoreceptor cells of the macula lutea.

LABEL: Abnormal choroid morphology
hasExactSynonym: Abnormality of the choroid
IAO_0000115: Any structural abnormality of the choroid (the posterior part of the uvea, the middle tunic of the eye, consisting mainly of blood vessels).

LABEL: Photophobia
hasExactSynonym: Extreme sensitivity of the eyes to light|Light hypersensitivity|Photodysphoria
IAO_0000115: Excessive sensitivity to light with the sensation of discomfort or pain in the eyes due to exposure to bright light.

LABEL: Abnormal nasolacrimal system morphology
hasExactSynonym: Abnormality of the nasolacrimal system
IAO_0000115: An abnormality of the nasolacrimal drainage system, which serves as a conduit for tear flow from the external eye to the nasal cavity.

LABEL: Abnormal pupil morphology
hasExactSynonym: Abnormal pupillary morphology|Abnormality of the pupil|Pupillary abnormalities|Pupillary abnormality
IAO_0000115: An abnormality of the pupil.

LABEL: Miosis
hasExactSynonym: Constricted pupils|Pupillary constriction
IAO_0000115: Abnormal (non-physiological) constriction of the pupil.

LABEL: Blindness
hasExactSynonym: Blindness|Total vision loss
IAO_0000115: Blindness is the condition of lacking visual perception defined as a profound reduction in visual perception. On the 6m visual acuity scale, blindness is defined as less than 3/60. On the 20ft visual acuity scale, blindness is defined as less than 20/400. On the decimal visual acuity scale, blindness is defined as less than 0.05. Blindness is typically characterized by a visual field of no greater than 10 degrees in radius around central fixation.

LABEL: Blurred vision
hasExactSynonym: Blurred vision
IAO_0000115: Lack of sharpness of vision resulting in the inability to see fine detail.

LABEL: Periorbital fullness
hasExactSynonym: Periorbital puffiness|Periorbital swelling|Puffiness around eye|Puffy eyes|Swelling around the eyes
IAO_0000115: Increase in periorbital soft tissue.

LABEL: Lacrimation abnormality
hasExactSynonym: Abnormality of tear production
IAO_0000115: Abnormality of tear production.

LABEL: Decreased lacrimation
hasExactSynonym: Decreased tear secretion|Hypolacrimia
IAO_0000115: Abnormally decreased lacrimation, that is, reduced tear production.

LABEL: Upper eyelid coloboma
hasExactSynonym: Cleft upper eyelid|Coloboma of the upper eyelid|Full thickness defect of the upper eyelid|Notched upper eyelid|Upper eyelid colobomas
IAO_0000115: A short discontinuity of the margin of the upper eyelid.

LABEL: Long palpebral fissure
hasExactSynonym: Broad opening between the eyelids|Broad palpebral fissure|Long opening between the eyelids|Long palpebral fissures|Wide opening between the eyelids|Wide palpebral fissure|Wide palpebral fissures
IAO_0000115: Distance between medial and lateral canthi is more than two standard deviations above the mean for age (objective); or, apparently increased length of the palpebral fissures.

LABEL: Nystagmus
hasExactSynonym: Involuntary, rapid, rhythmic eye movements
IAO_0000115: Rhythmic, involuntary oscillations of one or both eyes related to abnormality in fixation, conjugate gaze, or vestibular mechanisms.

LABEL: Blepharospasm
hasExactSynonym: Eyelid spasm|Eyelid twitching|Involuntary closure of eyelid|Spontaneous closure of eyelid
IAO_0000115: A focal dystonia that affects the muscles of the eyelids and brow, associated with involuntary recurrent spasm of both eyelids.

LABEL: Amblyopia
hasExactSynonym: Lazy eye|Wandering eye|Wandering eyes
IAO_0000115: Reduced visual acuity that is uncorrectable by lenses in the absence of detectable anatomic defects in the eye or visual pathways.

LABEL: Optic atrophy
hasExactSynonym: Optic nerve atrophy|Optic-nerve degeneration
IAO_0000115: Atrophy of the optic nerve. Optic atrophy results from the death of the retinal ganglion cell axons that comprise the optic nerve and manifesting as a pale optic nerve on fundoscopy.

LABEL: Abnormality of visual evoked potentials
hasExactSynonym: Abnormal vision evoked potentials|Abnormal visual evoked potential|Abnormal visual evoked responses|Abnormal visual-evoked potentials|VEP abnormalities
IAO_0000115: An anomaly of visually evoked potentials (VEP), which are electrical potentials, initiated by brief visual stimuli, which are recorded from the scalp overlying the visual cortex.

LABEL: Diplopia
hasExactSynonym: Double vision
IAO_0000115: Diplopia is a condition in which a single object is perceived as two images, it is also known as double vision.

LABEL: Decreased light- and dark-adapted electroretinogram amplitude
hasExactSynonym: Decreased ERG amplitude|Decreased amplitudes on flash visual electroretinogram|Decreased electroretinogram|Decreased electroretinogram amplitude|Decreased electroretinogram response|Flattened or absent electroretinogram|Reduced ERG|Reduced electroretinogram|Reduced or abolished electroretinogram
IAO_0000115: Decreased amplitude of eletrical response upon electroretinography.

LABEL: Oculomotor apraxia
hasExactSynonym: Ocular motor apraxia
IAO_0000115: Ocular motor apraxia is a deficiency in voluntary, horizontal, lateral, fast eye movements (saccades) with retention of slow pursuit movements. The inability to follow objects visually is often compensated by head movements. There may be decreased smooth pursuit, and cancelation of the vestibulo-ocular reflex.

LABEL: Synophrys
hasExactSynonym: Monobrow|Synophris|Unibrow
IAO_0000115: Meeting of the medial eyebrows in the midline.

LABEL: Horizontal nystagmus
hasExactSynonym: Nystagmus, horizontal
IAO_0000115: Nystagmus consisting of horizontal to-and-fro eye movements.

LABEL: Hypodontia
hasExactSynonym: Failure of development of between one and six teeth
IAO_0000115: The absence of five or less teeth from the normal series by a failure to develop.

LABEL: Oligodontia
hasExactSynonym: Failure of development of more than six teeth|Partial anodontia
IAO_0000115: The absence of six or more teeth from the normal series by a failure to develop.

LABEL: Dental crowding
hasExactSynonym: Crowded teeth|Dental crowding|Dental overcrowding|Overcrowding of teeth
IAO_0000115: Changes in alignment of teeth in the dental arch

LABEL: Delayed eruption of primary teeth
hasExactSynonym: Delayed eruption of baby teeth|Delayed eruption of deciduous teeth|Delayed eruption of milk teeth|Delayed primary teeth eruption|Late eruption of baby teeth|Late eruption of milk teeth|Late eruption of primary teeth
IAO_0000115: Delayed tooth eruption affecting the primary dentition.

LABEL: Abnormal dental enamel morphology
hasExactSynonym: Abnormal tooth enamel|Abnormality of dental enamel|Enamel abnormalities|Enamel abnormality
IAO_0000115: An abnormality of the dental enamel.

LABEL: Dental malocclusion
hasExactSynonym: Bad bite|Bilateral crossbite|Bilateral crossbite malocclusion|Incorrect relation between upper and lower dental arches|Malalignment of upper and lower dental arches|Malocclusion|Malocclusion of teeth|Misalignment of upper and lower dental arches|Occlusion anomaly
IAO_0000115: Dental malocclusion refers to an abnormality of the occlusion, or alignment, of the teeth and the way the upper and lower teeth fit together, resulting in overcrowding of teeth or in abnormal bite patterns.

LABEL: Agenesis of maxillary lateral incisor
hasExactSynonym: Absent upper lateral incisors|Failure of development of maxillary lateral incisor
IAO_0000115: Agenesis of one or more maxillary lateral incisor, comprising the maxillary lateral primary incisor and maxillary lateral secondary incisor.

LABEL: Microdontia
hasExactSynonym: Decreased size of tooth|Decreased width of tooth|Small teeth|Small tooth|Tooth hypoplasia|Tooth hypotrophy|Underdeveloped tooth
IAO_0000115: Decreased size of the teeth, which can be defined as a mesiodistal tooth diameter (width) more than 2 SD below mean. Alternatively, an apparently decreased maximum width of tooth.

LABEL: Tooth malposition
hasExactSynonym: Abnormal dental position|Abnormal teeth spacing|Abnormality of alignment of teeth|Abnormality of teeth spacing|Crooked teeth|Malaligned teeth|Malposition of teeth|Malpositioned teeth|Misalignment of teeth|Teeth, malposition
IAO_0000115: Abnormal alignment, positioning, or spacing of the teeth, i.e., misaligned teeth.

LABEL: Diastema
hasExactSynonym: Dental diastasis|Dental diastema|Diastasis of the teeth|Diastema of the teeth|Gap between teeth
IAO_0000115: Increased space between two adjacent teeth in the same dental arch.

LABEL: Abnormality of the nervous system
hasExactSynonym: Abnormality of the nervous system|Neurologic abnormalities|Neurological abnormality
IAO_0000115: An abnormality of the nervous system.

LABEL: Atypical behavior
hasExactSynonym: Behavioral abnormality|Behavioral changes|Behavioral disorders|Behavioral disturbances|Behavioral problems|Behavioral symptoms|Behavioral/psychiatric abnormalities|Behavioural abnormality|Behavioural changes|Behavioural disorders|Behavioural disturbances|Behavioural problems|Behavioural symptoms|Behavioural/Psychiatric abnormality|Psychiatric disorders|Psychiatric disturbances
IAO_0000115: Atypical behavior is an abnormality in a person's actions that can be controlled or modulated by the will of the individual. While abnormal behaviors can be difficult to control, they are distinct from other abnormal actions that cannot be affected by the individual's will.

LABEL: Emotional lability
IAO_0000115: Unstable emotional experiences and frequent mood changes; emotions that are easily aroused, intense, and/or disproportionate to events and circumstances.

LABEL: Agitation
hasExactSynonym: Psychomotor agitation
IAO_0000115: A state of excessive motor activity that is associated with mental distress or a feeling of substantial unease or inner tension. Distinguished from restlessness by the increased level of emotional distress and negative intensity of the experience. Agitation has a significant level of physical activity that is typically threatening to the self or others.

LABEL: Autism
hasExactSynonym: Autism
IAO_0000115: Autism is a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by impaired social interaction and communication, and by restricted and repetitive behavior. Autism begins in childhood. It is marked by the presence of markedly abnormal or impaired development in social interaction and communication and a markedly restricted repertoire of activity and interest. Manifestations of the disorder vary greatly depending on the developmental level and chronological age of the individual (DSM-IV).

LABEL: Aggressive behavior
hasExactSynonym: Aggression|Aggressive behavior|Aggressiveness
IAO_0000115: Behavior or an act aimed at harming a person, animal, or physical property (e.g., acts of physical violence; shouting, swearing, and using harsh language; slashing someone's tires).

LABEL: Compulsive behaviors
hasExactSynonym: OCD|Obsessive compulsive behavior|Obsessive compulsive behaviour|Obsessive compulsive disorder|Obsessive-compulsive behavior|Obsessive-compulsive behaviour|Obsessive-compulsive disorder
IAO_0000115: Behavior that consists of repetitive acts, characterized by the feeling that one "has to" perform them, while being aware that these acts are not in line with one's overall goal.

LABEL: Psychotic episodes
hasExactSynonym: Psychotic episodes
IAO_0000115: Periods of time during which an individual experiences significant disturbances in their thoughts, perceptions, emotions, and behavior, resulting in a loss of touch with reality. These episodes are hallmark features of psychotic disorders such as schizophrenia, schizoaffective disorder, and certain forms of bipolar disorder.

LABEL: Dementia
hasExactSynonym: Dementia|Dementia, progressive|Progressive dementia
IAO_0000115: A loss of global cognitive ability of sufficient amount to interfere with normal social or occupational function. Dementia represents a loss of previously present cognitive abilities, generally in adults, and can affect memory, thinking, language, judgment, and behavior.

LABEL: Autistic behavior
hasExactSynonym: ASD|Autistic behaviour|Pervasive developmental disorder
IAO_0000115: Persistent deficits in social interaction and communication and interaction as well as a markedly restricted repertoire of activity and interest as well as repetitive patterns of behavior.

LABEL: Inflexible adherence to routines
IAO_0000115: A need to strictly adhere to repetitive routines or patterns of behavior which are created by the environment. One becomes upset or distressed when their routines are disrupted or altered.

LABEL: Motor stereotypy
hasExactSynonym: Abnormal repetitive mannerism|Repetitive behavior|Repetitive behaviour Stereotypic behaviour|Repetitive movements|Repetitive, stereotypic behavior|Stereotyped|Stereotyped behavior|Stereotyped behaviors|Stereotyped behaviour|Stereotyped behaviours|Stereotypic behaviour|Stereotypic behaviours|Stereotypical motor behavior|Stereotypical motor behaviors|Stereotypical motor behaviour|Stereotypical motor behaviours|Stimming|repetitive behaviour
IAO_0000115: Use of the same abnormal action in response to certain triggers or at random. They may be used as a way to regulate one's internal state but must otherwise have no apparent functional purpose.

LABEL: Short attention span
hasExactSynonym: Easily distracted|Easy distractibility|High distractibility|Poor attention span|Problem paying attention|Short attention span
IAO_0000115: Reduced attention span characterized by distractibility and impulsivity.

LABEL: Irritability
hasExactSynonym: Cranky|Easily annoyed|Easily bothered|Easily upset|Grumpy|Hot-temper|Irritability|Irritable|Quick temper|Short fuse|Short tempered
IAO_0000115: An emotional state characterized by negative feelings of heightened frustration, annoyance, or feeling upset, often triggered by internal factors (e.g., fatigue, hunger, unfulfilled desires) or external factors (e.g., social or environmental challenges). Irritability may be unpredictable, and is accompanied by a lowered threshold for emotional reactivity and observable features (speech, facial expressions, or psychomotor activity).

LABEL: Hallucinations
hasExactSynonym: Hallucination|Hallucinations|Sensory hallucination
IAO_0000115: Perceptions in a conscious and awake state that, in the absence of external stimuli, have qualities of real perception. These perceptions are vivid, substantial, and located in external objective space.

LABEL: Anxiety
hasExactSynonym: Anxiety|Anxiousness|Excessive, persistent worry and fear
IAO_0000115: Intense feelings of nervousness, tension, or panic often arise in response to interpersonal stresses. There is worry about the negative effects of past unpleasant experiences and future negative possibilities. Individuals may feel fearful, apprehensive, or threatened by uncertainty, and they may also have fears of falling apart or losing control.

LABEL: Apathy
hasExactSynonym: Lack of feeling, emotion, interest|Lack of feeling, emotion, interest, motivation, initiation|State of indifference
IAO_0000115: Apathy is a quantitative reduction of interest, motivation and the initiation and persistence of goal-directed behavior, where often the accompanying emotions, thoughts, and social interactions are also diminished. The individual is typically non-reactive to provocations, positive or negative, and appears to not care. Distinguished from lethargy which involves lack of physical or mental energy.

LABEL: Self-mutilation
hasExactSynonym: Deliberate self-harm|Self mutilation|Self-mutilation
IAO_0000115: Deliberate harm to one's body resulting in tissue damage, without a conscious intent to die.

LABEL: Delusion
hasExactSynonym: Delusions
IAO_0000115: A delusion is a fixed false belief held despite evidence to the contrary. The term delusion broadly encompasses all false judgments that possess the following external characteristics to a significant, albeit unspecified, extent: (1) they are held with an exceptional level of conviction, accompanied by an unparalleled subjective certainty; (2) there is an inability to consider alternative experiences or compelling counter-arguments; (3) the content of the belief is impossible.

LABEL: Delayed speech and language development
hasExactSynonym: Deficiency of speech development|Delayed language development|Delayed speech|Delayed speech acquisition|Delayed speech and language development|Delayed speech development|Impaired speech and language development|Impaired speech development|Language delay|Language delayed|Language development deficit|Late-onset speech development|Poor language development|Speech and language delay|Speech and language difficulties|Speech delay
IAO_0000115: A degree of language development that is significantly below the norm for a child of a specified age.

LABEL: Personality changes
hasExactSynonym: Personality change|Personality changes
IAO_0000115: An abnormal shift in patterns of thinking, acting, or feeling.

LABEL: Hyperactivity
hasExactSynonym: Hyperactive behavior|Hyperactive behaviour|Hyperkinetic disorder|More active than typical
IAO_0000115: Hyperactivity is a condition characterized by constant and unusually high levels of activity, even in situations where it is deemed inappropriate.

LABEL: Abnormal nonverbal communicative behavior
hasExactSynonym: Impaired use of nonverbal behaviors|Impaired use of nonverbal behaviours
IAO_0000115: Abnormalities in eye contact, communicative facial expressions, gesture use, or the use of others' bodies to communicate convey shared meanings within a culture that replace or supplement verbal communication.

LABEL: Abnormal peripheral nervous system morphology
hasExactSynonym: Abnormal peripheral nervous system structure
IAO_0000115: A structural abnormality of the peripheral nervous system, which is composed of the nerves that lead to or branch off from the central nervous system. This includes the cranial nerves (olfactory and optic nerves are technically part of the central nervous system).

LABEL: Decreased nerve conduction velocity
hasExactSynonym: Decreased NCV|Decreased nerve conduction velocities|Delayed nerve conduction velocity|Reduced nerve conduction velocities|Slow nerve conduction velocity|Slowed nerve conduction velocities
IAO_0000115: A reduction in the speed at which electrical signals propagate along the axon of a neuron.

LABEL: Sensory neuropathy
hasExactSynonym: Damage to nerves that sense feeling|Peripheral sensory neuropathy
IAO_0000115: Peripheral neuropathy affecting the sensory nerves.

LABEL: Abnormal thorax morphology
hasExactSynonym: Abnormality of the chest|Abnormality of the thorax|Structural abnormality of the chest wall
IAO_0000115: Any abnormality of the thorax (the region of the body formed by the sternum, the thoracic vertebrae and the ribs).

LABEL: Abnormal sternum morphology
hasExactSynonym: Abnormality of the sternum|Pectus carinatum or pectus excavatum|Pectus deformities|Pectus deformity|Pectus excavatum or carinatum|Pectus excavatum or pectus carinatum|Pectus excavatum/carinatum|Sternal anomalies
IAO_0000115: An anomaly of the sternum, also known as the breastbone.

LABEL: Pectus excavatum
hasExactSynonym: Funnel chest
IAO_0000115: A defect of the chest wall characterized by a depression of the sternum, giving the chest ("pectus") a caved-in ("excavatum") appearance.

LABEL: Pectus carinatum
hasExactSynonym: Pigeon chest
IAO_0000115: A deformity of the chest caused by overgrowth of the ribs and characterized by protrusion of the sternum.

LABEL: Abnormality of the breast
hasExactSynonym: Abnormality of the breast
IAO_0000115: An abnormality of the breast.

LABEL: Gynecomastia
hasExactSynonym: Enlarged male breast|Gynaecomastia
IAO_0000115: Abnormal development of large mammary glands in males resulting in breast enlargement.

LABEL: Abnormal rib morphology
hasExactSynonym: Abnormality of the ribs|Rib abnormalities|Rib anomalies
IAO_0000115: An anomaly of the rib.

LABEL: Short ribs
hasExactSynonym: Hypoplastic ribs|Rib hypoplasia|Short ribs
IAO_0000115: Reduced rib length.

LABEL: Narrow chest
hasExactSynonym: Low chest circumference|Narrow chest|Narrow shoulders|Narrow thorax|Reduced anterior-posterior chest diameter
IAO_0000115: Reduced width of the chest from side to side, associated with a reduced distance from the sternal notch to the tip of the shoulder.

LABEL: Abnormality of the diaphragm
hasExactSynonym: Abnormality of the diaphragm|Diaphragm issues|Diaphragmatic defect
IAO_0000115: Any abnormality of the diaphragm, the sheet of skeletal muscle that separates the thoracic cavity from the abdominal cavity.

LABEL: Abnormal thymus morphology
hasExactSynonym: Abnormality of the thymus
IAO_0000115: Abnormality of the thymus, an organ located in the upper anterior portion of the chest cavity just behind the sternum and whose main function is to provide an environment for T lymphocyte maturation.

LABEL: Infertility
hasExactSynonym: Infertility

LABEL: Hematuria
hasExactSynonym: Blood in urine
IAO_0000115: The presence of blood in the urine. Hematuria may be gross hematuria (visible to the naked eye) or microscopic hematuria (detected by dipstick or microscopic examination of the urine).

LABEL: Uric acid nephrolithiasis
hasExactSynonym: Uric acid stones|Uric acid urolithiasis
IAO_0000115: The presence of uric acid-containing calculi (stones) in the kidneys.

LABEL: Cystic renal dysplasia
hasExactSynonym: Bilateral cystic dysplasia|Renal cystic dysplasia|Renal dysplasia, cystic

LABEL: Impotence
hasExactSynonym: Difficulty getting a full erection|Difficulty getting an erection
IAO_0000115: Inability to develop or maintain an erection of the penis.

LABEL: Renal cortical cysts
hasExactSynonym: Cortical cysts
IAO_0000115: Cysts of the cortex of the kidney.

LABEL: Hypergonadotropic hypogonadism
hasExactSynonym: Hypergonadotrophic hypogonadism|Primary hypogonadism
IAO_0000115: Reduced function of the gonads (testes in males or ovaries in females) associated with excess pituitary gonadotropin secretion and resulting in delayed sexual development and growth delay.

LABEL: Reduced eye contact
hasExactSynonym: Poor eye contact
IAO_0000115: A reduced frequency or duration of eye contact.

LABEL: Abnormality of the endocrine system
IAO_0000115: An abnormality of the endocrine system.

LABEL: Diabetes mellitus
IAO_0000115: A group of abnormalities characterized by hyperglycemia and glucose intolerance.

LABEL: Abnormality of the thyroid gland
hasExactSynonym: Abnormality of the thyroid gland|Thyroid abnormality
IAO_0000115: An abnormality of the thyroid gland.

LABEL: Hypertension
hasExactSynonym: Arterial hypertension|Systemic hypertension
IAO_0000115: The presence of chronic increased pressure in the systemic arterial system.

LABEL: Delayed puberty
hasExactSynonym: Delayed pubertal development|Delayed pubertal growth|Delayed puberty|Pubertal delay
IAO_0000115: Passing the age when puberty normally occurs with no physical or hormonal signs of the onset of puberty.

LABEL: Decreased response to growth hormone stimulation test
IAO_0000115: Insufficient responses to growth hormone (GH) provocation tests. GH deficiency is defined as a serum peak GH concentration less than 10 ng/mL on provocation with a combination of at least two separate stimulation tests.

LABEL: Hypoparathyroidism
hasExactSynonym: Decreased parathyroid hormone secretion|Low parathyroid hormone
IAO_0000115: A condition caused by a deficiency of parathyroid hormone characterized by hypocalcemia and hyperphosphatemia.

LABEL: Anterior hypopituitarism
IAO_0000115: A condition of reduced function of the anterior pituitary gland characterized by decreased secretion of one or more of the pituitary hormones growth hormone, thyroid-stimulating hormone, adrenocorticotropic hormone, prolactin, luteinizing hormone, and follicle-stimulating hormone.

LABEL: Primary hypothyroidism
IAO_0000115: A type of hypothyroidism that results from a defect in the thyroid gland.

LABEL: Abnormality of the adrenal glands
hasExactSynonym: Adrenal abnormalities
IAO_0000115: Abnormality of the adrenal glands, i.e., of the endocrine glands located at the top of the kindneys.

LABEL: Hyperinsulinemia
hasExactSynonym: Elevated insulin level
IAO_0000115: An increased concentration of insulin in the blood.

LABEL: Hyperparathyroidism
hasExactSynonym: Elevated blood parathyroid hormone level
IAO_0000115: Excessive production of parathyroid hormone (PTH) by the parathyroid glands.

LABEL: Adrenal insufficiency
hasExactSynonym: Hypoadrenalism
IAO_0000115: Insufficient production of steroid hormones (primarily cortisol) by the adrenal glands.

LABEL: Goiter
hasExactSynonym: Enlarged thyroid gland in neck|Goitre|Thyroid goiter|Thyroid goitre
IAO_0000115: An enlargement of the thyroid gland.

LABEL: Thyroid adenoma
IAO_0000115: The presence of a adenoma of the thyroid gland.

LABEL: Insulin resistance
hasExactSynonym: Body fails to respond to insulin
IAO_0000115: Increased resistance towards insulin, that is, diminished effectiveness of insulin in reducing blood glucose levels.

LABEL: Irregular menstruation
hasExactSynonym: Irregular menses|Irregular periods|Menstrual irregularities|Menstrual irregularity
IAO_0000115: Abnormally high variation in the amount of time between periods.

LABEL: Increased circulating aldosterone concentration
hasExactSynonym: Elevated plasma aldosterone|Increased aldosterone|Increased aldosterone production|Mineralocorticoid excess
IAO_0000115: Overproduction of the mineralocorticoid aldosterone by the adrenal cortex.

LABEL: Central diabetes insipidus
hasExactSynonym: Neurohypophyseal diabetes insipidus
IAO_0000115: A form of diabetes insipidus related to a failure of vasopressin (AVP) release from the hypothalamus.

LABEL: Increased circulating prolactin concentration
hasExactSynonym: Hyperprolactinaemia|Hyperprolactinemia|Prolactin excess
IAO_0000115: The presence of abnormally increased levels of prolactin in the blood. Prolactin is a peptide hormone produced by the anterior pituitary gland that plays a role in breast development and lactation during pregnancy.

LABEL: Oligomenorrhea
hasExactSynonym: Light or infrequent menstrual periods
IAO_0000115: Infrequent menses (less than 6 per year or more than 35 days between cycles).

LABEL: Hypoplastic scapulae
hasExactSynonym: Hypoplastic scapula|Scapular hypoplasia|Short scapulae|Small scapula|Small scapulae|Small shoulder blade
IAO_0000115: Underdeveloped scapula.

LABEL: Deformed rib cage
hasExactSynonym: Deformed rib cage
IAO_0000115: Malformation of the rib cage.

LABEL: Bifid ribs
hasExactSynonym: Cleft ribs|Split ribs
IAO_0000115: A bifid rib refers to cleavage of the sternal end of a rib, usually unilateral. Bifid ribs are usually asymptomatic, and are often discovered incidentally by chest x-ray.

LABEL: Short clavicles
hasExactSynonym: Clavicular hypoplasia|Hypoplastic clavicles|Short collarbone|Underdeveloped clavicles
IAO_0000115: Reduced length of the clavicles.

LABEL: Rib fusion
hasExactSynonym: Fused ribs|Rib fusion
IAO_0000115: Complete or partial merging of adjacent ribs.

LABEL: Abnormality of the costochondral junction
hasExactSynonym: Costochondral juctions abnormal
IAO_0000115: Any anomaly of the costochondral junction. The costochondral junctions are located between the distal part of the ribs and the costal cartilages, which are bars of hyaline cartilage that connect the ribs to the sternum.

LABEL: Missing ribs
hasExactSynonym: Absent ribs|Decreased rib number|Missing ribs
IAO_0000115: A developmental anomaly with absence of one or more ribs.

LABEL: Abnormality of the skeletal system
hasExactSynonym: Abnormality of the skeletal system|Skeletal abnormalities|Skeletal anomalies
IAO_0000115: An abnormality of the skeletal system.

LABEL: Abnormality of the vertebral column
hasExactSynonym: Abnormal spine|Abnormal vertebral column|Abnormality of the spine|Abnormality of the vertebral column
IAO_0000115: Any abnormality of the vertebral column.

LABEL: Platyspondyly
hasExactSynonym: Flat vertebral bodies|Flattened vertebrae|Flattened vertebral bodies
IAO_0000115: A flattened vertebral body shape with reduced distance between the vertebral endplates.

LABEL: Abnormal skull morphology
hasExactSynonym: Abnormality of the skull
IAO_0000115: An abnormality of the skull, the bony framework of the head which is comprised of the neurocranium (with eight cranial bones) and the viscerocranium (facial skeleton) that comprises fourteen facial bones with the mandible as its largest bone.

LABEL: Abnormal posterior cranial fossa morphology
hasExactSynonym: Abnormality of the posterior cranial fossa|Abnormality of the posterior fossa|Posterior fossa anomaly
IAO_0000115: An abnormality of the fossa cranii posterior (the posterior fossa), which is made up primarily of the occipital bone and which surrounds to the foramen magnum.

LABEL: Chondrocalcinosis
hasExactSynonym: Calcium deposits in joints
IAO_0000115: Radiographic evidence of articular calcification that represent calcium pyrophosphate depositions in soft tissue surrounding joints and at the insertions of tendons near joints (Entheses/Sharpey fibers) .

LABEL: Osteopenia
hasExactSynonym: Generalised osteopenia|Generalized osteopenia|Osteopaenia
IAO_0000115: Osteopenia is a term to define bone density that is not normal but also not as low as osteoporosis. By definition from the World Health Organization osteopenia is defined by bone densitometry as a T score -1 to -2.5.

LABEL: Osteoporosis
IAO_0000115: Osteoporosis is a systemic skeletal disease characterized by low bone density and microarchitectural deterioration of bone tissue with a consequent increase in bone fragility. According to the WHO criteria, osteoporosis is defined as a BMD that lies 2.5 standard deviations or more below the average value for young healthy adults (a T-score below -2.5 SD).

LABEL: Abnormality of the skin
hasExactSynonym: Abnormality of the skin|Dermatopathy|Dermopathy
IAO_0000115: An abnormality of the skin.

LABEL: Jaundice
hasExactSynonym: Icterus|Jaundice|Yellow skin|Yellowing of the skin
IAO_0000115: Yellow pigmentation of the skin due to bilirubin, which in turn is the result of increased bilirubin concentration in the bloodstream.

LABEL: Hyperpigmentation of the skin
hasExactSynonym: Cutaneous hyperpigmentation|Hyperpigmented lesion|Increased skin pigmentation|Patchy darkened skin|Skin hyperpigmentation
IAO_0000115: A darkening of the skin related to an increase in melanin production and deposition.

LABEL: Single transverse palmar crease
hasExactSynonym: Simian crease|Simian creases|Simian line|Single flexion crease|Single palmar crease|Single palmar creases|Single transverse palmar creases|Transverse palmar crease
IAO_0000115: The distal and proximal transverse palmar creases are merged into a single transverse palmar crease.

LABEL: Cafe-au-lait spot
hasExactSynonym: Cafe au lait spots|Cafe-au-lait macule|Cafe-au-lait macules
IAO_0000115: Cafe-au-lait spots are hyperpigmented lesions that can vary in color from light brown to dark brown with smooth borders and having a size of 1.5 cm or more in adults and 0.5 cm or more in children.

LABEL: Dry skin
hasExactSynonym: Dry skin|Xerosis
IAO_0000115: Skin characterized by the lack of natural or normal moisture.

LABEL: Sacral dimple
hasExactSynonym: Pilonidal dimple|Spinal dimple
IAO_0000115: A cutaneous indentation resulting from tethering of the skin to underlying structures (bone) of the intergluteal cleft.

LABEL: Cyanosis
hasExactSynonym: Blue discoloration of the skin
IAO_0000115: Bluish discoloration of the skin and mucosa due to poor circulation or inadequate oxygenation of arterial or capillary blood.

LABEL: Hyperkeratosis
hasExactSynonym: Epidermal hyperkeratosis
IAO_0000115: Hyperkeratosis is a histopathological term defining a thickened stratum corneum and may be present in many different skin conditions, with many possible overlaps. Hyperkeratosis refers to the increased thickness of the stratum corneum, the outer layer of the skin. Hyperkeratosis is subclassified as orthokeratotic or parakeratotic. Orthokeratotic hyperkeratosis refers to the thickening of the keratin layer with preserved keratinocyte maturation, while parakeratotic hyperkeratosis shows retained nuclei as a sign of delayed maturation of keratinocytes.

LABEL: Thin skin
hasExactSynonym: Thin skin
IAO_0000115: Reduction in thickness of the skin, generally associated with a loss of suppleness and elasticity of the skin.

LABEL: Eczematoid dermatitis
hasExactSynonym: Eczema
IAO_0000115: Eczema is a form of dermatitis that is characterized by scaly, pruritic, erythematous lesions located on flexural surfaces.

LABEL: Cutis marmorata
IAO_0000115: A reticular discoloration of the skin with cyanotic (reddish-blue appearing) areas surrounding pale central areas due to dilation of capillary blood vessels and stagnation of blood within the vessels. Cutis marmorata generally occurs on the legs, arms and trunk and is often more severe in cold weather.

LABEL: Hypohidrosis
hasExactSynonym: Decreased ability to sweat|Decreased sweating|Impaired sweating|Inadequate sweating|Oligohidrosis|Sweating, decreased
IAO_0000115: Abnormally diminished capacity to sweat.

LABEL: Edema
hasExactSynonym: Dropsy|Fluid retention|Hydrops|Oedema|Water retention
IAO_0000115: An abnormal accumulation of fluid beneath the skin, or in one or more cavities of the body.

LABEL: Anhidrosis
hasExactSynonym: Anhydrosis|Lack of sweating|Sudomotor dysfunction|Sweating dysfunction
IAO_0000115: Inability to sweat.

LABEL: Palmoplantar hyperkeratosis
hasExactSynonym: Hyperkeratosis of palms and soles|Hyperkeratosis of the palms and soles|Palmoplantar keratoses|Palmoplantar keratosis|Thick palms and soles|Thickened palms and soles|Thickening of the outer layer of the skin of the palms and soles
IAO_0000115: Abnormal thickening of the skin localized to the palm of the hand and the sole of the foot.

LABEL: Cutis laxa
hasExactSynonym: Chalazoderma|Cutaneous laxity|Dermatochalasia|Dermatomegaly|Elastolysis|Generalised elastolysis|Generalized elastolysis|Hypoelastic skin|Inelastic skin|Lax skin|Loose and inelastic skin|Loose skin|Skin laxity
IAO_0000115: Wrinkled, redundant, inelastic and sagging skin.

LABEL: Hyperextensible skin
hasExactSynonym: Hyperelastic skin|Skin hyperelasticity|Skin hyperextensibility|Stretchable skin
IAO_0000115: A condition in which the skin can be stretched beyond normal, and then returns to its initial position.

LABEL: Hyperhidrosis
hasExactSynonym: Diaphoresis|Excessive sweating|Increased sweating|Profuse sweating|Sweating|Sweating profusely|Sweating, increased
IAO_0000115: Abnormal excessive perspiration (sweating) despite the lack of appropriate stimuli like hot and humid weather.

LABEL: Soft skin
hasExactSynonym: Soft skin
IAO_0000115: Subjective impression of increased softness upon palpation of the skin.

LABEL: Bruising susceptibility
hasExactSynonym: Bruisability|Bruise easily|Bruising susceptibility|Easy bruisability|Easy bruising
IAO_0000115: An ecchymosis (bruise) refers to the skin discoloration caused by the escape of blood into the tissues from ruptured blood vessels. This term refers to an abnormally increased susceptibility to bruising. The corresponding phenotypic abnormality is generally elicited on medical history as a report of frequent ecchymoses or bruising without adequate trauma.

LABEL: Purpura
hasExactSynonym: Red or purple spots on the skin
IAO_0000115: Purpura (from Latin: purpura, meaning purple) is the appearance of red or purple discolorations on the skin that do not blanch on applying pressure. They are caused by bleeding underneath the skin. This term refers to an abnormally increased susceptibility to developing purpura. Purpura are larger than petechiae.

LABEL: Pallor
IAO_0000115: Abnormally pale skin.

LABEL: Palmoplantar keratoderma
hasExactSynonym: Keratoderma|Palmar and plantar keratoderma|Thickening of palms and soles
IAO_0000115: Abnormal thickening of the skin of the palms of the hands and the soles of the feet.

LABEL: Skin rash
hasExactSynonym: Skin rash
IAO_0000115: A red eruption of the skin.

LABEL: Pruritus
hasExactSynonym: Itching|Itchy skin|Skin itching
IAO_0000115: Pruritus is an itch or a sensation that makes a person want to scratch. This term refers to an abnormally increased disposition to experience pruritus.

LABEL: Cutaneous photosensitivity
hasExactSynonym: Photosensitive skin|Photosensitive skin rashes|Photosensitivity|Sensitivity to sunlight|Skin photosensitivity|Sun sensitivity
IAO_0000115: An increased sensitivity of the skin to light. Photosensitivity may result in a rash upon exposure to the sun (which is known as photodermatosis). Photosensitivity can be diagnosed by phototests in which light is shone on small areas of skin.

LABEL: Axillary freckling
IAO_0000115: The presence in the axillary region (armpit) of an increased number of freckles, small circular spots on the skin that are darker than the surrounding skin because of deposits of melanin.

LABEL: Hypertrichosis
IAO_0000115: Hypertrichosis is increased hair growth that is abnormal in quantity or location.

LABEL: Pyoderma
hasExactSynonym: Pus-filled lesion
IAO_0000115: Any manifestation of a skin disease associated with the production of pus.

LABEL: Abnormal skin pigmentation
hasExactSynonym: Abnormal pigmentation|Abnormal skin pigmentation|Abnormality of pigmentation|Abnormality of skin pigmentation|Pigmentary changes|Pigmentary skin changes|Pigmentation anomaly
IAO_0000115: An abnormality of the pigmentation of the skin.

LABEL: Lymphedema
hasExactSynonym: Lymphatic obstruction|Lymphoedema|Onset of lymphedema around puberty|Swelling caused by excess lymph fluid under skin
IAO_0000115: Localized fluid retention and tissue swelling caused by a compromised lymphatic system.

LABEL: Hirsutism
hasExactSynonym: Excessive hairiness
IAO_0000115: Abnormally increased hair growth referring to a male pattern of body hair (androgenic hair).

LABEL: Telangiectasia
hasExactSynonym: Telangiectases
IAO_0000115: Telangiectasias refer to small dilated blood vessels located near the surface of the skin or mucous membranes, measuring between 0.5 and 1 millimeter in diameter. Telangiectasia are located especially on the tongue, lips, palate, fingers, face, conjunctiva, trunk, nail beds, and fingertips.

LABEL: Hypopigmentation of the skin
hasExactSynonym: Hypopigmentation|Hypopigmented skin|Patchy lightened skin
IAO_0000115: A reduction of skin color related to a decrease in melanin production and deposition.

LABEL: Prominent superficial veins
hasExactSynonym: Marked subcutaneous veins|Prominent veins
IAO_0000115: A condition in which superficial veins (i.e., veins just under the skin) are more conspicuous or noticeable than normal.

LABEL: Albinism
hasExactSynonym: Achromasia|Albinism
IAO_0000115: An abnormal reduction in the amount of pigmentation (reduced or absent) of skin, hair and eye (iris and retina).

LABEL: Penetrating foot ulcers
hasExactSynonym: Penetrating foot ulcers

LABEL: Fragile skin
hasExactSynonym: Fragile skin|Skin fragility
IAO_0000115: Skin that splits easily with minimal injury.

LABEL: Subcutaneous lipoma
IAO_0000115: The presence of subcutaneous lipoma.

LABEL: Hypermelanotic macule
hasExactSynonym: Hyperpigmented macules|Hyperpigmented spots
IAO_0000115: A hyperpigmented circumscribed area of change in normal skin color without elevation or depression of any size.

LABEL: Seborrheic dermatitis
hasExactSynonym: Seborrhea|Seborrheic eczema
IAO_0000115: Seborrheic dermatitis is a form of eczema which is closely related to dandruff. It causes dry or greasy peeling of the scalp, eyebrows, and face, and sometimes trunk.

LABEL: Hypopigmented skin patches
hasExactSynonym: Patchy loss of skin color|Patchy loss of skin colour

LABEL: Numerous nevi
hasExactSynonym: Multiple pigmented nevi|Numerous moles

LABEL: Poor wound healing
hasExactSynonym: Poor wound healing
IAO_0000115: A reduced ability to heal cutaneous wounds.

LABEL: Striae distensae
hasExactSynonym: Purplish striae|Stretch marks|Striae|Striae atrophicae|Striae cutis distensae
IAO_0000115: Thinned, erythematous, depressed bands of atrophic skin. Initially, striae appear as flattened and thinned, pinkish linear regions of the skin. Striae tend to enlarge in length and become reddish or purplish. Later, striae tend to appear as white, depressed bands that are parallel to the lines of skin tension. Striae distensae occur most often in areas that have been subject to distension such as the lower back, buttocks, thighs, breast, abdomen, and shoulders.

LABEL: Mottled pigmentation
hasExactSynonym: Mottled skin coloring|Mottled skin colouring
IAO_0000115: Patchy and irregular skin pigmentation.

LABEL: Angiokeratoma corporis diffusum
hasExactSynonym: Fabry syndrome
IAO_0000115: Angiokeratoma corporis diffusum (ACD) is typically characterized by innumerable small red to black papules which occur in clusters and are situated symmetrically in the bathing trunks area. The number of lesions and the extension of the body increase steadily with time so that generalization and mucosal involvement are common. The single lesion begins with a minute reddish papule which enlarges to up to 10 mm in diameter, becomes dark red to black with a discrete keratotic overgrowth. Histologically, the papules are characterized by superficial dilated capillaries in papillary dermis with epidermal proliferation.

LABEL: Thickened skin
hasExactSynonym: Pachydermia|Thick skin|Thickened skin
IAO_0000115: Laminar thickening of skin.

LABEL: Cigarette-paper scars
hasExactSynonym: Cigarette paper scarring|Cigarette-paper scars
IAO_0000115: Thin (atrophic) and wide scars.

LABEL: Atrophic scars
hasExactSynonym: Sunken or indented skin due to damage|Thin, atrophic scars
IAO_0000115: Scars that form a depression compared to the level of the surrounding skin because of damage to the collagen, fat or other tissues below the skin.

LABEL: Biliary tract abnormality
IAO_0000115: An abnormality of the biliary tree.

LABEL: Cholecystitis
hasExactSynonym: Gallbladder inflammation|Recurrent cholecystitis|Unusual cholecystitis
IAO_0000115: The presence of inflammatory changes in the gallbladder.

LABEL: Iridocyclitis
IAO_0000115: A type of anterior uveitis, in which there is Inflammation of the iris and the ciliary body.

LABEL: Keratoconjunctivitis sicca
hasExactSynonym: Dry eyes|Keratitis sicca|Xerophthalmia
IAO_0000115: Dryness of the eye related to deficiency of the tear film components (aqueous, mucin, or lipid), lid surface abnormalities, or epithelial abnormalities. Keratoconjunctivitis sicca often results in a scratchy or sandy sensation (foreign body sensation) in the eyes, and may also be associated with itching, inability to produce tears, photosensitivity, redness, pain, and difficulty in moving the eyelids.

LABEL: Heterochromia iridis
hasExactSynonym: Different colored eyes|Different coloured eyes|Heterochromia irides
IAO_0000115: Heterochromia iridis is a difference in the color of the iris in the two eyes.

LABEL: Abnormal macular morphology
hasExactSynonym: Abnormality of the macula|Macula abnormality|Macular abnormality
IAO_0000115: A structural abnormality of the macula, a region that, in a clinical context, is typically used to describe the central part of the retina within the vascular arcades.

LABEL: Retinal atrophy
IAO_0000115: A nonspecific term denoting wasting, especially as a result of degeneration, of the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) and neurosensory retinal cells.

LABEL: Periorbital hyperpigmentation
hasExactSynonym: Dark circles around the eyes|Dark circles under the eyes|Darkening around the eyes|Idiopathic cutaneous hyperchromia at the orbital region|Infraorbital pigmentation|Periorbital melanosis|Pigmentation around the eyes
IAO_0000115: Increased pigmentation of the skin in the region surrounding the orbit of the eye.

LABEL: Xanthelasma
hasExactSynonym: Fatty deposits in skin around the eyes|Fatty deposits on eyelids|Xanthelasma palpebrarum|Xanthoma
IAO_0000115: The presence of xanthomata in the skin of the eyelid.

LABEL: Visual field defect
hasExactSynonym: Partial loss of field of vision|Visual field defects

LABEL: Trichiasis
hasExactSynonym: Ingrown eyelashes|Introversion of eyelashes|Trichiasis of eyelid eyelashes
IAO_0000115: Inversion and rubbing of the eyelashes against the globe of the eye.

LABEL: Lens subluxation
hasExactSynonym: Partially dislocated lens
IAO_0000115: Partial dislocation of the lens of the eye.

LABEL: Constriction of peripheral visual field
hasExactSynonym: Concentric narrowing of visual field|Constricted visual field|Constricted visual fields|Limited peripheral vision|Reduced peripheral vision|Visual field constriction
IAO_0000115: An absolute or relative decrease in retinal sensitivity extending from edge (periphery) of the visual field in a concentric pattern. The visual field is the area that is perceived simultaneously by a fixating eye.

LABEL: Limbal dermoid
hasExactSynonym: Epibulbar dermoid|Epibulbar dermoids
IAO_0000115: A benign tumor typically found at the junction of the cornea and sclera (limbal epibullar dermoid).

LABEL: Severely reduced visual acuity
hasExactSynonym: Marked vision impairment|Severe reduction in visual acuity|Severe vision loss|Severe visual impairment|Severe visual loss|Severely impaired vision
IAO_0000115: Severe reduction of the ability to see. On the 6m visual acuity scale, severe reduction is defined as less than 6/60 but at least 3/60. On the 20ft visual acuity scale, severe reduction is defined as less than 20/200 but at least 20/400. On the decimal visual acuity scale, severe reduction is defined as less than 0.1 but at least 0.05.

LABEL: Retinal exudate
hasExactSynonym: Retinal exudates
IAO_0000115: Yellow-white intraretinal deposits in the retina typically associated with damaged inner blood-retina barrier and exudation of serous fluid and lipids from the retinal microvasculature.

LABEL: Brachydactyly
hasExactSynonym: Brachydactyly syndrome|Short fingers or toes
IAO_0000115: Digits that appear disproportionately short compared to the hand/foot. The word brachydactyly is used here to describe a series distinct patterns of shortened digits (brachydactyly types A-E). This is the sense used here.

LABEL: Syndactyly
hasExactSynonym: Webbed fingers or toes
IAO_0000115: Webbing or fusion of the fingers or toes, involving soft parts only or including bone structure. Bony fusions are referred to as "bony" syndactyly if the fusion occurs in a radio-ulnar axis. Fusions of bones of the fingers or toes in a proximo-distal axis are referred to as "symphalangism".

LABEL: Hand polydactyly
hasExactSynonym: Extra finger|Finger polydactyly|Polydactyly of the hand|Supernumerary finger
IAO_0000115: A kind of polydactyly characterized by the presence of a supernumerary finger or fingers.

LABEL: Postaxial hand polydactyly
hasExactSynonym: Extra little finger|Extra pinkie finger|Extra pinky finger|Polydactyly affecting the 5th finger|Postaxial polydactyly of fingers|Postaxial polydactyly of hand|Postaxial polydactyly of hands
IAO_0000115: Supernumerary digits located at the ulnar side of the hand (that is, on the side with the fifth finger).

LABEL: Abnormal finger morphology
hasExactSynonym: Abnormalities of the fingers|Abnormality of finger
IAO_0000115: An anomaly of a finger.

LABEL: Abnormal thumb morphology
hasExactSynonym: Abnormality of the thumb|Abnormality of the thumbs|Thumb deformity
IAO_0000115: An abnormal structure of the first digit of the hand.

LABEL: Large hands
hasExactSynonym: Disproportionately large hands|Large hands|large hand

LABEL: Tapered finger
hasExactSynonym: Distally tapering fingers|Tapered finger|Tapered fingertips|Tapering fingers
IAO_0000115: The gradual reduction in girth of the finger from proximal to distal.

LABEL: Hyperextensibility of the finger joints
hasExactSynonym: Finger joint hyperextensibility|Hyperextensible digits|Hyperextensible finger
IAO_0000115: The ability of the finger joints to move beyond their normal range of motion.

LABEL: Single umbilical artery
hasExactSynonym: 2 vessel cord|2 vessel umbilical cord|Only one artery in umbilical cord instead of two|SUA|Two vessel cord|Two vessel umbilical cord|Two-vessel cord
IAO_0000115: Single umbilical artery (SUA) is the absence of one of the two umbilical arteries surrounding the fetal bladder and in the fetal umbilical cord.

LABEL: Abnormality of prenatal development or birth
hasExactSynonym: Abnormality of prenatal development or birth
IAO_0000115: An abnormality of the fetus or the birth of the fetus, excluding structural abnormalities.

LABEL: Triphalangeal thumb
hasExactSynonym: Accessory phalanx of the thumb|Digitalized thumb|Finger-like thumb|Triphalangeal thumbs|Triphalangy of thumb
IAO_0000115: A thumb with three phalanges in a single, proximo-distal axis. Thus, this term applies if the thumb has an accessory phalanx, leading to a digit like appearance of the thumb.

LABEL: Prominent fingertip pads
hasExactSynonym: Persistence of fingerpads|Persistent fetal fingertip pads|Persistent foetal fingertip pads|Prominent finger pads|Prominent fingertip pads
IAO_0000115: A soft tissue prominence of the ventral aspects of the fingertips. The term "persistent fetal fingertip pads" is often used as a synonym, but should better not be used because it implies knowledge of history of the patient which often does not exist.

LABEL: Camptodactyly of 2nd-5th fingers
IAO_0000115: The distal interphalangeal joint and/or the proximal interphalangeal joint of the second to fifth fingers cannot be extended to 180 degrees by either active or passive extension.

LABEL: Interphalangeal joint contracture of finger
hasExactSynonym: Interphalangeal joint flexion contractures
IAO_0000115: Chronic loss of joint motion in an interphalangeal joint of a finger due to structural changes in non-bony tissue.

LABEL: 2-3 finger cutaneous syndactyly
hasExactSynonym: Syndactyly 2nd-3rd fingers|Syndactyly, 2-3 finger|Webbed 2nd-3rd fingers
IAO_0000115: A soft tissue continuity in the anteroposterior axis between the second to the third fingers that extends distally to at least the level of the proximal interphalangeal joints.

LABEL: Small thenar eminence
hasExactSynonym: Decreased thenar eminence|Hypoplastic thenar eminences|Thenar hypoplasia|Thenar muscle hypoplasia
IAO_0000115: Underdevelopment of the thenar eminence with reduced palmar soft tissue mass surrounding the base of the thumb.

LABEL: Intellectual disability
hasExactSynonym: Intellectual disability|Mental deficiency|Mental retardation|Mental retardation, nonspecific|Mental-retardation|Nonprogressive intellectual disability|Nonprogressive mental retardation
IAO_0000115: The term intellectual disability or intellectual developmental disorder is used to describe significantly sub-average intellectual and adaptive functioning based on clinical assessment and as measured by individually administered, appropriately normed, standardized and validated tests of intellectual functioning and adaptive behavior, with onset during the developmental period from infancy through adolescence.

LABEL: Seizure
hasExactSynonym: Epileptic seizure|Seizures
IAO_0000115: A seizure is an intermittent abnormality of nervous system physiology characterized by a transient occurrence of signs and/or symptoms due to abnormal excessive or synchronous neuronal activity in the brain.

LABEL: Ataxia
hasExactSynonym: Cerebellar ataxia
IAO_0000115: Ataxia refers to impaired coordination of voluntary muscle movement. Cerebellar ataxia refers to ataxia due to dysfunction of the cerebellum. This causes a variety of elementary neurological deficits including asynergy (lack of coordination between muscles, limbs and joints), dysmetria (lack of ability to judge distances that can lead to under- or overshoot in grasping movements), and dysdiadochokinesia (inability to perform rapid movements requiring antagonizing muscle groups to be switched on and off repeatedly).

LABEL: Hypotonia
hasExactSynonym: Low muscle tone|Low or weak muscle tone|Muscle hypotonia|Muscular hypotonia
IAO_0000115: Hypotonia is an abnormally low muscle tone (the amount of tension or resistance to movement in a muscle). Even when relaxed, muscles have a continuous and passive partial contraction which provides some resistance to passive stretching. Hypotonia thus manifests as diminished resistance to passive stretching. Hypotonia is not the same as muscle weakness, although the two conditions can co-exist.

LABEL: Lethargy
hasExactSynonym: Dullness|Inaction|Inactivity|Languor|Lethargy|Slowness|Torpor
IAO_0000115: A state of fatigue, either physical or mental slowness and sluggishness, with difficulties in initiating or performing simple tasks. Distinguished from apathy which implies indifference and a lack of desire or interest in the task. A person with lethargy may have the desire, but not the energy to engage in personal or socially relevant tasks.

LABEL: Mild intellectual disability
hasExactSynonym: Intellectual disability, mild|Mental retardation, borderline-mild|Mild and nonprogressive mental retardation|Mild mental retardation
IAO_0000115: Mild intellectual disability (ID) is defined as a type of ID characterized by mildly sub-average adaptive functioning and intellectual functioning, with an intelligence quotient (IQ) the range of 50-69.

LABEL: Spasticity
hasExactSynonym: Involuntary muscle stiffness, contraction, or spasm|Muscle spasticity|Muscular spasticity
IAO_0000115: A motor disorder characterized by a velocity-dependent increase in tonic stretch reflexes with increased muscle tone, exaggerated (hyperexcitable) tendon reflexes.

LABEL: Spastic paraplegia
hasExactSynonym: Spastic paraplegia, lower limb
IAO_0000115: Complete loss of the ability to move the lower limbs accompanied by spasticity of the lower limbs.

LABEL: Coma
hasExactSynonym: Coma|Persistent vegetative state|Stupor|Unconsciousness
IAO_0000115: The complete absence of wakefulness and consciousness, which is evident through a lack of response to any form of external stimuli.

LABEL: Dysarthria
hasExactSynonym: Difficulty articulating speech|Dysarthric speech
IAO_0000115: Dysarthric speech is a general description referring to a neurological speech disorder characterized by poor articulation. Depending on the involved neurological structures, dysarthria may be further classified as spastic, flaccid, ataxic, hyperkinetic and hypokinetic, or mixed.

LABEL: Global developmental delay
hasExactSynonym: Delayed cognitive development|Delayed development|Delayed developmental milestones|Delayed intellectual development|Delayed milestones|Delayed psychomotor development|Developmental delay|Developmental delay in early childhood|Developmental delay, global|Developmental retardation|GDD|Lack of psychomotor development|Motor and developmental delay|Motormental retardation|Psychomotor delay|Psychomotor development deficiency|Psychomotor development failure|Psychomotor developmental delay|Retarded development|Retarded mental development|Retarded psychomotor development
IAO_0000115: A delay in the achievement of motor or mental milestones in the domains of development of a child, including motor skills, speech and language, cognitive skills, and social and emotional skills. This term should only be used to describe children younger than five years of age.

LABEL: Hyporeflexia
hasExactSynonym: Decreased reflex response|Decreased reflexes
IAO_0000115: Reduction of neurologic reflexes such as the knee-jerk reaction.

LABEL: Choreoathetosis
hasExactSynonym: Choreoathetoid movements
IAO_0000115: Involuntary movements characterized by both athetosis (inability to sustain muscles in a fixed position) and chorea (widespread jerky arrhythmic movements).

LABEL: Mental deterioration
hasExactSynonym: Cognitive decline|Cognitive decline, progressive|Intellectual deterioration|Mental deterioration|Progressive cognitive decline
IAO_0000115: Loss of previously present mental abilities, generally in adults.

LABEL: Hemiparesis
hasExactSynonym: Weakness of one side of body
IAO_0000115: Loss of strength in the arm, leg, and sometimes face on one side of the body. Hemiplegia refers to a complete loss of strength, whereas hemiparesis refers to an incomplete loss of strength.

LABEL: Motor delay
hasExactSynonym: Delay in development of motor milestones|Delay in motor development|Delayed development of motor milestones|Delayed early motor milestones|Delayed motor development|Delayed motor milestones|Locomotor delay|Motor developmental delay|Motor developmental milestones not achieved|Motor retardation|Retarded motor development|Slow development of motor milestones
IAO_0000115: A type of Developmental delay characterized by a delay in acquiring motor skills.

LABEL: Cerebellar atrophy
hasExactSynonym: Atrophic cerebellum|Degeneration of cerebellum
IAO_0000115: Cerebellar atrophy is defined as a cerebellum with initially normal structures, in a posterior fossa with normal size, which displays enlarged fissures (interfolial spaces) in comparison to the foliae secondary to loss of tissue. Cerebellar atrophy implies irreversible loss of tissue and result from an ongoing progressive disease until a final stage is reached or a single injury, e.g. an intoxication or infectious event.

LABEL: Abnormal corpus callosum morphology
hasExactSynonym: Abnormal corpus callosum|Abnormality of the corpus callosum|Corpus callosum abnormality
IAO_0000115: Abnormality of the corpus callosum.

LABEL: Agenesis of corpus callosum
hasExactSynonym: Absence of corpus callosum|Absent corpus callosum|Agenesis of the corpus callosum|Callosal agenesis|Corpus callosum agenesis|Dysplastic or absent corpus callosum
IAO_0000115: Absence of the corpus callosum as a result of the failure of the corpus callosum to develop, which can be the result of a failure in any one of the multiple steps of callosal development including cellular proliferation and migration, axonal growth or glial patterning at the midline.

LABEL: Hypertonia
hasExactSynonym: Hypertonicity|Increased muscle tone
IAO_0000115: A condition in which there is increased muscle tone so that arms or legs, for example, are stiff and difficult to move.

LABEL: Syncope
hasExactSynonym: Fainting spell
IAO_0000115: A transient loss of consciousness (i.e., characterized by a rapid onset, a short duration, and a spontaneous and complete recovery) due to cerebral hypoperfusion.

LABEL: Tetany
hasExactSynonym: Intermittent involuntary muscle spasm
IAO_0000115: A condition characterized by intermittent involuntary contraction of muscles (spasms) related to hypocalcemia or occasionally magnesium deficiency.

LABEL: Bulbar palsy
hasExactSynonym: Bulbar muscle weakness|Bulbar palsies|Bulbar weakness
IAO_0000115: Bulbar weakness (or bulbar palsy) refers to bilateral impairment of function of the lower cranial nerves IX, X, XI and XII, which occurs due to lower motor neuron lesion either at nuclear or fascicular level in the medulla or from bilateral lesions of the lower cranial nerves outside the brain-stem. Bulbar weakness is often associated with difficulty in chewing, weakness of the facial muscles, dysarthria, palatal weakness and regurgitation of fluids, dysphagia, and dysphonia.

LABEL: Areflexia
hasExactSynonym: Absent deep tendon reflexes|Absent tendon reflexes|Deep tendon reflexes absent|Loss of deep tendon reflexes|Lost deep tendon reflexes
IAO_0000115: Absence of neurologic reflexes such as the knee-jerk reaction.

LABEL: Spastic tetraparesis
hasExactSynonym: Spastic quadriparesis
IAO_0000115: Spastic weakness affecting all four limbs.

LABEL: Meningitis
hasExactSynonym: Unusual infectious meningitis|Unusual meningitis
IAO_0000115: Inflammation of the meninges.

LABEL: Gait disturbance
hasExactSynonym: Abnormal gait|Abnormal walk|Difficulty in walking|Gait abnormalities|Gait difficulties|Gait disturbances|Impaired gait|Walking disability
IAO_0000115: The term gait disturbance can refer to any disruption of the ability to walk.

LABEL: Confusion
hasExactSynonym: Confusion|Disorientation|Easily confused|Mental disorientation
IAO_0000115: Lack of clarity and coherence of thought, perception, understanding, or action.

LABEL: Generalized hypotonia
hasExactSynonym: Generalised decreased muscle tone|Generalised hypotonia|Generalised muscular hypotonia|Generalized decreased muscle tone|Generalized muscular hypotonia|Hypotonia, generalised|Hypotonia, generalized
IAO_0000115: Generalized muscular hypotonia (abnormally low muscle tone).

LABEL: Stroke
hasExactSynonym: Cerebral vascular events|Cerebrovascular accident|Stroke
IAO_0000115: Sudden impairment of blood flow to a part of the brain due to occlusion or rupture of an artery to the brain.

LABEL: Encephalopathy
IAO_0000115: Encephalopathy is a term that means brain disease, damage, or malfunction. In general, encephalopathy is manifested by an altered mental state.

LABEL: Parkinsonism
IAO_0000115: Characteristic neurologic anomaly resulting from degeneration of dopamine-generating cells in the substantia nigra, a region of the midbrain, characterized clinically by shaking, rigidity, slowness of movement and difficulty with walking and gait.

LABEL: Pachygyria
hasExactSynonym: Cerebral pachygyria|Fewer and broader ridges in brain|Macrogyria
