IAO_0000115: Pachygyria is a malformation of cortical development with abnormally wide gyri with sulci 1,5-3 cm apart and abnormally thick cortex measuring more than 5 mm (radiological definition). See also neuropathological definitions for 2-, 3-, and 4-layered lissencephaly.

LABEL: Torsion dystonia
hasExactSynonym: Dystonia musculorum deformans
IAO_0000115: Sustained involuntary muscle contractions that produce twisting and repetitive movements of the body.

LABEL: Dandy-Walker malformation
hasExactSynonym: Dandy-Walker cyst|Dandy-walker anomaly
IAO_0000115: A congenital brain malformation typically characterized by incomplete formation of the cerebellar vermis, dilation of the fourth ventricle, and enlargement of the posterior fossa. In layman's terms, Dandy Walker malformation is a cyst in the cerebellum (typically symmetrical) that is involved with the fourth ventricle. This may interfere with the ability to drain cerebrospinal fluid from the brain, resulting in hydrocephalus. Dandy Walker cysts are formed during early embryonic development, while the brain forms. The cyst in the cerebellum typically has several blood vessels running through it connecting to the brain, thereby prohibiting surgical removal.

LABEL: Tongue fasciculations
hasExactSynonym: Lingual fasciculations|Lingual fibrillations|Lingual twitching|Tongue fasciculation|Tongue fasciculations/fibrillations|Tongue twitching|Twitching of the tongue
IAO_0000115: Fasciculations or fibrillation affecting the tongue muscle.

LABEL: Dysmetria
hasExactSynonym: Lack of coordination of movement
IAO_0000115: A type of ataxia characterized by the inability to carry out movements with the correct range and motion across the plane of more than one joint related to incorrect estimation of the distances required for targeted movements.

LABEL: Diminished deep tendon reflex
hasExactSynonym: Absent or decreased deep tendon reflexes|Decreased deep tendon reflexes|Decreased tendon reflexes|Decreased to absent deep tendon reflexes|Decreased/absent deep tendon reflexes|Depressed tendon reflexes|Diminished deep tendon reflexes|Diminished or absent deep tendon reflexes|Diminished or absent tendon reflexes|Hypoactive to absent deep tendon reflexes|Impaired tendon reflexes|Reduced tendon reflexes|Reduced/absent deep tendon reflexes|Weak or absent deep tendon reflexes
IAO_0000115: A reduction (hyporeflexia) or complete absence (areflexia) of the involuntary muscle contraction normally elicited by a reflex stimulus, such as tapping a deep tendon.

LABEL: Abnormal cerebellum morphology
hasExactSynonym: Abnormality of the cerebellum|Cerebellar abnormalities|Cerebellar abnormality|Cerebellar anomaly|Cerebellar signs
IAO_0000115: Any structural abnormality of the cerebellum.

LABEL: Neonatal hypotonia
hasExactSynonym: Hypotonia, in neonatal onset|Hypotonia, neonatal|Low muscle tone, in neonatal onset
IAO_0000115: Muscular hypotonia (abnormally low muscle tone) manifesting in the neonatal period.

LABEL: Cerebellar vermis hypoplasia
hasExactSynonym: Cerebellar vermal hypoplasia|Hypoplasia of the cerebellar vermis|Hypoplastic cerebellar vermis
IAO_0000115: Underdevelopment of the vermis of cerebellum.

LABEL: Cerebellar hypoplasia
hasExactSynonym: Congenital cerebellar hypoplasia|Hypoplasia of cerebellum|Hypoplastic cerebellum|Small cerebellum|Underdeveloped cerebellum
IAO_0000115: Cerebellar hypoplasia is a descriptive term implying a cerebellum with a reduced volume, but a normal shape and is stable over time.

LABEL: Muscle weakness
hasExactSynonym: Muscle weakness|Muscular weakness
IAO_0000115: Reduced strength of muscles.

LABEL: Hypoglycemic coma
hasExactSynonym: Coma caused by low blood sugar|Coma, hypoglycemic|Hypoglycaemic coma|Loss of consciousness due to hypoglycemia
IAO_0000115: Coma induced by low blood sugar.

LABEL: Specific learning disability
IAO_0000115: Impairment of certain skills such as reading or writing, coordination, self-control, or attention that interfere with the ability to learn. The impairment is not related to a global deficiency of intelligence.

LABEL: Absent septum pellucidum
hasExactSynonym: Absence of septum pellucidum|Absence of the septum pellucidum|Agenesis of the septum pellucidum|Missing septum pellucidum
IAO_0000115: Absence of the septum pellucidum (meaning translucent wall in Latin - SP), also known as the ventricle of Sylvius. The septum pellucidum is a thin, triangular double membrane separating the frontal horns of the right and left lateral ventricles of the brain. It extends between the anterior portion of the corpus callosum, and the body of the fornix and its width varies from 1.5 to 3.0 mm.

LABEL: Dystonia
hasExactSynonym: Dystonic movements
IAO_0000115: An abnormally increased muscular tone that causes fixed abnormal postures. There is a slow, intermittent twisting motion that leads to exaggerated turning and posture of the extremities and trunk.

LABEL: Myoclonus
hasExactSynonym: Myoclonic jerks
IAO_0000115: Very brief, involuntary random muscular contractions occurring at rest, in response to sensory stimuli, or accompanying voluntary movements.

LABEL: Tremor
hasExactSynonym: Tremor|Tremors
IAO_0000115: An unintentional, oscillating to-and-fro muscle movement about a joint axis.

LABEL: Partial agenesis of the corpus callosum
hasExactSynonym: Corpus callosum agenesis, partial|Partial agenesis of corpus callosum|Partial corpus callosum agenesis|Partial or complete agenesis of corpus callosum|Partial to complete agenesis of corpus callosum|Partial-total agenesis of corpus callosum
IAO_0000115: A partial failure of the development of the corpus callosum.

LABEL: Lissencephaly
hasExactSynonym: Fewer or absent grooves in brain
IAO_0000115: A spectrum of malformations of cortical development caused by insufficient neuronal migration that subsumes the terms agyria, pachygyria and subcortical band heterotopia. See also neuropathological definitions for 2-, 3-, and 4-layered lissencephaly.

LABEL: Enhancement of the C-reflex
IAO_0000115: Increase in amplitude of a long-loop response upon somatosensory evoked potential testing, representing an electrically evoked myoclonic response.

LABEL: Olfactory lobe agenesis
hasExactSynonym: Olfactory lobe absence

LABEL: Absent speech
hasExactSynonym: Absent speech development|Lack of language development|Lack of speech|No speech development|No speech or language development|Nonverbal
IAO_0000115: Complete lack of development of speech and language abilities.

LABEL: Hyperreflexia
hasExactSynonym: Increased deep tendon reflexes|Increased reflexes
IAO_0000115: Hyperreflexia is the presence of hyperactive stretch reflexes of the muscles.

LABEL: Brisk reflexes
hasExactSynonym: Brisk deep tendon reflexes
IAO_0000115: Tendon reflexes that are noticeably more active than usual (conventionally denoted 3+ on clinical examination). Brisk reflexes may or may not indicate a neurological lesion. They are distinguished from hyperreflexia by the fact that hyerreflexia is characterized by hyperactive repeating (clonic) reflexes, which are considered to be always abnormal.

LABEL: Slurred speech
hasExactSynonym: Slurred speech
IAO_0000115: Abnormal coordination of muscles involved in speech.

LABEL: Plagiocephaly
hasExactSynonym: Flat head syndrome|Flattening of cranial vault|Flattening of cranium|Flattening of skull|Rhomboid shaped cranium|Rhomboid shaped skull
IAO_0000115: Asymmetric head shape, which is usually a combination of unilateral occipital flattening with ipsilateral frontal prominence, leading to rhomboid cranial shape.

LABEL: Arthritis
hasExactSynonym: Arthritis|Joint inflammation
IAO_0000115: Inflammation of a joint.

LABEL: Rheumatoid arthritis
hasExactSynonym: RA|Rheumatoid arthritis
IAO_0000115: Inflammatory changes in the synovial membranes and articular structures with widespread fibrinoid degeneration of the collagen fibers in mesenchymal tissues, as well as atrophy and rarefaction of bony structures.

LABEL: Flexion contracture
hasExactSynonym: Flexed joint that cannot be straightened|Flexion contractures|Flexion contractures of joints
IAO_0000115: A flexion contracture is a bent (flexed) joint that cannot be straightened actively or passively. It is thus a chronic loss of joint motion due to structural changes in muscle, tendons, ligaments, or skin that prevents normal movement of joints.

LABEL: Joint dislocation
hasExactSynonym: Joint dislocation|Joint dislocations
IAO_0000115: Displacement or malalignment of joints.

LABEL: Congenital hip dislocation
hasExactSynonym: Congenital dislocation of the hip|Congenital dislocation of the hips|Congenital hip anomaly|Congenital hip dislocations|Dislocated hip since birth

LABEL: Joint hypermobility
hasExactSynonym: Double-Jointed|Extensible joints|Flexible joints|Hyperextensible joints|Increased joint mobility|Increased mobility of joints|Joint hyperextensibility|Joint hyperflexibility|Joint hyperlaxity|Joint laxity|Joints move beyond expected range of motion|Lax joints|Loose-jointedness
IAO_0000115: The capability that a joint (or a group of joints) has to move, passively and/or actively, beyond normal limits along physiological axes.

LABEL: Abnormal hip joint morphology
hasExactSynonym: Abnormality of the hip joint
IAO_0000115: An abnormality of the hip joint.

LABEL: Hip dysplasia
hasExactSynonym: Congenital hip dysplasia|DDH|Developmental dysplasia of the hip
IAO_0000115: The presence of developmental dysplasia of the hip.

LABEL: Joint swelling
hasExactSynonym: Joint swelling

LABEL: Joint stiffness
hasExactSynonym: Joint stiffness|Stiff joint|Stiff joints
IAO_0000115: Joint stiffness is a perceived sensation of tightness in a joint or joints when attempting to move them after a period of inactivity. Joint stiffness typically subsides over time.

LABEL: Abnormality of the liver
hasExactSynonym: Abnormal liver|Abnormality of the liver|Liver abnormality
IAO_0000115: An abnormality of the liver.

LABEL: Cirrhosis
hasExactSynonym: Hepatic cirrhosis|Scar tissue replaces healthy tissue in the liver
IAO_0000115: A chronic disorder of the liver in which liver tissue becomes scarred and is partially replaced by regenerative nodules and fibrotic tissue resulting in loss of liver function.

LABEL: Hepatic fibrosis
hasExactSynonym: Liver fibrosis
IAO_0000115: The presence of excessive fibrous connective tissue in the liver. Fibrosis is a reparative or reactive process.

LABEL: Cholestasis
hasExactSynonym: Slowed or blocked flow of bile from liver
IAO_0000115: Impairment of bile flow due to obstruction in bile ducts.

LABEL: Hepatic steatosis
hasExactSynonym: Fatty infiltration of liver|Fatty liver|Liver steatosis|Steatosis
IAO_0000115: Steatosis is a term used to denote lipid accumulation within hepatocytes.

LABEL: Hepatic failure
hasExactSynonym: Hepatic insufficiency|Liver failure

LABEL: Periportal fibrosis
IAO_0000115: The presence of fibrosis affecting the interlobular stroma of liver.

LABEL: Hepatic cysts
hasExactSynonym: Liver cysts

LABEL: Decreased liver function
hasExactSynonym: Decreased liver function|Liver dysfunction
IAO_0000115: Reduced ability of the liver to perform its functions.

LABEL: X-linked inheritance
hasExactSynonym: X-linked|monoallelic_X
IAO_0000115: A mode of inheritance that is observed for traits related to a gene encoded on the X chromosome.

LABEL: X-linked recessive inheritance
hasExactSynonym: X-linked recessive|monoallelic_X_hemizygous
IAO_0000115: A mode of inheritance that is observed for recessive traits related to a gene encoded on the X chromosome. In the context of medical genetics, X-linked recessive disorders manifest in males (who have one copy of the X chromosome and are thus hemizygotes), but generally not in female heterozygotes who have one mutant and one normal allele.

LABEL: X-linked dominant inheritance
hasExactSynonym: X-linked dominant|monoallelic_X_heterozygous
IAO_0000115: A mode of inheritance that is observed for dominant traits related to a gene encoded on the X chromosome. In the context of medical genetics, X-linked dominant disorders tend to manifest very severely in affected males. The severity of manifestation in females may depend on the degree of skewed X inactivation.

LABEL: obsolete Heterogeneous
hasExactSynonym: Genetic heterogeneity

LABEL: Mitochondrial inheritance
hasExactSynonym: Mitochondrial|mitochondrial
IAO_0000115: A mode of inheritance that is observed for traits related to a gene encoded on the mitochondrial genome. Because the mitochondrial genome is essentially always maternally inherited, a mitochondrial condition can only be transmitted by females, although the condition can affect both sexes. The proportion of mutant mitochondria can vary (heteroplasmy).

LABEL: Hepatosplenomegaly
hasExactSynonym: Enlarged liver and spleen
IAO_0000115: Simultaneous enlargement of the liver and spleen.

LABEL: Abnormal abdomen morphology
hasExactSynonym: Abnormality of abdomen morphology|Abnormality of abdomen structure|Abnormality of the abdomen
IAO_0000115: A structural abnormality of the abdomen ('belly'), that is, the part of the body between the pelvis and the thorax.

LABEL: Delayed closure of the anterior fontanelle
hasExactSynonym: Delayed closure anterior fontanel|Delayed closure of anterior fontanelle|Delayed closure of the bregma sutures|Late closure of anterior fontanelle|Late closure of large anterior fontanel|Late closure of the bregma sutures|Later than typical closing of soft spot of skull|Persistent anterior fontanelle
IAO_0000115: A delay in closure (ossification) of the anterior fontanelle, which generally undergoes closure around the 18th month of life.

LABEL: Freckling
hasExactSynonym: Freckling
IAO_0000115: The presence of an increased number of freckles, small circular spots on the skin that are darker than the surrounding skin because of deposits of melanin.

LABEL: Subcutaneous nodule
hasExactSynonym: Firm lump under the skin|Growth of abnormal tissue under the skin
IAO_0000115: Slightly elevated lesions on or in the skin with a diameter of over 5 mm.

LABEL: Bilateral ptosis
hasExactSynonym: Drooping of both upper eyelids

LABEL: Carpal osteolysis
hasExactSynonym: Carpal bone osteolysis
IAO_0000115: Osteolysis affecting carpal bones.

LABEL: Growth abnormality
hasExactSynonym: Abnormal growth|Growth abnormality|Growth issue

LABEL: Failure to thrive
hasExactSynonym: FTT|Faltering weight|Postnatal failure to thrive|Weight faltering
IAO_0000115: Failure to thrive (FTT) refers to a child whose physical growth is substantially below the norm.

LABEL: Growth delay
hasExactSynonym: Delayed growth|Growth deficiency|Growth delay|Growth failure|Growth retardation|Poor growth|Retarded growth
IAO_0000115: A deficiency or slowing down of growth pre- and postnatally.

LABEL: Obesity
hasExactSynonym: Having too much body fat|Obesity
IAO_0000115: Accumulation of substantial excess body fat.

LABEL: Small for gestational age
hasExactSynonym: Birth weight less than 10th percentile|Low birth weight|Small for gestational age
IAO_0000115: Smaller than normal size according to sex and gestational age related norms, defined as a weight below the 10th percentile for the gestational age.

LABEL: Disproportionate tall stature
hasExactSynonym: Dolichostenomelia|Marfanoid body habitus|Marfanoid habitus|Reduced upper-lower segment ratio
IAO_0000115: A tall and slim body build with increased arm span to height ratio (>1.05) and a reduced upper-to-lower segment ratio (<0.85), i.e., unusually long arms and legs. The extremities as well as the hands and feet are unusually slim.

LABEL: Large for gestational age
hasExactSynonym: Birth weight > 90th percentile|Birthweight > 90th percentile|Fetal macrosomia|Foetal macrosomia|Macrosomia|Macrosomia, neonatal
IAO_0000115: The term large for gestational age applies to babies whose birth weight lies above the 90th percentile for that gestational age.

LABEL: Death in infancy
hasExactSynonym: Death in infancy|Infantile death|Lethal in infancy
IAO_0000115: Death within the first 24 months of life.

LABEL: Severe failure to thrive
hasExactSynonym: Marked failure to thrive|Severe faltering weight|Severe postnatal failure to thrive|Severe weight faltering

LABEL: Failure to thrive in infancy
hasExactSynonym: Failure to thrive in first year of life|Faltering weight in infancy|Weight faltering in infancy

LABEL: Umbilical hernia
hasExactSynonym: Umbilical hernias
IAO_0000115: Protrusion of abdominal contents through a defect in the abdominal wall musculature around the umbilicus. Skin and subcutaneous tissue overlie the defect.

LABEL: Ascites
hasExactSynonym: Accumulation of fluid in the abdomen|Peritoneal effusion
IAO_0000115: Accumulation of fluid in the peritoneal cavity (between the layers of the peritoneum that lines the abdomen).

LABEL: Anteriorly placed anus
hasExactSynonym: Anteriorly displaced anus|Anus anteposition
IAO_0000115: Anterior malposition of the anus.

LABEL: Overgrowth
hasExactSynonym: General overgrowth
IAO_0000115: Excessive postnatal growth which may comprise increased weight, increased length, and/or increased head circumference.

LABEL: Abnormal ileum morphology
hasExactSynonym: Abnormality of the ileum

LABEL: Barrel-shaped chest
hasExactSynonym: Barrel chest|Barrel-shaped chest
IAO_0000115: A rounded, bulging chest that resembles the shape of a barrel. That is, there is an increased anteroposterior diameter and usually some degree of kyphosis.

LABEL: Asymmetry of the thorax
hasExactSynonym: Asymmetric chest
IAO_0000115: Lack of symmetry between the left and right halves of the thorax.

LABEL: Decreased fetal movement
hasExactSynonym: Decreased fetal activity|Decreased fetal movements|Decreased foetal activity|Decreased foetal movement|Decreased foetal movements|Decreased movement in utero|Dminished fetal movement|Dminished foetal movement|Fetal hypokinesia|Foetal hypokinesia|Less than 10 fetal movements in 12 hours|Less than 10 foetal movements in 12 hours|Reduced fetal movement|Reduced fetal movements|Reduced foetal movement|Reduced foetal movements
IAO_0000115: An abnormal reduction in quantity or strength of fetal movements.

LABEL: Abnormality of the amniotic fluid
hasExactSynonym: Abnormal amniotic fluid
IAO_0000115: Abnormality of the amniotic fluid, which is the fluid contained in the amniotic sac surrounding the developing fetus.

LABEL: Polyhydramnios
hasExactSynonym: High levels of amniotic fluid|Hydramnios
IAO_0000115: The presence of excess amniotic fluid in the uterus during pregnancy.

LABEL: Oligohydramnios
hasExactSynonym: Low levels of amniotic fluid|Maternal oligohydramnios
IAO_0000115: Diminished amniotic fluid volume in pregnancy.

LABEL: Abnormality of the integument
IAO_0000115: An abnormality of the integument, which consists of the skin and the superficial fascia.

LABEL: Recurrent skin infections
hasExactSynonym: Recurrent cutaneous infections|Recurrent skin infections|Skin infections, recurrent
IAO_0000115: Infections of the skin that happen multiple times.

LABEL: Rotary nystagmus
hasExactSynonym: Rotatory Nystagmus
IAO_0000115: A form of nystagmus in which the eyeball makes rotary motions around the axis.

LABEL: Bell-shaped thorax
hasExactSynonym: Bell-shaped chest|Constricted, bell-shaped thorax|Narrow, bell-shaped thorax
IAO_0000115: The rib cage has the shape of a wide mouthed bell. That is, the superior portion of the rib cage is constricted, followed by a convex region, and the inferior portion of the rib cage expands again to have a large diameter.

LABEL: Selective tooth agenesis
hasExactSynonym: Agenesis of a tooth|Failure of development of a tooth
IAO_0000115: Agenesis of some but not all teeth.

LABEL: Alopecia
hasExactSynonym: Hair loss
IAO_0000115: A noncongenital process of hair loss, which may progress to partial or complete baldness.

LABEL: Abnormal nail morphology
hasExactSynonym: Abnormality of the nail
IAO_0000115: Abnormal structure or appearance of the nail.

LABEL: Abnormality of the larynx
hasExactSynonym: Laryngeal abnormalities|Laryngeal anomalies
IAO_0000115: An abnormality of the larynx.

LABEL: Laryngomalacia
hasExactSynonym: Softening of voice box tissue
IAO_0000115: Laryngomalacia is a congenital abnormality of the laryngeal cartilage in which the cartilage is floppy and prolapses over the larynx during inspiration.

LABEL: Vocal cord paralysis
hasExactSynonym: Inability to move vocal cords|Laryngeal paralysis
IAO_0000115: A loss of the ability to move the vocal folds.

LABEL: Hoarse voice
hasExactSynonym: Hoarse voice|Hoarseness|Husky voice
IAO_0000115: Hoarseness refers to a change in the pitch or quality of the voice, with the voice sounding weak, very breathy, scratchy, or husky.

LABEL: Hypernasal speech
hasExactSynonym: Hypernasal voice|Nasal speech|Nasal voice
IAO_0000115: A type of speech characterized by the presence of an abnormally increased nasal airflow during speech associated with structural abnormality of the nasal passages.

LABEL: Dysphonia
hasExactSynonym: Inability to produce voice sounds|Voice change
IAO_0000115: Difficulty in speaking due to a physical disorder of the mouth, tongue, throat, or vocal cords. Associated with a known physical or neurological cause.

LABEL: Abnormally high-pitched voice
hasExactSynonym: High pitched voice|High-pitched voice
IAO_0000115: A persistent (minutes to hours) abnormal increase in the pitch (frequency) of the voice for the context or social situation or significantly different from baseline of the individual.

LABEL: Breech presentation
hasExactSynonym: Breech presentation at birth|Feet or buttocks of fetus positioned near opening of uterus|Feet or buttocks of foetus positioned near opening of uterus
IAO_0000115: A position of the fetus at delivery in which the fetus enters the birth canal with the buttocks or feet first.

LABEL: Abnormality of the cardiovascular system
hasExactSynonym: Abnormality of the cardiovascular system|Cardiovascular abnormality
IAO_0000115: Any abnormality of the cardiovascular system.

LABEL: Abnormal heart morphology
hasExactSynonym: Abnormality of cardiac morphology|Abnormality of the heart|Abnormally shaped heart|Cardiac abnormality|Cardiac anomalies|Cardiac anomaly|Congenital heart defect|Congenital heart defects|Heart defect
IAO_0000115: Any structural anomaly of the heart.

LABEL: Abnormal mitral valve morphology
hasExactSynonym: Abnormality of the mitral valve
IAO_0000115: Any structural anomaly of the mitral valve.

LABEL: Mitral valve prolapse
IAO_0000115: One or both of the leaflets (cusps) of the mitral valve bulges back into the left atrium upon contraction of the left ventricle.

LABEL: Congestive heart failure
hasExactSynonym: CHF|Cardiac failure|Cardiac failures|Cardiac insufficiency|Chronic heart failure|Heart failure
IAO_0000115: The presence of an abnormality of cardiac function that is responsible for the failure of the heart to pump blood at a rate that is commensurate with the needs of the tissues or a state in which abnormally elevated filling pressures are required for the heart to do so. Heart failure is frequently related to a defect in myocardial contraction.

LABEL: Tetralogy of Fallot
hasExactSynonym: Tetrology of fallot
IAO_0000115: A congenital cardiac malformation comprising pulmonary stenosis, overriding aorta, ventricular septum defect, and right ventricular hypertrophy. The diagnosis of TOF is made if at least three of the four above mentioned features are present.

LABEL: Pulmonic stenosis
hasExactSynonym: Narrowing of pulmonic valve|Pulmonary stenosis|Pulmonary valve stenosis|Pulmonic valve stenosis
IAO_0000115: A narrowing of the right ventricular outflow tract that can occur at the pulmonary valve (valvular stenosis), below the pulmonary valve (infundibular stenosis), or above the pulmonary valve (supravalvar stenosis).

LABEL: Patent ductus arteriosus
hasExactSynonym: Ductus arteriosus|PDA|Patent ductus Botalli|Persistent arterial duct|Persistent ductus arteriosus
IAO_0000115: In utero, the ductus arteriosus (DA) serves to divert ventricular output away from the lungs and toward the placenta by connecting the main pulmonary artery to the descending aorta. A patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) in the first 3 days of life is a physiologic shunt in healthy term and preterm newborn infants, and normally is substantially closed within about 24 hours after bith and completely closed after about three weeks. Failure of physiologcal closure is referred to a persistent or patent ductus arteriosus (PDA). Depending on the degree of left-to-right shunting, PDA can have clinical consequences.

LABEL: Dilated cardiomyopathy
hasExactSynonym: Cardiomyopathy, dilated|Congestive cardiomyopathy|DCM|Stretched and thinned heart muscle
IAO_0000115: Dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) is defined by the presence of left ventricular dilatation and left ventricular systolic dysfunction in the absence of abnormal loading conditions (hypertension, valve disease) or coronary artery disease sufficient to cause global systolic impairment. Right ventricular dilation and dysfunction may be present but are not necessary for the diagnosis.

LABEL: Abnormal aortic valve morphology
hasExactSynonym: Abnormality of the aortic valve
IAO_0000115: Any abnormality of the aortic valve.

LABEL: Bicuspid aortic valve
hasExactSynonym: Aortic valve has two leaflets rather than three
IAO_0000115: The presence of an aortic valve with two instead of the normal three cusps (flaps). LABEL: Tachycardia

LABEL: Aortic regurgitation

LABEL: Abnormal tricuspid valve morphology
hasExactSynonym: Abnormality of the tricuspid valve

LABEL: Splenomegaly

LABEL: Single ventricle

IAO_0000115: A contracture of the Achilles tendon.

hasExactSynonym: Abnormalities of the toes|Abnormality of toe

hasExactSynonym: Narrowing of kidney artery
IAO_0000115: The presence of stenosis of the renal artery.

IAO_0000115: An abnormality of the viscera of the abdomen.

LABEL: Vomiting

IAO_0000115: Forceful ejection of the contents of the stomach through the mouth by means of a series of involuntary spasmic contractions.

LABEL: Diarrhea
hasExactSynonym: Diarrhea|Diarrhoea|Watery stool
IAO_0000115: Abnormally increased frequency (usually defined as three or more) loose or watery bowel movements a day.

LABEL: Dysphagia
hasExactSynonym: Difficulty swallowing|Poor swallowing|Swallowing difficulties|Swallowing difficulty
IAO_0000115: Difficulty in swallowing.

LABEL: Nausea and vomiting
hasExactSynonym: Nausea and vomiting
IAO_0000115: Nausea is a commonly encountered symptom that has been defined as an unpleasant painless subjective feeling that one will imminently vomit. Vomiting has been defined as the forceful expulsion of the contents of the stomach, duodenum, or jejunum through the oral cavity. While nausea and vomiting are often thought to exist on a temporal continuum, this is not always the case. There are situations when severe nausea may be present without emesis and less frequently, when emesis may be present without preceding nausea.

LABEL: Nausea
hasExactSynonym: Nausea
IAO_0000115: A sensation of unease in the stomach together with an urge to vomit.

LABEL: Constipation
hasExactSynonym: Constipation|Costiveness|Dyschezia
IAO_0000115: Infrequent or difficult evacuation of feces.

LABEL: Gastroesophageal reflux
hasExactSynonym: Acid reflux|Acid reflux disease|GERD|GORD|Gastro-esophageal reflux|Gastro-oesophageal reflux|Gastroesophageal reflux disease|Heartburn
IAO_0000115: A condition in which the stomach contents leak backwards from the stomach into the esophagus through the lower esophageal sphincter.

LABEL: Malabsorption
hasExactSynonym: Intestinal malabsorption|Malabsorption
IAO_0000115: Impaired ability to absorb one or more nutrients from the intestine.

LABEL: Abdominal pain
hasExactSynonym: Abdominal pain|Pain in stomach|Stomach pain
IAO_0000115: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) and perceived to originate in the abdomen.

LABEL: Chronic diarrhea
hasExactSynonym: Chronic diarrhea|Chronic diarrhoea
IAO_0000115: The presence of chronic diarrhea, which is usually taken to mean diarrhea that has persisted for over 4 weeks.

LABEL: Abnormal esophagus morphology
hasExactSynonym: Abnormal oesophagus morphology|Abnormality of esophagus structure|Abnormality of oesophagus structure|Anomaly of the esophagus|Anomaly of the oesophagus
IAO_0000115: A structural abnormality of the esophagus.

LABEL: Esophageal atresia
hasExactSynonym: Birth defect in which part of esophagus did not develop|Birth defect in which part of oesophagus did not develop|EA
IAO_0000115: A developmental defect resulting in complete obliteration of the lumen of the esophagus such that the esophagus ends in a blind pouch rather than connecting to the stomach.

LABEL: Poor suck
hasExactSynonym: Poor suck|Poor sucking|Sucking weakness
IAO_0000115: An inadequate sucking reflex, resulting in the difficult of newborns to be breast-fed.

LABEL: Abnormal rectum morphology
hasExactSynonym: Abnormality of the rectum|Anomaly of the rectum
IAO_0000115: An abnormaltiy of the rectum, the final segment of the large intestine that stores solid waste until it passes through the anus.

LABEL: Rectal prolapse
hasExactSynonym: Rectum protrudes through anus
IAO_0000115: Protrusion of the rectal mucous membrane through the anus.

LABEL: Hiatus hernia
hasExactSynonym: Hiatal hernia|Stomach hernia
IAO_0000115: The presence of a hernia in which the upper part of the stomach, i.e., mainly the gastric cardia protrudes through the diaphragmatic esophageal hiatus.

LABEL: Inflammation of the large intestine
hasExactSynonym: Inflammation of the large intestine
IAO_0000115: Inflammation, or an inflammatory state in the large intestine.

LABEL: Anorexia
hasExactSynonym: Anorexia|Deliberately not eating|Obsessive dieting|Refusing to eat
IAO_0000115: Lack of desire to eat (loss of appetite).

LABEL: Esophageal stricture
hasExactSynonym: Narrowing of esophagus due to inflammation and scar tissue|Narrowing of oesophagus due to inflammation and scar tissue
IAO_0000115: A pathological narrowing of the esophagus that is caused by the development of a ring of scar tissue that constricts the esophageal lumen.

LABEL: Hypothermia
hasExactSynonym: Abnormally low body temperature|Hypothermia
IAO_0000115: Reduced body temperature due to failed thermoregulation.

LABEL: Malignant hyperthermia
IAO_0000115: Malignant hyperthermia is characterized by a rapid increase in temperature to 39-42 degrees C. Malignant hyperthermia may occur in response to either inhalational anesthetics such as halothane, to muscle relaxants such as succinylcholine, or to exercise.

LABEL: Myopathic facies
hasExactSynonym: Myopathic face|Myopathic facial appearance
IAO_0000115: A facial appearance characteristic of myopathic conditions. The face appears expressionless with sunken cheeks, bilateral ptosis, and inability to elevate the corners of the mouth, due to muscle weakness.

LABEL: Cerebral atrophy
hasExactSynonym: Degeneration of cerebrum
IAO_0000115: Atrophy (wasting, decrease in size of cells or tissue) affecting the cerebrum.

LABEL: Abnormal cerebral morphology
hasExactSynonym: Abnormality of the cerebrum|Abnormality of the telencephalon|Cerebral lesion
IAO_0000115: Any structural abnormality of the telencephalon, which is also known as the cerebrum.

LABEL: Lower limb spasticity
hasExactSynonym: Lower extremities spasticity|Lower extremity spasticity|Spastic lower extremities|Spastic lower extremity|Spastic lower limb|Spastic lower limbs|Spasticity in lower extremities|Spasticity in lower extremity|Spasticity in lower limb|Spasticity in lower limbs|Spasticity of lower extremities|Spasticity of lower extremity|Spasticity of lower limb|Spasticity of lower limbs
IAO_0000115: Spasticity (velocity-dependent increase in tonic stretch reflexes with increased muscle tone and hyperexcitable tendon reflexes) in the muscles of the lower limbs, hips, and pelvis.

LABEL: Rigidity
hasExactSynonym: Muscle rigidity|Rigidity
IAO_0000115: Continuous involuntary sustained muscle contraction. When an affected muscle is passively stretched, the degree of resistance remains constant regardless of the rate at which the muscle is stretched. This feature helps to distinguish rigidity from muscle spasticity.

LABEL: Spastic gait
hasExactSynonym: Spastic walk
IAO_0000115: Spasticity is manifested by increased stretch reflex which is intensified with movement velocity. This results in excessive and inappropriate muscle activation which can contribute to muscle hypertonia. Spastic gait is characterized by manifestations such as muscle hypertonia, stiff knee, and circumduction of the leg.

LABEL: Gait ataxia
hasExactSynonym: Ataxia of gait|Ataxic gait|Inability to coordinate movements when walking
IAO_0000115: A type of ataxia characterized by the impairment of the ability to coordinate the movements required for normal walking. Gait ataxia is characteirzed by a wide-based staggering gait with a tendency to fall.

LABEL: Bradykinesia
hasExactSynonym: Slow movements|Slowness of movements
IAO_0000115: Bradykinesia literally means slow movement, and is used clinically to denote a slowness in the execution of movement (in contrast to hypokinesia, which is used to refer to slowness in the initiation of movement).

LABEL: Bilateral tonic-clonic seizure
hasExactSynonym: Bilateral convulsive seizures|Generalised convulsion|Generalised tonic-clonic seizure (without specification of onset)|Generalized convulsion|Generalized tonic-clonic seizure (without specification of onset)|Grand mal|Grand mal seizures|Seizures, tonic-clonic|Tonic-clonic convulsion|Tonic-clonic convulsions
IAO_0000115: A bilateral tonic-clonic seizure is a seizure defined by a tonic (bilateral increased tone, lasting seconds to minutes) and then a clonic (bilateral sustained rhythmic jerking) phase.

LABEL: Limb ataxia
hasExactSynonym: Appendicular ataxia
IAO_0000115: A kind of ataxia that affects movements of the extremities.

LABEL: Chorea
hasExactSynonym: Choreic movements|Choreiform movements
IAO_0000115: Chorea (Greek for 'dance') refers to widespread arrhythmic involuntary movements of a forcible, jerky and restless fashion. It is a random-appearing sequence of one or more discrete involuntary movements or movement fragments. Movements appear random because of variability in timing, duration or location. Each movement may have a distinct start and end. However, movements may be strung together and thus may appear to flow randomly from one muscle group to another. Chorea can involve the trunk, neck, face, tongue, and extremities.

LABEL: Progressive cerebellar ataxia
hasExactSynonym: Cerebellar ataxia, progressive|Progressive ataxia

LABEL: Dysdiadochokinesis
hasExactSynonym: Difficulty performing quick and alternating movements|Dysdiadochokinesia
IAO_0000115: A type of ataxia characterized by the impairment of the ability to perform rapidly alternating movements, such as pronating and supinating his or her hand on the dorsum of the other hand as rapidly as possible.

LABEL: Hypoplasia of the corpus callosum
hasExactSynonym: Corpus callosum hypoplasia|Hypoplasia of corpus callosum|Hypoplastic corpus callosum|Underdevelopment of part of brain called corpus callosum
IAO_0000115: Underdevelopment of the corpus callosum.

LABEL: Intention tremor
IAO_0000115: A type of kinetic tremor that occurs during target directed movement is called intention tremor. That is, an oscillatory cerebellar ataxia that tends to be absent when the limbs are inactive and during the first part of voluntary movement but worsening as the movement continues and greater precision is required (e.g., in touching a target such as the patient's nose or a physician's finger).

LABEL: Encephalocele
hasExactSynonym: Bifid skull|Cranium bifidum
IAO_0000115: A neural tube defect characterized by sac-like protrusions of the brain and the membranes that cover it through openings in the skull.

LABEL: Abnormality of the respiratory system
hasExactSynonym: Respiratory abnormality
IAO_0000115: An abnormality of the respiratory system, which include the airways, lungs, and the respiratory muscles.

LABEL: Abnormal lung morphology
hasExactSynonym: Abnormality of lung structure|Abnormality of the lungs|Abnormally shaped lung|Unusual lung shape
IAO_0000115: Any structural anomaly of the lung.

LABEL: Pulmonary hypoplasia
hasExactSynonym: Hypoplastic lung|Hypoplastic lungs|Lung hypoplasia|Poorly developed lungs|Small lung|Underdeveloped lung

LABEL: Pneumonia
hasExactSynonym: Pneumonia
IAO_0000115: Inflammation of any part of the lung parenchyma.

LABEL: Restrictive ventilatory defect
hasExactSynonym: Restrictive deficit on pulmonary function testing|Restrictive deficit on pulmonary function tests|Restrictive respiratory disease|Restrictive respiratory insufficiency|Restrictive respiratory syndrome|Spirometric restriction|Stiff lung or chest wall causing decreased lung volume
IAO_0000115: A functional defect characterized by reduced total lung capacity (TLC) not associated with abnormalities of expiratory airflow or airway resistance. Spirometrically, a restrictive defect is defined as FEV1 (forced expiratory volume in 1 second) and FVC (forced vital capacity) less than 80 per cent. Restrictive lung disease may be caused by alterations in lung parenchyma or because of a disease of the pleura, chest wall, or neuromuscular apparatus.

LABEL: Respiratory insufficiency
hasExactSynonym: Respiratory impairment

LABEL: Dyspnea
hasExactSynonym: Abnormal breathing|Breathing difficulty|Difficult to breathe|Difficulty breathing|Dyspnoea|Shortness of breath|Trouble breathing
IAO_0000115: Difficult or labored breathing. Dyspnea is a subjective feeling only the patient can rate, e.g., on a Borg scale.

LABEL: Respiratory distress
hasExactSynonym: Breathing difficulties|Labored breathing|Laboured breathing
IAO_0000115: Respiratory distress is objectively observable as the physical or emotional consequences from the experience of dyspnea. The physical presentation of respiratory distress is generally referred to as labored breathing, while the sensation of respiratory distress is called shortness of breath or dyspnea.

LABEL: Asthma
hasExactSynonym: Asthma|Bronchial asthma
IAO_0000115: Asthma is characterized by increased responsiveness of the tracheobronchial tree to multiple stimuli, leading to narrowing of the air passages with resultant dyspnea, cough, and wheezing.

LABEL: Pleuritis
hasExactSynonym: Inflammation of tissues lining lungs and chest|Pleurisy
IAO_0000115: Inflammation of the pleura.

LABEL: Apnea
hasExactSynonym: Absence of spontaneous respiration|Apneic episodes|Apnoea
IAO_0000115: Lack of breathing with no movement of the respiratory muscles and no exchange of air in the lungs. This term refers to a disposition to have recurrent episodes of apnea rather than to a single event.

LABEL: Hemoptysis
hasExactSynonym: Coughing up blood|Haemoptysis
IAO_0000115: Coughing up (expectoration) of blood or blood-streaked sputum from the larynx, trachea, bronchi, or lungs.

LABEL: Pneumothorax
hasExactSynonym: Collapsed lung
IAO_0000115: Accumulation of air in the pleural cavity leading to a partially or completely collapsed lung.

LABEL: Spontaneous pneumothorax
hasExactSynonym: Spontaneous collapsed lung
IAO_0000115: Pneumothorax occurring without traumatic injury to the chest or lung.

LABEL: Bronchiectasis
hasExactSynonym: Permanent enlargement of the airways of the lungs
IAO_0000115: Persistent abnormal dilatation of the bronchi owing to localized and irreversible destruction and widening of the large airways.

LABEL: Ventriculomegaly
hasExactSynonym: Cerebral ventricular dilatation|Dilated cerebral ventricle|Dilated cerebral ventricles|Dilated ventricles|Enlarged cerebral ventricles|Enlarged ventricles|Enlarged ventricular system|Large cerebral ventricles and cisternae|Ventricular dilatation
IAO_0000115: An increase in size of the ventricular system of the brain.

LABEL: Cerebral cortical atrophy
hasExactSynonym: Cerebral cortex atrophy|Cortical atrophy|Decrease in size of the outer layer of the brain due to loss of brain cells
IAO_0000115: Atrophy of the cortex of the cerebrum.

LABEL: Generalized non-motor (absence) seizure
hasExactSynonym: Absence seizure|Absence seizures|Brief seizures with staring spells|Generalised non-motor (absence) seizure|Generalised non-motor seizure|Petit mal|Petit mal seizure|Petit mal seizures
IAO_0000115: A generalized non-motor (absence) seizure is a type of a type of dialeptic seizure that is of electrographically generalized onset. It is a generalized seizure characterized by an interruption of activities, a blank stare, and usually the person will be unresponsive when spoken to. Any ictal motor phenomena are minor in comparison to these non-motor features.

LABEL: Generalized myoclonic seizure
hasExactSynonym: Generalised epileptic myoclonus|Generalised myoclonic seizure|Generalised myoclonic seizures|Generalized epileptic myoclonus|Generalized myoclonic seizures|Myoclonus seizures
IAO_0000115: A generalized myoclonic seizure is a type of generalized motor seizure characterized by bilateral, sudden, brief (<100 ms) involuntary single or multiple contraction of muscles or muscle groups of variable topography (axial, proximal limb, distal). Myoclonus is less regularly repetitive and less sustained than is clonus.

LABEL: Abnormal upper motor neuron morphology
hasExactSynonym: Abnormal shape of upper motor neuron
IAO_0000115: Any structural anomaly that affects the upper motor neuron.

LABEL: Porencephalic cyst
hasExactSynonym: Cavity within brain
IAO_0000115: A cavity within the cerebral hemisphere, filled with cerebrospinal fluid, that communicates directly with the ventricular system.

LABEL: Abnormal basal ganglia morphology
hasExactSynonym: Abnormality of the basal ganglia|Anomaly of the basal ganglia|Basal ganglia disease
IAO_0000115: Abnormality of the basal ganglia.

LABEL: Basal ganglia calcification
hasExactSynonym: Basal ganglia calcifications|Basal ganglion calcification|Calcification of the basal ganglia
IAO_0000115: The presence of calcium deposition affecting one or more structures of the basal ganglia.

LABEL: Broad-based gait
hasExactSynonym: Broad based gait|Wide based gait|Wide based walk|Wide-based gait
IAO_0000115: An abnormal gait pattern in which persons stand and walk with their feet spaced widely apart. This is often a component of cerebellar ataxia.

LABEL: Ischemic stroke
hasExactSynonym: Ischaemic stroke
IAO_0000115: Acute ischemic stroke (AIS) is defined by the sudden loss of blood flow to an area of the brain with the resulting loss of neurologic function. It is caused by thrombosis or embolism that occludes a cerebral vessel supplying a specific area of the brain. During a vessel occlusion, there is a core area where damage to the brain is irreversible and an area of penumbra where the brain has lost function owing to decreased blood flow but is not irreversibly injured.

LABEL: Gait imbalance
hasExactSynonym: Abnormality of balance|Abnormality of equilibrium|Imbalanced walk

LABEL: Tethered cord
hasExactSynonym: Occult spinal dysraphism
IAO_0000115: During normal embryological development, the spinal cord first occupies the entire length of the vertebral column but goes on to assume a position at the level of L1 due to differential growth of the conus medullaris and the vertebral column. The filum terminale is a slender, threadlike structure that remains after the normal regression of the distal embryonic spinal cord and attaches the spinal cord to the coccyx. A tethered cord results if there is a thickened rope-like filum terminale which anchors the cord at the level of L2 or below, potentially causing neurologic signs owing to abnormal tension on the spinal cord.

LABEL: Frontotemporal dementia
IAO_0000115: A dementia associated with degeneration of the frontotemporal lobe and clinically associated with personality and behavioral changes such as disinhibition, apathy, and lack of insight. The hallmark feature of frontotemporal dementia is the presentation with focal syndromes such as progressive language dysfunction, or aphasia, or behavioral changes characteristic of frontal lobe disorders.

LABEL: Hypophosphatemia
hasExactSynonym: Decreased phosphate ion concentration|Decreased phosphate ion level|Decreased phosphate ion level in blood|Hypophosphataemia|Low blood phosphate level|Reduced phosphate ion concentration|Reduced phosphate ion level|Reduced phosphate ion level in blood
IAO_0000115: The concentration of phosphate ion in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal.

LABEL: Hyperuricemia
hasExactSynonym: Elevated uric acid concentration|Elevated uric acid level|Elevated uric acid level in blood|High blood uric acid level|Hyperuricaemia|Increased uric acid concentration|Increased uric acid level|Increased uric acid level in blood
IAO_0000115: The concentration of uric acid in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

LABEL: Hypercalciuria
hasExactSynonym: Elevated urine calcium levels|Hypercalcinuria

LABEL: Increased circulating lactate concentration
hasExactSynonym: Increased blood lactate|Increased serum lactate
IAO_0000115: Abnormally increased level of blood lactate (2-hydroxypropanoic acid). Lactate is produced from pyruvate by lactate dehydrogenase during normal metabolism. The terms lactate and lactic acid are often used interchangeably but lactate (the component measured in blood) is strictly a weak base whereas lactic acid is the corresponding acid. Lactic acidosis is often used clinically to describe elevated lactate but should be reserved for cases where there is a corresponding acidosis (pH below 7.35).

LABEL: Hyperkalemia
hasExactSynonym: Elevated potassium(1+) concentration|Elevated potassium(1+) level|Elevated potassium(1+) level in blood|Increased circulating potassium concentration|Increased potassium(1+) concentration|Increased potassium(1+) level|Increased potassium(1+) level in blood
IAO_0000115: The concentration of potassium(1+) in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

LABEL: Hyperglycinemia
hasExactSynonym: Elevated blood glycine levels|Hyperglycinaemia
IAO_0000115: An elevated concentration of glycine in the blood.

LABEL: Homocystinuria
hasExactSynonym: High urine homocystine levels
IAO_0000115: An increased concentration of homocystine in the urine.

LABEL: Hyperhomocystinemia
hasExactSynonym: Elevated blood homocystine|Elevated homocystine concentration|Elevated homocystine level|Elevated homocystine level in blood|Homocystinemia|Increased homocystine concentration|Increased homocystine level|Increased homocystine level in blood
IAO_0000115: The concentration of homocystine in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

LABEL: Low posterior hairline
hasExactSynonym: Low hairline at back of neck|Low posterior hair line
IAO_0000115: Hair on the neck extends more inferiorly than usual.

LABEL: Nail dysplasia
hasExactSynonym: Atypical nail growth|Dysplastic nails|Onychodysplasia
IAO_0000115: The presence of developmental dysplasia of the nail.

LABEL: Nail pterygium
hasExactSynonym: Pterygium of nails
IAO_0000115: Inward advance of skin over the nail plate.

LABEL: Impaired vibration sensation in the lower limbs
hasExactSynonym: Decreased lower limb vibratory sense|Decreased vibratory sense in lower limbs|Decreased vibratory sense in the lower extremities|Decreased vibratory sense in the lower limbs|Diminished vibratory sensation in the legs|Distal sensory loss, especially vibratory sense|Distal vibratory impairment of the lower limbs|Impaired vibration sensation in the lower limbs
IAO_0000115: A decrease in the ability to perceive vibration in the legs.

LABEL: Abnormal speech pattern
hasExactSynonym: Abnormal speech|Abnormal vocalisation|Abnormal vocalization|Abnormality of speech or vocalization
IAO_0000115: An abnormality in the sound (volume) or cadence (rate) of speech.

LABEL: Clonus
hasExactSynonym: Involuntary rhythmic muscular contractions and relaxations
IAO_0000115: A series of rhythmic and involuntary muscle contractions (at a frequency of about 5 to 7 Hz) that occur in response to an abruptly applied and sustained stretch.

LABEL: Intracranial hemorrhage
hasExactSynonym: Bleeding within the skull|Intracranial haemorrhage
IAO_0000115: Hemorrhage occurring within the skull.

LABEL: Gliosis
hasExactSynonym: Cerebral gliosis|Excess astrocytes in brain
IAO_0000115: Gliosis is the focal proliferation of glial cells in the central nervous system.

LABEL: Postural instability
hasExactSynonym: Balance impairment
IAO_0000115: A tendency to fall or the inability to keep oneself from falling; imbalance. The retropulsion test is widely regarded as the gold standard to evaluate postural instability, Use of the retropulsion test includes a rapid balance perturbation in the backward direction, and the number of balance correcting steps (or total absence thereof) is used to rate the degree of postural instability. Healthy subjects correct such perturbations with either one or two large steps, or without taking any steps, hinging rapidly at the hips while swinging the arms forward as a counterweight. In patients with balance impairment, balance correcting steps are often too small, forcing patients to take more than two steps. Taking three or more steps is generally considered to be abnormal, and taking more than five steps is regarded as being clearly abnormal. Markedly affected patients continue to step backward without ever regaining their balance and must be caught by the examiner (this would be called true retropulsion). Even more severely affected patients fail to correct entirely, and fall backward like a pushed toy soldier, without taking any corrective steps.

LABEL: Neurodegeneration
hasExactSynonym: Ongoing loss of nerve cells
IAO_0000115: Progressive loss of neural cells and tissue.

LABEL: Cerebral edema
hasExactSynonym: Brain edema|Brain oedema|Cerebral oedema|Swelling of brain
IAO_0000115: Abnormal accumulation of fluid in the brain.

LABEL: Phonophobia
hasExactSynonym: Fear of loud sounds
IAO_0000115: An abnormally heightened sensitivity to loud sounds.

LABEL: Neurofibrillary tangles
hasExactSynonym: NFTs|Neurofibrillary tangles composed of disordered microtubules in neurons|Paired helical filaments|Tau-positive neurofibrillary tangles|Tau-positive tangle
IAO_0000115: Pathological protein aggregates formed by hyperphosphorylation of a microtubule-associated protein known as tau, causing it to aggregate in an insoluble form.

LABEL: Profound intellectual disability
hasExactSynonym: IQ less than 20|Intellectual disability, profound|Mental retardation, profound|Profound mental retardation
IAO_0000115: Profound intellectual disability (ID) is defined as a type of ID characterized by profoundly sub-average adaptive functioning and intellectual functioning, with an intelligence quotient (IQ) below 20.

LABEL: Delayed CNS myelination
hasExactSynonym: Delay in central nervous system myelination
IAO_0000115: Delayed myelination in the central nervous system.

LABEL: Progressive spasticity
hasExactSynonym: Spasticity, progressive
IAO_0000115: Spasticity that increases in degree with time.

LABEL: Delayed gross motor development
hasExactSynonym: Delayed attainment of gross motor milestones|Delayed attainment of gross motor skills|Delayed development of gross motor milestones|Delayed development of gross motor skills|Delayed gross motor milestones|Delayed gross motor skills|Delayed motor skills|Developmental delay, gross motor|Gross motor delay|Limited gross motor development|Limited gross motor skills
IAO_0000115: A type of motor delay characterized by a delay in acquiring the ability to control the large muscles of the body for walking, running, sitting, and crawling.

LABEL: Dysgenesis of the cerebellar vermis
IAO_0000115: Defective development of the vermis of cerebellum.

LABEL: Myelopathy
IAO_0000115: Myelopathy is an descriptive term, referring to pathology leading to a neurologic deficit related to the spinal cord. The clinical diagnosis of myelopathy requires a detailed history and physical examination to define the clinical syndrome. Neuroimaging is indicated in most instances of new-onset myelopathy. It is indicated also when the worsening of a myelopathy is unexplained.

LABEL: Generalized-onset seizure
hasExactSynonym: Generalised onset seizure|Generalised seizures|Generalised-onset seizure|Generalized onset seizure|Generalized seizures|Generalized-onset seizures|Primary generalised seizure|Primary generalized seizure
IAO_0000115: A generalized-onset seizure is a type of seizure originating at some point within, and rapidly engaging, bilaterally distributed networks. The networks may include cortical and subcortical structures but not necessarily the entire cortex.

LABEL: Pleural effusion
hasExactSynonym: Fluid around lungs
IAO_0000115: The presence of an excessive amount of fluid in the pleural cavity.

LABEL: Pulmonary embolism
hasExactSynonym: Blood clot in artery of lung
IAO_0000115: An embolus (that is, an abnormal particle circulating in the blood) located in the pulmonary artery and thereby blocking blood circulation to the lung. Usually the embolus is a blood clot that has developed in an extremity (for instance, a deep venous thrombosis), detached, and traveled through the circulation before becoming trapped in the pulmonary artery.

LABEL: Recurrent respiratory infections
hasExactSynonym: Frequent respiratory infections|Multiple respiratory infections|Recurrent respiratory infections|Susceptibility to respiratory infections|respiratory infections, recurrent
IAO_0000115: An increased susceptibility to respiratory infections as manifested by a history of recurrent respiratory infections.

LABEL: Coarse hair
hasExactSynonym: Coarse hair|Coarse hair texture
IAO_0000115: Hair shafts are rough in texture.

LABEL: Sparse scalp hair

IAO_0000115: Decreased number of hairs per unit area of skin of the scalp.

LABEL: White forelock
hasExactSynonym: Poliosis of anterior hair|Poliosis of forelock hair|White part of hair above forehead
IAO_0000115: A triangular depigmented region of white hairs located in the anterior midline of the scalp.

LABEL: Premature graying of hair
hasExactSynonym: Early graying|Early greying|Premature graying|Premature graying of hair|Premature greying|Premature greying of hair|Premature hair graying|Premature hair greying
IAO_0000115: Development of gray hair at a younger than normal age.

LABEL: Facial hypertrichosis
hasExactSynonym: Increased facial hair growth
IAO_0000115: Excessive, increased hair growth located in the facial region.

LABEL: Absent axillary hair
IAO_0000115: Absence of axillary hair.

LABEL: Woolly hair
hasExactSynonym: Kinked hair|Wooly hair
IAO_0000115: The term wooly hair refers to an abnormal variant of hair that is fine, with tightly coiled curls, and often hypopigmented. Optical microscopy may reveal the presence of tight spirals and a clear diameter reduction as compared with normal hair. Electron microscopy may show flat, oval hair shafts with reduced transversal diameter.

LABEL: White eyebrow
hasExactSynonym: Depigmented eyebrow|Hypopigmented eyebrow|Pale eyebrow|White eyebrow
IAO_0000115: White color (lack of pigmentation) of the eyebrow.

LABEL: White eyelashes
hasExactSynonym: Blonde eyelashes|Depigmented eyelashes|Pale eyelashes|White eyelashes
IAO_0000115: White color (lack of pigmentation) of the eyelashes.

LABEL: Frontal upsweep of hair
hasExactSynonym: Cowlick|Frontal Cowlick|Frontal upsweep of hair|Upswept frontal hair
IAO_0000115: Upward and/or sideward growth of anterior hair.

LABEL: Gastrointestinal hemorrhage
hasExactSynonym: GI haemorrhage|GI hemorrhage|Gastrointestinal bleeding|Gastrointestinal haemorrhage
IAO_0000115: Hemorrhage affecting the gastrointestinal tract.

LABEL: Hepatomegaly
hasExactSynonym: Enlarged liver
IAO_0000115: Abnormally increased size of the liver.

LABEL: Abnormal intestine morphology
hasExactSynonym: Abnormality of the intestine|Enteropathy
IAO_0000115: An abnormality of the intestine. The closely related term enteropathy is used to refer to any disease of the intestine.

LABEL: Protein-losing enteropathy
IAO_0000115: Abnormal loss of protein from the digestive tract related to excessive leakage of plasma proteins into the lumen of the gastrointestinal tract.

LABEL: Abnormal duodenum morphology
hasExactSynonym: Abnormality of the duodenum
IAO_0000115: An abnormality of the duodenum, i.e., the first section of the small intestine.

LABEL: Hematemesis

IAO_0000115: Rickets is divided into two major categories including calcipenic and phosphopenic. Hypophosphatemia is described as a common manifestation of both categories. LABEL: Reduced circulating complement concentration

LABEL: Craniofacial dysostosis

IAO_0000115: A characteristic appearance resulting from defective ossification of craniofacial bones.

LABEL: Coronal craniosynostosis

LABEL: Lambdoidal craniosynostosis
hasExactSynonym: Lambdoid suture craniosynostosis|Lambdoid suture synostosis
IAO_0000115: A kind of craniosynostosis affecting the lambdoidal suture.

LABEL: Spherocytosis
IAO_0000115: The presence of erythrocytes that are sphere-shaped.

LABEL: Overfolding of the superior helices
hasExactSynonym: Overfolding of superior helix
IAO_0000115: A condition in which the superior portion of the helix is folded over to a greater degree than normal.

LABEL: Preauricular pit

IAO_0000115: Small indentation anterior to the insertion of the ear.

LABEL: Persistent open anterior fontanelle

IAO_0000115: The anterior fontanelle generally ossifies by around the 18th month of life. A persistent open anterior fontanelle is diagnosed if closure is delayed beyond this age.

LABEL: Progressive macrocephaly
hasExactSynonym: Macrocephaly, progressive|Progressively abnormally enlarging cranium|Progressively abnormally enlarging skull
IAO_0000115: The progressive development of an abnormally large skull.

LABEL: Relative macrocephaly
hasExactSynonym: Disproportionately large head|Macrocephaly, relative|Relatively large head
IAO_0000115: A relatively mild degree of macrocephaly in which the head circumference is not above two standard deviations from the mean, but appears dysproportionately large when other factors such as body stature are taken into account.

LABEL: Craniofacial asymmetry
hasExactSynonym: Uneven craniofacial structures
IAO_0000115: Asymmetry of the bones of the skull and the face.

LABEL: Macrocephaly at birth
hasExactSynonym: Big cranium present at birth|Big cranium present since birth|Big skull present at birth|Big skull present since birth|Congenital large cranium|Congenital large skull|Congenital macrocephaly|Head circumference large for gestational age|Large cranium present at birth|Large cranium present since birth|Large skull present at birth|Large skull present since birth
IAO_0000115: The presence of an abnormally large skull with onset at birth.

LABEL: Sacral hypertrichosis

LABEL: Scarring alopecia of scalp
hasExactSynonym: Cicatricial alopecia

LABEL: Generalized hypertrichosis
hasExactSynonym: Generalised hypertrichosis
IAO_0000115: Generalized excessive, abnormal hairiness.

LABEL: Pear-shaped vertebrae
hasExactSynonym: Pear-shaped vertebral bodies
IAO_0000115: Bulbous appearance of the anterior vertebral bodies, such that the vertebral bodies have the greatest vertical height anteriorly as well as bulbous anterior superior-inferior contours.

LABEL: Cervical C2/C3 vertebral fusion
hasExactSynonym: Fusion of cervical vertebrae c2-3|Klippel-Feil anomaly|Klippel-Feil syndrome
IAO_0000115: Fusion of cervical vertebrae at C2 and C3, caused by a failure in the normal segmentation or division of the cervical vertebrae during the early weeks of fetal development, leading to a short neck with a low hairline at the back of the head, and restricted mobility of the upper spine.

LABEL: Absent vertebral body mineralization
IAO_0000115: A lack of bone mineralization of the vertebral bodies.

LABEL: Talipes valgus
IAO_0000115: Outward turning of the heel, resulting in clubfoot with the person walking on the inner part of the foot.

LABEL: 2-3 toe syndactyly
hasExactSynonym: 2-3 syndactyly of feet|2-3 toe soft tissue syndactyly|2-3 toes syndactyly|Syndactyly of second and third toes|Toe syndactyly, 2-3|Webbed 2nd and 3rd toes|partial or complete syndactyly 2nd-3rd toes
IAO_0000115: Syndactyly with fusion of toes two and three.

LABEL: 4-5 toe syndactyly
hasExactSynonym: Symmetric syndactyly, toes 4 and 5|Syndactyly of toes 4 and 5|Webbed 4th-5th toes
IAO_0000115: Syndactyly with fusion of toes four and five.

LABEL: Hyperechogenic kidneys
hasExactSynonym: Echogenic kidneys|Increased echogenicity of the renal parenchyma
IAO_0000115: An increase in amplitude of waves returned in ultrasonography of the kidney, which is generally displayed as increased brightness of the signal.

LABEL: Calcium nephrolithiasis
hasExactSynonym: Ca kidney stone|Ca nephrolithiasis|Ca2+ kidney stone|Ca2+ nephrolithiasis|Calcium kidney stone
IAO_0000115: The presence of calcium-containing calculi (stones) in the kidneys.

LABEL: Acute tubulointerstitial nephritis
IAO_0000115: Acute inflammation of the kidney affecting the interstitium of the kidneys surrounding the tubules.

LABEL: Chronic tubulointerstitial nephritis
IAO_0000115: Chronic inflammation of the kidney affecting the interstitium of the kidneys surrounding the tubules.

LABEL: Paroxysmal ventricular tachycardia
hasExactSynonym: Episodes of ventricular tachycardia
IAO_0000115: Episodes of ventricular tachycardia that have a sudden onset and ending.

LABEL: Supraventricular tachycardia
hasExactSynonym: SVT|Supraventricular tachyarrhythmia
IAO_0000115: Supraventricular tachycardia (SVT) is an abnormally increased heart rate (over 100 beats per minute at rest) with origin above the level of the ventricles.

LABEL: Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation
hasExactSynonym: Atrial fibrillation, paroxysmal|Intermittent atrial fibrillation|Paroxysmal AF
IAO_0000115: Episodes of atrial fibrillation that typically last for several hours up to one day and terminate spontaneously.

LABEL: Effort-induced polymorphic ventricular tachycardia
hasExactSynonym: Catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia|Exercise-induced polymorphic ventricular tachycardia
IAO_0000115: Polymorphic ventricular arrhythmias of varying morphologythat do not exist under resting conditions but appear only upon physical exercise or catecholamine administration.

LABEL: Paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia
hasExactSynonym: Episodic supraventricular tachycardia|PSVT
IAO_0000115: An episodic form of supraventricular tachycardia with abrupt onset and termination.

LABEL: Myxomatous mitral valve degeneration
IAO_0000115: Myxomatous mitral valve is defined as the presence of excess leaflet tissue and leaflet thickening greater than 5 mm, resulting in a prolapse greater than 2 mm into the left atrium on parasternal long axis view.

LABEL: Duodenal polyposis
hasExactSynonym: Multiple duodenal polyps
IAO_0000115: Presence of multiple polyps in the duodenum.

LABEL: Fulminant hepatitis
IAO_0000115: Acute hepatitis complicated by acute liver failure with hepatic encephalopathy occurring less than 8 weeks after the onset of jaundice.

LABEL: Lactose intolerance
hasExactSynonym: Lactose intolerance|Milk intolerance
IAO_0000115: An inability to digest lactose.

LABEL: Gastrointestinal obstruction
hasExactSynonym: GI obstruction|Gastrointestinal obstruction|Obstruction in digestive tract

hasExactSynonym: Recurrent gastrointestinal infections|Recurrent infection of the GI tract|Recurrent infection of the gastrointestinal tract
IAO_0000115: Recurrent infection of the gastrointestinal tract.

LABEL: Congenital hemolytic anemia
hasExactSynonym: Congenital haemolytic anaemia|Congenital haemolytic anemia|Congenital hemolytic anaemia
IAO_0000115: A form of hemolytic anemia with congenital onset.

LABEL: Neonatal alloimmune thrombocytopenia
IAO_0000115: Low platelet count associated with maternal platelet-specific alloantibodies.

LABEL: Pyropoikilocytosis
hasExactSynonym: hereditary pyropoikilocytosis
IAO_0000115: A form of severe hemolytic anemia characterized by erythrocyte morphology reminiscent of that seen in patients after a thermal burn.

LABEL: Hypochromic microcytic anemia
hasExactSynonym: Hypochromic microcytic anaemia|Hypochromic, microcytic anaemia|Hypochromic, microcytic anemia
IAO_0000115: A type of anemia characterized by an abnormally low concentration of hemoglobin in the erythrocytes and lower than normal size of the erythrocytes.

LABEL: Reduced factor XII activity
hasExactSynonym: Factor XII deficiency|Hageman factor deficiency
IAO_0000115: Decreased activity of coagulation factor XII. Factor XII (fXII) is part of the intrinsic coagulation pathway and binds to exposed collagen at site of vessel wall injury, activated by high-MW kininogen and kallikrein, thereby initiating the coagulation cascade.

LABEL: Acute monocytic leukemia
hasExactSynonym: AML-M5|AMoL|Acute monoblastic leukaemia|Acute monoblastic leukemia|Acute monocytic leukaemia
IAO_0000115: The accumulation of transformed primitive hematopoietic blast cells, which lose their ability of normal differentiation and proliferation.

LABEL: Intermittent thrombocytopenia
IAO_0000115: Reduced platelet count that occurs sporadically, i.e., it comes and goes.

LABEL: Reduced protein S activity
IAO_0000115: An abnormality of coagulation related to a decreased concentration of vitamin K-dependent protein S. Protein S is a cofactor of protein C.

LABEL: Normochromic microcytic anemia
hasExactSynonym: Normochromic microcytic anaemia
IAO_0000115: A type of anemia characterized by an normal concentration of hemoglobin in the erythrocytes and lower than normal size of the erythrocytes.

LABEL: Thiamine-responsive megaloblastic anemia
hasExactSynonym: Thiamine-responsive megaloblastic anaemia
IAO_0000115: A type of megaloblastic anemia (i.e., anemia characterized by the presence of erythroblasts that are larger than normal) that improves upon the administration of thiamine.

LABEL: Impaired ADP-induced platelet aggregation
IAO_0000115: Abnormal platelet response to ADP as manifested by reduced or lacking aggregation of platelets upon addition of ADP.

LABEL: Incisional hernia
hasExactSynonym: Recurrent abdominal hernia
IAO_0000115: An abdominal hernia that occurs at a site of weakness in the abdominal wall resulting from an incompletely-healed surgical wound.

LABEL: Respiratory failure requiring assisted ventilation
hasExactSynonym: Respiratory distress necessitating mechanical ventilation|Respiratory distress requiring endotracheal intubation|Respiratory distress requiring mechanical ventilation
IAO_0000115: A state of respiratory distress that requires a life saving intervention in the form of gaining airway access and instituting positive pressure ventilation.

LABEL: Persistent lactic acidosis
IAO_0000115: A continuous form of lactic acidemia.

LABEL: Severe lactic acidosis
IAO_0000115: A severe form of lactic acidemia.

LABEL: Congenital lactic acidosis
IAO_0000115: A form of lactic acidemia with congenital onset.

LABEL: Chronic lactic acidosis
IAO_0000115: A chronic form of lactic acidemia.

LABEL: Pulmonary artery dilatation
IAO_0000115: An abnormal widening of the diameter of the pulmonary artery.

LABEL: Ascending aortic dissection
hasExactSynonym: Type A aortic dissection
IAO_0000115: A separation of the layers within the wall of the ascending aorta. Tears in the intimal layer result in the propagation of dissection (proximally or distally) secondary to blood entering the intima-media space.

LABEL: Pulmonary artery atresia
hasExactSynonym: Atresia of the pulmonary artery|Pulmonary atresia
IAO_0000115: A congenital anomaly with a narrowing or complete absence of the opening between the right ventricle and the pulmonary artery.

LABEL: Venous thrombosis
hasExactSynonym: Blood clot in vein
IAO_0000115: Formation of a blood clot (thrombus) inside a vein, causing the obstruction of blood flow.

LABEL: Dilatation of the cerebral artery
IAO_0000115: The presence of a localized dilatation or ballooning of a cerebral artery.

LABEL: Peripheral arterial stenosis
hasExactSynonym: Peripheral artery disease
IAO_0000115: Narrowing of peripheral arteries with reduction of blood flow to the limbs. This feature may be quantified as an ankle-brachial index of less than 0.9, and may be manifested clinically as claudication.

LABEL: Generalized arterial tortuosity
hasExactSynonym: Generalised arterial tortuosity|Generalised twisted arteries|Generalized twisted arteries
IAO_0000115: Abnormal tortuous (i.e., twisted) form of arteries affecting most or all arteries.

LABEL: Peripheral pulmonary artery stenosis
hasExactSynonym: Narrowing of peripheral lung artery|Peripheral pulmonic stenosis|peripheral pulmonary stenosis
IAO_0000115: Stenosis of a peripheral branch of the pulmonary artery.

IAO_0000115: An abnormal localized widening (dilatation) of the tubular part of the ascending aorta.

LABEL: Elevated mean arterial pressure
IAO_0000115: An abnormal increase in the average blood pressure in an individual during a single cardiac cycle.

LABEL: Knee dislocation
hasExactSynonym: Dislocations of the knees|Knee dislocations

LABEL: Rhizomelic arm shortening
IAO_0000115: Disproportionate shortening of the proximal segment of the arm (i.e. the humerus).

LABEL: Large joint dislocations
hasExactSynonym: Large joint dislocations

LABEL: Distal ulnar hypoplasia
hasExactSynonym: Distal shortening of ulna|Hypoplastic distal ulna
IAO_0000115: Underdevelopment of the distal portion of the ulna.

LABEL: Limited knee flexion/extension
IAO_0000115: A limited ability of the knee joint to perform extension and flexion.

LABEL: Streaky metaphyseal sclerosis
hasExactSynonym: Streak increase in bone density in wide portion of wide bone
IAO_0000115: The presence of streaks (bands) of abnormally increased density of metaphyseal bone.

LABEL: High-frequency hearing impairment
hasExactSynonym: Hearing loss, high-frequency|High frequency hearing loss|High-frequency deafness|Progressive high frequency hearing loss|Progressive high-frequency hearing loss
IAO_0000115: A type of hearing impairment affecting primarily the higher frequencies of sound (3,000 to 6,000 Hz).

LABEL: Arterial tortuosity
IAO_0000115: Abnormal tortuous (i.e., twisted) form of arteries.

LABEL: Elevated diastolic blood pressure
hasExactSynonym: Elevated diastolic BP
IAO_0000115: Abnormal increase in diastolic blood pressure.

LABEL: Abnormal cardiac atrium morphology
hasExactSynonym: Abnormality of cardiac atrium morphology|Abnormality of heart atrium
IAO_0000115: Any structural abnormality of a cardiac atrium.

LABEL: Pericardial constriction
IAO_0000115: Compression of the heart caused by rigid, thickened, or fused pericardial membranes.

LABEL: Right ventricular dilatation
hasExactSynonym: Dilated heart right ventricle
IAO_0000115: Enlargement of the chamber of the right ventricle, which can be defined echocardiographically as a right ventricular to left ventricular ratio greater than 1:1.

LABEL: Abnormal atrioventricular conduction
IAO_0000115: An impairment of the electrical continuity between the atria and ventricles.

LABEL: Concentric hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
hasExactSynonym: Symmetric, concentric, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
IAO_0000115: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with an symmetrical and concentric pattern of hypertrophy.

LABEL: Dysplastic pulmonary valve
hasExactSynonym: Dysplasia of pulmonary valve|Pulmonary valve dysplasia
IAO_0000115: A congenital malformation of the pulmonary valve characterized by leaflet deformation.

LABEL: Shortened PR interval
hasExactSynonym: Electrocardiographic short PR interval|Short P-R interval|Shortened PR interval on EKG
IAO_0000115: Reduced time for the PR interval (beginning of the P wave to the beginning of the QRS complex). In adults, normal values are 120 to 200 ms long.

LABEL: Elevated right atrial pressure
IAO_0000115: An abnormal increase in magnitude of the pressure in the right atrium.

LABEL: Tricuspid regurgitation
hasExactSynonym: Tricuspid insufficiency|Tricuspid valve regurgitation
IAO_0000115: Failure of the tricuspid valve to close sufficiently upon contraction of the right ventricle, causing blood to regurgitate (flow backward) into the right atrium.

LABEL: Premature coronary artery atherosclerosis
hasExactSynonym: Premature coronary artery disease
IAO_0000115: Reduction of the diameter of the coronary arteries as the result of an accumulation of atheromatous plaques within the walls of the coronary arteries before age of 45.

LABEL: Prolonged QTc interval
IAO_0000115: A longer than normal interval (corrected for heart rate) between the Q and T waves in the heart's cycle. Prolonged QTc can cause premature action potentials during late phase depolarizations thereby leading to ventricular arrhythmias and ventricular fibrillations.

LABEL: Pancreatic pseudocyst
IAO_0000115: Cyst-like space not lined by epithelium and contained within the pancreas. Pancreatic pseudocysts are often associated with pancreatitis.

LABEL: Secretory diarrhea
hasExactSynonym: Secretory diarrhoea
IAO_0000115: Watery voluminous diarrhea resulting from an imbalance between ion and water secretion and absorption.

LABEL: Rectal abscess
hasExactSynonym: Perirectal abscess
IAO_0000115: A collection of pus in the area of the rectum.

LABEL: Biliary tract obstruction
IAO_0000115: Obstruction affecting the biliary tree.

LABEL: Total intestinal aganglionosis
IAO_0000115: A congenital defect characterized by the lack of ganglion cells in the entire intestine, i.e., the aganglionic segment comprises the entire large and small bowel.

LABEL: Thoracic hypoplasia
hasExactSynonym: Small chest|Small thorax

IAO_0000115: Abnormality of the nostril.

LABEL: Arterial dissection
IAO_0000115: A separation (dissection) of the layers of an artery.

LABEL: Large vessel vasculitis
IAO_0000115: A type of vasculitis (inflammation of blood vessel walls) affecting large arteries such as the aorta and branches of the aorta.

LABEL: Increased pulmonary vascular resistance
IAO_0000115: Pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR) more than 3 wood units, as defined by the current definition of pulmonary hypertension. 95% of individuals have a PVR of less than 2.4 wood units.

LABEL: Progeroid facial appearance
hasExactSynonym: Aged facial appearance|Premature aged appearance|Prematurely aged face|Prematurely aged facial appearance|Wizened face
IAO_0000115: A degree of wrinkling of the facial skin that is more than expected for the age of the individual, leading to a prematurely aged appearance.

LABEL: Abnormal vena cava morphology
IAO_0000115: An abnormality of the structure of the veins that return deoxygenated blood from the body into the heart, i.e., the superior vena cava and the inferior vena cava.

LABEL: Severe T-cell immunodeficiency
hasExactSynonym: Severe T-cell immunodeficiency
IAO_0000115: A primary immune deficiency that is characterized by defects or deficiencies of T-lymphocytes that causes specific susceptibility to intracellular micro-organisms.

LABEL: Aplasia of the thymus
hasExactSynonym: Absent thymus|Athymia
IAO_0000115: Absence of the thymus. This feature may be appreciated by the lack of a thymic shadow upon radiographic examination.

LABEL: Combined immunodeficiency
IAO_0000115: A group of phenotypically heterogeneous genetic disorders characterized by profound deficiencies of T- and B-cell function, which predispose the patients to both infectious and noninfectious complications.

LABEL: Obtuse angle of mandible
hasExactSynonym: High mandibular plane angle|Steep mandibular plane angle
IAO_0000115: Abnormally flat (obtuse) angle of the mandible. The angle of the mandibular, located at the junction between the body and the ramus of the mandible, is normally close to being a right angle. This terms describes an abnormal increase of this angle such that the mandible appears flatter than normal.

LABEL: Premature closure of fontanelles
hasExactSynonym: Early closure of the fontanelles|Obliterated fontanelles|Premature fontanel closure
IAO_0000115: Normally, the posterior and lateral fontanelles are obliterated by about six months after birth, the anterior fontanelle closes by about the middle of the second year. This term refers to the situation in which the fontanelles close at an inappropriately early time point.
