This is a nodular tumor found in the periphery of the lung. It can occur at any age. The prognosis is related to the stage of the disease at the time of resection. Pulmonary blastoma is divided into two subtypes: epithelial predominant and biphasic.

LABEL: recurrent pneumonia
hasExactSynonym: recurrent pneumonia|recurrent pneumonia (disease)
IAO_0000115: Infections with nontuberculous mycobacteria (atypical mycobacteria): M. kansasii, M. marinum, M. scrofulaceum, M. flavescens, M. gordonae, M. obuense, M. gilvum, M. duvali, M. szulgai, M. intracellulare (see mycobacterium avium complex;), M. xenopi (littorale), M. ulcerans, M. buruli, M. terrae, M. fortuitum (minetti, giae), M. chelonae.

LABEL: REM sleep behavior disorder
IAO_0000115: A disorder characterized by episodes of vigorous and often violent motor activity during rem sleep (sleep, rem). The affected individual may inflict self injury or harm others, and is difficult to awaken from this condition. Episodes are usually followed by a vivid recollection of a dream that is consistent with the aggressive behavior. This condition primarily affects adult males. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p393)

LABEL: renal tuberculosis
hasExactSynonym: kidney tuberculosis|tuberculosis of kidney
IAO_0000115: Infection of the kidney due to mycobacteria.

LABEL: Reoviridae infectious disease
IAO_0000115: Infections produced by reoviruses, general or unspecified.

LABEL: respirovirus infectious disease
IAO_0000115: Infections with viruses of the genus respirovirus, family paramyxoviridae. Host cell infection occurs by adsorption, via hemagglutinin, to the cell surface.

LABEL: retroperitoneal cancer
hasExactSynonym: cancer of retroperitoneal space|malignant neoplasm of retroperitoneal space|malignant neoplasm of retroperitoneum and peritoneum|malignant retroperitoneal neoplasm|malignant retroperitoneal space neoplasm|malignant tumour of peritoneum and retroperitoneum|retroperitoneal space cancer
IAO_0000115: A primary or metastatic malignant neoplasm involving the retroperitoneum. The vast majority of cases are carcinomas, lymphomas, or sarcomas.

LABEL: Reye syndrome
hasExactSynonym: Reye's syndrome
IAO_0000115: An acute and potentially fatal metabolic disorder characterized by cerebral edema, fatty liver and hypoglycemia. It occurs primarily in children and has been associated with the use of aspirin for the treatment of viral infections. However, it can also occur in the absence of aspirin use.

LABEL: Rhabditida infectious disease
IAO_0000115: Infections with nematodes of the order rhabditida.

LABEL: Rhabdoviridae infectious disease
IAO_0000115: Virus diseases caused by rhabdoviridae. Important infections include rabies; ephemeral fever; and vesicular stomatitis.

LABEL: rhinoscleroma
IAO_0000115: A granulomatous disease caused by klebsiella rhinoscleromatis infection. Despite its name, this disease is not limited to the nose and nasopharynx but may affect any part of the respiratory tract, sometimes with extension to the lip and the skin.

LABEL: rhinosporidiosis
hasExactSynonym: Rhinosporidium seeberi caused disease or disorder|Rhinosporidium seeberi disease or disorder|Rhinosporidium seeberi infectious disease
IAO_0000115: Chronic, localized granulomatous infection of mucocutaneous tissues, especially the nose, and characterized by hyperplasia and the development of polyps. It is found in humans and other animals and is caused by the mesomycetozoean organism rhinosporidium seeberi.

LABEL: rickettsial pneumonia
hasExactSynonym: Rickettsiaceae caused pneumonia|Rickettsiaceae pneumonia
IAO_0000115: Pneumonia caused by infection with bacteria of the family rickettsiaceae.

LABEL: roseolovirus infectious disease
hasExactSynonym: Roseolovirus caused disease or disorder|Roseolovirus disease or disorder|Roseolovirus infectious disease
IAO_0000115: Infection with roseolovirus, the most common in humans being exanthema subitum, a benign disease of infants and young children.

LABEL: Salmonella gastroenteritis
hasExactSynonym: Salmonella caused gastroenteritis
IAO_0000115: Poisoning caused by ingestion of food harboring species of salmonella. Conditions of raising, shipping, slaughtering, and marketing of domestic animals contribute to the spread of this bacterium in the food supply.

LABEL: scarlet fever
hasExactSynonym: scarlatina
IAO_0000115: A streptococcal infection, mainly occurring among children, that is characterized by a red skin rash, sore throat, and fever.

LABEL: scirrhous adenocarcinoma
hasExactSynonym: FIBROADENOCARCINOMA, malignant|adenocarcinoma with productive fibrosis|fibrocarcinoma|scirrhous adenocarcinoma|scirrhous adenocarcinoma (morphologic abnormality)|scirrhous carcinoma
IAO_0000115: An infiltrating adenocarcinoma characterized by the presence of desmoplastic stromal reaction.

LABEL: screw worm infectious disease
hasExactSynonym: Cochliomyia hominivorax caused disease or disorder|Cochliomyia hominivorax disease or disorder|Cochliomyia hominivorax infectious disease
IAO_0000115: Infection with larvae of the blow fly Cochliomyia hominivorax (Callitroga americanum), a common cause of disease in livestock in the southern and southwestern U.S.A.

LABEL: septicemic plague
IAO_0000115: A plague in which the bacteria have entered the bloodstream.

LABEL: setariasis
hasExactSynonym: Setaria <nematode> caused disease or disorder|Setaria <nematode> disease or disorder|Setaria <nematode> infectious disease
IAO_0000115: Infection with nematodes of the genus Setaria. This condition is usually seen in cattle and equines and is of little pathogenic significance, although migration of the worm to the eye may lead to blindness.

LABEL: sick building syndrome
IAO_0000115: A group of symptoms that are two- to three-fold more common in those who work in large, energy-efficient buildings, associated with an increased frequency of headaches, lethargy, and dry skin. Clinical manifestations include hypersensitivity pneumonitis (alveolitis, extrinsic allergic); allergic rhinitis (rhinitis, allergic, perennial); asthma; infections, skin eruptions, and mucous membrane irritation syndromes. Current usage tends to be less restrictive with regard to the type of building and delineation of complaints. (From Segen, Dictionary of Modern Medicine, 1992)

LABEL: silicosis
hasExactSynonym: pneumoconiosis due to silica|silicosis
IAO_0000115: Silicosis is a respiratory disease caused by breathing in (inhaling) silica dust. There are three types of silicosis: Simple chronic silicosis, the most common type of silicosis, results from long-term exposure (usually more than 20years) to low amounts of silica dust. Simple chronic silicosismay causepeople to have difficulty breathing. Accelerated silicosis occurs after 5 to 15 yearsof exposure of higher levels of silica.Swelling of the lungsand other symptoms occur faster in this type of silicosis than in the simple chronic form. Acute silicosis results from short-term exposure (weeks or months) of large amounts of silica.The lungs become very inflamed and can fill with fluid, causing severe shortness of breath and low blood oxygen levels. A cough, weight loss, and fatigue may also be present. Acute silicosis progresses rapidly and can be fatal within months. People who work in jobs where they are exposed to silica dust (mining, quarrying, construction, sand blasting, stone cutting) are at risk of developing this condition.

LABEL: sinusitis
IAO_0000115: An acute or chronic inflammatory process affecting the mucous membranes of any sinus cavity.

LABEL: skeletal tuberculosis
IAO_0000115: Tuberculosis of the bones or joints.

LABEL: sparganosis
hasExactSynonym: Spirometra caused disease or disorder|Spirometra disease or disorder|Spirometra infectious disease|infection by sparganum|sparganosis [larval diphyllobothriasis]
IAO_0000115: A condition resulting from infection with the second stage larvae of the parasite Spirometra.

LABEL: sphenoid sinusitis
hasExactSynonym: sinusitis of sphenoid bone|sphenoid bone sinusitis|sphenoidal sinusitis
IAO_0000115: An acute or chronic inflammatory process affecting the mucous membrane of the sphenoid sinus.

LABEL: spinal stenosis
IAO_0000115: Narrowing of the spinal canal.

LABEL: spleen cancer
hasExactSynonym: cancer of spleen|cancer of the spleen|malignant neoplasm of spleen|malignant neoplasm of the spleen|malignant spleen neoplasm|malignant splenic neoplasm|malignant splenic tumor|malignant splenic tumour|malignant tumor of spleen|malignant tumor of the spleen|malignant tumour of the spleen|spleen cancer|splenic cancer
IAO_0000115: A malignant neoplasm involving the spleen

LABEL: splenic tuberculosis
IAO_0000115: Infection of the spleen with species of mycobacterium.

LABEL: sporotrichosis
IAO_0000115: The commonest and least serious of the deep mycoses, characterized by nodular lesions of the cutaneous and subcutaneous tissues. It is caused by inhalation of contaminated dust or by infection of a wound.

LABEL: st. Louis encephalitis
hasExactSynonym: Neuroinvasive St. Louis encephalitis virus infection|Saint Louis encephalitis|St. Louis encephalitis virus caused infectious encephalitis|St. Louis encephalitis virus infectious encephalitis
IAO_0000115: A viral encephalitis caused by the St. Louis encephalitis virus (encephalitis virus, st. louis), a flavivirus. It is transmitted to humans and other vertebrates primarily by mosquitoes of the genus culex. The primary animal vectors are wild birds and the disorder is endemic to the midwestern and southeastern United States. Infections may be limited to an influenza-like illness or present as an aseptic meningitis or encephalitis. Clinical manifestations of the encephalitic presentation may include seizures, lethargy, myoclonus, focal neurologic signs, coma, and death. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p750)

LABEL: staphylococcal pneumonia
hasExactSynonym: Staphylococcus caused pneumonia|Staphylococcus pneumonia
IAO_0000115: Pneumonia caused by infections with bacteria of the genus staphylococcus, usually with staphylococcus aureus.

LABEL: staphyloenterotoxemia
hasExactSynonym: staphylococcal food poisoning|staphylococcal toxemia due to food
IAO_0000115: Food poisoning that is caused by Staphylococcal infection.

LABEL: streptococcal pneumonia
hasExactSynonym: Streptococcus pneumoniae caused pneumonia|Streptococcus pneumoniae pneumonia|pneumococcal pneumonia|pneumonia due to streptococcus|streptococcal pneumonia
IAO_0000115: A febrile disease caused by streptococcus pneumoniae.

LABEL: Strongylida infectious disease
IAO_0000115: Infections with nematodes of the order strongylida.

LABEL: strongyloidiasis
hasExactSynonym: Anguilluliasis|Anguillulosis
IAO_0000115: An infection that is caused by nematodes of the genus Strongyloides, most commonly Strongyloides stercoralis, which is a soil-transmitted helminth, and which is characterized by a variety of gastrointestinal, dermatologic, and, occasionally, pulmonary manifestations. The worm's autoinfective life cycle can lead to hyper-infection and life-threatening dissemination in immunocompromised hosts decades after initial infection.

LABEL: suppurative otitis media
IAO_0000115: Inflammation of the middle ear with purulent discharge.

LABEL: syphilis
hasExactSynonym: Treponema pallidum caused disease or disorder|Treponema pallidum disease or disorder|Treponema pallidum infectious disease
IAO_0000115: A contagious bacterial infection caused by the spirochete Treponema pallidum. It is a sexually transmitted disorder, although it can also be transmitted from the mother to the fetus in utero. Typically, it is initially manifested with a single sore which heals without treatment. If the infection is left untreated, the initial stage is followed by skin rash and mucous membrane lesions. A late stage follows, which is characterized by damage of the internal organs, including the nervous system.

LABEL: tabes dorsalis
IAO_0000115: A form of neurosyphilis characterized by slowly progressive degeneration of the spinal cord. Signs and symptoms include pain, ataxia, loss of coordination, personality changes, blindness, urinary incontinence, dementia, and degeneration of the joints.

LABEL: theileriasis
IAO_0000115: Infection of cattle, sheep, or goats with protozoa of the genus theileria. This infection results in an acute or chronic febrile condition.

LABEL: thoracic outlet syndrome
hasExactSynonym: TOS|thoracic outlet compression syndrome
IAO_0000115: A syndrome resulting from the compression of the blood vessels or nerves in the space between the clavicle and first rib (thoracic outlet). It is caused by car accident injuries or repetitive job or sport-related injuries. Signs and symptoms include pain in the shoulders and neck, numbness in the fingers, and weakening grip.

LABEL: tick infestation
hasExactSynonym: Ixodoidea caused disease or disorder|Ixodoidea disease or disorder|Ixodoidea infectious disease
IAO_0000115: Infestations with soft-bodied (Argasidae) or hard-bodied (Ixodidae) ticks.

LABEL: tick paralysis
IAO_0000115: Paralysis caused by a neurotropic toxin secreted by the salivary glands of ticks.

LABEL: tinea infection
hasExactSynonym: Tinea|Tinea caused disease or disorder|Tinea disease or disorder|Tinea infection|Tinea infectious disease
IAO_0000115: A skin infection caused by a fungus.

LABEL: tinea favosa
hasExactSynonym: favus
IAO_0000115: A severe, chronic fungal skin infection, usually of the scalp, characterized by the development of thick, yellow cup-shaped crusts and scarring over hair follicles.

LABEL: tinea pedis
hasExactSynonym: athlete's foot|dermatophytosis of foot|dermatophytosis of pes|pes dermatophytosis
IAO_0000115: Dermatological pruritic lesion in the feet, caused by Trichophyton rubrum, T. mentagrophytes, or Epidermophyton floccosum.

LABEL: Togaviridae infectious disease
hasExactSynonym: Togaviridae caused disease or disorder|Togaviridae disease or disorder
IAO_0000115: Virus diseases caused by the togaviridae.

LABEL: torovirus infectious disease
hasExactSynonym: Torovirus caused disease or disorder|Torovirus disease or disorder|Torovirus infectious disease
IAO_0000115: Infections with viruses of the genus torovirus, family coronaviridae.

LABEL: toxascariasis
hasExactSynonym: Toxascaris caused disease or disorder|Toxascaris disease or disorder|Toxascaris infectious disease
IAO_0000115: Infections with nematodes of the genus toxascaris.

LABEL: toxocariasis
hasExactSynonym: Toxocara caused disease or disorder|Toxocara disease or disorder|Toxocara infection|Toxocara infectious disease|visceral larva migrans
IAO_0000115: A parasitic infection caused by worms found in domestic animals. In humans nematode larvae enter the portal system from the small intestine and disseminate in visceral organs causing inflammatory reactions. Signs and symptoms include eosinophilia, hepatomegaly, splenomegaly, and lung infections.

LABEL: toxoplasmosis
hasExactSynonym: Toxoplasma gondii caused disease or disorder|Toxoplasma gondii disease or disorder|Toxoplasma gondii infectious disease
IAO_0000115: A parasitic disease contracted by the ingestion or fetal transmission of toxoplasma gondii.

LABEL: tracheitis
hasExactSynonym: acute tracheitis|inflammation of tracheal mucosa|tracheal Inflammation|tracheal mucosa inflammation
IAO_0000115: A tracheal disease which involves bacterial infection of the trachea often caused by Staphylococcus aureus and streptococci that follows a recent viral upper respiratory infection. The symptoms include barking croup cough, loud squeaking noise while breathing, scratchy feeling in the throat, high fever, and production of large amounts of pus-filled secretions.

LABEL: trench fever
hasExactSynonym: Bartonella quintana caused disease or disorder|Bartonella quintana disease or disorder|Bartonella quintana infectious disease|His-Werner disease|Wolhynian fever|bartonellosis due to Bartonella quintana infection|quintan fever|shin bone fever|trench fever
IAO_0000115: An intermittent fever characterized by intervals of chills, fever, and splenomegaly each of which may last as long as 40 hours. It is caused by bartonella quintana and transmitted by the human louse.

LABEL: Trichomonas vaginitis urogenital infection
hasExactSynonym: Trichomonas vaginalis caused disease of genitourinary system|Trichomonas vaginalis disease of genitourinary system|Trichomonas vaginitis|urogenital infection by Trichomonas vaginalis
IAO_0000115: A sexually transmitted parasitic infection caused by Trichomonas vaginalis. Symptoms include vaginal discharge, vaginal odor, vaginal itching, and discomfort during intercourse.

LABEL: trichostrongyloidiasis
hasExactSynonym: Trichostrongyloidea caused disease or disorder|Trichostrongyloidea disease or disorder|Trichostrongyloidea infectious disease
IAO_0000115: Infection by roundworms of the superfamily trichostrongyloidea, including the genera trichostrongylus; ostertagia; Cooperia, haemonchus; Nematodirus, Hyostrongylus, and dictyocaulus.

LABEL: trichostrongylosis
hasExactSynonym: Trichostrongyliasis|Trichostrongylus caused disease or disorder|Trichostrongylus disease or disorder|Trichostrongylus infectious disease
IAO_0000115: Infestation with nematode worms of the genus trichostrongylus. Humans become infected by swallowing larvae, usually with contaminated food or drink, although the larvae may penetrate human skin.

LABEL: trichuriasis
hasExactSynonym: Trichuris trichiura caused disease or disorder|Trichuris trichiura disease or disorder|Trichuris trichiura infectious disease|trichuriasis infection|whipworm disease
IAO_0000115: An infection that is caused by the nematode Trichuris trichiura, a soil-transmitted helminth, which is transmitted via food and/or water contaminated with the eggs of the worm. Symptoms are usually mild and include abdominal pain, diarrhea, fatigue, and possibly anemia secondary to blood loss in diarrhea.

LABEL: tricuspid valve stenosis
hasExactSynonym: tricuspid stenosis
IAO_0000115: Narrowing or stricture of the tricuspid orifice of the heart.

LABEL: trombiculiasis
hasExactSynonym: Trombiculidae caused disease or disorder|Trombiculidae disease or disorder|Trombiculidae infectious disease
IAO_0000115: Infestation with mites of the genus Trombiculidae, whose larvae carry the rickettsial agent of scrub typhus.

LABEL: tuberculous empyema
hasExactSynonym: tuberculous empyema (& pleural)
IAO_0000115: An empyema resulting from infection by Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

LABEL: tuberculous peritonitis
hasExactSynonym: Mycobacterium tuberculosis caused peritonitis|Mycobacterium tuberculosis peritonitis
IAO_0000115: A form of peritonitis seen in patients with tuberculosis, characterized by lesion either as a miliary form or as a pelvic mass on the peritoneal surfaces. Most patients have ascites, abdominal swelling, abdominal pain, and other systemic symptoms such as fever; weight loss; and anemia.

LABEL: urinary schistosomiasis
hasExactSynonym: Schistosoma haematobium (& vesical schistosomiasis)|Schistosoma hematobium infection|schistosomiasis due to Schistosoma haematobium|urinary bladder schistosomiasis
IAO_0000115: A bladder infection that occurs as a manifetation of a systemic infection with one or more species of the parasitic worms of the Schistosoma type; this can progress to bladder cancer in time.

LABEL: urogenital tuberculosis
hasExactSynonym: genitourinary system tuberculosis
IAO_0000115: A general term for mycobacterium infections of any part of the urogenital system in either the male or the female.

LABEL: uterine corpus cancer
hasExactSynonym: body of uterus cancer|cancer of body of uterus|cancer of the corpus uteri|corpus uteri cancer|malignant body of uterus neoplasm|malignant neoplasm of body of uterus|uterine (including endometrial) cancer|uterine corpus cancer
IAO_0000115: A malignant neoplasm involving the body of uterus.

LABEL: vasomotor rhinitis
IAO_0000115: Inflammation in the nasal cavity mucosa that results from the abnormal regulation of the blood flow in the nose. It may be caused by temperature fluctuations, air pollution, strong odors, and tobacco smoke. It results in chronic nasal congestion, sneezing, and running nose.

LABEL: Venezuelan equine encephalitis
hasExactSynonym: Venezuelan equine encephalitis virus caused disease or disorder|Venezuelan equine encephalitis virus disease or disorder|Venezuelan equine encephalitis virus infectious disease
IAO_0000115: A condition caused by infection by the Venezuelan equine encephalitis virus, which is characterized by headache, fever, myalgia, nausea, and vomiting.

LABEL: verrucous carcinoma
hasExactSynonym: verrucous carcinoma|verrucous carcinoma NOS (morphologic abnormality)|verrucous epidermoid carcinoma|verrucous epidermoid cell carcinoma|verrucous squamous carcinoma|verrucous squamous cell carcinoma
IAO_0000115: A well differentiated squamous cell carcinoma characterized by a papillary growth pattern, acanthosis, mild cytologic atypia, and pushing tumor margins. The most commonly affected anatomic sites are the oral cavity, nasal cavity, larynx, esophagus, anus, vagina, vulva, and the plantar region of the foot.

LABEL: vesicoureteral reflux
hasExactSynonym: vesicoureteral reflux|vesicoureteral reflux (disease)
IAO_0000115: Abnormal flow of urine from the urinary bladder back into the ureters.

LABEL: vestibular neuronitis
IAO_0000115: Idiopathic inflammation of the vestibular nerve, characterized clinically by the acute or subacute onset of vertigo; nausea; and imbalance. The cochlear nerve is typically spared and hearing loss and tinnitus do not usually occur. Symptoms usually resolve over a period of days to weeks. (Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p304)

LABEL: viral encephalitis
hasExactSynonym: Viruses caused encephalitis|Viruses encephalitis|viral encephalitis
IAO_0000115: Encephalitis resulting from viral infection.

LABEL: salmonid viral hemorrhagic septicemia
IAO_0000115: A systemic infection of various salmonid and a few nonsalmonid fishes caused by Viral hemorrhagic septicemia virus (see novirhabdovirus),

LABEL: viral hepatitis
hasExactSynonym: Hepatitis viral|Viruses caused hepatitis|Viruses hepatitis|viral Hepatitis|viral human hepatitis
IAO_0000115: An acute or chronic inflammation of the liver parenchyma caused by viruses. Representative examples include hepatitis A, B, and C, cytomegalovirus hepatitis, and herpes simplex hepatitis.

LABEL: viral pneumonia
hasExactSynonym: Viruses caused pneumonia|Viruses pneumonia
IAO_0000115: Inflammation of the lung parenchyma that is caused by a viral infection.

LABEL: vulvovaginal candidiasis
hasExactSynonym: candidal vulvovaginitis|candidal: [vulvovaginitis NOS] or [cervix]|candidal: cervix|candidiasis of vulva and vagina|monilial vulvovaginitis|vaginal candidiasis|vulvovaginal candidiasis
IAO_0000115: Infection of the vulva and vagina with a fungus of the genus CANDIDA. It is a disease associated with HIV infection.

LABEL: Waterhouse-Friderichsen syndrome
hasExactSynonym: WFS|meningococcal hemorrhagic adrenalitis
IAO_0000115: A serious disorder characterized by massive adrenal gland hemorrhage secondary to a bacterial infection, most often Neisseria meningitidis infection. It is manifested with decreased blood pressure, shock, disseminated intravascular coagulation, and adrenocortical insufficiency.

LABEL: Wissler syndrome
hasExactSynonym: Wissler syndrome|Wissler's syndrome|Wissler-Fanconi syndrome (finding)
IAO_0000115: A rheumatic syndrome of possibly allergic origin, usually affecting children and adolescents, and characterized by high fever, exanthema, arthralgia, leukocytosis, and increased sedimentation rate.

LABEL: yaws
hasExactSynonym: Bouba|Treponema pallidum subsp. pertenue caused disease or disorder|Treponema pallidum subsp. pertenue disease or disorder|Treponema pallidum subsp. pertenue infectious disease|frambesia|frambesia tropica
IAO_0000115: An endemic, infectious, nonvenereal disease in humans that presents mainly in children younger than 15 years. The disease occurs primarily in warm, humid, tropical areas of Africa, Asia, South America, and Oceania, among poor rural populations where conditions of overcrowding and poor sanitation prevail. Infection with Treponema pertenue, a subspecies of Treponema pallidum, causes the disease.

LABEL: Prinzmetal angina
hasExactSynonym: angina inversa|variant angina
IAO_0000115: A syndrome typically consisting of angina (cardiac chest pain) at rest that occurs in cycles. It is caused by vasospasm, a narrowing of the coronary arteries caused by contraction of the smooth muscle tissue in the vessel walls rather than directly by atherosclerosis (buildup of fatty plaque and hardening of the arteries). For a portion of patients Prinzmetal's angina may be a manifestation of vasospastic disorder and is associated with migraine, Raynaud's phenomenon or aspirin-induced asthma.

LABEL: acidosis disorder
hasExactSynonym: acidosis
IAO_0000115: An abnormally high acidity of the blood and other body tissues. Acidosis can be either respiratory or metabolic.

LABEL: autosomal recessive disease
hasExactSynonym: autosomal recessive disease or disorder|autosomal recessive hereditary disease|autosomal recessive hereditary disorder|autosomal recessive inherited disease|autosomal recessive inherited disorder|disease or disorder, autosomal recessive|disease, autosomal recessive
IAO_0000115: Autosomal recessive form of disease.

LABEL: urinary bladder disorder
hasExactSynonym: bladder disease|bladder disorder|disease of urinary bladder|disease or disorder of urinary bladder|disorder of urinary bladder|urinary bladder disease|urinary bladder disease or disorder|urinary bladder disorder
IAO_0000115: A disease involving the urinary bladder.

LABEL: breast synovial sarcoma
hasExactSynonym: breast synovial sarcoma (disease)
IAO_0000115: A synovial sarcoma (disease) that involves the breast.

LABEL: cecum adenocarcinoma
hasExactSynonym: adenocarcinoma of cecum|adenocarcinoma of the cecum|caecum adenocarcinoma|cecal adenocarcinoma|cecum adenocarcinoma
IAO_0000115: A carcinoma that arises from glandular epithelial cells of the caecum

LABEL: cecum carcinoma
hasExactSynonym: caecum carcinoma|carcinoma of caecum|carcinoma of cecum|carcinoma of the cecum|cecum carcinoma
IAO_0000115: A carcinoma that arises from epithelial cells of the caecum

LABEL: chronic cystitis
hasExactSynonym: cystitis, chronic
IAO_0000115: Recurrent infections of the urinary bladder.

LABEL: chronic rhinosinusitis
hasExactSynonym: chronic sinusitis|sinusitis, chronic
IAO_0000115: Chronic form of sinusitis.

LABEL: cystitis
hasExactSynonym: bladder infection|inflammation of urinary bladder|urinary bladder inflammation
IAO_0000115: Inflammation of the urinary bladder.

LABEL: diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma
hasExactSynonym: DIPG
IAO_0000115: A neuroglial tumor that arises from the middle portion of the brain stem. It usually affects children and has a poor prognosis.

LABEL: gastric adenosquamous carcinoma
hasExactSynonym: adenosquamous carcinoma of stomach|adenosquamous carcinoma of the stomach|gastric (stomach) adenosquamous cancer|gastric adenosquamous carcinoma|stomach adenosquamous carcinoma
IAO_0000115: A carcinoma that arises from the stomach and is characterized by the presence of malignant cells with glandular and squamous differentiation.

LABEL: gastric tubular adenocarcinoma
hasExactSynonym: gastric tubular adenocarcinoma|stomach tubular adenocarcinoma|tubular adenocarcinoma of stomach|tubular adenocarcinoma of the stomach
IAO_0000115: A variant of gastric adenocarcinoma characterized by prominent dilated or slit-like tubules.

LABEL: granulosa cell tumor
hasExactSynonym: granulosa cell neoplasm|granulosa cell neoplasm (disease)|granulosa cell tumor|granulosa cell tumor, adult type (morphologic abnormality)|granulosa cell tumor, sarcomatoid|neoplasm of granulosa cell|tumor of granulosa cell|tumour of granulosa cell
IAO_0000115: A slow-growing, malignant tumor, characterize by the presence of granulosa-like cells and Call-Exner bodies, that is almost always found in the ovary. In rare cases, it has also been found in the testicle. There are two types of granulosa cell tumor that can be distinguished under the microscope: the adult and the juvenile. The testicular juvenile granulosa cell tumors are perhaps the most common congenital testicular neoplasms.

LABEL: hydrolethalus syndrome
IAO_0000115: Hydrolethalus (HLS) is a severe fetal malformation syndrome characterized by craniofacial dysmorphic features, central nervous system, cardiac, respiratory tract and limb abnormalities.

LABEL: indeterminate colitis
hasExactSynonym: colitis of indeterminate type
IAO_0000115: It describes patients in whom a diagnosis of ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease cannot be made based on standard clinical testing, including colonoscopy, imaging, laboratory tests, and biopsy.

LABEL: infectious colitis
hasExactSynonym: infectious colitis
IAO_0000115: A viral or bacterial infectious process affecting the large intestine.

LABEL: lactic acidosis
IAO_0000115: Metabolic acidosis characterized by the accumulation of lactate in the body. It is caused by tissue hypoxia.

LABEL: lung carcinoid tumor
hasExactSynonym: carcinoid tumor (disease) of lung|carcinoid tumor of lung|carcinoid tumor of the lung|carcinoid tumour (disease) of lung|carcinoid tumour of lung|carcinoid tumour of the lung|lung carcinoid tumor|lung carcinoid tumor (disease)|lung carcinoid tumour (disease)|pulmonary carcinoid tumor|pulmonary carcinoid tumour
IAO_0000115: A neuroendocrine neoplasm that arises from the lung. It is characterized by the presence of uniform polygonal cells with small or moderate amount of cytoplasm and inconspicuous nucleoli. The cells are usually arranged in organoid and trabecular patterns. It is classified as typical or atypical carcinoid tumor based on the number of mitotic figures and the absence or presence of necrosis. Atypical carcinoid tumors have a worse prognosis.

LABEL: meningeal tuberculosis
hasExactSynonym: Meningitis, Tuberculous|TB meningitis|TBM|tubercular meningitis|tuberculous meningitis
IAO_0000115: A bacterial infection of the membranes covering the brain and the spinal cord caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

LABEL: metaplastic breast carcinoma
hasExactSynonym: metaplastic breast carcinoma|metaplastic carcinoma of breast|metaplastic carcinoma of the breast
IAO_0000115: A group of invasive breast carcinomas characterized by the presence of an adenocarcinomatous component which is admixed with a dominant component that is composed of squamous cells, spindle cells, or mesenchymal cells.

LABEL: nephrosclerosis

LABEL: ovarian clear cell adenocarcinoma
hasExactSynonym: clear cell adenocarcinoma of ovary|ovarian clear cell adenocarcinoma|ovary clear cell adenocarcinoma
IAO_0000115: A malignant glandular epithelial neoplasm characterized by the presence of clear and hobnail cells. It is highly associated with ovarian endometriosis, pelvic endometriosis and paraendocrine hypercalcemia.

LABEL: ovarian serous cystadenocarcinoma
hasExactSynonym: ovarian serous cystadenocarcinoma
IAO_0000115: A malignant serous cystic epithelial neoplasm arising from the ovary. It is characterized by the presence of glandular, papillary, or solid structures. Psammoma bodies may be present. In well differentiated cases the malignant epithelial cells resemble the cells of fallopian tube epithelium. In poorly differentiated cases the malignant epithelial cells show anaplastic features.

LABEL: pancreatic adenocarcinoma
hasExactSynonym: adenocarcinoma - pancreas|adenocarcinoma of pancreas|adenocarcinoma of the pancreas|pancreas adenocarcinoma|pancreatic adenocarcinoma
IAO_0000115: A carcinoma that arises from glandular epithelial cells of the pancreas

LABEL: papillary lung adenocarcinoma
hasExactSynonym: lung papillary adenocarcinoma|lung papillary-adenocarcinoma|papillary adenocarcinoma of lung|papillary adenocarcinoma of the lung|papillary lung adenocarcinoma
IAO_0000115: A morphologic variant of lung adenocarcinoma characterized by the presence of papillary structures.

LABEL: pleomorphic breast carcinoma
hasExactSynonym: anaplastic breast carcinoma
IAO_0000115: A rare, aggressive, high grade invasive ductal carcinoma, not otherwise specified. It is characterized by the presence of pleomorphic and bizarre malignant cells that constitute more than 50 percent of the malignant cellular infiltrate.

LABEL: pulmonary tuberculosis
hasExactSynonym: lung TB|lung tuberculosis|pulmonary TB

IAO_0000115: A carcinoma composed of malignant glandular cells and malignant squamous cells.

IAO_0000115: A rare, cytologically malignant ameloblastoma that may metastasize.

LABEL: angiolipoma
hasExactSynonym: angiolipoma, benign
IAO_0000115: A lipoma with prominent vascularity. The vascular tissue is more abundant at the periphery of the tumor and contains fibrin thrombi. It occurs more frequently in younger individuals as a painful subcutaneous nodule, often on the arms.

LABEL: angiomyxoma

Morphologically, it is characterized by a proliferation of neoplastic glandular cells and it is associated with dysplasia. According to the growth pattern, it may be classified as tubular, villous, or tubulovillous. The dysplasia is classified as mild, moderate, or severe.

LABEL: appendix hyperplastic polyp

IAO_0000115: A primitive neuroectodermal tumor (small round blue cell tumor) of the thorax which can involve the periosteum, thoracic wall and/or pleura though it spares the lung parenchyma.

IAO_0000115: An endometrial hyperplasia characterized by cytologic and architectural changes which may lead to endometrial carcinoma. LABEL: basaloid carcinoma

IAO_0000115: A malignant epithelial neoplasm characterized by the presence of neoplastic cells with hyperchromatic nuclei, small amount of cytoplasm, and peripheral nuclear palisading.

LABEL: benign carotid body paraganglioma

The reactive C-cell hyperplasia is also known as physiological or secondary C-cell hyperplasia and it is associated with conditions that cause hypercalcemia (e.g., hyperparathyroidism).

IAO_0000115: A benign well-circumscribed paucicellular lesion arising from the soft tissues. It is characterized by the presence of fibroblasts, lymphoplasmacytic infiltrates, collagenous stroma formation, psammoma bodies, and dystrophic calcifications.

IAO_0000115: A rare malignant tumor that arises from the liver and occurs in children. It is characterized by the presence of nested epithelioid and spindle cells. Desmoplasia, calcifications, and bone formation may also be present.

LABEL: cerebellar liponeurocytoma
hasExactSynonym: cerebellar liponeurocytoma|cerebellar liponeurocytoma (WHO grade II)|lipomatous medulloblastoma
IAO_0000115: A rare, WHO grade II cerebellar neoplasm which shows consistent neuronal, variable astrocytic and focal lipomatous differentiation. It occurs in adults, has a low proliferative potential and usually has a favorable prognosis. (Adapted from WHO)
