IAO_0000115: A condition that results from excessive fluoride ingestion during tooth development, resulting in tooth discoloration ranging from white streaks to brown stains and cracks or pits in the tooth enamel.

LABEL: denture stomatitis
IAO_0000115: Inflammation of the mouth due to denture irritation.

LABEL: diaphragmatic eventration
hasExactSynonym: diaphragmatic eventration|diaphragmatic eventration (disease)
IAO_0000115: A congenital or acquired abnormality characterized by elevation of the hemidiaphragm.

LABEL: diastolic heart failure
IAO_0000115: Heart failure caused by abnormal myocardial relaxation during diastole leading to defective cardiac filling.

LABEL: discrete subaortic stenosis
IAO_0000115: A type of constriction that is caused by the presence of a fibrous ring (discrete type) below the aortic valve, anywhere between the aortic valve and the mitral valve. It is characterized by restricted outflow from the left ventricle into the aorta.

LABEL: drug psychosis
hasExactSynonym: drug-induced psychotic disorder
IAO_0000115: Psychotic organic mental disorders resulting from the toxic effect of drugs and chemicals or other harmful substance.

LABEL: drug-induced akathisia
IAO_0000115: An uncomfortable feeling of inner restlessness and inability to stay still. It can be a side effect of psychotropic medications.

LABEL: drug-induced dyskinesia
IAO_0000115: Abnormal movements, including hyperkinesis; hypokinesia; tremor; and dystonia, associated with the use of certain medications or drugs. Muscles of the face, trunk, neck, and extremities are most commonly affected. Tardive dyskinesia refers to abnormal hyperkinetic movements of the muscles of the face, tongue, and neck associated with the use of neuroleptic agents (see antipsychotic agents). (Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p1199)

LABEL: dry eye syndrome
hasExactSynonym: dry eye|dry eye syndrome|dry eye(s)|eye(s), dry|keratoconjunctivitis sicca|sicca, keratoconjunctivitis
IAO_0000115: A syndrome characterized by dryness of the cornea and conjunctiva. It is usually caused by a deficiency in tear production. Symptoms include a feeling of burning eyes and a possible foreign body presence in the eye.

LABEL: benign duodenal neoplasm
hasExactSynonym: benign duodenal neoplasm|benign duodenal tumor|benign duodenal tumour|benign neoplasm of duodenum|benign neoplasm of the duodenum|benign tumor of duodenum|benign tumor of the duodenum|benign tumour of duodenum|benign tumour of the duodenum|duodenum benign neoplasm
IAO_0000115: A non-metastasizing neoplasm arising from the wall of the duodenum.

LABEL: duodenogastric reflux
hasExactSynonym: duodenogastric reflux (finding)
IAO_0000115: Retrograde flow of duodenal contents (bile acids; pancreatic juice) into the stomach.

LABEL: dysplasia of cervix
IAO_0000115: Abnormal development of immature squamous epithelial cells of the uterine cervix, a term used to describe premalignant cytological changes in the cervical epithelium. These atypical cells do not penetrate the epithelial basement membrane.

LABEL: dystocia
IAO_0000115: Slow or difficult obstetric labor or childbirth.

LABEL: eccrine acrospiroma
hasExactSynonym: eccrine acrospiroma|eccrine poroma|poroma|poroma (acrospiroma)
IAO_0000115: A rare cutaneous tumor of eccrine sweat gland origin. It is most commonly found on the extremities and is usually benign. There is no indication that heredity or external agents cause these tumors.

LABEL: Ehrlich tumor carcinoma
IAO_0000115: A transplantable, poorly differentiated malignant tumor which appeared originally as a spontaneous breast carcinoma in a mouse. It grows in both solid and ascitic forms.

LABEL: empty sella syndrome
hasExactSynonym: empty sella|empty sella syndrome
IAO_0000115: Empty sella syndrome (ESS) is a condition that involves the sella turcica, a bony structure at the base of the brain that protects the pituitary gland. There is a primary and secondary form of the condition. The primary form occurs when a structural defect above the pituitary gland increases pressure in the sella turcica and causes the gland to flatten. The secondary form occurs when the pituitary gland is damaged due to injury, a tumor, surgery or radiation therapy. Some people with ESS have no symptoms. People with secondary ESS may have symptoms of decreased pituitary function such as absence of menstruation, infertility, fatigue, and intolerance to stress and infection. In children, ESS may be associated with early onset of puberty, growth hormone deficiency, pituitary tumors, or pituitary gland dysfunction. Treatment focuses on the symptoms present in each person.

LABEL: encephalomalacia
IAO_0000115: Localized atrophy of the brain parenchyma due to aging, hemorrhage, infarct, or inflammation.

LABEL: endemic goiter
hasExactSynonym: iodine-deficiency-related endemic goiter|simple goiter
IAO_0000115: Thyroid gland enlargement caused by inadequate dietary iodine intake. It occurs in areas in which the soil lacks iodine compounds or there is low seafood consumption.

LABEL: endocrine tuberculosis
IAO_0000115: Infection of the endocrine glands with species of mycobacterium, most often mycobacterium tuberculosis.

LABEL: endolymphatic hydrops
IAO_0000115: An accumulation of endolymph in the inner ear (labyrinth) leading to buildup of pressure and distortion of intralabyrinthine structures, such as cochlea and semicircular canals. It is characterized by sensorineural hearing loss; tinnitus; and sometimes vertigo.

LABEL: endometrioid stromal sarcoma
hasExactSynonym: ESS|endometrial stromal sarcoma|endometrial stromal sarcomas|endometrioid stromal sarcoma|ess|sarcomas, endometrial stromal|stromal sarcoma of the corpus uteri|stromal sarcoma, endometrial|stromal sarcoma, endometrial, malignant|stromal sarcomas, endometrial
IAO_0000115: A malignant mesenchymal neoplasm that affects the uterine corpus, and rarely, the ovaries, cervix, and vagina. In the uterine corpus it is classified as low grade or high grade endometrial stromal sarcoma. In the remainder of the anatomic sites it is classified as low grade endometrioid stromal sarcoma.

LABEL: endomyocardial fibrosis
hasExactSynonym: African endomyocardial fibrosis
IAO_0000115: A disease characterized by fibrotic thickening of the endocardium, particularly the right and/or left inflow tracts. The disease often involves the atrioventricular valves, leading to valvular regurgitaion. It most commonly occurs in children living within 15 degrees of the equator.

LABEL: enterotoxemia
IAO_0000115: Disease caused by the liberation of exotoxins of clostridium perfringens in the intestines of sheep, goats, cattle, foals, and piglets. Type B enterotoxemia in lambs is lamb dysentery; type C enterotoxemia in mature sheep produces 'struck', and in calves, lambs and piglets it produces hemorrhagic enterotoxemia; type D enterotoxemia in sheep and goats is pulpy-kidney disease or overeating disease.

LABEL: obsolete epilepsia partialis continua
IAO_0000115: OBSOLETE. A variant of epilepsy characterized by continuous focal jerking of a body part over a period of hours, days, or even years without spreading to other body regions. Contractions may be aggravated by movement and are reduced, but not abolished during sleep. electroencephalography demonstrates epileptiform (spike and wave) discharges over the hemisphere opposite to the affected limb in most instances. The repetitive movements may originate from the cerebral cortex or from subcortical structures (e.g., brain stem; basal ganglia). This condition is associated with Russian Spring and Summer encephalitis; Rasmussen syndrome; multiple sclerosis; diabetes mellitus; brain neoplasms; and cerebrovascular disorders.

LABEL: Erysipelothrix infectious disease
hasExactSynonym: Erysipelothrix caused disease or disorder|Erysipelothrix disease or disorder
IAO_0000115: Infections with bacteria of the genus erysipelothrix.

LABEL: Erysipelothrix rhusiopathiae infectious disease
hasExactSynonym: Erysipelothrix rhusiopathiae caused disease or disorder|Erysipelothrix rhusiopathiae disease or disorder|erysipeloid
IAO_0000115: A disease caused by infection with Erysipelothrix rhusiopathiae.

LABEL: Escherichia coli meningitis
IAO_0000115: A form of gram-negative meningitis that tends to occur in neonates, in association with anatomical abnormalities (which feature communication between the meninges and cutaneous structures) or as opportunistic infections in association with immunologic deficiency syndromes. In premature neonates the clinical presentation may be limited to anorexia; vomiting; lethargy; or respiratory distress. Full-term infants may have as additional features fever; seizures; and bulging of the anterior fontanelle. (From Menkes, Textbook of Child Neurology, 5th ed, pp398-400)

LABEL: esophageal diverticulosis
IAO_0000115: A pathological condition characterized by the presence of a number of esophageal diverticula in the esophagus.

LABEL: euthyroid sick syndrome
hasExactSynonym: euthyroid sick syndrome|sick euthyroid syndrome|sick-euthyroid syndrome
IAO_0000115: Abnormal thyroid function tests, low triiodothyronine with elevated reverse triiodothyronine, in the setting of non-thyroidal illness.

LABEL: extrahepatic cholestasis
hasExactSynonym: cholestasis of extrahepatic bile duct|extrahepatic bile duct cholestasis|extrahepatic cholestasis (finding)
IAO_0000115: Impairment of the bile flow caused by an obstruction in the portion of the bile duct system located outside of the liver.

LABEL: female genital tuberculosis
IAO_0000115: Mycobacterium infections of the female reproductive tract (genitalia, female).

LABEL: femoral neuropathy
hasExactSynonym: femoral nerve peripheral nerve lesion|peripheral nerve lesion of femoral nerve
IAO_0000115: Neuropathy of the femoral nerve.

LABEL: fetal erythroblastosis
hasExactSynonym: HDFN|erythroblastosis fetalis|hemolytic disease of the fetus or newborn|hemolytic disease of the foetus or newborn|hemolytic disease of the newborn|isoimmune hemolytic disease of the newborn
IAO_0000115: A disorder of the fetus or newborn that occurs when fetal cells that are coated with IgG alloantibodies from the mother attack antigens inherited from the father. Severity can range from absence of symptoms to death.

LABEL: fibromuscular dysplasia
hasExactSynonym: FMDA|fibromuscular dysplasia|fibromuscular dysplasia of arteries
IAO_0000115: A disorder characterized by fibrous thickening of the arterial wall resulting in narrowing of the arterial lumen. It most often affects the renal artery and less often the carotid artery and abdominal arteries. It can cause hypertension and aneurysm formation.

LABEL: freemartinism
IAO_0000115: A condition occurring in the female offspring of dizygotic twins (twin, dizygotic) in a mixed-sex pregnancy, usually in cattle. Freemartinism can occur in other mammals. When placental fusion between the male and the female fetuses permits the exchange of fetal cells and fetal hormones, testicular hormones from the male fetus can androgenize the female fetus producing a sterile xx/xy chimeric 'female'(chimerism).

LABEL: frozen shoulder
hasExactSynonym: adhesive capsulitis|adhesive capsulitis of shoulder
IAO_0000115: A painful inflammatory process leads to a mechanical block in active and passive range of motion (ROM) of the shoulder. Adhesive capsulitis of the shoulder is characterized by functional loss of passive and active shoulder motion. This inflammatory process results in fibroblastic proliferation and extensive scar tissue formation. Fibroblastic proliferation, a late phase of the inflammatory process involved in tissue repair, leads to thickening, fibrosis, and adhesion of the capsule to itself and the humerus.

LABEL: fungal meningitis
hasExactSynonym: Fungi caused infectious meningitis|Fungi infectious meningitis
IAO_0000115: Meningitis caused by fungal agents which may occur as opportunistic infections or arise in immunocompetent hosts.

LABEL: Fusobacterium infectious disease
hasExactSynonym: Fusobacterium caused disease or disorder|Fusobacterium disease or disorder|infection due to Fusobacterium
IAO_0000115: Infections with bacteria of the genus fusobacterium.

LABEL: gait apraxia
hasExactSynonym: Gait apraxia (finding)
IAO_0000115: Impaired ambulation not attributed to sensory impairment or motor weakness. frontal lobe disorders; basal ganglia diseases (e.g., parkinsonian disorders); dementia, multi-infarct; alzheimer disease; and other conditions may be associated with gait apraxia.

LABEL: gastric antral vascular ectasia
hasExactSynonym: GAVE
IAO_0000115: Dilatation of the vessels in the antrum of the stomach. It is associated with portal hypertension, scleroderma, and chronic renal failure. It may cause gastric bleeding.

LABEL: gastroparesis
hasExactSynonym: gastroparalysis|gastroparesis|gastroparesis (disease)|gastroparesis syndrome
IAO_0000115: Paralysis of the muscles of the stomach wall resulting in delayed emptying of the gastric contents into the small intestine.

LABEL: giant cell reparative granuloma
hasExactSynonym: GCLSB|central giant cell (reparative) granuloma|central giant cell granuloma|giant cell lesion of small bones
IAO_0000115: A rare tumor-like lesion of the hands and feet characterized by the presence of hemorrhagic fibrous tissue, hemosiderin deposition, osteoclast-like giant cells which are irregularly distributed, and reactive bone formation. Pain and swelling are the most frequent symptoms. It may recur following curettage, but is usually cured after a second procedure.

LABEL: glossitis
hasExactSynonym: inflammation of tongue|tongue inflammation
IAO_0000115: Inflammation of the tongue.

LABEL: gonadal tissue neoplasm
IAO_0000115: Neoplasms composed of tissues of the ovary or the testis, not neoplasms located in the ovaries or testes. Gonadal tissues include germ cells, cells from the sex cord, and gonadal stromal cells.

LABEL: habitual spontaneous abortion
IAO_0000115: Three or more consecutive spontaneous abortions.

LABEL: hairy tongue
hasExactSynonym: hairy tongue
IAO_0000115: A benign condition affecting the dorsum of the tongue. It is characterized by defective desquamation resulting in elongation of the filiform papillae. The dorsum of the tongue has a furry appearance and is usually stained black.

LABEL: halo nevus
hasExactSynonym: halo nevi
IAO_0000115: A benign melanocytic nevus with a halo appearance.

LABEL: heart aneurysm
hasExactSynonym: cardiac aneurysm
IAO_0000115: A localized bulging or dilatation in the muscle wall of a heart (myocardium), usually in the left ventricle. Blood-filled aneurysms are dangerous because they may burst. Fibrous aneurysms interfere with the heart function through the loss of contractility. True aneurysm is bound by the vessel wall or cardiac wall. False aneurysms are hematoma caused by myocardial rupture.

LABEL: Helicobacter pylori infectious disease
hasExactSynonym: Helicobacter pylori caused disease or disorder|Helicobacter pylori disease or disorder
IAO_0000115: Infections with organisms of the genus HELICOBACTER, particularly, in humans, HELICOBACTER PYLORI. The clinical manifestations are focused in the stomach, usually the gastric mucosa and antrum, and the upper duodenum. This infection plays a major role in the pathogenesis of type B gastritis and peptic ulcer disease.

LABEL: hemometra
hasExactSynonym: hematometra
IAO_0000115: Blood-filled uterus.

LABEL: hemopneumothorax
IAO_0000115: Collection of air and blood in the pleural cavity.

LABEL: hemorrhagic disease of newborn
hasExactSynonym: hemorrhagic disease of newborn|vitamin K deficiency bleeding in newborn
IAO_0000115: A condition characterized as a coagulation disturbance in newborns due to vitamin K deficiency resulting in impaired production of coagulation factors II, VII, IX, and X, and proteins C and S by the liver.

LABEL: hepatic vein thrombosis
hasExactSynonym: hepatic vein thrombosis
IAO_0000115: A condition in which the hepatic venous outflow is obstructed anywhere from the small hepatic veins to the junction of the inferior vena cava and the right atrium. Usually the blockage is extrahepatic and caused by blood clots (thrombus) or fibrous webs. Parenchymal fibrosis is uncommon.

LABEL: hidrocystoma
hasExactSynonym: Hydrocystoma|apocrine/eccrine hidrocystoma|hidrocystoma|hidrocystoma (morphologic abnormality)
IAO_0000115: A benign cystic proliferation of the sweat glands with apocrine or eccrine differentiation. It usually presents as a dome-shaped, cystic papular or nodular lesion usually in the face and neck. It is a unilocular or mutlilocular lesion lined by an inner and an outer layer of epithelium. Complete excision is usually curative.

LABEL: hyperamylasemia
IAO_0000115: Abnormally high level of amylase in the blood.

LABEL: hypercementosis
hasExactSynonym: cementation hyperplasia
IAO_0000115: A regressive change of teeth characterized by excessive development of secondary cementum on the tooth surface. It may occur on any part of the root, but the apical two-thirds are most commonly affected. (Dorland, 27th ed)

LABEL: hyperemesis gravidarum
hasExactSynonym: hyperemesis gravidarum|hyperemesis gravidarum (disease)
IAO_0000115: Severe, intractable vomiting during pregnancy (usually the first trimester) accompanied by dehydration, weight loss, and electrolyte imbalances.

LABEL: hyperglobulinemic purpura
IAO_0000115: Purplish or brownish red discoloration of the skin associated with increase in circulating polyclonal globulins, usually gamma-globulins. This syndrome often occurs on the legs of women aged 20 to 40 years.

LABEL: hyperpituitarism
IAO_0000115: Disease of the glandular, anterior portion of the pituitary (pituitary gland, anterior) resulting in hypersecretion of adenohypophyseal hormones such as growth hormone; prolactin; thyrotropin; luteinizing hormone; follicle stimulating hormone ; and adrenocorticotropic hormone. Hyperpituitarism usually is caused by a functional adenoma.

LABEL: hypersensitivity vasculitis
hasExactSynonym: leukocytoclastic vasculitis
IAO_0000115: A small vessel vasculitis affecting the skin and/or internal organs. It is characterized by the presence of neutrophils and fibrinoid necrosis in small arteries and venules. It may be idiopathic or the result of drug treatment, infections, food intake, collagen vascular disorders, inflammatory bowel disease, or cancer.

LABEL: hypersplenism
hasExactSynonym: hypersplenia|hypersplenism|hypersplenism (disease)
IAO_0000115: Overactive functioning of the spleen, resulting in excessive destruction of blood cells.

LABEL: hypertensive encephalopathy
IAO_0000115: Encephalopathy resulting from hypertension.

LABEL: hypertensive retinopathy
IAO_0000115: Retinopathy due to hypertension.

LABEL: hypervitaminosis A
hasExactSynonym: hypervitaminosis type A
IAO_0000115: A symptom complex resulting from ingesting excessive amounts of vitamin A.

LABEL: hypothalamic neoplasm
hasExactSynonym: hypothalamic neoplasms|hypothalamic tumor|hypothalamic tumour|hypothalamus neoplasm|hypothalamus tumor|hypothalamus tumour|neoplasm of hypothalamus|neoplasm of the hypothalamus|tumor of hypothalamus|tumor of the hypothalamus|tumour of hypothalamus|tumour of the hypothalamus
IAO_0000115: A primary or metastatic neoplasm that affects the hypothalamus.

LABEL: ideomotor apraxia
hasExactSynonym: classic apraxia (finding) [ambiguous]|limb-kinetic apraxia (finding)|transcortical apraxia (finding)
IAO_0000115: A form of apraxia characterized by an acquired inability to carry out a complex motor activity despite the ability to mentally formulate the action. This condition has been attributed to a disruption of connections between the dominant parietal cortex and supplementary and premotor cortical regions in both hemispheres. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p57)

LABEL: ileal neoplasm
hasExactSynonym: ileal tumor|ileal tumour|ileum neoplasm|ileum neoplasm (disease)|ileum tumor|ileum tumour|neoplasm of ileum|neoplasm of the ileum|tumor of ileum|tumor of the ileum|tumour of ileum|tumour of the ileum
IAO_0000115: A benign or malignant neoplasm that affects the wall of the ileum. Representative examples include adenoma, carcinoma, and lymphoma.

LABEL: inappropriate ADH syndrome
hasExactSynonym: SIADH|ectopic ADH secretion|ectopic antidiuretic hormone secretion|inappropriate ADH secretion|inappropriate Arginine vasopressin secretion|inappropriate antidiuretic hormone secretion syndrome|syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone|syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone secretion|syndrome of inappropriate secretion of antidiuretic hormone|syndrome of inappropriate vasopressin secretion
IAO_0000115: A syndrome characterized by abnormal secretion of antidiuretic hormone in conjunction with neoplastic growth occurring anywhere in the body.

LABEL: inferior myocardial infarction
IAO_0000115: Myocardial infarction in which the inferior wall of the heart is involved. It is often caused by occlusion of the right coronary artery.

LABEL: inflammatory breast carcinoma
hasExactSynonym: inflammatory breast cancer|inflammatory breast carcinoma|inflammatory carcinoma of breast|inflammatory carcinoma of the breast|mastitis Carcinomatosa|mastitis carcinomatosa
IAO_0000115: An advanced, invasive breast adenocarcinoma characterized by the presence of distinct changes in the overlying skin. These changes include diffuse erythema, edema, peau d'orange (skin of an orange) appearance, tenderness, induration, warmth, enlargement, and in some cases a palpable mass. The skin changes are the consequence of lymphatic obstruction from the underlying invasive breast adenocarcinoma. Microscopically, the dermal lymphatics show prominent infiltration by malignant cells. The invasive breast adenocarcinoma is usually of ductal, NOS type. There is not significant inflammatory cell infiltrate present, despite the name of this carcinoma.

LABEL: intermediate coronary syndrome
hasExactSynonym: Preinfarction angina|angina at rest|anginal chest pain at rest|impending infarction|unstable angina|worsening angina
IAO_0000115: Angina pectoris (or equivalent type of ischemic discomfort) which has recently changed in frequency, duration, intensity, or occurs at rest.

LABEL: intermediate uveitis
hasExactSynonym: IU|intermediate uveitis|intermediate uveitis (disease)
IAO_0000115: Inflammation of the pars plana.

LABEL: intestinal perforation
hasExactSynonym: bowel perforation|perforation of intestine
IAO_0000115: A rupture in the wall of the small or large intestine due to traumatic or pathologic processes.

LABEL: intracranial arterial disease
IAO_0000115: Pathological conditions involving arteries in the skull, such as arteries supplying the cerebrum, the cerebellum, the brain stem, and associated structures. They include atherosclerotic, congenital, traumatic, infectious, inflammatory, and other pathological processes.

LABEL: intracranial embolism
IAO_0000115: Blocking of a blood vessel in the skull by an embolus which can be a blood clot (thrombus) or other undissolved material in the blood stream. Most emboli are of cardiac origin and are associated with heart diseases. Other non-cardiac sources of emboli are usually associated with vascular diseases.

LABEL: intracranial hypertension
IAO_0000115: A finding characterized by increased cerebrospinal fluid pressure within the skull.

LABEL: intracranial hypotension
IAO_0000115: Reduction of cerebrospinal fluid pressure characterized clinically by headache which is maximal in an upright posture and occasionally by an abducens nerve palsy (see abducens nerve diseases), neck stiffness, hearing loss (see deafness); nausea; and other symptoms. This condition may be spontaneous or secondary to spinal puncture; neurosurgical procedures; dehydration; uremia; trauma (see also craniocerebral trauma); and other processes. Chronic hypotension may be associated with subdural hematomas (see hematoma, subdural) or hygromas. (From Semin Neurol 1996 Mar;16(1):5-10; Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, pp637-8)

LABEL: intracranial vasospasm
IAO_0000115: Constriction of arteries in the skull due to sudden, sharp, and often persistent smooth muscle contraction in blood vessels. Intracranial vasospasm results in reduced vessel lumen caliber, restricted blood flow to the brain, and brain ischemia that may lead to hypoxic-ischemic brain injury (hypoxia-ischemia, brain).

LABEL: intradermal nevus
hasExactSynonym: dermal Nevus
IAO_0000115: A nevus characterized by the proliferation of nevus cells in the dermis without involvement of the dermal-epidermal junction.

LABEL: iritis
hasExactSynonym: inflammation of iris|iris inflammation|iritis|iritis (disease)
IAO_0000115: Inflammation of the iris.

LABEL: jejunal cancer
hasExactSynonym: cancer of jejunum|jejunum cancer|malignant jejunum neoplasm|malignant neoplasm of jejunum|malignant tumour of jejunum
IAO_0000115: A malignant neoplasm involving the jejunum.

LABEL: arthropathy
hasExactSynonym: Joint disorder|arthropathy|disease of skeletal joint|disease or disorder of skeletal joint|disorder of skeletal joint|disorder, Joint|skeletal joint disease|skeletal joint disease or disorder
IAO_0000115: Any disorder of the joints.

LABEL: juxtacortical osteosarcoma
hasExactSynonym: juxtacortical osteogenic sarcoma|juxtacortical osteosarcoma|parosteal osteogenic sarcoma|parosteal osteosarcoma
IAO_0000115: A low grade malignant bone-forming mesenchymal neoplasm arising from the surface of the bone. It usually affects the distal posterior femur, the proximal tibia, and proximal humerus. Painless swelling is the usual clinical sign. Most patients are young adults and the prognosis is usually excellent.

LABEL: kidney cortex necrosis
IAO_0000115: Death of cells in the kidney cortex, a common final result of various renal injuries including hypoxia; ischemia; and drug toxicity.

LABEL: kidney papillary necrosis
hasExactSynonym: renal papillitis necrotizing
IAO_0000115: A complication of kidney diseases characterized by cell death involving kidney papilla in the kidney medulla. Damages to this area may hinder the kidney to concentrate urine resulting in polyuria. Sloughed off necrotic tissue may block kidney pelvis or ureter. Necrosis of multiple renal papillae can lead to kidney failure.

LABEL: Klinefelter syndrome
hasExactSynonym: 47,XXY syndrome|Klinefelter syndrome|Klinefelter's syndrome|Klinefelter's syndrome, XXY|XXY syndrome|XXY syndrome (Klinefelter syndrome)
IAO_0000115: A sex chromosome disorder caused by the presence of an extra X chromosome in the male karyotype. Affected individuals are infertile and have a small penis and testes. They tend to have tall stature and long legs and may have difficulties with speech and language development. Gynecomastia may be present.

LABEL: Krebs 2 carcinoma
IAO_0000115: Carcinoma having known association to krebs2 gene mutation

LABEL: kuru
IAO_0000115: A prion disease found exclusively among the Fore linguistic group natives of the highlands of new guinea. The illness is primarily restricted to adult females and children of both sexes. It is marked by the subacute onset of tremor and ataxia followed by motor weakness and incontinence. Death occurs within 3-6 months of disease onset. The condition is associated with ritual cannibalism, and has become rare since this practice has been discontinued. Pathologic features include a noninflammatory loss of neurons that is most prominent in the cerebellum, glial proliferation, and amyloid plaques. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p773)

LABEL: kwashiorkor
hasExactSynonym: nutritional edema with dyspigmentation of skin and/or hair|nutritional oedema with dyspigmentation of skin and hair
IAO_0000115: A syndrome produced by severe protein deficiency, characterized by retarded growth, changes in skin and hair pigment, edema, and pathologic changes in the liver, including fatty infiltration, necrosis, and fibrosis. The word is a local name in Gold Coast, Africa, meaning 'displaced child'. Although first reported from Africa, kwashiorkor is now known throughout the world, but mainly in the tropics and subtropics. It is considered to be related to marasmus. (From Dorland, 27th ed)

LABEL: lateral medullary syndrome
hasExactSynonym: Posterior inferior cerebellar artery syndrome|Wallenberg syndrome|Wallenberg's syndrome
IAO_0000115: A syndrome caused by an infarct in the vertebral or posterior inferior cerebellar artery. It is characterized by sensory defects affecting the same side of the face as the infarct and the opposite side of the trunk as the infarct. Patients experience difficulty swallowing and/or speaking.

LABEL: nasal cavity and paranasal sinus lethal midline granuloma
hasExactSynonym: Midline lethal granuloma of nasal cavity and paranasal sinus|Midline lethal granuloma of the nasal cavity and paranasal sinus|midfacial Necrotising lesion|nasal cavity and paranasal sinus lethal Midline granuloma
IAO_0000115: An aggressive, progressive, and destructive lesion affecting the nasal cavities, paranasal sinuses, and the palate. The vast majority of cases are malignant lymphoproliferations affecting the midline of the face in patients with nasal type extranodal NK/T-cell lymphoma.

LABEL: leukemoid reaction
IAO_0000115: A hematology test result that indicates the presence of an increased white blood cell count and increased neutrophil precursors resembling leukemia, in a peripheral blood smear.

LABEL: leukoplakia of penis
hasExactSynonym: kraurosis of penis|kraurosis penis|leukoplakia of the penis|penile leukoplakia
IAO_0000115: A precancerous condition characterized by the presence of abnormal whitish areas on the glans or prepuce of the penis. Risk factors include chronic irritation, inflammation, and infection of the penis, and poor genital hygiene.

LABEL: leukostasis
hasExactSynonym: leukostasis (morphologic abnormality)
IAO_0000115: A disorder involving the aberrant infiltration and aggregation of leukocytes into the vasculature of the body. Leukostasis is typically detected in the brain and lungs of persons with leukemia. It requires substantial ablative modalities to both reduce the number of cells present and to ensure dispersion of the aggregates.

LABEL: lingual goiter
IAO_0000115: Pathological enlargement of the lingual thyroid, ectopic thyroid tissue at the base of the tongue. It may cause upper airway obstruction; dysphagia; or hypothyroidism symptoms.

LABEL: lip cancer
hasExactSynonym: cancer of lip|lip cancer|malignant Lip neoplasm|malignant Lip tumor|malignant Lip tumour|malignant lip neoplasm|malignant neoplasm of Lip|malignant neoplasm of lip|malignant neoplasm of lip, inner aspect|malignant neoplasm of lip, unspecified|malignant neoplasm of lip, unspecified, inner aspect|malignant neoplasm of lip, unspecified, vermilion border|malignant neoplasm of oral aspect of lip, not specified whether upper or lower|malignant neoplasm of the Lip|malignant tumor of Lip|malignant tumor of commissure of lip|malignant tumor of labial commissure|malignant tumor of lip|malignant tumor of the Lip|malignant tumour of Lip|malignant tumour of commissure of lip|malignant tumour of labial mucosa|malignant tumour of lip|malignant tumour of lower labial mucosa|malignant tumour of the Lip
IAO_0000115: A primary or metastatic malignant neoplasm involving the lip.

LABEL: minimal change disease
hasExactSynonym: lipoid nephrosis|minimal change disease|minimal change glomerulonephritis|minimal change nephropathy|nil disease
IAO_0000115: A glomerular disorder characterized by the electron microscopic finding of loss of podocyte foot processes. Light microscopic examination does not show glomerular changes. Patients present with proteinuria and nephrotic syndrome.

LABEL: Listeria meningitis
hasExactSynonym: Listeria meningitis|Listeria monocytogenes caused infectious meningitis|Listeria monocytogenes infectious meningitis
IAO_0000115: Inflammation of the meninges caused by listeria monocytogenes infection, usually occurring in individuals under the age of 3 years or over the age of 50 years. It may occur at any age in individuals with immunologic deficiency syndromes. Clinical manifestations include fever, altered mentation, headache, meningeal signs, focal neurologic signs, and seizures. (From Medicine 1998 Sep;77(5):313-36)

LABEL: low tension glaucoma
hasExactSynonym: normal tension glaucoma
IAO_0000115: A form of glaucoma in which chronic optic nerve damage and loss of vision normally attributable to buildup of intraocular pressure occurs despite prevailing conditions of normal intraocular pressure.

LABEL: lupus vulgaris
IAO_0000115: A form of cutaneous tuberculosis. It is seen predominantly in women and typically involves the nasal mucosa; buccal mucosa; and conjunctival mucosa.

LABEL: Lutembacher syndrome
hasExactSynonym: Lutembacher's syndrome
IAO_0000115: A condition characterized by a combination of ostium secundum atrial septal defect and an acquired mitral valve stenosis.

LABEL: lymphangiectasis
IAO_0000115: Dilatation of the lymphatic vessels.

LABEL: lymphangioendothelioma
hasExactSynonym: acquired progressive lymphangioma
IAO_0000115: A lymphangioma characterized by the presence of collagen bundle formation. It has an indolent clinical course and may be associated with skin plaques.

LABEL: lymphangiomyoma
hasExactSynonym: lymphangioleiomyoma|lymphangiomyoma
IAO_0000115: A neoplasm with perivascular epithelioid cell differentiation, often associated with tuberous sclerosis. It is characterized by the presence of smooth muscle and epithelioid cells and by the proliferation of lymphatic vessels. Sites of involvement include the lymph nodes, lung, mediastinum, and retroperitoneum.

LABEL: macular holes
hasExactSynonym: macular hole
IAO_0000115: A hole in the macula of the retina.

LABEL: magnesium deficiency
IAO_0000115: A nutritional condition produced by a deficiency of magnesium in the diet, characterized by anorexia, nausea, vomiting, lethargy, and weakness. Symptoms are paresthesias, muscle cramps, irritability, decreased attention span, and mental confusion, possibly requiring months to appear. Deficiency of body magnesium can exist even when serum values are normal. In addition, magnesium deficiency may be organ-selective, since certain tissues become deficient before others. (Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 12th ed, p1936)

LABEL: male genital tuberculosis
hasExactSynonym: male genital tuberculosis|male reproductive system tuberculosis
IAO_0000115: Mycobacterium infections of the male reproductive tract (genitalia, male).

LABEL: malignant hypertension
hasExactSynonym: accelerated-malignant hypertension|hypertensive emergency|malignant phase hypertension
IAO_0000115: Severe hypertension that is characterized by rapid onset of extremely high blood pressure and hypertension-mediated organ damage.

LABEL: malignant lymphatic vessel tumor
IAO_0000115: Neoplasms composed of lymphoid tissue, a lattice work of reticular tissue the interspaces of which contain lymphocytes. The concept does not refer to neoplasms located in lymphatic vessels.

LABEL: marasmus
hasExactSynonym: nutritional marasmus
IAO_0000115: The lack of sufficient energy or protein to meet the body's metabolic demands, as a result of either an inadequate dietary intake of protein, intake of poor quality dietary protein, increased demands due to disease, or increased nutrient losses.

LABEL: mastitis
hasExactSynonym: breast infection|breast inflammation|inflammation of breast|inflammatory disease of breast
IAO_0000115: Inflammation of breast tissue during lactation or postpartum due to an obstructed duct or infection. Mastitis can also occur in non-breastfeeding women, and rarely in men.

LABEL: maxillary sinus neoplasm
hasExactSynonym: maxillary antrum neoplasm|maxillary antrum tumor|maxillary antrum tumour|maxillary sinus neoplasm|maxillary sinus neoplasm (disease)|maxillary sinus tumor|maxillary sinus tumour|maxillofacial sinus neoplasm|maxillofacial sinus tumor|maxillofacial sinus tumour|neoplasm of maxillary antrum|neoplasm of maxillary sinus|neoplasm of maxillofacial sinus|neoplasm of the maxillary antrum|neoplasm of the maxillary sinus|neoplasm of the maxillofacial sinus|tumor of maxillary antrum|tumor of maxillary sinus|tumor of the maxillary antrum|tumor of the maxillary sinus|tumor of the maxillofacial sinus|tumour of maxillary antrum|tumour of maxillary sinus|tumour of maxillofacial sinus|tumour of the maxillary antrum|tumour of the maxillary sinus|tumour of the maxillofacial sinus
IAO_0000115: A benign or malignant neoplasm that affects the maxillary sinus. Representative examples of benign neoplasms include Schneiderian papilloma and salivary gland-type adenoma. Representative examples of malignant neoplasms include carcinoma and lymphoma.

LABEL: meconium aspiration syndrome
hasExactSynonym: MAS|meconium aspiration|meconium aspiration syndrome|neonatal aspiration of meconium
IAO_0000115: A serious condition in which a newborn breathes a mixture of meconium (the first intestinal discharge) and amniotic fluid into the lungs around the time of delivery. Meconium aspiration syndrome occurs in 5-10 percent of births and typically occurs when the infant is stressed, as when the infant is past its due date.

LABEL: mesenchymal chondrosarcoma
hasExactSynonym: mesenchymal chondrosarcoma
IAO_0000115: A morphologic variant of chondrosarcoma arising from bone and soft tissue. It is characterized by the presence of malignant small round cells, biphasic growth pattern, and well differentiated hyaline cartilage. Clinical presentation includes pain and swelling. The clinical course is aggressive, with local recurrences and distant metastases.

LABEL: mesenchymoma
hasExactSynonym: mesenchymoma
IAO_0000115: A term describing a soft tissue tumor which consists of two or more mesenchymal lines of differentiation, excluding a fibroblastic line of differentiation.

LABEL: mesenteric vascular occlusion
IAO_0000115: Obstruction of the flow in the splanchnic circulation by atherosclerosis; embolism; thrombosis; stenosis; trauma; and compression or intrinsic pressure from adjacent tumors. Rare causes are drugs, intestinal parasites, and vascular immunoinflammatory diseases such as periarteritis nodosa and thromboangiitis obliterans. (From Juergens et al., Peripheral Vascular Diseases, 5th ed, pp295-6)

LABEL: mesothelial neoplasm
hasExactSynonym: mesothelial neoplasm|mesothelial tumor|mesothelial tumour
IAO_0000115: A benign or malignant neoplasm arising from mesothelial cells. Mesothelial cells are the lining cells of the pleura and peritoneum. -- 2003

LABEL: middle cerebral artery infarction
IAO_0000115: Necrosis occurring in the middle cerebral artery distribution system which brings blood to the entire lateral aspects of each cerebral hemisphere. Clinical signs include impaired cognition; aphasia; agraphia; weak and numbness in the face and arms, contralaterally or bilaterally depending on the infarction.

LABEL: mouth disorder
hasExactSynonym: disease of mouth|disease or disorder of mouth|disorder of mouth|mouth disease|mouth disease or disorder|oral disease|oral disorder
IAO_0000115: A disease involving the mouth.

LABEL: mucinous cystadenoma
hasExactSynonym: adenoma, mucinous, benign|mucinous adenoma|mucinous cystadenoma|mucinous cystoma|pseudomucinous cystadenoma
IAO_0000115: A benign or low malignant potential cystic epithelial neoplasm composed of cells which contain intracytoplasmic mucin. It may arise from the ovary, pancreas, appendix, and lung.

LABEL: myeloid sarcoma
hasExactSynonym: chloroma|extramedullary myeloid tumor|extramedullary myeloid tumour|myeloid sarcoma|sarcoma, myeloid, malignant
IAO_0000115: A tumor mass composed of myeloblasts or immature myeloid cells. It occurs in extramedullary sites or the bone. (WHO, 2001)

LABEL: myofascial pain syndrome
IAO_0000115: Muscular pain in numerous body regions that can be reproduced by pressure on trigger points, localized hardenings in skeletal muscle tissue. Pain is referred to a location distant from the trigger points. A prime example is the temporomandibular joint dysfunction syndrome.

LABEL: myxosarcoma
hasExactSynonym: myxosarcoma|myxosarcoma (morphologic abnormality)|myxosarcoma, malignant
IAO_0000115: An infiltrating malignant soft tissue neoplasm characterized by the presence of immature undifferentiated cells and abundant myxoid stroma formation.

LABEL: necrotizing sialometaplasia
IAO_0000115: A benign, inflammatory, variably ulcerated, occasionally bilateral, self-healing lesion of the minor salivary glands that is often confused clinically and histologically with carcinoma.

LABEL: necrotizing ulcerative gingivitis
hasExactSynonym: ANUG|Vincent angina|Vincent's angina|acute necrotising ulcerative gingivitis [ambiguous]|acute necrotising ulcerative gingivostomatitis [ambiguous]
IAO_0000115: A bacterial infectious process affecting the gums. It is characterized by the development of necrotic, ulcerated, and painful lesions with creation of pseudomembranes extending along the gingival margins.

LABEL: neonatal myasthenia gravis
hasExactSynonym: neonatal myasthenia gravis
IAO_0000115: A disorder of neuromuscular transmission that occurs in a minority of newborns born to women with myasthenia gravis. Clinical features are usually present at birth or develop in the first 3 days of life and consist of hypotonia and impaired respiratory, suck, and swallowing abilities. This condition is associated with the passive transfer of acetylcholine receptor antibodies through the placenta. In the majority of infants the myasthenic weakness resolves (i.e., transient neonatal myasthenia gravis) although this disorder may rarely continue beyond the neonatal period (i.e., persistent neonatal myasthenia gravis). (From Menkes, Textbook of Child Neurology, 5th ed, p823; Neurology 1997 Jan;48(1):50-4)

LABEL: neurogenic bowel
IAO_0000115: Loss or absence of normal intestinal function due to nerve damage or birth defects. It is characterized by the inability to control the elimination of stool from the body.

LABEL: nodular goiter
hasExactSynonym: goiter, nodular|nodular goiter|nodular goiter (disease)|nodular goitre (disease)
IAO_0000115: Goiter characterized by discrete tissue mass(es) that may or may not produce thyroid hormones.

LABEL: non-gestational choriocarcinoma
IAO_0000115: A highly malignant choriocarcinoma derived from the non-placental origin such as the totipotent cells in the testis, the ovary, and the pineal gland. It produces high levels of chorionic gonadotropin and can metastasize widely through the bloodstream to the lungs, brain, liver, bone, and other viscera by the time of diagnosis.

LABEL: nutritional deficiency disease
hasExactSynonym: malnourished|malnutrition
IAO_0000115: A condition produced by dietary or metabolic deficiency. The term includes all diseases caused by an insufficient supply of essential nutrients, i.e., protein (or amino acids), vitamins, and minerals. It also includes an inadequacy of calories. (From Dorland, 27th ed; Stedman, 25th ed)

LABEL: obstructive jaundice
hasExactSynonym: obstructive hyperbilirubinemia
IAO_0000115: A finding indicating increased bilirubin levels in the blood and urine, due to intrahepatic or extrahepatic obstruction of the biliary system.

LABEL: ocular hypertension
IAO_0000115: Abnormally high intraocular pressure.

LABEL: ocular tuberculosis
IAO_0000115: Tuberculous infection of the eye, primarily the iris, ciliary body, and choroid.

LABEL: oophoritis
hasExactSynonym: inflammation of ovary|ovary inflammation
IAO_0000115: Inflammation of the ovary, generally caused by an ascending infection of organisms from the endocervix.

LABEL: Moraxellaceae infectious disease
hasExactSynonym: Moraxellaceae caused disease or disorder|Moraxellaceae disease or disorder
IAO_0000115: Infections with bacteria of the family moraxellaceae.

LABEL: optic papillitis
hasExactSynonym: Choked disc|Choked discs|Choked disk|Choked disks|Edemas, optic disc|Edemas, optic disk|decreased intraocular pressure associated papilledema|decreased intraocular pressure-associated papilledema|disk, Choked|disks, Choked|edema of the optic disk|edema, optic disc|edema, optic disk|edema, optic papilla|increased intracranial pressure associated papilledema|increased intracranial pressure-associated papilledema|inflammation of optic disc|inflammation of optic disk|oedema of the optic disc|optic disc inflammation|optic disc oedema|optic discitis|optic disk edema|optic disk inflammation|optic nerve papillitis|optic papilla edema|optic papilla oedema|optic papillitis|papilledema|papilledema associated with decreased intraocular pressure|papilledema associated with increased intracranial pressure|papillitis|papillitis, optic|papillitis, optic nerve|papilloedema
IAO_0000115: Swelling of the optic disk, usually in association with increased intracranial pressure, characterized by hyperemia, blurring of the disk margins, microhemorrhages, blind spot enlargement, and engorgement of retinal veins. Chronic papilledema may cause optic atrophy and visual loss. (Miller et al., Clinical Neuro-Ophthalmology, 4th ed, p175)

LABEL: oral leukoedema
IAO_0000115: A disorder of the buccal mucosa resembling early leukoplakia, characterized by the presence of filmy opalescence of the mucosa in the early stages to a whitish gray cast with a coarsely wrinkled surface in the later stages, associated with intracellular edema of the spinous or malpighian layer. (Dorland, 27th ed)

LABEL: orbital cellulitis
hasExactSynonym: orbital cellulitis
IAO_0000115: Inflammation of the eye tissues posterior to the orbital septum, and generally secondary to an infection spread from adjacent sinuses. Signs and symptoms of the affected eye include sudden loss of vision, erythema, edema, decreased eye movement, and pain. Treatment is conducted via intravenous antibiotics, observation, and surgical intervention when necessary.

LABEL: orchitis
hasExactSynonym: orchitis|orchitis (disease)|testis inflammation|testisitis
IAO_0000115: Inflammation of one or both testes due to viral or bacterial infections. Signs and symptoms include enlargement or tenderness of the affected testis, inguinal lymphadenopathy, blood in the semen, and pain during urination, intercourse, or ejaculation.

LABEL: malignant superior sulcus neoplasm
hasExactSynonym: Pancoast tumor|Pancoast's tumor|malignant Superior sulcus lung neoplasm|malignant Superior sulcus lung tumor|malignant Superior sulcus lung tumour|malignant Superior sulcus neoplasm|malignant Superior sulcus neoplasm of lung|malignant Superior sulcus neoplasm of the lung|malignant Superior sulcus tumor|malignant Superior sulcus tumor of lung|malignant Superior sulcus tumor of the lung|malignant Superior sulcus tumour of lung|malignant Superior sulcus tumour of the lung|malignant pulmonary sulcus neoplasm|pulmonary sulcus neoplasm, malignant
IAO_0000115: A malignant neoplasm originating from the apical lung. Most malignant superior sulcus neoplasms are bronchogenic carcinomas. This tumor may be associated with Pancoast syndrome. It is also known as Pancoast tumor.

LABEL: panophthalmitis
IAO_0000115: Acute suppurative inflammation of the inner eye with necrosis of the sclera (and sometimes the cornea) and extension of the inflammation into the orbit. Pain may be severe and the globe may rupture. In endophthalmitis the globe does not rupture.

LABEL: thyroid gland papillary and follicular carcinoma
hasExactSynonym: papillary and follicular adenocarcinoma|papillary and follicular carcinoma|thyroid gland papillary and follicular carcinoma
IAO_0000115: A thyroid neoplasm of mixed papillary and follicular arrangement. Its biological behavior and prognosis is the same as that of a papillary adenocarcinoma of the thyroid. (From DeVita Jr et al., Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 3d ed, p1271)

LABEL: parametritis
hasExactSynonym: inflammation of parametrium|parametrium inflammation
IAO_0000115: Inflammation of the parametrium, the connective tissue of the pelvic floor, extending from the subserous coat of the uterus laterally between the layers of the broad ligament.

LABEL: paraneoplastic polyneuropathy
hasExactSynonym: paraneoplastic polyneuropathy
IAO_0000115: A diffuse or multifocal peripheral neuropathy caused by the effects of a distant neoplasm. It may be attributed, in part, to the immune response to neoplasm-elaborated proteins. The neuropathy may be sensory, motor, mixed or autonomic. It may be the initial presentation of an occult neoplasm. Detection and resection of the neoplasm may result in cure.

LABEL: paraphimosis
IAO_0000115: A condition in which the foreskin of an uncircumcised male is retracted and cannot be pulled back over the glans penis. It results in painful swelling of the glans penis and, if is not corrected, may lead to gangrene.

LABEL: parathyroid gland adenoma
hasExactSynonym: adenoma of parathyroid|adenoma of parathyroid gland|adenoma of the parathyroid|parathyroid adenoma|parathyroid gland adenoma
IAO_0000115: A benign tumor arising from the parenchymal cells of the parathyroid glands. In the vast majority of cases, the tumor involves a single parathyroid gland. It is associated with the symptoms of primary hyperparathyroidism, resulting from the excessive production of parathyroid hormone. It is usually surrounded by a well-defined capsule. Capsular invasion, vascular invasion, and perineural invasion are absent.

LABEL: partial motor epilepsy
IAO_0000115: A simple partial seizure consisting of clonus or spasm of a muscle or muscle group; it may be single or in a continuous and repetitive series or may spread to adjacent muscles.

LABEL: partial sensory epilepsy
IAO_0000115: A disorder characterized by recurrent focal onset seizures which have sensory (i.e., olfactory, visual, tactile, gustatory, or auditory) manifestations. Partial seizures that feature alterations of consciousness are referred to as complex partial seizures (epilepsy, complex partial).

LABEL: Pasteurella hemorrhagic septicemia
IAO_0000115: Any of several bacterial diseases, usually caused by pasteurella multocida, marked by the presence of hemorrhagic areas in the subcutaneous tissues, serous membranes, muscles, lymph glands, and throughout the internal organs. The diseases primarily affect animals and rarely humans.

LABEL: patellofemoral pain syndrome
IAO_0000115: A syndrome characterized by retropatellar or peripatellar pain resulting from physical and biochemical changes in the patellofemoral joint. The pain is most prominent when ascending or descending stairs, squatting, or sitting with flexed knees. There is a lack of consensus on the etiology and treatment. The syndrome is often confused with (or accompanied by) chondromalacia patellae, the latter describing a pathological condition of the cartilage and not a syndrome.

LABEL: penile neoplasm
hasExactSynonym: neoplasm of penis|neoplasm of the penis|penile neoplasm|penile neoplasms|penile tumor|penile tumour|penis neoplasm|penis neoplasm (disease)|penis tumor|penis tumour|tumor of penis|tumor of the penis|tumour of penis|tumour of the penis
IAO_0000115: A benign, borderline, or malignant neoplasm that affects the penis. Representative examples include penile hemangioma, penile intraepithelial neoplasia, and penile carcinoma.

LABEL: peptic esophagitis
IAO_0000115: Inflammation of the esophagus that is caused by the reflux of gastric juice with contents of the stomach and duodenum.

LABEL: periapical granuloma
IAO_0000115: Chronic nonsuppurative inflammation of periapical tissue resulting from irritation following pulp disease or endodontic treatment.

LABEL: periarthritis
IAO_0000115: Inflammation of the tissues around a joint. (Dorland, 27th ed)

LABEL: pericoronitis
IAO_0000115: Inflammation of the gingiva surrounding the crown of a tooth.

LABEL: perinephritis
hasExactSynonym: inflammation of perirenal fat|perirenal fat inflammation
IAO_0000115: Inflammation of the connective and adipose tissues surrounding the kidney.

LABEL: peritoneal neoplasm
hasExactSynonym: neoplasm of peritoneum|peritoneal neoplasm|peritoneum neoplasm|peritoneum neoplasm (disease)|peritoneum tumor|peritoneum tumour|tumor of peritoneum|tumour of peritoneum
IAO_0000115: A benign or malignant neoplasm that affects the peritoneal cavity. Representative examples of benign neoplasms include adenomatoid tumor and disseminated peritoneal leiomyomatosis. Representative examples of malignant neoplasms include primary peritoneal carcinoma, metastatic carcinoma to the peritoneum, and malignant mesothelioma.

LABEL: peroneal nerve paralysis
hasExactSynonym: nerve palsy, peroneal|palsy, peroneal nerve
IAO_0000115: Paralysis of the nerves located in the legs.

LABEL: phimosis
IAO_0000115: A condition in which there is constriction in the tip of the foreskin resulting in inability to fully retract the foreskin over the glans penis. Causes include balanoposthitis, balanitis xerotica obliterans, and untreated diabetes.

LABEL: pigmented spindle cell nevus
hasExactSynonym: spindle cell Nevus of Reed
IAO_0000115: A benign, small and slightly elevated brown or black skin lesion with usually well-demarcated borders. It is characterized by the presence of a melanocytic proliferation resulting in the formation of uniform cellular nests. Sometimes the clinical and morphologic features may be difficult to distinguish from melanoma.

LABEL: pilar sheath acanthoma
hasExactSynonym: Infundibuloisthmicoma|Pilar sheath acanthoma|acanthoma of Pilar sheath|acanthoma of the Pilar sheath
IAO_0000115: A benign, small, papular or nodular skin neoplasm that usually arises above the upper lip. It is characterized by an epithelial proliferation with a central cavity. The cavity wall is lined with keratinocytes.

LABEL: pituitary apoplexy
hasExactSynonym: pituitary gland apoplexy
IAO_0000115: A rare, potentially life-threatening disorder caused by acute ischemic infarction or hemorrhage in the pituitary gland. It is most often associated with the presence of a pituitary gland adenoma. Signs and symptoms include headache, vomiting, visual disturbances, and endocrine dysfunction.

LABEL: pituitary dwarfism
IAO_0000115: Proportionately decreased bodily growth due to failure of the pituitary gland to produce an adequate supply of growth hormone.

LABEL: pneumatosis cystoides intestinalis
IAO_0000115: The presence of gas within the wall of the large or small intestine.

LABEL: pneumococcal meningitis
hasExactSynonym: Streptococcus pneumoniae caused infectious meningitis|Streptococcus pneumoniae infectious meningitis
IAO_0000115: An acute purulent infection of the meninges and subarachnoid space caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae, most prevalent in children and adults over the age of 60. This illness may be associated with otitis media; mastoiditis; sinusitis; respiratory tract infections; sickle cell disease (anemia, sickle cell); skull fractures; and other disorders. Clinical manifestations include fever; headache; neck stiffness; and somnolence followed by seizures; focal neurologic deficits (notably deafness); and coma. (From Miller et al., Merritt's Textbook of Neurology, 9th ed, p111)

LABEL: polyradiculoneuropathy
IAO_0000115: Diseases characterized by injury or dysfunction involving multiple peripheral nerves and nerve roots. The process may primarily affect myelin or nerve axons. Two of the more common demyelinating forms are acute inflammatory polyradiculopathy (guillain-barre syndrome) and polyradiculoneuropathy, chronic inflammatory demyelinating. Polyradiculoneuritis refers to inflammation of multiple peripheral nerves and spinal nerve roots.

LABEL: postcholecystectomy syndrome
IAO_0000115: Abdominal symptoms after removal of the gallbladder. The common postoperative symptoms are often the same as those present before the operation, such as colic, bloating, nausea, and vomiting. There is pain on palpation of the right upper quadrant and sometimes jaundice. The term is often used, inaccurately, to describe such postoperative symptoms not due to gallbladder removal.

LABEL: posterior cerebral artery infarction
IAO_0000115: Necrosis induced by ischemia in the posterior cerebral artery distribution system which supplies portions of the brain stem; the thalamus; temporal lobe, and occipital lobe. Depending on the size and location of infarction, clinical features include olfaction disorders and visual problems (agnosia; alexia; hemianopsia).

LABEL: posterior uveitis
hasExactSynonym: chorioretinal region inflammation|inflammation of chorioretinal region
IAO_0000115: Inflammation of the choroid as well as the retina and vitreous body. Some form of visual disturbance is usually present. The most important characteristics of posterior uveitis are vitreous opacities, choroiditis, and chorioretinitis.

LABEL: potassium deficiency
IAO_0000115: A condition due to decreased dietary intake of potassium, as in starvation or failure to administer in intravenous solutions, or to gastrointestinal loss in diarrhea, chronic laxative abuse, vomiting, gastric suction, or bowel diversion. Severe potassium deficiency may produce muscular weakness and lead to paralysis and respiratory failure. Muscular malfunction may result in hypoventilation, paralytic ileus, hypotension, muscle twitches, tetany, and rhabomyolysis. Nephropathy from potassium deficit impairs the concentrating mechanism, producing polyuria and decreased maximal urinary concentrating ability with secondary polydipsia. (Merck Manual, 16th ed)

LABEL: prediabetes syndrome
hasExactSynonym: borderline diabetes|prediabetes
IAO_0000115: A condition in which blood glucose levels are high, but not high enough to be classified as type 2 diabetes.

LABEL: Actinomycetales infectious disease
hasExactSynonym: actinomycetales caused disease or disorder|actinomycetales disease or disorder|actinomycetales infection|actinomycetales infections|actinomycete infection|actinomycete infections|actinomycotic infection|actinomycotic infectious disease|infection, actinomycetales|infection, actinomycete|infections, actinomycetales|infections, actinomycete
IAO_0000115: Infections with bacteria of the order actinomycetales.

LABEL: Anaplasmataceae infectious disease
hasExactSynonym: Anaplasmataceae caused disease or disorder|Anaplasmataceae disease or disorder
IAO_0000115: Infections with bacteria of the family anaplasmataceae.

LABEL: Bacillaceae infectious disease
hasExactSynonym: Bacillaceae caused disease or disorder|Bacillaceae disease or disorder
IAO_0000115: Infections with bacteria of the family bacillaceae.

LABEL: Bartonellaceae infectious disease
hasExactSynonym: Bartonellaceae caused disease or disorder|Bartonellaceae disease or disorder
IAO_0000115: Infections with bacteria of the family bartonellaceae.

LABEL: Fusobacteriaceae infectious disease
hasExactSynonym: Fusobacteriaceae caused disease or disorder|Fusobacteriaceae disease or disorder
IAO_0000115: Infections with bacteria of the family Fusobacteriaceae, in the order Fusobacterales, phylum fusobacteria.

LABEL: haemophilus infectious disease
hasExactSynonym: Haemophilus caused disease or disorder|Haemophilus disease or disorder|Haemophilus infectious disease|haemophilus infectious disease
IAO_0000115: Infections with bacteria of the genus haemophilus.

LABEL: Rickettsiaceae infectious disease
hasExactSynonym: Rickettsiaceae caused disease or disorder|Rickettsiaceae disease or disorder
IAO_0000115: Infections with bacteria of the family rickettsiaceae.

LABEL: Proteus infectious disease
hasExactSynonym: Proteus <enterobacteria> caused disease or disorder|Proteus <enterobacteria> disease or disorder|Proteus <enterobacteria> infectious disease
IAO_0000115: Infections with bacteria of the genus proteus.

LABEL: pseudobulbar palsy
hasExactSynonym: pseudobulbar palsy
IAO_0000115: A condition affecting cranial nerves IX-XII resulting from upper motor neuron damage arising from a variety of causes.

LABEL: pulmonary coin lesion
hasExactSynonym: coin lesion of lung (context-dependent category)|coin lesion of lung (finding)
IAO_0000115: A single lung lesion that is characterized by a small round mass of tissue, usually less than 1 cm in diameter, and can be detected by chest radiography. A solitary pulmonary nodule can be associated with neoplasm, tuberculosis, cyst, or other anomalies in the lung, the chest wall, or the pleura.

LABEL: pulmonary edema
hasExactSynonym: edema, pulmonary
IAO_0000115: Accumulation of fluid in the lung tissues causing disturbance of the gas exchange that may lead to respiratory failure. It is caused by direct injury to the lung parenchyma or congestive heart failure. The symptoms may appear suddenly or gradually. Suddenly appearing symptoms include difficulty breathing, feeling of suffocation, and coughing associated with frothy sputum. Gradually appearing symptoms include difficulty breathing while lying in bed, shortness of breath during activity, and weight gain (in patients with congestive heart failure).

LABEL: pulmonary plasma cell granuloma
IAO_0000115: A tumor-like inflammatory lesion of the lung that is composed of plasma cells and fibrous tissue. It is also known as an inflammatory pseudotumor, often with calcification and measuring between 2 and 5 cm in diameter.

LABEL: pulmonary subvalvular stenosis
hasExactSynonym: congenital infundibular stenosis|infundibular pulmonic stenosis, congenital|pulmonary infundibular stenosis|subvalvular pulmonic stenosis
IAO_0000115: The obstruction of the right ventricular outflow tract that originates within the body of the right ventricle, that exists at the time of birth; it often occurs in association with other intracardiac anomalies.

LABEL: pulmonary valve stenosis
IAO_0000115: The pathologic narrowing of the orifice of the pulmonary valve. This lesion restricts blood outflow from the right ventricle to the pulmonary artery. When the trileaflet valve is fused into an imperforate membrane, the blockage is complete.

LABEL: pulpitis
hasExactSynonym: dental pulp inflammation|inflammation of dental pulp
IAO_0000115: Inflammation of the dental pulp.

LABEL: pyelitis
hasExactSynonym: inflammation of renal pelvis|renal pelvis inflammation
IAO_0000115: Inflammation of the renal pelvis.

LABEL: pyelonephritis
hasExactSynonym: kidney infection
IAO_0000115: An inflammatory process affecting the kidney. The cause is most often bacterial, but may also be fungal in nature. Signs and symptoms may include fever, chills, flank pain, painful and frequent urination, cloudy or bloody urine, and confusion.

LABEL: radial nerve lesion
hasExactSynonym: lesion of radial nerve|peripheral nerve lesion of radial nerve|radial nerve peripheral nerve lesion
IAO_0000115: A peripheral nerve lesion that involves the radial nerve.

LABEL: rat-bite fever
hasExactSynonym: Streptobacillosis|spirillosis
IAO_0000115: An infectious disease that is caused transmitted by the bite of a rat. Two species of bacteria can cause the infection: Streptobacillus moniliformis and Spirillum minus.

LABEL: renal aminoaciduria
IAO_0000115: A group of inherited kidney disorders characterized by the abnormally elevated levels of amino acids in urine. Genetic mutations of transport proteins result in the defective reabsorption of free amino acids at the proximal renal tubules. Renal aminoaciduria are classified by the specific amino acid or acids involved.

LABEL: renal artery obstruction
IAO_0000115: Narrowing or occlusion of the renal artery or arteries. It is due usually to atherosclerosis; fibromuscular dysplasia; thrombosis; embolism, or external pressure. The reduced renal perfusion can lead to renovascular hypertension (hypertension, renovascular).

LABEL: renal osteodystrophy
hasExactSynonym: renal rickets
IAO_0000115: Abnormalities of bone mineral metabolism associated with chronic kidney disease.

LABEL: renovascular hypertension
hasExactSynonym: renovascular hypertension|renovascular hypertension (disease)
IAO_0000115: High blood pressure secondary to renal artery stenosis.

LABEL: retinal artery occlusion
IAO_0000115: An occlusion of the retinal artery.

LABEL: retinal drusen
IAO_0000115: Colloid or hyaline bodies lying beneath the retinal pigment epithelium. They may occur either secondary to changes in the choroid that affect the pigment epithelium or as an autosomal dominant disorder of the retinal pigment epithelium.

LABEL: retinal vasculitis
hasExactSynonym: retinal vasculitis
IAO_0000115: Inflammation of the retinal vasculature with various causes including infectious disease; lupus erythematosus, systemic; multiple sclerosis; behcet syndrome; and chorioretinitis.

LABEL: retinal vein occlusion
hasExactSynonym: retinal vein occlusion
IAO_0000115: An occlusion of the retinal vein.

LABEL: retinopathy of prematurity
hasExactSynonym: ROP|Terry syndrome|retrolental fibroplasia
IAO_0000115: A bilateral retinopathy characterized by neovascularization, scarring, retinal detachment, and eventually blindness. It may be mild or severe. It occurs in babies born prematurely. Causes include oxygen toxicity and hypoxia.

LABEL: Rh isoimmunization
IAO_0000115: The mother develops antibodies against red blood cell Rhesus antigens. This may lead to potential fetal adverse outcomes such as anemia.

LABEL: rheumatic heart disease
hasExactSynonym: RHD|disease, rheumatic heart|heart disease, rheumatic|rheumatic carditis
IAO_0000115: An autoinflammatory condition following an infection with Group A Beta Hemolytic Streptococcus (GABHS), in which the heart is attacked by antibodies formed in reaction to a recent GABHS infection. Chief anatomic changes of the valve include leaflet thickening, commissural fusion, and shortening and thickening of the tendinous cords, all of which can result in valvular dysfunction.

LABEL: Rickettsiosis
hasExactSynonym: Rickettsia caused disease or disorder|Rickettsia disease or disorder|Rickettsia infection|Rickettsia infectious disease|Rickettsiae disease|Rickettsial disease|Rickettsial infectious disease|Rickettsial infectious disorder|Rickettsiosis|infection, Rickettsia|infections, Rickettsia
IAO_0000115: A group of infectious diseases that is caused by Rickettsia.

LABEL: root caries
hasExactSynonym: cementum dental caries|dental caries of cementum|dental caries of root surface
IAO_0000115: Dental caries involving the tooth root, cementum, or cervical area of the tooth.

LABEL: sciatic neuropathy
IAO_0000115: Disease or damage involving the SCIATIC NERVE, which divides into the PERONEAL NERVE and TIBIAL NERVE (see also PERONEAL NEUROPATHIES and TIBIAL NEUROPATHY). Clinical manifestations may include SCIATICA or pain localized to the hip, PARESIS or PARALYSIS of posterior thigh muscles and muscles innervated by the peroneal and tibial nerves, and sensory loss involving the lateral and posterior thigh, posterior and lateral leg, and sole of the foot. The sciatic nerve may be affected by trauma; ISCHEMIA; COLLAGEN DISEASES; and other conditions. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p1363)

LABEL: scrapie
IAO_0000115: A fatal disease of the nervous system in sheep and goats, characterized by pruritus, debility, and locomotor incoordination. It is caused by proteinaceous infectious particles called prions.

LABEL: sebaceous adenocarcinoma
hasExactSynonym: adenocarcinoma, sebaceous, malignant|carcinoma of sebaceous gland|carcinoma of the sebaceous gland|sebaceous cancer|sebaceous carcinoma|sebaceous gland adenocarcinoma|sebaceous gland carcinoma
IAO_0000115: An adenocarcinoma with sebaceous differentiation. It presents as a painless mass and it may be multifocal. It grows in the ocular adnexae and in the skin of head and neck, trunk, genitals, and extremities. It is characterized by the presence of malignant cells with multivesicular and clear cytoplasm. It may recur and metastasize.

LABEL: sebaceous gland neoplasm
hasExactSynonym: neoplasm of sebaceous gland|sebaceous gland neoplasm|sebaceous gland neoplasm (disease)|sebaceous gland tumor|sebaceous gland tumour|sebaceous neoplasm|sebaceous tumor|sebaceous tumour|tumor of sebaceous gland|tumour of sebaceous gland
IAO_0000115: A benign or malignant neoplasm that arises from the sebaceous glands. Representative examples include sebaceous adenoma and sebaceous carcinoma.

LABEL: secondary hyperparathyroidism
hasExactSynonym: secondary hyperparathyroidism|secondary hyperparathyroidism (disease)
IAO_0000115: Overproduction of parathyroid hormone in response to influence external to the parathyroid glands.

LABEL: secondary hypertrophic osteoarthropathy
hasExactSynonym: hypertrophic pulmonary osteoarthropathy|hypertrophic pulmonary osteoarthropathy (disorder) [ambiguous]
IAO_0000115: Symmetrical osteitis of the four limbs, chiefly localized to the phalanges and the terminal epiphyses of the long bones of the forearm and leg, sometimes extending to the proximal ends of the limbs and the flat bones, and accompanied by dorsal kyphosis and joint involvement. It is often secondary to chronic conditions of the lungs and heart. (Dorland, 27th ed)

LABEL: secondary Parkinson disease
hasExactSynonym: secondary Parkinsonism|secondary parkinsonism (disorder) [ambiguous]|secondary parkinsonism, unspecified
IAO_0000115: A condition with a clinical picture similar to that of Parkinson disease, but which is caused by external factors, including medication.

LABEL: shoulder impingement syndrome
hasExactSynonym: shoulder impingement syndrome (disorder) [ambiguous]
IAO_0000115: Compression of the rotator cuff tendons and subacromial bursa between the humeral head and structures that make up the coracoacromial arch and the humeral tuberosities. This condition is associated with subacromial bursitis and rotator cuff (largely supraspinatus) and bicipital tendon inflammation, with or without degenerative changes in the tendon. Pain that is most severe when the arm is abducted in an arc between 40 and 120 degrees, sometimes associated with tears in the rotator cuff, is the chief symptom. (From Jablonski's Dictionary of Syndromes and Eponymic Diseases, 2d ed)

LABEL: sialadenitis
hasExactSynonym: lymphadenitis (disease) of saliva-secreting gland|saliva-secreting gland lymphadenitis (disease)|sialitis|sialoadenitis
IAO_0000115: Sialadenitis is an infection of the salivary glands. It is usually caused by a virus or bacteria. The parotid (in front ofthe ear) and submandibular (under the chin) glands are most commonly affected. Sialadenitis may be associated with pain, tenderness, redness, and gradual, localized swelling of the affected area. Sialadenitis most commonly affects the elderly and chronically ill especially those with dry mouth or who are dehydrated, but can also affected people of any age including newborn babies. Diagnosis is usually made by clinical exam but a CT scan, MRI scan or ultrasound may be done if the doctor suspects an abscess or to look for stones. Treatment may include an antibiotic (if bacterial), warm compresses, increasing fluid intake and good oral hygiene. Most salivary gland infections go away on their own or are cured with treatment. Complications are not common.

LABEL: sialolithiasis
hasExactSynonym: Stone of salivary gland or duct|sialolith
IAO_0000115: A concretion in the salivary gland.

LABEL: sigmoid neoplasm
hasExactSynonym: neoplasm of sigmoid colon|sigmoid colon neoplasm|sigmoid colon neoplasm (disease)|sigmoid colon tumor|sigmoid colon tumour|tumor of sigmoid colon|tumour of sigmoid colon
IAO_0000115: Tumors or cancer of the sigmoid colon.

LABEL: silo filler disease
hasExactSynonym: silo filler disease
IAO_0000115: A form of alveolitis or pneumonitis caused by hypersensitivity to high level of inhaled nitrogen oxides, decomposition products of silage.

LABEL: skin appendage carcinoma
hasExactSynonym: adnexal carcinoma|carcinoma of adnexa|carcinoma of cutaneous appendage|carcinoma of skin appendage|carcinoma, adnexal, malignant|cutaneous appendage carcinoma|skin appendage carcinoma
IAO_0000115: A carcinoma arising from the sebaceous glands, sweat glands, or the hair follicles. Representative examples include sebaceous carcinoma, apocrine carcinoma, eccrine carcinoma, and pilomatrical carcinoma.

LABEL: small cell sarcoma
hasExactSynonym: small cell sarcoma|small cell sarcomas
IAO_0000115: A sarcoma characterized by the presence of small round or elongated malignant cells with a small amount of cytoplasm.

LABEL: smooth muscle tumor
hasExactSynonym: neoplasm of smooth muscle|neoplasm of the smooth muscle|smooth muscle neoplasm|smooth muscle tumor|tumor of smooth muscle|tumor of the smooth muscle|tumour of smooth muscle|tumour of the smooth muscle
IAO_0000115: A benign or malignant myomatous neoplasm arising from smooth muscle.

LABEL: somatostatinoma
hasExactSynonym: Delta cell tumor|Delta cell tumour|somatostatin cell tumor|somatostatin producing tumor|somatostatin producing tumour|somatostatin-producing NET|somatostatin-producing neuroendocrine tumor|somatostatin-producing neuroendocrine tumour|somatostatin-producing tumor|somatostatin-producing tumour|somatostatinoma|tumor of Delta cells|tumor of the Delta cells|tumour of Delta cells|tumour of the Delta cells
IAO_0000115: A rare, usually malignant neuroendocrine tumor arizing from delta cells. This neoplasm produces large amounts of somatostatin, which may result in a syndrome characterized by diarrhea, steatorrhea, weight loss, and gastric hyposecretion. Sixty percent are found in the pancreas and 40% in the duodenum or jejunum. The peak incidence occurs between 40 and 60 years of age; women are affected more than men by 2:1.

LABEL: spermatocele
IAO_0000115: A benign testicular cyst that is located in the epididymis, and which contains serous fluid, lymphocytes, spermatozoa, and debris.

LABEL: splenic infarction
IAO_0000115: Insufficiency of arterial or venous blood supply to the spleen due to emboli, thrombi, vascular torsion, or pressure that produces a macroscopic area of necrosis. (From Stedman, 25th ed)

LABEL: struma ovarii
hasExactSynonym: struma ovarii|struma ovarii (morphologic abnormality)|struma ovarii NOS (morphologic abnormality)
IAO_0000115: An ovarian mature teratoma characterized by the presence of aberrant thyroid tissue. The aberrant thyroid tissue shows morphologic changes identical to thyroid adenoma or carcinoma. Patients may present with abdominal mass and unusual symptoms due to thyrotoxicosis, or Meigs syndrome (ascites and pleural effusion).

LABEL: subacute bacterial endocarditis
hasExactSynonym: SBE|Subacute bacterial endocarditis
IAO_0000115: Subacute inflammation of the endocardium. Streptococcus viridans is the usual etiologic agent of subacute bacterial endocarditis. The distinction between "acute" and "subacute" endocarditis has traditionally been made based on the pathogenic organism and clinical presentation.

LABEL: subacute thyroiditis
hasExactSynonym: De Quervain thyroiditis|De Quervain's thyroiditis|DeQuervain thyroiditis|Subacute granulomatous thyroiditis|Subacute thyroiditis|de Quervain's thyroiditis|giant-cell thyroiditis|granulomatous thyroiditis
IAO_0000115: Self-limited inflammation of the thyroid gland characterized by the presence of multinucleated giant cells. Patients present with neck pain, often associated with fever and dysphagia. The clinical course includes an initial phase of hyperthyroidism, followed by a phase of hypothyroidism, and eventually a return to normal thyroid function.

LABEL: subclavian steal syndrome
hasExactSynonym: subclavian artery stenosis
IAO_0000115: An uncommon neurovascular condition seen with exertion of the upper extremity. It is usually caused by atherosclerotic stenosis or occlusion of the subclavian artery proximal to the origin of the vertebral artery. In order to maintain adequate perfusion of the arm during exercise on the affected side, the narrowed subclavian artery siphons off retrograde blood flow from the ipsilateral vertebral artery. This is possible due to lower blood pressure distal to the site of narrowing and collateral circulation through the circle of Willis. Affected individuals may remain asymptomatic until the oxygen demand generated from upper extremity exercise requires a large enough compensatory volume of blood to be diverted from the vertebral artery to provoke vertebrobasilar insufficiency and its accompanying neurological sequelae. Presenting clinical signs may include pain or numbness of the affected arm (with diminished pulses and a brachial systolic blood pressure differential of greater than 20 mmHg as compared to the opposite arm), vertigo, tinnitus, dysarthria, diplopia and syncope. Notably, unlike cerebral infarction, the clinical course does not lead to chronic neurologic disability. Prognosis for recovery of normal anterograde circulation is favorable following endovascular or surgical intervention.

LABEL: subdural empyema
IAO_0000115: An intracranial or rarely intraspinal suppurative process invading the space between the inner surface of the dura mater and the outer surface of the arachnoid.

LABEL: substernal goiter
IAO_0000115: An enlarged thyroid gland with at least 50% of the gland situated behind the sternum. It is an unusual presentation of an intrathoracic goiter. Substernal goiters frequently cause compression on the trachea leading to deviation, narrowing, and respiratory symptoms.

LABEL: subvalvular aortic stenosis
IAO_0000115: An aortic stenosis caused by fibromuscular stenosis or hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. It may be associated with congenital heart defects.

LABEL: sulfhemoglobinemia
hasExactSynonym: Sulfemoglobinemia
IAO_0000115: A morbid condition due to the presence of sulfmethemoglobin in the blood. It is marked by persistent cyanosis, but the blood count does not reveal any special abnormality in the blood. It is thought to be caused by the action of hydrogen sulfide absorbed from the intestine. (Stedman, 25th ed)

LABEL: suppurative periapical periodontitis
hasExactSynonym: dentoalveolar abscess|periapical dental abscess
IAO_0000115: Localized collection of pus in the tissues that enclose the root of a tooth.

LABEL: suppurative uveitis
IAO_0000115: Intraocular infection caused mainly by pus-producing bacteria and rarely by fungi. The infection may be caused by an injury or surgical wound (exogenous) or by endogenous septic emboli in such diseases as bacterial endocarditis or meningococcemia.

LABEL: syphilitic aortitis
IAO_0000115: Cardiovascular manifestations of syphilis, an infection of treponema pallidum. In the late stage of syphilis, sometimes 20-30 years after the initial infection, damages are often seen in the blood vessels including the aorta and the aortic valve. Clinical signs include syphilitic aortitis, aortic insufficiency, or aortic aneurysm.

LABEL: systolic heart failure
IAO_0000115: Heart failure caused by abnormal myocardial contraction during systole leading to defective cardiac emptying.

LABEL: tarsal tunnel syndrome
IAO_0000115: Tarsal tunnel syndrome is a nerve disorder that is characterized by pain in the ankle, foot, and toes. This condition is caused by compression of the posterior tibial nerve, which runs through a canal near the heel into the sole of the foot. When tissues around this nerve become inflamed, they can press on the nerve and cause the pain associated with tarsal tunnel syndrome.

LABEL: tethered spinal cord syndrome
hasExactSynonym: spinal cord syndrome|tethered cord
IAO_0000115: A progressive neurological disorder characterized by the limitation of movement of the spinal cord within the spine.
