Eye abnormalities (glaucoma, irregular iris pigmentation, hyperopia) have also been reported.

LABEL: distal trisomy 7p
hasExactSynonym: distal duplication 7p|distal trisomy type 7p|telomeric duplication 7p|trisomy 7pter
IAO_0000115: Distal trisomy 7p is a rare chromosomal anomaly syndrome, resulting from the partial duplication of the short arm of chromosome 7, with highly variable phenotype typically characterized by severe to profound psychomotor delay, intellectual disability, dysmorphic features (incl. dolichocephaly, microbrachycephaly, high and/or broad forehead, large anterior fontanel, hypertelorism, downslanting palpebral fissures, low-set, dysplastic ears, low, broad and prominent nasal bridge, abnormal palate, micro-/retrognathia), and hypotonia. LABEL: 8p inverted duplication/deletion syndrome
hasExactSynonym: Invdupdel(8p)|inverted 8p duplication/deletion syndrome
IAO_0000115: 8p inverted duplication/deletion [invdupdel(8p)] syndrome is a rare chromosomal anomaly characterized clinically by mild to severe intellectual deficit, severe developmental delay (psychomotor and speech development), hypotonia with tendency to develop progressive hypertonia and severe orthopedic problems over time, minor facial anomalies and agenesis of the corpus callosum.

LABEL: distal trisomy 2q
hasExactSynonym: distal duplication 2q|distal trisomy type 2q|telomeric duplication 2q|trisomy 2qter

LABEL: 3q26 microduplication syndrome
hasExactSynonym: Cornelia de Lange-like syndrome|dup(3)(q26)|dup(3q) syndrome|trisomy 3q26
IAO_0000115: 3q26 microduplication syndrome is a rare chromosomal anomaly characterized by prenatal and postnatal growth retardation, developmental delay, intellectual impairment, dysmorphic signs and variable combination of congenital anomalies, including cardiovascular, genitourinary and skeletal anomalies and spectrum of caudal malformations.

LABEL: distal trisomy 4q
hasExactSynonym: distal duplication 4q|distal trisomy type 4q|telomeric duplication 4q|trisomy 4qter
IAO_0000115: Distal trisomy 4q is a rare chromosomal anomaly syndrome, resulting from the partial duplication of the long arm of chromosome 4, with highly variable phenotype typically characterized by psychomotor delay, intellectual disability, craniofacial dysmorphism (microcephaly, low-set, prominent ears, downslanting palpebral fissures, hypertelorism, epicanthic folds, broad, prominent nasal bridge, high arched and cleft palate, micro-/retrognathia), seizures, as well as tooth and digital anomalies (clinodactyly, polydactyly). LABEL: distal trisomy 5q
hasExactSynonym: distal duplication 5q|distal trisomy type 5q|telomeric duplication 5q|trisomy 5qter
IAO_0000115: Distal trisomy 5q is a rare chromosomal anomaly syndrome, resulting from a partial duplication of the long arm of chromosome 5, characterized by short stature, moderate intellectual disability, and craniofacial dysmorphism (microcephaly, flat facies, large, low-set dysplastic ears, down-slanted, almond-shaped palpebral fissures, hypertelorism, epicanthal folds, small nose, long philtrum, small mouth with thin upper lip, and micrognathia). LABEL: distal trisomy 6q
hasExactSynonym: Chromosome 6, Partial Trisomy 6q|distal duplication 6q|distal trisomy type 6q|telomeric duplication 6q|trisomy 6qter
IAO_0000115: Distal trisomy 6q is a rare chromosomal anomaly syndrome resulting from the partial duplication of the long arm of chromosome 6, with highly variable phenotype, typically characterized by growth and developmental delay, intellectual disability, craniofacial dysmorphism (microcephaly, flat facial profile, frontal bossing, hypertelorism, downward-slanting palpebral fissures, flat nasal bridge, anteverted nares, bow shaped mouth, micrognathia), short webbed neck and joint contractures. Cardiac, urogenital, ophthalmologic and hand and foot anomalies, as well as umbilical hernia, spasticity, and seizures, are other features that have been reported.

LABEL: distal trisomy 8q
hasExactSynonym: distal duplication 8q|distal trisomy type 8q|telomeric duplication 8q|trisomy 8qter
IAO_0000115: Distal trisomy 8q is a rare chromosomal anomaly syndrome resulting from the partial duplication of the long arm of chromosome 8, with a highly variable phenotype, typically characterized by growth and developmental delay, intellectual disability, short stature, craniofacial dysmorphism (microcephaly, prominent forehead, hypertelorism, abnormal palpebral fissures, low-set, large ears, anteverted tip of nose, micro/retrognathia), congenital heart defects and skeletal and limb anomalies. Other reported features include ophthalmologic abnormalities (e.g. megalocornea), cryptorchidism, hypertrichosis, and neurologic manifestations (e.g. hypotonia, hearing loss, and seizures).

LABEL: ring chromosome 15

IAO_0000115: Ring chromosome 15 is a chromosome abnormality that affects growth, learning, and speech. People with ring chromosome 15 often have growth delays before and after birth, resulting in short stature; varying degrees of intellectual disability ; low muscle tone (hypotonia); craniofacial malformations; and limb abnormalities. Other symptoms might include congenital heart defects, kidney problems, congenital dislocation of the hips, and cafe-au-lait spots. Ring chromosome 15 is caused by an abnormal chromosome known as a ring chromosome 15 or r(15). A ring chromosome is a circular structure that occurs when a chromosome breaks in two places and the broken ends fuse together. The features of ring chromosome 15 appear to result from the loss (deletion) of genetic material from the long (q) arm of chromosome 15. Ring chromosome 15 is usually caused by spontaneous (de novo) errors very early in embryonic development. In rare cases, it is passed through families, either from a parent who also has a ring chromosome 15, or from a parent who has a balanced translocation. Treatment for ring chromosome 15 is focused on addressing the symptoms present in each individual and may require a team of medical specialists.

LABEL: chromosome 20 trisomy
IAO_0000115: Chromosome 20 trisomy, (also called trisomy 20) is a condition in which a fetus or individual has an extra full or partial copy of chromosome 20 in some or allof of his/her cells. An extra full copy of chromosome 20 in all of a person's cells is rare, and almost all fetuses with this do not survive past the first trimester ofpregnancy. The presence of an extra copyof only part of chromosome 20 is called partial trisomy 20; and an extra copy of chromosome 20 in only some of a person's cells is called mosaic trisomy 20. Mosaic trisomy 20 is the most common type of chromosome 20 trisomy and is one of the more common chromosomal abnormalities found during prenatal diagnostic testing. Studies have shown that the child is normal in the vast majority of prenatally diagnosed individuals. However, features that have been reported include spinal abnormalities (including spinal stenosis, vertebral fusion, and kyphosis), hypotonia (decreased muscle tone), life long constipation, sloped shoulders, and significant learning disabilities despite normal intelligence. Trisomy 20 usually results from an error that occurs when an egg or sperm cell develops (before fertilization); mosaic trisomy 20 usually results from errors in cell division soon after fertilization.

These clusters of colon cancer are likely due to a combination of gene(s) and other shared factors such as environment and lifestyle. High-risk cancer screening and other preventative measures such as prophylactic surgeries are typically recommended in people who have an increased risk for colon cancer based on their personal and/or family histories.

People with OPDM present with progressive eye and throat (pharyngeal) problems and involvement of the muscles of the lower legs and arms. Symptoms may include eyelid drooping (ptosis), swallowing difficulty, hoarse and nasal voice, leg and arm weakness, as well as muscle wasting in the face and in the legs and arms. Many people have respiratory problems due to respiratory muscle weakness. In rare cases, there is also hearing loss, as well as severe weakness in muscles of the forearms and thighs. As the disease progresses, other muscles may be affected. A blood exam may show an increased creatine kinase level and an abnormal EMG. Inheritance may be autosomal dominant or autosomal recessive. The specific cause is still unknown.

LABEL: prurigo nodularis
IAO_0000115: Prurigonodularis (PN) is a skin disease in which hard crusty lumps are formed on the skin that itches intensely. Repetitive rubbing, scratching, and touching results in more lesions in the skin. The itching is so intense that people scratch themselves to the point of bleeding or pain. The lumps formed in the skin are hard, and have about a half inch across, with a dry and rough top that is often scratched open. They tend to be located in the areas most easily reached and are worse on the outer sides: arms, shoulders and legs. The trunk, face and even palms can also be affected. The exact cause is unknown but some factors triggering PN include liver and kidneys problems, nervous and mental conditions and other skin diseases. Prurigo nodulares, in some cases, can be seen in other diseases such as lymphoma, chronic autoimmune cholestatic hepatitis, HIV infection, severe anemia,or a chronic kidney disease-related itching known as uremic pruritus. Treatment is very difficult, and may include corticoids, antihistaminic and other medication such as thalidomide and similar (Lenalidomide). In some cases, cryotherapy, photochemotherapy and habit reversal therapy for the itch-scratch cycle has improved the symptoms. PN can last for many years, and the itching is so intense that may affect all the everyday activities.

People who have undergone allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation are at an increased risk for developing HHV-6 encephalitis, particularly when umbilical cord blood stem cells are used. People with immune system disorders may also be at an increased risk for developing this infection. Signs and symptoms vary, but often include confusion, anterograde amnesia (difficulty learning new information following the onset of amnesia), short-term memory loss, and seizures.Diagnosis often involves lumbar puncture, virus testing, and MRI. EEG 's may also be recommendedwhen seizures are suspected. HHV-6 encephalitis is treated with an antiviral agent with activity against HHV-6. Long term outlook (chance of full recovery) can vary considerably depending individual patient factors.

Signs and symptoms typically develop when the narrowing of the opening is severe and may include chest pain (angina) or tightness; shortness of breath or fatigue (especially during exertion); feeling faint or fainting; heart palpitations; and heart murmur. IAO_0000115: Group of diseases encompassing a spectrum of disorders characterized by Warburg Micro Syndrome (characterized by eye, nervous system, and endocrine abnormalities) and Martsolf Syndrome phenotypes (characterized by similar ? but milder ? findings). The hallmark ophthalmologic findings are bilateral congenital cataracts, usually accompanied by microphthalmia, microcornea (diameter <10), and small atonic pupils. Individuals with Warburg micro syndrome have severe to profound intellectual disability (ID); those with Martsolf syndrome have mild to moderate ID. In Martsolf syndrome infantile hypotonia is followed primarily by slowly progressive lower-limb spasticity. Hypogonadism ? when present ? manifests in both syndromes, in males as micropenis and/or cryptorchidism and in females as hypoplastic labia minora, clitoral hypoplasia, and small introitus.

Chronic rejection can be mediated by either humoral or cellular mechanisms linked to memory/plasma cells and antibodies. The presence of tertiary lymphoid organs in the graft is a characteristic of this form of rejection.

LABEL: TNNT2-related cardiomyopathy
hasExactSynonym: TNNT2-related cardiomyopathy
IAO_0000115: A genetically heterogeneous cardiac disorder caused by pathogenic variants in the TNNT2 gene and inherited in an autosomal dominant manner. Affected individuals present with a spectrum of cardiomyopathy phenotypes, including dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM), hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM), restrictive cardiomyopathy (RCM), and left ventricular noncompaction (LVNC). Clinical features may include heart failure, ventricular arrhythmias, and sudden cardiac death. Overlapping or mixed cardiomyopathy phenotypes, as well as variable expressivity within families, have also been reported.

LABEL: KY-related neuromyopathy
hasExactSynonym: KY-related neuromyopathy
IAO_0000115: Any neuromyopathy in which the cause of the disease is mutation in the KY gene.

LABEL: oocyte/zygote/embryo maturation arrest 16

IAO_0000115: Any inherited oocyte maturation defect marked by early embryonic arrest and female infertility due to a varition in the PADI6 gene.

LABEL: dysplasia of the proximal femoral epiphyses
IAO_0000115: A developmental disorder affecting the growth and development of the proximal end of the femur (thigh bone) near the hip joint characterized by avascular necrosis of the femoral head, cystic changes of the femoral head, and/or sclerosis of the femoral head. It is a relatively milder form of the other skeletal disorders associated with COL2A1.

LABEL: Mycoplasmoides infection
hasExactSynonym: mycoplasmosis
IAO_0000115: A disease caused by infection with Mycoplasmoides.

LABEL: mosaic SMO syndrome
IAO_0000115: A somatic mosaic condition caused by a postzygotic mutation (c.1234 C>T p.Leu412Phe) in the SMO gene. Two overlapping clinical syndromes associated with this variant in SMO have been reported; Curry-Jones Syndrome (MIM:601707) and Happle-Tinschert Syndrome. The syndrome is characterized by cutaneous and skeletal manifestations such as linear hypo? or hyperpigmented lesions, basaloid follicular hamartomas, palmoplantar pitting, atrophoderma, hypertrichosis, polydactyly or syndactyly, rib anomalies (rudimentary ribs), and limb?length anomalies. Craniofacial and dental abnormalities such as dysmorphic facies, macrocephaly, craniosynostosis, jaw tumors (ameloblastoma) have also been reported. Additional abnormalities impacting the gastrointestinal, cerebral, ophthalmic, and gonadal organs should also be considered. Some of these features include anal anomaly, colonic adenocarcinoma, severe constipation, myelofibrosis and smooth muscle hamartomas, malrotation, medulloblastoma, cerebral malformations, developmental delay, cataract, microphthalmia, coloboma, glaucoma, and cryptorchidism.

LABEL: hypertensive urgency
hasExactSynonym: hypertensive crisis without acute organ damage|severely elevated blood pressure without acute organ damage
IAO_0000115: A hypertensive disorder that is characterized by marked elevation in blood pressure, such as systolic blood pressure greater than 180 mmHg or diastolic blood pressure greater than 110 mmHg, and without evidence of target organ damage, such as pulmonary edema, cardiac ischemia, neurologic deficits, or acute renal failure.

LABEL: mitral valve insufficiency
hasExactSynonym: insufficiency, mitral|mitral insufficiency|mitral valve incompetence|mitral valve insufficiency/ regurgitation
IAO_0000115: A mitral valve disorder characterized by incomplete valve closure.

LABEL: acquired porphyria
IAO_0000115: A porphyria disorder that is acquired during the lifetime of the individual.

LABEL: TP63-related ectodermal dysplasia spectrum with limb and orofacial malformations
IAO_0000115: Any developmental defect during embryogenesis in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the TP63 gene. This disease is characterized by variable ectodermal dysplasia, limb defects, and orofacial clefting.

LABEL: PIK3CA-related overgrowth spectrum
IAO_0000115: Any overgrowth syndrome resulting from pathogenic gain-of-function variants in the PIK3CA gene. The variants can be germline or somatic

LABEL: KCND2-related neurodevelopmental disorder with or without seizures
IAO_0000115: A neurodevelopmental disorder caused by variation in the KCND2 gene. This disorder is characterized by early-onset global developmental delay with impaired motor, speech and cognitive development. Patients often present muscle hypotonia, and less frequently, developmental epileptic encephalopathy, visual impairment and physical dysmorphisms.

LABEL: PIK3R2-related overgrowth spectrum
IAO_0000115: Any overgrowth syndrome resulting from pathogenic gain-of-function variants in the PIK3R2 gene. The variants can be germline or somatic

LABEL: CTR9-related neurodevelopmental disorder
IAO_0000115: Any neurodevelopmental disorder in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the CTR9 gene. This disorder is characterised by varying degrees of intellectual disability, neurodevelopmental delay, hypotonia, fatigability, behavioral abnormalities including autism spectrum disorder, anxiety and aggressive behavior, cardiac anomalies, and mild facial dysmorphism.

LABEL: CAMK2D-related neurodevelopmental disorder and dilated cardiomyopathy
IAO_0000115: A neurodevelopmental disorder caused by variation in the CAMK2D gene. This disorder is characterised by intellectual disability, speech and motor delay, behavioural problems and dilated cardiomyopathy. Patients often present brain structural anomalies and hypotonia, and less frequently, seizures.

LABEL: TRIP11-related skeletal dysplasia
IAO_0000115: Any skeletal dysplasia in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the TRIP11 gene. Reduced protein function in TRIP11 causes a spectrum of skeletal symptoms from a more mild phenotype, called ondontochondrodysplasia, with features including short stature and joint laxity to a more severe phenotype, called achondrogenesis type 1A, which presents as a lethal prenatal or neonatal skeletal dysplasia. The clinical severity of achondrogenesis compared to ondontochondrodysplasia is related to the residual function of the gene which is not currently possible to anticipate based on genotype alone. The phenotype cannot fully be predicted by genotype alone, evidenced by variants being reported with both phenotypes.

LABEL: IRF6-related condition
IAO_0000115: Van der Woude syndrome, popliteal pterygium syndrome, cleft lip with or without palate, or a spectrum of one or two of those conditions in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the IRF6 gene.

LABEL: PI4KA-related disorder
IAO_0000115: Any human disease in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the PI4KA gene. This disease is characterized primarily by neurologic dysfunction (limb spasticity, developmental delay, intellectual disability, seizures, ataxia, nystagmus), gastrointestinal manifestations (multiple intestinal atresia, inflammatory bowel disease), and combined immunodeficiency (leukopenia, variable immunoglobulin defects). Age of onset is typically antenatal or in early childhood; individuals can present with any combination of these features. Rare individuals present with later-onset hereditary spastic paraplegia. Brain MRI findings can include hypomyelinating leukodystrophy, cerebellar hypoplasia/atrophy, thin or dysplastic corpus callosum, and/or perisylvian polymicrogyria.

LABEL: PPFIA3-related neurodevelopmental disorder
IAO_0000115: A neurodevelopmental disorder caused by variation in the PPFIA3 gene. This disorder is characterised by developmental delay and intellectual disability. Most patients present variable additional features, including dysmorphisms, microcephaly or macrocephaly, hypotonia, autism spectrum disorder or autistic features, abnormal electroencephalogram, and epilepsy.

LABEL: infectious disease with sepsis
IAO_0000115: An infectious disease characterized by life-threatening organ dysfunction due to a dysreguated host response.

LABEL: cerebral artery stenosis
IAO_0000115: A cerebrovascular disorder characterized by an abnormal narrowing of a cerebral artery.

LABEL: intestinal fistula
IAO_0000115: An intestinal disorder characterized by an opening in the intestine to some epithelial surface.

LABEL: Enterococcus infectious disease
hasExactSynonym: Enterococcus caused disease or disorder
IAO_0000115: A bacterial disease caused by infection with Enterococcus.

LABEL: congenital myasthenic syndrome 4
IAO_0000115: Any postsynaptic congenital myasthenic syndrome in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the CHRNE gene.

LABEL: linkeropathy
IAO_0000115: Group of rare heritable connective tissue disorders, characterized by a variable degree of short stature, skeletal dysplasia, joint laxity, cutaneous anomalies, dysmorphism, heart malformation, and developmental delay. The LK genes encode for enzymes that add glycosaminoglycan chains onto proteoglycans via a common tetrasaccharide linker region.

LABEL: NDUFB11-related disorders
IAO_0000115: A group of rare genetic conditions caused by variants in the NDUFB11 gene. Presentation is heterogenous including neurologic, cardiac, ocular, and dermatological abnormalities.

LABEL: metastatic malignant neoplasm in the brain
IAO_0000115: A malignant neoplasm that has spread to the brain from another anatomic site.

LABEL: Sharpin-related autoinflammatory syndrome
hasExactSynonym: sharpenia
IAO_0000115: An autoinflammatory disease in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the Sharpin gene.

LABEL: GBA1-related Parkinson disease, susceptibility
IAO_0000115: A susceptibility or predisposition to Parkinsons disease in which the cause of the disease is the presence of a monoallelic pathogenic variant or risk allele in the GBA1 gene.

LABEL: dyneinopathy
IAO_0000115: A spectrum of diseases related to monoallelic variants in DYNC1H1 and characterized by variable neuromuscular and/or neurodevelopmental presentations. While not absolute, there appear to be genotype-phenotype correlations based on the location of the variant. Patients with variants in the stem domain of DYNC1H1 have been reported with a predominantly neuromuscular presentation, including congenital myopathy, spinal muscular atrophy, Charcot-Marie-Tooth (CMT), and less frequently, intellectual disability and autism. Patients with variants in the motor domain predominantly present with neurodevelopmental presentations including intellectual disability, seizures, malformations of cortical development (abnormal brain MRI findings such as pachygyria, heterotopias, enlarged ventricles, hypoplasia of CC, brain stem, cerebellum), autism, and less frequently, neuromuscular phenotypes.

LABEL: EN1-related dorsoventral syndrome
hasExactSynonym: ENDOVE syndrome|ENDOVES
IAO_0000115: A human mesomelic and rhizo-mesomelic dysplasia characterized by marked mesomelic shortening of the lower limbs, cutaneous syndactyly and nail abnormalities (placed on the palmar side of the finger, dysplastic or absent) in hands and feet due mutations in EN1 gene. Other clinical features may include genitourinary abnormalities (including bilateral cryptorchidism, vesicoureteral reflux, hydronephrosis, hypoplastic labia majora), spasticity and seizures.

LABEL: congenital muscular dystrophy without intellectual disability
hasExactSynonym: CMD without intellectual disability|CMD-no MR|congenital muscular dystrophy-dystroglycanopathy without intellectual disability
IAO_0000115: A congenital muscular dystrophy due to dystroglycanopathy characterized by a wide phenotypic spectrum which includes hypotonia and muscular weakness present at birth or early infancy, delayed or arrested motor development, and normal intellectual abilities with normal (or only mild abnormalities) neuroimaging studies. Feeding difficulties, joint and spinal deformities, and respiratory insufficiency may be associated. Decreased alpha-dystroglycan on immunohistochemical muscle staining and elevated serum creatine kinase are observed.

LABEL: IMPG1-related dominant retinopathy
hasExactSynonym: IMPG1-related dominant retinopathy
IAO_0000115: Any retinopathy caused by an autosomal dominant variant in the IMPG1 gene.

LABEL: IMPG1-related recessive retinopathy
hasExactSynonym: IMPG1-related recessive retinopathy
IAO_0000115: Any retinopathy caused by autosomal recessive variants in the IMPG1 gene.

LABEL: OFD1-related ciliopathy
hasExactSynonym: OFD1-related ciliopathy
IAO_0000115: Any ciliopathy caused by monoallelic, biallelic, or hemizygous variants in the OFD1 gene. This disease is characterized by a broad range of phenotypes including Joubert syndrome, orofaciodigital syndrome, retinitis pigmentosa, and primary ciliary dyskinesia.

LABEL: HGSNAT-related retinopathy
hasExactSynonym: HGSNAT-related retinopathy
IAO_0000115: Any isolated retinopathy caused by variants in the HGSNAT gene.

LABEL: FZD4-related exudative vitreoretinopathy
hasExactSynonym: FZD4-related exudative vitreoretinopathy
IAO_0000115: Any exudative vitreoretinopathy caused by a variant in the FZD4 gene.

LABEL: BBS7-related ciliopathy
hasExactSynonym: BBS7-related ciliopathy
IAO_0000115: Any ciliopathy caused by variants in the BBS7 gene.

LABEL: BBS1-related ciliopathy
hasExactSynonym: BBS1-related ciliopathy
IAO_0000115: Any ciliopathy caused by variants in the BBS1 gene.

LABEL: BBS12-related ciliopathy
hasExactSynonym: BBS12-related ciliopathy
IAO_0000115: Any ciliopathy caused by variants in the BBS12 gene.

LABEL: BBS2-related ciliopathy
hasExactSynonym: BBS2-related ciliopathy
IAO_0000115: Any ciliopathy caused by variants in the BBS2 gene.

LABEL: MKKS-related ciliopathy
hasExactSynonym: MKKS-related ciliopathy
IAO_0000115: Any ciliopathy caused by variants in the MKKS gene.

LABEL: IMPDH1-related retinopathy
hasExactSynonym: IMPDH1-related retinopathy
IAO_0000115: Any retinopathy caused by a variant in the IMPDH1 gene.

LABEL: PROM1-related recessive retinopathy
hasExactSynonym: PROM1-related recessive retinopathy
IAO_0000115: Any retinopathy caused by autosomal recessive variants in the PROM1 gene.

LABEL: PROM1-related dominant retinopathy
hasExactSynonym: PROM1-related dominant retinopathy
IAO_0000115: Any retinopathy caused by an autosomal dominant variant in the PROM1 gene.

LABEL: DHDDS-CDG
hasExactSynonym: DHDDS-CDG
IAO_0000115: Any congenital disorder of glycosylation caused by variants in the DHDDS gene.

LABEL: PRPH2-related retinopathy
hasExactSynonym: PRPH2-related retinopathy
IAO_0000115: Any retinopathy caused by a variant or variants in the PRPH2 gene.

LABEL: PROM1-related retinopathy
IAO_0000115: Any retinopathy caused by variants in the PROM1 gene.

LABEL: KCNV2-related retinopathy
hasExactSynonym: KCNV2-related retinopathy
IAO_0000115: Any retinopathy caused by variants in the KCNV2 gene.

LABEL: CRX-related retinopathy
hasExactSynonym: CRX-related retinopathy
IAO_0000115: Any retinopathy caused by a variant in the CRX gene.

LABEL: REEP6-related retinopathy
hasExactSynonym: REEP6-related retinopathy
IAO_0000115: Any retinopathy caused by variants in the REEP6 gene.

LABEL: MKS1-related ciliopathy
hasExactSynonym: MKS1-related ciliopathy
IAO_0000115: Any ciliopathy caused by variants in the MKS1 gene.

LABEL: SPATA7-related retinopathy
hasExactSynonym: SPATA7-related retinopathy
IAO_0000115: Any retinopathy caused by variants in the SPATA7 gene.

LABEL: CYP7B1-related disorder of oxysterol accumulation
hasExactSynonym: CYP7B1-related disorder of oxysterol accumulation
IAO_0000115: Any disorder of oxysterol accumulation caused by biallelic loss of function variants in the CYP7B1 gene. A disorder of oxysterol accumulation is a condition where there is an abnormal buildup of oxysterols, which are oxidized cholesterol derivatives, in the body.

LABEL: PURA-related severe neonatal hypotonia-seizures-encephalopathy syndrome
hasExactSynonym: PURA-related neurodevelopmental disorders
IAO_0000115: A rare neurologic disease characterized by neonatal hypotonia, global developmental delay, feeding difficulties, and often seizures or seizure-like episodes. Other frequently observed signs and symptoms include variable dysmorphic features, myopathic facies, respiratory problems, and visual abnormalities, such as strabismus or esotropia. Brain imaging may show delayed myelination and other white matter abnormalities.

LABEL: PLEC-related muscular dystrophy-epidermolysis bullosa simplex spectrum disorder
hasExactSynonym: PLEC-related muscular dystrophy-epidermolysis bullosa simplex spectrum disorder
IAO_0000115: A spectrum of disease associated with loss or disrupted function of the PLEC gene. These disorders primarily affect the skin and muscles, leading to a range of symptoms including skin blistering (EBS), progressive muscle weakness (muscular dystrophy), and other complications.

LABEL: TUBB4B-related ciliopathy
hasExactSynonym: TUBB4B-related ciliopathy
IAO_0000115: Any ciliopathy in which the cause of the disease is a variant in the TUBB4B gene. Please note that patient diagnoses can include disorders such as Leber congenital amaurosis and/or primary ciliary dyskinesia.

LABEL: FDXR-related optic atrophy mitochondrial dysfunction syndrome
hasExactSynonym: FDXR-related optic atrophy mitochondrial dysfunction syndrome
IAO_0000115: Any mitochondrial disorder in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the FDXR gene.

LABEL: MYCBP2-related developmental delay with corpus callosum defects
hasExactSynonym: MDCD|MYCBP2-related developmental delay with corpus callosum defects
IAO_0000115: Any neurodevelopmental disorder in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the MYCBP2 gene. This condition is characterized by variable corpus callosum defects consistent with dysgenesis, and a broad spectrum of neurobehavioural deficits including developmental delay, intellectual disability, epilepsy, and autistic features.

LABEL: ACO2-related optic atrophy with or without extraocular features
hasExactSynonym: ACO2-related optic atrophy with or without extraocular features
IAO_0000115: An optic atrophy in which the cause of the disease is monoallelic or biallelic variants in the ACO2 gene. ACO2 is a mitochondrial protein and thus, in addition to the optic atrophy features, features of this disease include abnormal mitochondrial morphology and can affect other organ systems. Extraocular features can include ataxia, spastic paraplegia, CNS abnormalities, neurodevelopmental phenotypes, and retinal degeneration.

LABEL: GRIN1-related complex neurodevelopmental disorder
hasExactSynonym: GRIN1-related developmental and epileptic encephalopathy|GRIN1-related neurodevelopmental disorder
IAO_0000115: A neurodevelopmental disorder caused by variation in the GRIN1 gene. It is characterized by mild-to-profound developmental delay/intellectual disability (DD/ID) in all affected individuals. Other common manifestations are epilepsy, muscular hypotonia, movement disorders, spasticity, feeding difficulties, and behavior issues. A subset of individuals show a malformation of cortical development consisting of extensive and diffuse bilateral polymicrogyria.

LABEL: PIK3R1-related immunodeficiency and SHORT syndrome
IAO_0000115: A group of disorders caused by a variation in PIK3R1 gene that produces a structurally altered but present p85? protein, disrupting PI3K signaling and leading to features such as immune deficiency, autoimmunity, short stature, and distinct facial and skeletal features.

LABEL: GRIN-related complex neurodevelopmental disorder
hasExactSynonym: GRIN-related encephalopathy|GRIN-related neurodevelopmental disorder|GRINpathies
IAO_0000115: A group of neurological and neurodevelopmental disorders caused by pathogenic variants in genes encoding subunits of the N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptor, including GRIN1, GRIN2A, GRIN2B, and GRIN2D. These disorders are associated with a spectrum of symptoms such as developmental delay, intellectual disability, epilepsy, movement disorders, speech and language impairment, and neuropsychiatric features. The clinical presentation and severity vary depending on the specific gene and mutation involved.

LABEL: GRIN2A-related complex neurodevelopmental disorder
IAO_0000115: A group of neurological and neurodevelopmental disorders caused by variants in the GRIN2A gene, characterized by a broad spectrum of symptoms including developmental delay or intellectual disability, epilepsy, speech and language impairments, movement disorders, and neuropsychiatric features.

LABEL: retinitis pigmentosa 7, digenic
IAO_0000115: A digenic form of retinitis pigmentosa resulting from a mutation in the PRPH2 gene and a null mutation of the ROM1 gene, leading to progressive degeneration of the retina and vision loss.

LABEL: Leber congenital amaurosis 18
hasExactSynonym: LCA18
IAO_0000115: A Leber congenital amaurosis that is caused by a variation in the PRPH2 gene.

LABEL: FGFR1-related Pfeiffer syndrome
hasExactSynonym: FGFR1-related Pfeiffer syndrome
IAO_0000115: Any Pfeiffer syndrome in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the FGFR1 gene.

LABEL: FGFR2-related Pfeiffer syndrome
hasExactSynonym: FGFR2-related Pfeiffer syndrome
IAO_0000115: Any Pfeiffer syndrome in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the FGFR2 gene.

LABEL: ACAN-related short stature spectrum
IAO_0000115: A rare semidominant genetic skeletal disorder caused by a variation in ACAN gene, characterized by short stature with variable phenotypic features which may include osteochondritis dissecans, advanced bone age, early-onset arthritis, and/or features consistent with spondyloepiphyseal dysplasia, Kimberley type caused by a single allele whereas biallelic variation can cause spondyloepimetaphyseal dysplasia, aggrecan type.

LABEL: schizoaffective depressive disorder
hasExactSynonym: schizoaffective disorder depressive type
IAO_0000115: A schizoaffective disorder marked by episodes of only major depression.

LABEL: INTU-related skeletal ciliopathy
IAO_0000115: A skeletal ciliopathy caused by a mutation in INTU gene and is characterized by facial dysmorphism, tongue nodules, developmental delay, and polydactyly. Some individuals may also present with short stature, or other variable syndromic findings.

LABEL: complex movement disorder with or without neurodevelopmental features
hasExactSynonym: complex movement disorder with or without neurodevelopmental features
IAO_0000115: A movement disorder characterized by having one or more different types of movement disorders, such as abnormal muscle tone, abnormal degree of movement, dystonia or torsion, which may occur with or without neurodevelopmental features, such as developmental delay or intellectual disability.

LABEL: inherited distal renal tubular acidosis
IAO_0000115: A form of distal renal tubular acidosis that is inherited.

LABEL: acquired distal renal tubular acidosis
IAO_0000115: A form of distal renal tular acidosis that develops secondary to another condition, usually disease or drug.

LABEL: ELANE-related neutropenia
IAO_0000115: Any neutropenia in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the ELANE gene.

LABEL: HAVCR2-related cancer predisposition
hasExactSynonym: HAVCR2-related SPTCL and/or HLH predisposition|HAVCR2-related subcutaneous panniculitis-like T-cell lymphoma and/or hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis predisposition
IAO_0000115: Hereditary cancer predisposition due to variation(s) in the HAVCR2 gene, which confers the predisposition to susceptibility to subcutaneous panniculitis-like T-cell lymphoma (SPTCL) and hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH). Affected individuals typically present with multiple subcutaneous nodules and systemic B symptoms.

LABEL: diffuse midline glioma, H3 K27-altered
hasExactSynonym: DMG, H3 K27-altered
IAO_0000115: A diffuse midline glioma characterized by H3 K27 alteration and usually either a histone H3 K27M mutation, an EGFR mutation, or aberrant overexpression of EZHIP. The prognosis is poor.

LABEL: FAM111A-related skeletal dysplasia
hasExactSynonym: FAM111A-related skeletal dysplasia
IAO_0000115: Any skeletal dysplasia in which the cause of the disease is a variation in FAM111A gene.

LABEL: FLNB-associated autosomal dominant filamin related bone disorder
hasExactSynonym: FLNB-associated autosomal dominant filamin related bone disorder
IAO_0000115: Any autosomal dominant filamin related bone disorder in which the cause of the disease is a variation in FLNB gene.

LABEL: systemic lupus erythematosus related to C1QA
hasExactSynonym: systemic lupus erythematosus related to C1QA
IAO_0000115: Any systemic lupus erythematosus in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the C1QA gene.

LABEL: systemic lupus erythematosus related to C1S
hasExactSynonym: systemic lupus erythematosus related to C1S
IAO_0000115: Any systemic lupus erythematosus in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the C1S gene.

LABEL: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 119
hasExactSynonym: DEE119|RNU2-2 developmental and epileptic encephalopathy|RNU2-2 syndrome|developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 119
IAO_0000115: A developmental and epileptic encephalopathy caused by the variants in the RNU2-2 gene, in which most reported variants are de novo. It is characterized by global developmental delay, hypotonia, impaired intellectual development, microcephaly, autistic behavior, and characteristically complex seizures.

LABEL: RNU5B-1 related neurodevelopmental disorder with seizures and joint laxity
hasExactSynonym: NEDSJL|RNU5B-1 related neurodevelopmental disorder with seizures and joint laxity|neurodevelopmental disorder with seizures and joint laxity
IAO_0000115: A neurodevelopmental disorder in which the cause of the disease is a variation in RNU5B-1 gene and is characterized by global developmental delay, hypotonia, macrocephaly, failure to thrive, abnormality of the eye, seizures, and joint laxity

LABEL: brain stem glioblastoma
IAO_0000115: A glioblastoma localized in the brain stem.

LABEL: systemic lupus erythematosus 18
hasExactSynonym: SLEB18|systemic lupus erythematosus related to PLD4
IAO_0000115: Any systemic lupus erythematosus in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the PLD4 gene.

LABEL: APP-related brain and vascular amyloidosis
hasExactSynonym: APP-related brain and vascular amyloidosis
IAO_0000115: A hereditary amyloidosis characterized by a spectrum of neurodegenerative and neurovascular phenotypes caused by pathogenic variant in the APP gene, resulting in an abnormal clearance of amyloid peptides, either by overproduction and decreased clearance of amyloid peptides, with deposition of amyloid in plaques and blood vessel walls. Affected individuals may present with progressive cognitive decline, cerebral vascular amyloidosis with white matter changes, and stroke with or without hemorrhage.

LABEL: ciliopathy-IFT74
hasExactSynonym: ciliopathy-IFT74
IAO_0000115: Any ciliopathy caused by variants in the IFT74 gene.

LABEL: CASK-related intellectual disability
hasExactSynonym: CASK-related disorder
IAO_0000115: A syndromic disorder in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the CASK gene. It is associated with a wide phenotypic spectrum ranging from mild-to-severe intellectual disability with or without nystagmus to moderate-to-profound intellectual disability and progressive microcephaly with pontine and cerebellar hypoplasia, often associated with seizures.

LABEL: ischemic stroke
hasExactSynonym: ischaemic stroke
IAO_0000115: A stroke disorder caused by obstruction of blood flow to the brain, due to thrombotic (local blood clot formation) or embolic (due to a blood clot or other material traveling from another site) event.

LABEL: hemorrhagic stroke
hasExactSynonym: haemorrhagic stroke
IAO_0000115: A stroke disorder caused by bleeding into the brain parenchyma or surrounding spaces. Hemorrhagic stroke includes intracerebral hemorrhage (bleeding within the brain tissue) and subarachnoid hemorrhage (bleeding in the space between the brain and the surrounding membrane).

LABEL: primary hyperthyroidism
IAO_0000115: A form of hyperthyroidism caused by overproduction of thyroid hormones (T3 and T4) due to pathology within the thyroid gland itself. Primary hyperthyroidism is characterized by low TSH levels and elevated T3/T4 levels.

LABEL: secondary hyperthyroidism
IAO_0000115: A form of hyperthyroidism caused by overproduction of thyroid hormones (T3 and T4) due to pathology outside of the thyroid gland, namely in the hypothalamus or pituitary gland. Secondary hyperthyroidism is characterized by elevated TSH levels and elevated T3/T4 levels.

LABEL: menstrual disorder
IAO_0000115: A disorder of the female reproductive system characterized by abnormalities in the menstrual cycle, including disturbances in timing, flow, or associated pain.

LABEL: NR5A1-related sex development disorder
hasExactSynonym: NR5A1-related sex development disorder
IAO_0000115: A reproductive system disorder caused by a variation in the NR5A1 gene, and characterized by varying phenotypes, including partial or complete gonadal dysgenesis, ambiguous genitalia, and spermatogenic failure in the male, and premature ovarian failure and ovarian dysgenesis in the female.

LABEL: CRYAB-related myofibrillar myopathy-cataract-cardiomyopathy spectrum disorder
hasExactSynonym: CRYAB-related myofibrillar myopathy-cataract-cardiomyopathy spectrum disorder
IAO_0000115: A syndromic disease caused by a variation in the CRYAB gene, and characterized by a spectrum of phenotypes including cardiomyopathy, cataract, and/or myopathy.

LABEL: reticular pseudodrusen
hasExactSynonym: RPD|SDD|subretinal drusenoid deposit
IAO_0000115: A retinal drusen characterized by subretinal deposits located internal to the retinal pigment epithelium, composed of material aggregations in the subretinal space between photoreceptors and the retinal pigment epithelium. These deposits have a bluish-white appearance by biomicroscopy and appear as hyperreflective lesions above the retinal pigment epithelium on optical coherence tomography.

LABEL: SYCE1-related gametogenic failure
hasExactSynonym: SYCE1-related gametogenic failure
IAO_0000115: An infertility disorder caused by variation in the SYCE1 gene. Affected males may present with non-obstructive azoospermia due to maturation arrest or meiotic failure, while affected females may present with primary ovarian insufficiency.

LABEL: TSEN2-related neurodevelopmental disorder with or without thrombotic microangiopathy
hasExactSynonym: TSEN2-related neurodevelopmental disorder with or without thrombotic microangiopathy
IAO_0000115: Any neurodevelopmental disorder in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the TSEN2 gene. This condition is associated with intellectual disability, growth delay, hypotonia, motor delay, ataxia, vision issues, cardiac features (including left ventricular hypertrophy), and pulmonary complications (such as acute respiratory distress and edema). It is also linked to brain structural anomalies such as pontine and cerebellar hypoplasia, cortical atrophy, and dilated ventricles. Renal features include proteinuria, thrombotic microangiopathy, end-stage kidney disease, and high-severity hypertension.

LABEL: RNU12-related minor spliceopathy disorder
hasExactSynonym: RNU12-related minor spliceopathy disorder
IAO_0000115: Any hereditary disease caused by a variation in the RNU12 gene, resulting in abnormal splicing of pre-mRNA via the minor spliceosome. The phenotypic spectrum includes craniosynostosis-anal anomalies-porokeratosis (CDAGS) syndrome and autosomal recessive spinocerebellar ataxia 33.

LABEL: systemic lupus erythematosus related to C1QC
hasExactSynonym: systemic lupus erythematosus related to C1QC
IAO_0000115: Any systemic lupus erythematosus in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the C1QC gene.

LABEL: systemic lupus erythematosus related to C1QB
hasExactSynonym: systemic lupus erythematosus related to C1QB
IAO_0000115: Any systemic lupus erythematosus in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the C1QB gene.

LABEL: AIP-related pituitary adenoma predisposition
hasExactSynonym: AIP-related pituitary adenoma predisposition|PAP|pituitary adenoma predisposition
IAO_0000115: A predisposition to pituitary adenoma due to variation(s) in the AIP gene.

LABEL: congenital insensitivity to pain
hasExactSynonym: CIP
IAO_0000115: A rare hereditary sensory and autonomic neuropathy characterized by the inability to perceive physical pain from birth. Affected individuals do not feel pain from injuries, burns, or infections and cannot detect harmful levels of heat, cold, or pressure, which can lead to repeated unrecognized injuries, impaired healing, and serious complications.

LABEL: Mediator complex-related neurodevelopmental disorder
IAO_0000115: A group of neurodevelopmental disorders caused by germline mutations in genes encoding subunits of the Mediator complex, a multi-protein assembly required for RNA polymerase II-dependent transcription. Shared phenotypic features include intellectual disability, speech and language delay, behavioral abnormalities, and variable structural brain anomalies.

LABEL: P2RY12-related platelet disorder, autosomal dominant
hasExactSynonym: P2RY12-related platelet disorder, autosomal dominant
IAO_0000115: A platelet type bleeding disorder of autosomal dominant inheritance caused by a variation in the P2RY12 gene that exerts a dominant negative effect by disrupting receptor homodimerization, leading to markedly impaired adenosine diphosphate induced platelet aggregation despite normal receptor expression. Affected individuals may exhibit severe bleeding symptoms due to defective amplification of platelet activation signals.

LABEL: GJB2-related disorder
hasExactSynonym: GJB2-related conditions
IAO_0000115: A genetic disorder caused by a variation in the GJB2 gene, primarily associated with hearing loss and/or deafness.

LABEL: GP1BA-related Bernard-Soulier syndrome
hasExactSynonym: Bernard-Soulier syndrome, type A1|GP1BA-related Bernard-Soulier syndrome
IAO_0000115: Any Bernard-Soulier syndrome in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the GP1BA gene, characterized by macrothrombocytopenia, reduced or absent expression of the GPIb-IX-V complex, and lifelong mucocutaneous bleeding. Affected individuals have large platelets with defective ristocetin-induced agglutination, reflecting the absence or dysfunction of GPIb? on the platelet surface. Variants in GP1BA impair production, trafficking, or incorporation of GPIb? into the receptor complex, preventing normal surface assembly and leading to the classic BSS adhesion defect.

LABEL: AARS2-related disorder
hasExactSynonym: AARS2-RD|AARS2-related disorders|alanyl-tRNA synthetase 2-related disorder
IAO_0000115: Any disease in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the AARS2 gene.

LABEL: EDA-related ectodermal dysplasia
hasExactSynonym: EDA-related ectodermal dysplasia
IAO_0000115: Any ectodermal dysplasia syndrome in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the EDA gene. Key features are hypohidrosis and hypotrichosis; the condition is also characterized by skin anomalies such as soft, thin, and dry skin, eczema, and pigmentation anomalies, as well as fine or brittle hair, dental anomalies such as hypodontia or oligodontia, vocal hoarseness, and hyperthermia susceptibility.

LABEL: THG1L-related disorder
IAO_0000115: Any hereditary disease in which the cause of the disease is a biallelic variation in the THG1L gene, encompassing a phenotypic spectrum that ranges from mild cerebellar ataxia with developmental delay to severe epileptic encephalopathy.

LABEL: THG1L-related epileptic encephalopathy
IAO_0000115: Any genetic developmental and epileptic encephalopathy in which the cause of the disease is a biallelic variation in the THG1L gene, characterized by profound developmental delay, microcephaly, intractable epilepsy, and cerebellar hypoplasia.

LABEL: SCN2A-related disorder
hasExactSynonym: SCN2A disorders|SCN2A related conditions|SCN2A-RD
IAO_0000115: Any nervous system disorder in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the SCN2A gene, which encodes the Nav1.2 sodium channel critical for neuronal function. SCN2A-related disorders span a broad phenotypic spectrum, from self-limited familial neonatal-infantile epilepsy through severe early-onset epileptic encephalopathies to later-onset epilepsy, autism spectrum disorder and intellectual disability without seizures, and episodic ataxia. Because Nav1.2 is essential for brain development as well as neuronal excitability, the presentation is predominantly neurodevelopmental where developmental delay, intellectual disability, and autism spectrum disorder are the most consistent features across the spectrum, present even in the absence of seizures. Clinical severity is broadly associated with the functional effect of the variant on the Nav1.2 channel, with gain-of-function changes typically linked to early severe epilepsy and loss-of-function changes more often associated with autism spectrum disorder and intellectual disability or intellectual disability, although these relationships are complex and not fully understood.

LABEL: EIF2B1-related permanent neonatal diabetes with transient liver dysfunction
hasExactSynonym: EIF2B1-related permanent neonatal diabetes with transient liver dysfunction
IAO_0000115: Any permanent neonatal diabetes mellitus in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the EIF2B1 gene, often accompanied by transient liver dysfunction.

LABEL: SMARCAL1-related tumor predisposition
hasExactSynonym: SMARCAL1-related tumor predisposition
IAO_0000115: Hereditary tumor predisposition due to variation(s) in the SMARCAL12 gene.

LABEL: Refsum disease, classic
hasExactSynonym: Refsum disease, adult, 1|adult Refsum disease due to PHYH|classic Refsum disease|hereditary motor and sensory neuropathy 4|hereditary sensory and motor neuropathy type 4
IAO_0000115: An adult Refsum disease in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the PHYH gene.

LABEL: phenylalanine hydroxylase deficiency
hasExactSynonym: PAH deficiency
IAO_0000115: A disorder of phenylalanine metabolism caused by biallelic variants in the PAH gene, encompassing the full spectrum of phenylalanine hydroxylase deficiency from mild hyperphenylalaninemia, which requires no treatment, to phenylketonuria, in which untreated blood phenylalanine concentrations warrant phenylalanine-restricted dietary treatment.

LABEL: SMARCB1-related tumor predisposition
hasExactSynonym: SMARCB1-related tumor predisposition
IAO_0000115: Hereditary tumor predisposition due to variation(s) in the SMARCB1 gene. Pathogenic germline loss-of-function variants confer autosomal dominant predisposition to schwannomas, meningiomas, rhabdoid tumors and other rare types of tumors. The phenotype correlates with the variant's degree of loss of function: the schwannomatosis phenotype is more commonly observed with partial loss-of-function or hypomorphic variants, while the rhabdoid tumor phenotype is more commonly associated with complete loss-of-function variants.

LABEL: severe chronic neutropenia
hasExactSynonym: neutropenia, severe chronic
IAO_0000115: A neutropenia characterized by persistent absolute neutrophil count below 0.5 x 10^9/L lasting for at least 3 months, not explained by medication use, infection or another underlying condition, and associated with recurrent and potentially life-threatening bacterial infections. The major clinical subtypes include congenital, cyclic, idiopathic, and autoimmune neutropenia, which share common diagnostic evaluation, treatment strategies, and long-term follow-up.

LABEL: severe idiopathic neutropenia
IAO_0000115: An idiopathic form of severe chronic neutropenia that cannot be classified as congenital, cyclic or autoimmune neutropenia, and is not explained by drug exposure, bone marrow failure, malignancy or systemic autoimmune disease. Symptoms are usually less severe than in congenital neutropenia, but infections can be life-threatening in some patients.

LABEL: severe autoimmune neutropenia
IAO_0000115: An autoimmune form of severe chronic neutropenia in which neutrophil-specific antibodies increase the destruction of circulating neutrophils, in the absence of systemic autoimmune disease. It is most common in children aged 6 months to 4 years, and it can also occur in adults. Serious bacterial infections are infrequent.

LABEL: fibrous dysplasia/McCune-Albright syndrome
hasExactSynonym: FD/MAS|FD/MAS spectrum|FD/MAS syndrome|Fibrous Dysplasia / McCune-Albright Syndrome|Fibrous dysplasia/McCune-Albright spectrum
IAO_0000115: A skeletal system disorder caused by a variation in the GNAS gene, characterized by involvement of the skin, skeleton and certain endocrine organs. Fibrous dysplasia ranges from an isolated monostotic lesion to severe polyostotic disease. McCune-Albright syndrome is diagnosed when fibrous dysplasia occurs with at least one extra-skeletal feature, or when two or more extra-skeletal features occur alone. The condition is not inherited. The signs and symptoms associated with the disorder vary greatly from person to person, depending upon the specific body cells and tissues that are affected by the gene variant.

LABEL: compressive optic neuropathy
IAO_0000115: An optic nerve disorder caused by mechanical compression of the optic nerve or chiasm along its course, for example by orbital or intracranial tumours, sinus mucoceles or thyroid eye disease, resulting in progressive visual loss.

LABEL: secondary glaucoma
IAO_0000115: A glaucoma in which elevation of intraocular pressure results from an identifiable pathophysiological mechanism, such as intraocular inflammation, pigment dispersion, hemorrhage, trauma, corticosteroid use or elevated episcleral venous pressure, in contrast to primary glaucoma. Secondary glaucomas form a heterogeneous group of diseases.

LABEL: FBN1-related geleophysic and acromelic dysplasia
hasExactSynonym: FBN1-related geleophysic and acromelic dysplasia
IAO_0000115: Any skeletal dysplasia in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the FBN1 gene. This condition is characterized by short stature, delayed bone age, stiff joints, acromegaly, hip dysplasia, respiratory issues (including sleep apnea and asthma), short hands/feet, and facial anomalies (such as a long philtrum, bulbous nose, broad/depressed nasal bridge, thick lips, and elongation of the eyelashes).

LABEL: CAMK2A-related neurodevelopmental disorder
IAO_0000115: Any neurodevelopmental disorder in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the CAMK2A gene.

LABEL: NUS1-related disorder
hasExactSynonym: NUS1 related disorders|NUS1-related disorders
IAO_0000115: Any hereditary disease in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the NUS1 gene. Biallelic variants cause a congenital disorder of glycosylation. Heterozygous variants, including deletions, cause a complex neurological disorder with developmental delay, intellectual disability, epilepsy including developmental and epileptic encephalopathy and progressive myoclonus epilepsy, and movement disorders including myoclonus, dystonia, ataxia, tremor and parkinsonism. Rare NUS1 variants have also been associated with Parkinson's disease.

LABEL: TUBB-related tubulinopathy
hasExactSynonym: TUBB-related tubulinopathy
IAO_0000115: Any tubulinopathy in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the TUBB gene. Heterozygous TUBB variants cause two overlapping developmental disorders, complex cortical dysplasia with other brain malformations (CDCBM) and congenital symmetric circumferential skin creases (CSCSC), also known as circumferential skin creases Kunze type. The clinical findings are diverse and include abnormalities of the cortex, basal ganglia, corpus callosum, brain stem and cerebellum, microcephaly, intellectual disability, facial dysmorphism, excess skin folding and growth retardation.

LABEL: cystic fibrosis-related diabetes
hasExactSynonym: CF-related diabetes|CFRD
IAO_0000115: A form of diabetes mellitus unique to individuals with cystic fibrosis (CF), arising primarily from progressive fibrotic destruction of the pancreas leading to insulin deficiency, with additional contributions from insulin resistance. CFRD affects approximately 20% of adolescents and 40-50% of adults with CF. It shares features with both type 1 and type 2 diabetes but is a distinct clinical entity with its own diagnostic criteria and management guidelines.

LABEL: CFTR-related disorder
hasExactSynonym: CFTR-RD
IAO_0000115: A disease associated with CFTR (cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator) dysfunction that does not fulfill the diagnostic criteria for cystic fibrosis (CF). CFTR-related disorders are characterized by clinical evidence of CFTR dysfunction limited to a single organ system, a sweat chloride concentration below the CF diagnostic threshold (typically less than 60 mmol/L), and CFTR genotypes that often include at least one variant not classified as CF-causing. Recognized CFTR-related disorders include congenital bilateral absence of the vas deferens (CBAVD), acute recurrent or chronic pancreatitis, and disseminated bronchiectasis.

LABEL: cystic fibrosis-related liver disease
hasExactSynonym: CF liver disease|CF-related liver disease|CFLD
IAO_0000115: A liver disorder that arises as a consequence of cystic fibrosis. Cystic fibrosis-related liver disease encompasses a spectrum of hepatobiliary abnormalities caused by CFTR dysfunction in cholangiocytes, including focal biliary cirrhosis, multilobular biliary cirrhosis, hepatic steatosis, and cholangiopathy. It is a significant cause of non-pulmonary morbidity and mortality in CF, affecting approximately 5-10% of CF patients.

IAO_0000115: An Ehlers-Danlos syndrome characterized by skin hyperextensibility with velvety skin texture and absence of atrophic scarring, generalized joint hypermobility with or without recurrent dislocations, and easily bruised skin or spontaneous.

LABEL: kyphoscoliotic Ehlers-Danlos syndrome
hasExactSynonym: kEDS|kyphoscoliotic EDS
IAO_0000115: A rare systemic disease for which two subtypes exist, either related to the gene PLOD1 or FKBP14, and for which the clinically overlapping characteristics include congenital muscle hypotonia, congenital or early-onset kyphoscoliosis (progressive or non-progressive), and generalized joint hypermobility with dislocations/subluxations (in particular of the shoulders, hips, and knees). Additional features which may occur in both subtypes are skin hyperextensibility, easy bruising of the skin, rupture/aneurysm of a medium-sized artery, osteopenia/osteoporosis, blue sclerae, umbilical or inguinal hernia, chest deformity, marfanoid habitus, talipes equinovarus, and refractive errors. Gene-specific features, with variable presentation, are additionally observed in each subtype.

LABEL: plant ovule
IAO_0000115: A plant organ (PO:0009008) that has as parts a nucellus (PO:0020020) in which a female gametophyte (PO:0025279) is located, one or two integuments (PO:0020021), and a funicle (PO:0020006).

LABEL: megaspore
hasExactSynonym: megaspora|???
IAO_0000115: The larger, in general, of the two kinds of spores produced after meiosis in the life cycle of a heterosporous plant, and on germination giving rise to the female gametophyte (embryo sac).

LABEL: nucellus
IAO_0000115: A megasporangium (PO:0025201) in a seed plant, composed of fleshy subepidermal tissue that is part of a plant ovule (PO:0020003) and surrounds a megasporocyte (PO:0000431).

LABEL: cotyledon
hasExactSynonym: seed leaf
IAO_0000115: A vascular leaf (PO:0009025) formed at the first shoot node (PO:0005004) of a plant embryo (PO:0009009) or a seedling (PO:0000003).

LABEL: radicle
IAO_0000115: An embryo root (PO:0000045) that is the basal continuation of a hypocotyl (PO:0020100) in a plant embryo (PO:0009009) or a seedling (PO:0000003).

LABEL: mesocotyl
IAO_0000115: A shoot internode that is the part of an embryo axis or the stem of a seedling above the scutellum and below the coleoptile.

LABEL: petiole
IAO_0000115: A stalk of a leaf.

LABEL: leaf lamina
IAO_0000115: A phyllome lamina (PO:0025396) that is the part of a leaf (PO:0025034) exclusive of the petiole (PO:0020038) or leaf sheath (PO:0020104), if either is present.

LABEL: leaf base
IAO_0000115: A phyllome base (PO:0025140) that is part of a leaf (PO:0025034).

LABEL: microspore
hasExactSynonym: microspora|???
IAO_0000115: The smaller, in general, of the two kinds of spores produced after meiosis in the life cycle of a heterosporous plant, and on germination giving rise to the male gametophyte.

LABEL: microgametophyte vegetative cell
IAO_0000115: A native plant cell (PO:0025606) that is the larger cell of a microgametophyte (PO:0025280) in seed plants. It does not divide further and develops into a pollen tube cell (PO:0025195).

LABEL: hypocotyl
IAO_0000115: A stem internode (PO:0020142) below the cotyledonary node (PO:0025321) and transitional to a root (PO:0009005) of a plant embryo (PO:0009009) or a seedling (PO:0000003).

LABEL: flag leaf
hasExactSynonym: boot leaf
IAO_0000115: The last mature leaf before the inflorescence in a cereal crop plant.

LABEL: leaf sheath
IAO_0000115: A tubular portion of the leaf surrounding the stem, as in the Poaceae.

LABEL: lateral root
IAO_0000115: A root (PO:0009005) that develops from a lateral root primordium (PO:0000016) that is part of another root on the same plant.

LABEL: root cap
IAO_0000115: A portion of root parenchyma (PO:0025095) tissue that is part of the root tip (PO:0000025) and covers the root apical meristem (PO:0020147).

LABEL: root stele
IAO_0000115: A stele that is part of a root

LABEL: tassel inflorescence
IAO_0000115: A staminate inflorescence (PO:0025601) in Zea species that bears the tassel spikelet (PO:0006309) on a terminal inflorescence axis (PO:0020122).

LABEL: primary root
hasExactSynonym: tap root
IAO_0000115: A root (PO:0009005) that develops directly from a seedling radicle (PO:0020127).

LABEL: lateral root cap
hasExactSynonym: peripheral cells
IAO_0000115: A portion of root parenchyma tissue that is part of a root cap and is parallel to the sides of a root axis.

LABEL: columella root cap cell
IAO_0000115: Cell that constitutes the central part of the root cap, arranged in longitudinal files.

LABEL: ear inflorescence
IAO_0000115: A pistillate inflorescence (PO:0025598) in Zea species that is highly compacted and bears the ear spikelets (PO:0006320) on a lateral inflorescence axis (PO:0020122).

LABEL: stem node
IAO_0000115: A shoot node that is part of a stem.

LABEL: stem internode
IAO_0000115: A shoot internode that is part of a stem.

LABEL: apical meristem
IAO_0000115: A maximal portion of meristem tissue (PO:0009013) located at a shoot apex (PO:0000037) or root tip (PO:0000025).

LABEL: root apical meristem
hasExactSynonym: apical root meristem|root meristem - apical

LABEL: shoot apical meristem
hasExactSynonym: apical shoot meristem|shoot meristem - apical

LABEL: quiescent center
IAO_0000115: A portion of meristem tissue (PO:0009013) that is part of a root apical meristem (PO:0020147) and consists of mitotically and metabolically inactive cells and is located behind the protoderm (PO:0006210) of the root (PO:0009005).

LABEL: cardinal organ part
hasExactSynonym: cardinal part of plant organ
IAO_0000115: A cardinal part of multi-tissue plant structure (PO:0025498) that is a proper part of a plant organ (PO:0009008) and includes portions of plant tissue (PO:0009007) of at least two different types.

LABEL: collective leaf structure
hasExactSynonym: leaf whorl|rosette

LABEL: shoot axis
IAO_0000115: A plant axis (PO:0025004) that is part of a shoot system (PO:0009006).

LABEL: leaf
IAO_0000115: A phyllome (PO:0006001) that is not associated with a reproductive structure.

LABEL: embryo sac
IAO_0000115: A megagametophyte (PO:0025279) that is located in a plant ovary ovule (PO:0025490).

LABEL: phyllid
IAO_0000115: leaf of a moss or liverwort

LABEL: pollen sperm cell
IAO_0000115: A plant sperm cell (PO:0000084) that is part of the pollen (PO:0025281).

LABEL: plant anatomical entity
hasExactSynonym: plant component
IAO_0000115: An anatomical entity that is or was part of a plant.

LABEL: leaf tip
hasExactSynonym: leaf lamina tip
IAO_0000115: A phyllome tip (PO:0025141) that is part of a leaf apex (PO:0020137).

LABEL: basal endosperm transfer layer
IAO_0000115: A portion of plant tissue that is part of an endosperm and is composed of basal endosperm transfer cells.

LABEL: stele
IAO_0000115: A cardinal organ part (PO:0025001) that is the central column of a plant axis that consists of the primary vascular tissue and associated ground tissue.

LABEL: vegetative shoot apex
IAO_0000115: A shoot apex PO:0000037) that has as part a vegetative shoot apical meristem (PO:0008016).

LABEL: megagametophyte
IAO_0000115: A whole plant in the gametophyte development stage (PO:0028003) that produces only plant egg cells (PO:0020094).

LABEL: microgametophyte
hasExactSynonym: male gametophyte
IAO_0000115: A whole plant (PO:0000003) in the gametophyte development stage (PO:0028003) that produces plant sperm cells (PO:0000084).

LABEL: pollen
hasExactSynonym: pollen grain
IAO_0000115: A microgametophyte (PO:0025280) that develops from a microspore (PO:0020048) is located in a pollen sac (PO:0025277).

LABEL: corm
IAO_0000115: A rounded thick modified underground stem base bearing membranous or scaly leaves and buds and acting as a vegetative reproductive structure.

LABEL: coleorhiza emergence stage
IAO_0000115: A root development stage during which a coleorhiza emerges from the seed coat.

LABEL: fruit formation stage
IAO_0000115: A fruit development stage (PO:0001002) that begins with the formation of a plant zygote (PO:0000423) that is contained in the fruit (PO:0009001) being studied and ends when that fruit's fruit ripening stage (PO:0025502) begins.

LABEL: fruit ripening stage
IAO_0000115: A fruit development stage (PO:0001002) during which a single fruit (PO:0009001) participates in the process of fruit ripening (GO:0009835).

LABEL: fruit size up to 10% stage
IAO_0000115: A fruit formation stage (PO:0025501) that begins when the plant cells (PO:0009002) in a fruit (PO:0009001) begin to divide or expand, and ends when the fruit has reached 10% of its final size.

LABEL: fruit size 30 to 50% stage
IAO_0000115: A fruit formation stage (PO:0025501) that spans the interval when a fruit (PO:0009001) has reached 30 to 50% of its final size.

LABEL: fruit size 50 to 70% stage
IAO_0000115: A fruit formation stage (PO:0025501) that spans the interval when a fruit (PO:0009001) has reached 50 to 70% of its final size.

LABEL: fruit size 70% to final size stage
IAO_0000115: A fruit formation stage (PO:0025501) that spans begins when a fruit (PO:0009001) has reached 70% of its final size and ends when a fruit has reached its final size and a fruit ripening stage (PO:0025502) begins.

LABEL: tuber
IAO_0000115: A plant axis (PO:0025004) that is radially enlarged.

LABEL: floral organ formation stage
hasExactSynonym: flower morphogenesis stage
IAO_0000115: A flower development stage (PO:0007615) that occurs in an individual flower (PO:000904) during the interval between the onset of a floral organ meristem development stage (PO:0007601) and the onset of a flowering stage (PO:0007616).

LABEL: pistillate inflorescence
hasExactSynonym: carpellate inflorescence|female inflorescence
IAO_0000115: An inflorescence (PO:0009049) that includes as part only pistillate flowers (PO:0025599).

LABEL: staminate inflorescence
hasExactSynonym: male inflorescence
IAO_0000115: An inflorescence (PO:0009049) that includes as part only staminate flowers (PO:0025600).

LABEL: native plant cell
IAO_0000115: A plant cell (PO:0009002) that is either part of a multicellular whole plant (PO:0000003) 'in vivo' or a unicellular organism 'in natura' (i.e. part of a natural environment).

LABEL: rosette
IAO_0000115: A collective leaf structure (PO:0025022) consisting of a group of rosette leaves (PO:0000014), generally borne at the base of the plant, that are separated by very short stem internodes (PO:0020142).

LABEL: sporophyte development stage
hasExactSynonym: Arabidopsis developmental stage|sporophytic phase
IAO_0000115: A whole plant development stage that has as primary participant a whole plant during the interval between fertilization (or apogamy) and death.

LABEL: protonema
IAO_0000115: A portion of chlorenchyma tissue that develops directly from a spore and grows by division of an apical cell to form filaments that are one cell wide and dichotomously branching.

LABEL: chloronema
hasExactSynonym: chloronemata|portion of chloronema tissue
IAO_0000115: A portion of protonema tissue that consists of only chloronema cells.

LABEL: meristematic apical cell
hasExactSynonym: apical cell
IAO_0000115: A single meristematic cell (PO:0004010) at the tip of a plant structure where apical growth occurs.

LABEL: gametophyte meristematic apical cell
hasExactSynonym: gametophyte apical cell|gametophyte apical initial|gametophytic meristematic apical cell
IAO_0000115: An apical cell that is part of a whole plant in the gametophytic phase.

LABEL: sporophyte meristematic apical cell
hasExactSynonym: sporophytic meristematic apical cell
IAO_0000115: A meristematic apical cell that is part of a whole plant in the sporophytic phase.

LABEL: thallus
IAO_0000115: A plant body that is characteristic of thallophytes , lacks differentiation into distinct members (as stem, leaves, and roots), and does not grow from an apical point.|a primitive plant body of gametophytes that has not differentiated into roots, stems or leaves

LABEL: E3 ubiquitin ligase SFC complex Skp1 subunit
IAO_0000115: A protein that has a core domain composition consisting of an N-terminal Skp1 family, tetramerisation domain (Pfam:PF03931) followed by a Skp1 family, dimerisation domain (Pfam:PF01466). Skp1 proteins bind several F-box-containing proteins, and are involved in the ubiquitin protein degradation pathway.

LABEL: HLH DNA-binding protein inhibitor
hasExactSynonym: DNA-binding protein inhibitor ID
IAO_0000115: A protein that belongs to the clade D of the bHLH proteins (see PMID:20219281) with a core domain composition consisting of a helix-loop-helix DNA-binding domain (Pfam:PF00010) (HLH), common to the basic HLH family of transcription factors, but lacking the DNA binding domain to the consensus E box response element (CANNTG). By binding to basic HLH transcription factors, proteins in this class regulate gene expression.
