IAO_0000115: Quantification of the ratio between absolute lymphocyte count and absolute monocyte count.

LABEL: peritoneal solute transfer rate
hasExactSynonym: peritoneal transport rate
IAO_0000115: Quantification of the rate at which small molecules cross the peritoneal membrane typically measured as the ratio of the concentration of creatinine in the dialysate at 4 hours of a dwell of dialysate solution to that in the plasma (4-hr D/P creatinine).

LABEL: response to peritoneal dialysis
IAO_0000115: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a peritoneal dialysis.

LABEL: complement factor H-related protein 4 measurement
hasExactSynonym: CFHL4 protein measurement|FHR-4 protein measurement|FHR4 protein measurement
IAO_0000115: Quantification of the amount of complement factor H-related protein 4 in a sample.

LABEL: complement factor H-like 1 protein measurement
hasExactSynonym: FHL-1 protein measurement
IAO_0000115: Quantification of complement factor H-like 1 protein in a sample.

LABEL: response to cosmetics
IAO_0000115: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a cosmetic product stimulus.

LABEL: primary dental caries
IAO_0000115: The decay of any primary tooth, in which it becomes softened, discolored, and/or porous.

LABEL: permanent dental caries
IAO_0000115: The decay of any permanent tooth, in which it becomes softened, discolored, and/or porous.

LABEL: spatial proteomics
IAO_0000115: An assay that allows for visualization and quantification of proteins or associated antibodies used for evaluating in situ protein spatial distribution.

LABEL: PhenoCycler-Fusion
IAO_0000115: A spatial discovery system where whole-slide staining of tissues using pre-designed or custom antibody panels are imaged through automated fluidics (PhenoCycler) and high-speed image acquisition (PhenoImager).

LABEL: PhenoCycler
IAO_0000115: An automated fluidics system that uses oligonucleotide conjugated antibodies for tissue staining, followed by iterative cycles of applying fluorophore-conjugated reporter oligonucletides and gentle washing to generate multiplexed imaging data.

LABEL: BD Rhapsody Whole Transcriptome Analysis
hasExactSynonym: BD Rhapsody WTA
IAO_0000115: A BD Biosciences-based technology that sequences mRNA from the 3' end in an unbiased manner.

LABEL: BD Rhapsody Targeted mRNA
IAO_0000115: A BD Biosciences-based technology that utilizes multiplex PCR to sequence mRNA from the 3' end of specific genes from a predetermined panel.

LABEL: Abseq
IAO_0000115: A method that uses DNA-tagged antibodies to quantify proteins in single cells.

LABEL: ExSeq
hasExactSynonym: expansion sequencing
IAO_0000115: A spatial transcriptomics assay that involves physically expanding specimens with polymer- and hydrogel-based systems followed by in situ sequencing.

LABEL: targeted ExSeq
IAO_0000115: A spatial transcriptomics assay that involves physically expanding specimens with polymer- and hydrogel-based systems followed by targeted padlock probe hybridization, amplification, and in situ sequencing of padlock barcode.

LABEL: untargeted ExSeq
IAO_0000115: A spatial transcriptomics assay that involves physically expanding specimens with polymer- and hydrogel-based systems followed by reverse transcription, amplification, and in situ sequencing of untargeted RNA using FISSEQ.

LABEL: transvaginal ultrasound-guided oocyte retrieval
hasExactSynonym: ultrasound-guided transvaginal needle aspiration of follicles
IAO_0000115: A surgical technique used by medical professionals to extract mature eggs directly from an ovary with the guidance of ultrasound imaging.

LABEL: TruDrop
hasExactSynonym: TruSeq-inDrop
IAO_0000115: A droplet-based microfluidic library construction platform based on inDrop that incorporates dual-indexing to detect index-hopping and standard Illumina sequencing primers for high-throughput sequencing.

LABEL: GEXSCOPE technology
IAO_0000115: A microwell-based technology developed by Singleron to prepare mRNA from single cells or single nuclei and generate a next generation sequencing (NGS) library for high-throughput sequencing.

LABEL: library preparation for spatial transcriptomics
IAO_0000115: The library preparation step of a spatial transcriptomics assay.

LABEL: oral rinse collection
IAO_0000115: A saliva collection method where a solution such as a saline solution or other solution is used to rinse the mouth before collection of saliva.

LABEL: ECCITE-seq
hasExactSynonym: expanded CRISPR-compatible CITE-seq|expanded CRISPR-compatible cellular indexing of transcriptomes and epitopes by sequencing
IAO_0000115: The collective capabilities of CITE-seq and Cell Hashing adapted for compatibility with the 5P / V(D)J single cell kit from 10x Genomics, to allow researchers to perform sample multiplexing, doublet detection and protein detection together with 5? gene expression and V(D)J reconstruction.

LABEL: PacBio Sequel II system
hasExactSynonym: Pacific BioSciences Sequel II
IAO_0000115: The PacBio Sequel II system is a high-throughput, long-read sequencing machine developed by PacBio.

LABEL: Smart-seq v4
hasExactSynonym: SMART-Seq v4
IAO_0000115: Library construction method using SMART (Switching Mechanism at the 5' end of the RNA Template) to generate high-quality cDNA from ultra-low amounts of total RNA or directly from multiple intact cells (<1,000 cells). Smart-seq v4 improves upon the Smart-seq2 method by incorporating both the novel use of locked nucleic acid (LNA) technology and an optimized template switching oligo.

LABEL: pseudo-bulk aggregation of single-cell ATAC-seq data
hasExactSynonym: pseduo-bulk scATAC-seq data
IAO_0000115: A processed matrix generation method that involves combining (binary or quantitative) single-cell ATAC seq data from multiple cells within the same biological sample and/or cell types, depending on the intended downstream values. Ideally, aggregation is done within predefined regions of the genome e.g., using called peaks or tiles across the genome. The aggregated profiles can then be used in the same manner as bulk ATAC-seq or DNase-seq data.

LABEL: BGI MGISEQ-2000
IAO_0000115: A next-generation sequencing (NGS) sequencer from Beijing Genomics Institute (BGI) based on DNA nanoball (DNB) and probe-anchor synthesis (cPAS) technology, which were also used in the previous version of the BGISEQ-500 device; however, the reagents for MGISEQ-2000 have been refined and the platform utilizes updated software.

LABEL: ONT PromethION 2 Solo
hasExactSynonym: ONT P2 Solo
IAO_0000115: The ONT PromethION 2 Solo is a compact modular sequencing unit developed by Oxford Nanopore Technologies that can run up to two PromethION flow cells and connect to ONT GridION Mk1 devices.

LABEL: autosomal recessive Emery-Dreifuss muscular dystrophy
hasExactSynonym: EDMD3|Emery-Dreifuss muscular dystrophy, autosomal recessive
IAO_0000115: Autosomal recessive form of Emery-Dreifuss muscular dystrophy.

LABEL: familial mesial temporal lobe epilepsy with febrile seizures
hasExactSynonym: febrile seizures, familial, type 11
IAO_0000115: A rare, genetic, familial partial epilepsy disease characterized by simple partial seizures, complex partial seizures and/or secondarily generalized seizures, originating from the inner aspect of the temporal lobe, associated with an antecedant history of febrile seizures, ocurring in various members of a family. Hippocampal abnormalities (e.g. hippocampal sclerosis) may also be associated.

LABEL: autosomal recessive optic atrophy
IAO_0000115: A rare hereditary optic atrophy characterized by an early onset of bilateral optic nerve degeneration without other systemic features. Clinical manifestations include pallor of the optic disks, severe but slowly progressing visual impairment, and in some patients also paracentral scotoma, photophobia and dyschromatopsia.

LABEL: autosomal dominant pure spastic paraplegia
hasExactSynonym: autosomal dominant pure HSP|autosomal dominant pure SPG|autosomal dominant pure hereditary spastic paraplegia|autosomal dominant uncomplicated HSP|autosomal dominant uncomplicated SPG|autosomal dominant uncomplicated spastic paraplegia|pure hereditary spastic paraplegia, autosomal dominant
IAO_0000115: Autosomal dominant form of pure hereditary spastic paraplegia.

LABEL: autosomal recessive complex spastic paraplegia
hasExactSynonym: autosomal recessive complex HSP|autosomal recessive complex SPG|autosomal recessive complex hereditary spastic paraplegia|autosomal recessive complicated HSP|autosomal recessive complicated SPG|autosomal recessive complicated spastic paraplegia|complex hereditary spastic paraplegia, autosomal recessive
IAO_0000115: Autosomal recessive form of complex hereditary spastic paraplegia.

LABEL: gastroesophageal disease
IAO_0000115: A class of gastroenterological diseases involving the stomch and or esophagus.

LABEL: brain inflammatory disease
hasExactSynonym: brain inflammation|inflammation of brain
IAO_0000115: An inflammatory disease involving a pathogenic inflammatory response in the brain.

LABEL: syndromic anorectal malformation
hasExactSynonym: syndrome associated with anorectal malformation|syndromic anorectal malformation
IAO_0000115: Anorectal malformations (ARMs) represent a complex group of congenital anomalies resulting from abnormal development of the hindgut, allantois and Mullerian duct resulting in complete or partial urorectal septal malformations. 50 % of cases are syndromic although many may have other associated anomalies.

LABEL: autosomal dominant hereditary axonal motor and sensory neuropathy
IAO_0000115: A form of axonal hereditary motor and sensory neuropathy with autosomal dominant inheritance.

LABEL: autosomal recessive hereditary demyelinating motor and sensory neuropathy
hasExactSynonym: AR demyelinating HMSN
IAO_0000115: A form of demyelinating hereditary motor and sensory neuropathies (HMSN) with autosomal recessive inheritance. HMSNs are a group of inherited progressive neuropathies with markedly decreased nerve conduction velocity and chronic segmental demyelination in the peripheral nerve.

LABEL: autosomal dominant hereditary sensory and autonomic neuropathy
hasExactSynonym: hereditary sensory and autonomic neuropathy, autosomal dominant
IAO_0000115: A form of hereditary sensory autonomic neuropathy (HSAN) with autosomal dominant inheritance. HSANs are a group of rare peripheral neuropathies where neurons and/or axons are affected. The major feature of these conditions is the loss of large myelinated and unmyelinated fibers.

LABEL: autosomal recessive hereditary sensory and autonomic neuropathy
hasExactSynonym: hereditary sensory and autonomic neuropathy, autosomal recessive
IAO_0000115: A form of hereditary sensory autonomic neuropathy (HSAN) with autosomal recessive inheritance. HSANs are a group of rare peripheral neuropathies where neurons and/or axons are affected. The major feature of these conditions is the loss of large myelinated and unmyelinated fibers.

LABEL: lateral facial cleft
hasExactSynonym: Tessier number 7 facial cleft|transverse facial cleft
IAO_0000115: Lateral facial clefting (macrostomia) is a rare congenital malformation. It may occur either as an isolated phenomenon or in combination with other congenital anomalies.

LABEL: benign familial mesial temporal lobe epilepsy
hasExactSynonym: benign FMTLE
IAO_0000115: Benign familial mesial temporal lobe epilepsy is a rare epilepsy characterized by seizures with viscerosensory or experential auras, onset in adolescence or early adulthood and good prognosis. It is defined as at least 24 months of seizure freedom with or without antiepileptic medication.

LABEL: autosomal thrombocytopenia with normal platelets
IAO_0000115: A form of hereditary thrombocytopenia with normal platelets.

LABEL: congenital myopathy with cores
IAO_0000115: Congenital myopathies represent a clinically and genetically heterogeneous group of early-onset neuromuscular diseases with characteristic, but not always specific, histopathological features, often presenting with stable and/or slowly progressive truncal and proximal weakness. The ?core myopathies? collectively represent the most common form of congenital myopathies, and the name pathologically corresponds to histochemical appearance of focally reduced oxidative enzyme activity and myofibrillar changes on ultrastructural studies.

LABEL: syndromic hypothyroidism
hasExactSynonym: syndrome associated with hypothyroidism|syndromic hypothyroidism
IAO_0000115: Some forms of congenital hypothyroidism associated with defects in other organ systems are classified as syndromic hypothyroidism. These include Pendred syndrome, Bamforth-Lazarus syndrome and Kocher - Deber - Semilange syndrome.

LABEL: acquired neutropenia
hasExactSynonym: acquired neutropenia|immunologic neutropenia
IAO_0000115: An instance of neutropenia that is acquired during the lifetime of the individual.

LABEL: primary immunodeficiency due to a defect in adaptive immunity
IAO_0000115: Disorders of adaptive immunity (i.e., T-cell, B-cell or combined immunodeficiencies), a type of primary immunodeficiency disorder (PID), which constitute a heterogeneous group of disorders that result from defects in immune system development and/or function.

LABEL: cerebellar malformation
IAO_0000115: Cerebellar malformations are diverse congenital anomalies frequently associated with developmental disability.

LABEL: ARX-related epileptic encephalopathy
hasExactSynonym: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy-1 (DEE1)
IAO_0000115: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy-1 (DEE1) is a severe form of epilepsy characterized by frequent tonic seizures or spasms beginning in infancy. DEE1 is caused by mutation in the ARX gene.

LABEL: cerebral malformation
hasExactSynonym: brain malformation
IAO_0000115: Disorders of the developing brain that constitute a wide variety of complex malformations that account for a significant fraction of childhood onset epilepsy, intellectual disability, and autism.

LABEL: congenital myotonia
hasExactSynonym: Myotonia congenita
IAO_0000115: Myotonia congenita (MC) is a genetic neuromuscular channelopathy which usually presents in early childhood resulting in a delay of skeletal muscle relaxation following contraction.

LABEL: qualitative or quantitative defects of merosin
IAO_0000115: Defects in merosin proteins, a group of laminins that share the alpha2 subunit encoded by the LAMA2 gene. Laminins are a family of high molecular weight glycoproteins that function as extracellular matrix components of the structural basement membrane.

LABEL: qualitative or quantitative defects of calpain
IAO_0000115: Defects in calpain protein, an intracellular protease that requires calcium for its catalytic activity.

LABEL: qualitative or quantitative defects of myotubularin
IAO_0000115: Defects in myotubularin, a protein required for muscle cell differentiation.

LABEL: chronic acquired demyelinating polyneuropathy
hasExactSynonym: CADP|acquired peripheral neuropathy, chronic|chronic acquired peripheral neuropathy
IAO_0000115: Chronic form of acquired peripheral neuropathy.

LABEL: autosomal dominant proximal spinal muscular atrophy
hasExactSynonym: proximal spinal muscular atrophy, autosomal dominant
IAO_0000115: A group of rare, genetic, motor neuron disease characterized by childhood or adult onset progressive, predominantly proximal, muscular weakness and wasting. Included diseases are Autosomal dominant adult-onset proximal spinal muscular atrophy, Lower motor neuron syndrome with late-adult onset, and Autosomal dominant childhood-onset proximal spinal muscular atrophy.

LABEL: primary congenital hypothyroidism
IAO_0000115: Primary congenital hypothyroidism is a type of permanent congenital hypothyroidism, a permanent thyroid hormone deficiency that is present from birth.

LABEL: isolated Klippel-Feil syndrome
hasExactSynonym: Klippel-Feil malformation|Klippel-Feil sequence|congenital cervical vertebral fusion|congenital fused cervical segments|nonsyndromic Klippel-Feil syndrome
IAO_0000115: Klippel-Feil Syndrome is characterised by improper segmentation of cervical segments resulting in congenitally fused cervical vertebrae.

LABEL: autosomal recessive lymphoproliferative disease
hasExactSynonym: CD27 deficiency
IAO_0000115: A rare combined T and B cell immunodeficiency with a predisposition to lymphoproliferative syndrome. It is characterized by persistent symptomatic EBV-viremia and hypogammaglobulinemia variably presenting with fever, lymphadenopathy and systemic inflammatory conditions including hepatitis, pneumonia and sepsis. It may be associated with lymphoma, hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis, and aplastic anemia.

LABEL: progressive cerebello-cerebral atrophy
hasExactSynonym: PCCA
IAO_0000115: A rare genetic neurological disorder characterized by postnatal onset of severe global developmental delay, profound mental retardation, progressive microcephaly, progressive spasticity evolving into spastic quadriplegia with joint contractures, generalized seizures, and irritability. Brain imaging shows progressive cerebellar atrophy followed by cerebral atrophy affecting both white and grey matter, but no pontine involvement.

LABEL: autosomal dominant secondary polycythemia
hasExactSynonym: autosomal dominant secondary erythrocytosis|secondary polycythemia, autosomal dominant
IAO_0000115: A rare, genetic, hematologic disease characterized by increased levels of serum hemoglobin, hematocrit and erythrocyte mass, associated with elevated or inappropriately normal erythropoietin serum levels, occurring in various members of a family and with autosomal dominant inheritance.

LABEL: oligoastrocytic tumor
hasExactSynonym: mixed oligodendroglial and astrocytic tumor|mixed oligodendroglial and astrocytic tumour
IAO_0000115: Oligoastrocytomas (OA) are mixed gliomas with distinct oligodendroglial and astrocytic neoplastic components.

LABEL: neuronal tumor
IAO_0000115: Neuronal brain tumors are an uncommon group of central nervous system tumors that arise from cells with neuronal differentiation. These tumors may be purely neuronal in origin or have mixed neuronal and glial components, which comprise a subset of glioneuronal tumors.

LABEL: Duchenne and Becker muscular dystrophy
hasExactSynonym: severe dystrophinopathy, Duchenne and Becker type
IAO_0000115: Duchenne and Becker muscular dystrophies (DMD and BMD) are neuromuscular diseases characterized by progressive muscle wasting and weakness due to degeneration of skeletal, smooth and cardiac muscle.

LABEL: hereditary thrombocytopenia with normal platelets
IAO_0000115: A rare, genetic, isolated constitutional thrombocytopenia disease characterized by decreased platelet counts, not associated with platelet morphology or function impairment, in multiple members of a family. Manifestations are variable, typically ranging from asymptomatic to mild bleeding diathesis (e.g. easy bruising, epistaxis, petechiae). Occasionally, a more severe bleeding tendency has been associated and a mild predisposition to infection and eczema has been reported.

LABEL: midline cerebral malformation
hasExactSynonym: Midline brain malformation
IAO_0000115: Cerebral midline anomalies are defects of anatomical relationships between the two hemispheres. They include holoprosencephalies, septal and commissural agenesis.

LABEL: hereditary cardiac anomaly
hasExactSynonym: genetic cardiac anomaly|Inherited cardiac conditions (ICC)
IAO_0000115: A group of inherited cardiac conditions (ICCs) that comprise a broad range of syndromes affecting the heart and major blood vessels, including cardiomyopathies, arrhythmias, aortopathies, familial hypercholesterolemia (FH), and congenital structural heart defects.

LABEL: hereditary ATTR amyloidosis
hasExactSynonym: familial TTR-related amyloidosis|familial transthyretin-related amyloidosis|hereditary ATTR amyloidosis
IAO_0000115: A rare genetic systemic disease characterized by adult onset, progressive sensorimotor and autonomic neuropathy and infiltrative cardiomyopathy. The disease also frequently manifests with a range of additional clinical signs and symptoms due to associated ocular, renal, central nervous system and gastrointestinal involvement.

LABEL: sickle cell disease and related diseases

LABEL: non-syndromic male infertility due to sperm motility disorder

IAO_0000115: Non-syndromic male infertility due to sperm motility disorder is a rare, genetic, non-syndromic male infertility disorder characterized by infertility due to sperm with defects in their cilia/flagella structure, leading to absent motility or reduced forward motility in fresh ejaculate. LABEL: septopreoptic holoprosencephaly
hasExactSynonym: Septopreoptic HPE
IAO_0000115: Septopreoptic holoprosencephaly (HPE) is a very rare subtype of lobar HPE characterized by midline fusion limited to the septal and/or preoptic regions of the telencephalon without a significant frontal neocortical fusion.

LABEL: inherited prion disease
hasExactSynonym: familial prion disease|hereditary prion disease
IAO_0000115: An instance of prion disease that is caused by an inherited modification of the individual's genome.

LABEL: split hand or/and split foot malformation
IAO_0000115: Split hand/foot malformation (SHFM) is a limb abnormality that is present at birth. It is characterized by absence of certain fingers and toes (ectrodactyly) that suggest a claw-like appearance and webbing of fingers and toes may also be present.

LABEL: familial infantile gigantism
hasExactSynonym: X-LAG (X-linked acrogigantism)|hereditary infantile gigantism|hereditary pituitary hyperplasia|infantile gigantism due to pituitary hyperplasia
IAO_0000115: A rare, genetic pituitary disease characterized by infantile-onset, rapid and excessive acceleration of linear growth and body size due to mixed growth hormone (GH)- and prolactin-secreting adenomas and/or pituitary hyperplasia. LABEL: sodium channelopathy-related small fiber neuropathy
IAO_0000115: A rare, genetic, peripheral neuropathy disorder due to gain-of-function mutations in voltage-gated sodium channels present in the small peripheral nerve fibers characterized by neuropathic pain of varying intensity (often beginning in the distal extermities and with a burning quality) associated with autonomic dysfunction (e.g. orthostatic dizziness, palpitations, dry eyes and mouth), abnormal quantitative sensory testing, and reduction in intraepidermal nerve ?ber density. Large fiber functions (i.e. normal strength, tendon reflexes, and vibration sense) and nerve conduction studies are typically normal.

LABEL: pure or complex autosomal recessive spastic paraplegia
hasExactSynonym: Pure or complicated autosomal recessive spastic paraplegia
IAO_0000115: A form of hereditary spastic paraplegia with autosomal recessive inheritence.

LABEL: deafness-onychodystrophy syndrome
IAO_0000115: Deafness-onychodystrophy syndrome is a group of rare, genetic, developmental defect during embryogenesis disorders characterized by the association of sensorineural deafness and onychodystrophy (e.g. absent/hypoplastic finger and toenails), as well as brachydactyly and finger-like thumbs. Additional features present in one of the diseases comprising this group include osteodystrophy, intellectual disability, seizures, developmental delay, and distinctive facies.

LABEL: microcephalic primordial dwarfism
IAO_0000115: Primordial dwarfism with microcephaly.

LABEL: isolated scaphocephaly
hasExactSynonym: isolated dolichocephaly|non-syndromic sagittal synostosis
IAO_0000115: Isolated scaphocephaly is a form of nonsyndromic craniosynostosis characterized by premature fusion of the sagittal suture.

LABEL: isolated plagiocephaly
hasExactSynonym: non-syndromic unicoronal synostosis|synostotic plagiocephaly
IAO_0000115: isolated plagiocephaly is a form of non-syndromic unicoronal synostosis.

LABEL: isolated brachycephaly
hasExactSynonym: non-syndromic bicoronal synostosis
IAO_0000115: Isolated brachycephaly is a relatively frequent nonsyndromic craniosynostosis consisting of premature fusion of both coronal sutures leading to skull deformity with a broad flat forehead and palpable coronal ridges.

LABEL: congenital myasthenic syndromes with glycosylation defect
IAO_0000115: Congenital myasthenic syndrome with glycosylation defect is a group of genetic disorders of impaired neuromuscular transmission at the motor endplate characterized by fatigable muscle weakness with a defect in glycosylation.

LABEL: hereditary intestinal polyposis
hasExactSynonym: familial intestinal polyposis|genetic intestinal polyposis
IAO_0000115: An inherited form of intestinal polyps that include familial adenomatous polyposis and juvenile polyposis syndrome.

LABEL: primary short bowel syndrome
IAO_0000115: Short bowel syndrome is a complex disease that occurs due to the physical loss or the loss of function of a portion of the small and/or large intestine. Consequently, individuals with short bowel syndrome often have a reduced ability to absorb nutrients such as fats, carbohydrates (sugars) vitamins, minerals, trace elements and fluids (malabsorption).

LABEL: homozygous 2p21 microdeletion syndrome
hasExactSynonym: 2p21 contiguous gene deletion syndrome
IAO_0000115: Homozygous deletion of chromosome 2p21, containing two closely located genes, SLC3A1, and PREPL, has been linked to the hypotonia?cystinuria syndrome. Symptoms include generalized hypotonia at birth, failure to thrive, cystinuria, and growth retardation.

LABEL: fetal anticonvulsant syndrome
hasExactSynonym: FACS|fetal AEDS|fetal antiepileptic drug syndrome|foetal AEDS|foetal antiepileptic drug syndrome
IAO_0000115: Syndromes associated with congenital malformations and cognitive disorders in children whose mothers took antiepileptic drugs in pregnancy.

LABEL: congenital muscular dystrophy with cerebellar involvement
hasExactSynonym: CMD with cerebellar involvement|CMD-CRB
IAO_0000115: A rare, congenital muscular dystrophy due to dystroglycanopathy characterized by proximal muscle weakness with a tendency for muscle hypertrophy and pseudohypertrophy, variable cognitive impairment, microcephaly, cerebellar hypoplasia with or without cysts, and other structural brain anomalies.

LABEL: primary qualitative or quantitative defects of alpha-dystroglycan
hasExactSynonym: primary alpha-dystroglycanopathy|primary dystroglycanopathy
IAO_0000115: Defects in the alpha unit of the dystroglycan protein, a high-affinity receptor for several extracellular matrix components.

LABEL: hereditary isolated aplastic anemia
IAO_0000115: Hereditary isolated aplastic anemia is a rare, genetic, constitutional aplastic anemia disorder characterized by severe peripheral blood pancytopenia and bone marrow hypoplasia in multiple individuals of a family, in the absence of any somatic symptoms.

LABEL: male infertility with azoospermia or oligozoospermia due to single gene mutation
IAO_0000115: Male infertility with azoospermia or oligospermia due to single gene mutation is a rare, genetic male infertility due to sperm disorder characterized by the absence of a measurable amount of spermatozoa in the ejaculate (azoospermia), or a number of sperm in the ejaculate inferior to 15 million/mL (oligozoospermia), resulting from a mutation in a single gene known to cause azoo- or oligo-spermia. LABEL: HTRA1-related cerebral small vessel disease

LABEL: intractable diarrhea of infancy

Its hallmark feature is an abnormality of the long bones in the arms and legs in which the ends (metaphyses) of the bones are abnormally broad; the shape of the bones resembles a boat oar or paddle. The broad metaphyses are due to enlargement of the spongy inner layer of bone (trabecular bone). Although trabecular bone is expanded, the dense outermost layer of bone (cortical bone) is thinner than normal. As a result, the bones are fragile and fracture easily. LABEL: CUT&Tag

LABEL: diffusion tensor imaging measurement
IAO_0000115: A quantitative measurement technique derived from diffusion-weighted magnetic resonance imaging that characterizes the three-dimensional diffusion of water molecules within biological tissues. LABEL: mean diffusivity measurement
hasExactSynonym: average diffusivity|mean diffusivity
IAO_0000115: A quantitative parameter derived from diffusion tensor imaging that measures the average magnitude of water molecule diffusion across all spatial directions within a tissue. Mean diffusivity (MD) is calculated as the mean of the three eigenvalues of the diffusion tensor and provides information about tissue microstructure, cellularity, and integrity. This measurement can be applied to various biological tissues including brain, kidney, skeletal muscle, and other organs.

LABEL: axial diffusivity measurement
hasExactSynonym: axial diffusivity|longitudinal diffusivity|parallel diffusivity
IAO_0000115: A quantitative parameter derived from diffusion tensor imaging that measures water molecule diffusion parallel to the principal direction of the diffusion tensor. Axial diffusivity (AD or AxD) represents the largest eigenvalue (?1) of the diffusion tensor and provides information about axonal integrity and tissue microstructure. This measurement can be applied to various biological tissues including brain white matter, skeletal muscle, kidney, and other organs.

LABEL: radial diffusivity measurement
hasExactSynonym: perpendicular diffusivity|radial diffusivity|transverse diffusivity
IAO_0000115: A quantitative parameter derived from diffusion tensor imaging that measures water molecule diffusion perpendicular to the principal direction of the diffusion tensor. Radial diffusivity (RD) is calculated as the average of the second and third eigenvalues ((?2 + ?3)/2) of the diffusion tensor and provides information about myelin integrity and tissue microstructure. This measurement can be applied to various biological tissues including brain white matter, skeletal muscle, kidney, and other organs.

LABEL: neutrophilic bronchiectasis
hasExactSynonym: neutrophil-predominant bronchiectasis|neutrophilic bronchiectasis endotype
IAO_0000115: A bronchiectasis inflammatory endotype characterized by excessive neutrophil-driven airway inflammation with elevated levels of neutrophil-associated mediators including neutrophil elastase (NE), IL-8, and TNF-alpha. This is the most common inflammatory phenotype of bronchiectasis, strongly associated with chronic Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection, severe disease, frequent exacerbations, and poor prognosis.

LABEL: eosinophilic bronchiectasis
hasExactSynonym: eosinophilic bronchiectasis endotype
IAO_0000115: A bronchiectasis inflammatory endotype characterized by elevated blood eosinophils (?300 cells/?L) or sputum eosinophils (?3%), associated with type 2 (Th2) inflammation, elevated fractional exhaled nitric oxide (FeNO), and IL-5/IL-13 signaling. This phenotype affects approximately 20% of patients with bronchiectasis and may be responsive to inhaled corticosteroids and biologic agents targeting Th2 pathways.

LABEL: mixed granulocytic bronchiectasis
hasExactSynonym: mixed neutrophilic-eosinophilic bronchiectasis
IAO_0000115: A bronchiectasis inflammatory endotype characterized by concurrent neutrophilic and eosinophilic (type 2/Th2) inflammation, with co-expression of neutrophil-associated markers (neutrophil elastase, IL-8) and eosinophilic markers (IL-5, IL-13, FeNO). This endotype represents a distinct biological subgroup associated with increased exacerbation risk and potential responsiveness to combined therapeutic strategies.

LABEL: paucigranulocytic bronchiectasis
IAO_0000115: A bronchiectasis inflammatory endotype characterized by low levels of both neutrophils (<60%) and eosinophils (<3%) in the sputum, with reduced concentrations of inflammatory mediators including IL-8 and IL-13. This phenotype is associated with milder disease presentation on imaging and lower exacerbation burden, though it remains less well-characterized than other bronchiectasis endotypes.

LABEL: CFTR dysfunction bronchiectasis
hasExactSynonym: CFTR-predominant bronchiectasis|CFTR-related bronchiectasis|cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator dysfunction bronchiectasis
IAO_0000115: A bronchiectasis endotype characterized by cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) dysfunction that does not meet full diagnostic criteria for cystic fibrosis, typically presenting with elevated sweat chloride concentration (intermediate range 30-59 mmol/L), mucociliary clearance defects, and susceptibility to nontuberculous mycobacterial pulmonary infection. Patients may carry heterozygous CFTR mutations or have reduced CFTR function without detectable mutations, and may be candidates for CFTR modulator therapy.

LABEL: ciliary dysfunction bronchiectasis
hasExactSynonym: ciliary-predominant bronchiectasis
IAO_0000115: A bronchiectasis endotype characterized by ciliary dysfunction that does not meet full diagnostic criteria for primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD), typically presenting with abnormally low nasal nitric oxide levels, ciliary beat frequency abnormalities, and impaired mucociliary clearance. This endotype represents a spectrum of ciliopathy-associated bronchiectasis distinct from classical PCD.

LABEL: heritable connective tissue disorder-associated bronchiectasis
hasExactSynonym: connective tissue-predominant bronchiectasis
IAO_0000115: A bronchiectasis endotype associated with heritable connective tissue disorder features, characterized by a tall asthenic morphotype with high rates of scoliosis, pectus excavatum, mitral valve prolapse, and dural ectasia. This endotype is associated with susceptibility to pulmonary nontuberculous mycobacterial infection and may involve genetic variation in connective tissue and transforming growth factor-beta (TGF-beta)-related pathway genes.

LABEL: immune deficient-predominant bronchiectasis
hasExactSynonym: immunodeficiency-associated bronchiectasis
IAO_0000115: A bronchiectasis endotype characterized by underlying immune deficiency, presenting with impaired systemic immunity and increased susceptibility to mycobacterial infection, particularly nontuberculous mycobacteria. This endotype encompasses a spectrum of primary and acquired immunodeficiencies that predispose to chronic airway infection and bronchiectatic disease.

LABEL: functional assay in yeast
hasExactSynonym: yeast functional assay|yeast-based functional assay
IAO_0000115: An assay that evaluates the biological function or activity of a gene, protein, or variant by measuring a phenotypic or molecular readout in a yeast cell system, typically through growth, morphology, stress sensitivity, reporter expression, or related outputs.

LABEL: response to amphetamine
hasExactSynonym: amphetamine response|response to amphetamines
IAO_0000115: A physiological or behavioral change that occurs in response to amphetamine, a central nervous system stimulant that acts primarily by increasing the release and blocking the reuptake of monoamine neurotransmitters including dopamine, norepinephrine, and serotonin.

LABEL: response to penicillin
hasExactSynonym: penicillin response
IAO_0000115: A physiological or immunological change that occurs in response to penicillin, a beta-lactam antibiotic that inhibits bacterial cell wall synthesis. Response may include therapeutic efficacy, allergic or hypersensitivity reactions, or other adverse effects.

LABEL: response to tocilizumab
hasExactSynonym: tocilizumab response
IAO_0000115: A physiological or therapeutic change that occurs in response to tocilizumab, a humanized monoclonal antibody that binds to both soluble and membrane-bound interleukin-6 receptors (IL-6R), thereby inhibiting IL-6-mediated signaling and inflammatory responses.

LABEL: response to sunitinib
hasExactSynonym: sunitinib response
IAO_0000115: A physiological or therapeutic change that occurs in response to sunitinib, a multi-targeted receptor tyrosine kinase inhibitor that inhibits VEGFR, PDGFR, c-KIT, RET, and FLT3 signaling pathways, affecting tumor angiogenesis and proliferation.

LABEL: response to nintedanib
hasExactSynonym: nintedanib response
IAO_0000115: A physiological or therapeutic change that occurs in response to nintedanib, a triple angiokinase inhibitor that blocks VEGFR, FGFR, and PDGFR tyrosine kinases, inhibiting angiogenesis and fibrotic processes.

LABEL: response to vandetanib
hasExactSynonym: vandetanib response
IAO_0000115: A physiological or therapeutic change that occurs in response to vandetanib, a multi-kinase inhibitor that targets VEGFR, EGFR, and RET tyrosine kinases, primarily used in the treatment of medullary thyroid cancer.

LABEL: response to vemurafenib
hasExactSynonym: vemurafenib response
IAO_0000115: A physiological or therapeutic change that occurs in response to vemurafenib, a selective BRAF kinase inhibitor that targets the BRAF V600E mutation, primarily used in the treatment of BRAF-mutant melanoma.

LABEL: response to mesalamine
hasExactSynonym: 5-aminosalicylic acid response|mesalamine response|mesalazine response
IAO_0000115: A physiological or therapeutic change that occurs in response to mesalamine (5-aminosalicylic acid), an anti-inflammatory drug that acts locally in the gastrointestinal tract, primarily used in the treatment of inflammatory bowel disease including ulcerative colitis and Crohn's disease.

LABEL: response to zonisamide
hasExactSynonym: zonisamide response
IAO_0000115: A physiological or pathological response to exposure to zonisamide, a benzisoxazole sulfonamide anticonvulsant drug. This response encompasses changes in motor symptoms, wearing-off effects, and therapeutic outcomes observed following zonisamide administration in patients with Parkinson's disease experiencing motor fluctuations.

LABEL: response to GLP-1 receptor agonist
hasExactSynonym: GLP-1 receptor agonist response|glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist response
IAO_0000115: A physiological or pathological response to exposure to a glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonist. GLP-1 receptor agonists are a class of incretin-mimetic drugs that bind to and activate the GLP-1 receptor, stimulating glucose-dependent insulin secretion, suppressing glucagon release, delaying gastric emptying, and promoting satiety. This response encompasses glycemic control outcomes including HbA1c reduction, body weight changes, and other metabolic effects observed following GLP-1 receptor agonist treatment.

LABEL: response to dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitor
hasExactSynonym: DPP-4 inhibitor response|dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitor response|gliptin response|response to gliptin
IAO_0000115: A physiological or pathological response to exposure to a dipeptidyl peptidase-4 (DPP-4) inhibitor. DPP-4 inhibitors are a class of oral antidiabetic drugs that inhibit the enzyme dipeptidyl peptidase-4, thereby increasing the half-life of endogenous incretin hormones. This response encompasses both therapeutic outcomes such as glycemic control and adverse effects including drug-induced bullous pemphigoid.

LABEL: nucleic acid delivery method
IAO_0000115: A transfection that describes the means by which nucleic acid molecules (DNA or RNA) are physically or chemically introduced into target cells.|Method by which nucleic acids are delivered or engineered into a cell.

LABEL: viral transduction method
IAO_0000115: A nucleic acid delivery method that uses viral vectors to introduce nucleic acid cargo into target cells by exploiting viral mechanisms of cell entry and genome delivery.|Viral-based transfection, or more specifically known as transduction, involves using a viral vector to carry a specific nucleic acid sequence into a host cell.

LABEL: stable viral transduction method
IAO_0000115: A viral transduction method in which the viral nucleic acid cargo stably integrates into the host cell genome, enabling heritable and long-term transgene expression.|Stable transfection ensures long-term expression of a transgene by integrating the introduced DNA into the host genome, therefore, maintaining the expression even after replication.

LABEL: lentivirus transduction
IAO_0000115: A stable viral transduction method that uses lentiviral vectors, derived from lentiviruses such as HIV-1, to deliver nucleic acid cargo into both dividing and non-dividing cells via stable integration into the host chromosomal DNA.|Stable transfection method involving the transgene introduction into the cells of interest using engineered lentiviral particles.

LABEL: retrovirus transduction
IAO_0000115: A stable viral transduction method that uses retroviral vectors, derived from oncoretroviruses such as gammaretroviruses, to deliver nucleic acid cargo into dividing cells via stable integration of the retroviral genome into the host chromosomal DNA.|Stable transfection method involving the transgene introduction into the cells of interest using engineered retroviral particles.

LABEL: transient viral transduction method
IAO_0000115: A viral transduction method in which the viral nucleic acid cargo enters target cells but does not stably integrate into the host genome, resulting in transient transgene expression that is lost upon cell division.|Transient transfection is the introduction of foreign nucleic acids into eukaryotic cells resulting in temporary expression of the introduced genes, without integration into the host genome.

LABEL: adenovirus transduction
IAO_0000115: A transient viral transduction method that uses adenoviral vectors to deliver nucleic acid cargo into target cells, where the viral DNA persists as an episomal element without integrating into the host genome.|Transient transfection method involving the transgene introduction into the cells of interest using engineered adenoviral particles. Adenoviral particles can transduce both replicating and non-dividing cells. Adenoviral DNA does not integrate into the host genome, but rather, resides episomally in the host nucleus.

LABEL: adeno-associated virus transduction
IAO_0000115: A transient viral transduction method that uses adeno-associated virus (AAV) vectors to deliver nucleic acid cargo into target cells, where the vector DNA predominantly persists as episomal concatemers with minimal integration into the host genome.|Transient transfection method involving the transgene introduction into the cells of interest using engineered adeno-associated virus (AAV) particles. AAV particles can transduce both replicating and non-dividing cells. Engineered AAV DNA does not integrate into the host genome, but rather, resides episomally in the host nucleus. In comparison to adenoviral vectors, AAVs have low immunogenicity and cytotoxicity.

LABEL: herpes virus transduction
IAO_0000115: A transient viral transduction method that uses herpesviral vectors, derived from herpesviruses such as herpes simplex virus (HSV), to deliver nucleic acid cargo into target cells, particularly neurons, without permanent integration into the host genome.|Transient transfection method involving the transgene introduction into the cells of interest using engineered Herpes simplex virus (HSV) particles. HSV particles can transduce both replicating and non-dividing cells. Engineered HSV DNA does not integrate into the host genome, but rather, resides episomally in the host nucleus. HSV vectors have comparatively large transgene capacity (approx. 30kB) and have low immunogenicity.

LABEL: non-viral transfection method
IAO_0000115: A nucleic acid delivery method that uses physical or chemical approaches other than viral vectors to introduce nucleic acids into target cells.|Non-viral transfection methods rely on physical or chemical means to introduce nucleic acids into cells without the use of viral vectors. LABEL: electroporation
IAO_0000115: A non-viral transfection method in which brief, high-voltage electrical pulses are applied to cells, transiently permeabilizing the plasma membrane to allow uptake of nucleic acids into the cell.|Electroporation is the process of using an electric pulse to introduce DNA into cells by creating temporary pores in the cell membrane, allowing for efficient gene delivery.

LABEL: nucleofection
IAO_0000115: A non-viral transfection method that combines cell-type-specific electrical parameters and proprietary reagents to deliver nucleic acids directly into the nucleus of cells, including difficult-to-transfect primary and non-dividing cells.|Nucleofection is a type of specialized electroporation which is designed to deliver genetic material directly to the nuclei of cells.

LABEL: lipofection
IAO_0000115: A non-viral transfection method in which cationic lipid formulations spontaneously form complexes with negatively charged nucleic acids and fuse with the cell membrane to deliver the nucleic acid cargo into target cells.|Lipofection is a liposome-based transfection technique whereby the nucleic acid is encapsulated within a phospholipid vesicle that can either directly fuse with cell membranes or be endocytosed by a cell, allowing delivery of the genetic material to the cell.

LABEL: nanoparticle-based transfection
IAO_0000115: A non-viral transfection method in which nanoparticles, such as polymeric, inorganic, or lipid nanoparticles, are used as carriers to encapsulate and deliver nucleic acid cargo into target cells.|Nanoparticle-mediated transfection is a method for delivering genetic material into cells using small (<100 nm in diameter) nanoparticles, which can encapsulate genetic material and facilitate its entry into the cell. The nanoparticles can be engineered to enhance cellular specificity, protect the genetic material from degradation, and release it once inside the cell.

LABEL: microinjection
IAO_0000115: A non-viral transfection method in which a fine glass capillary needle is used under microscopic guidance to directly inject nucleic acids or other macromolecules into individual cells.|Microinjection is a method that enables introduction of exogenous genetic material (or other substances, such as proteins) directly into the cytoplasm or nucleus of individual cells using a micrometer-diameter pipette by piercing the cell and/or nuclear membrane under visual control.

LABEL: optical transfection
IAO_0000115: A non-viral transfection method in which a focused laser beam creates transient pores in the cell membrane, enabling the entry of nucleic acids into the cell without mechanical penetration.|Nucleic acid delivery method which involves short low-power bursts of laser beam to create transient pores in the cell membrane to allow entry of genetic material to the cell.

LABEL: sonoporation
IAO_0000115: A non-viral transfection method that uses ultrasound waves, often combined with microbubbles, to transiently permeabilize cell membranes and facilitate cellular uptake of nucleic acids.|Sonoporation is a technique for delivering genetic material into cells using sonication. In this process, externally applied acoustic pressure waves create temporary pores in the cell membrane, enabling the genetic material to enter the cell.

LABEL: nucleic acid integration state
IAO_0000115: A property of a transfected nucleic acid that describes the mode by which the delivered nucleic acid persists in the host cell in relation to the host genome, including integration into chromosomal DNA or episomal persistence.|The state of nucleic acid (DNA or RNA) being integrated into a host genome, often as a result of viral infection or genetic engineering.

LABEL: random locus integration
IAO_0000115: A nucleic acid integration state in which the delivered nucleic acid inserts into the host genome at non-specific, random chromosomal locations, as typically occurs with retroviral and lentiviral vectors.|Random locus integration refers to the process where an exogenous genetic material is inserted into the host genome at an arbitrary, rather than a specific, location.

LABEL: targeted locus integration
IAO_0000115: A nucleic acid integration state in which the delivered nucleic acid is directed to integrate at a specific, pre-defined chromosomal locus using site-specific recombination systems or precision genome editing tools.|Targeted locus integration refers to the process where an exogenous genetic material is inserted into the host genome at specifically pre-determined location using cell's homology-directed repair mechanisms. In contrast to the random locus integration approach, this minimises the risk of insertional mutagenesis and ensures more consistent transgene expression.

LABEL: native locus replacement
IAO_0000115: A nucleic acid integration state in which the delivered nucleic acid sequence replaces an endogenous sequence at the native genomic locus via homology-directed repair, preserving the natural chromosomal context.|Native locus replacement refers to the process where the exogenously introduced genetic material replaces the host's native genomic sequence. This is achieved by introducing double-stranded DNA breaks in the host genome using gene editing tools, such as CRISPR/Cas9 or TALENS, together with template DNA (often a corrected or modified version of the gene) flanked by homology arms to promote the sequence incorporation into the host's genome at a native locus by means of homology-directed repair.

LABEL: not-integrative transgene expression
IAO_0000115: A nucleic acid integration state in which the delivered nucleic acid persists episomally in the host cell without integration into the chromosomal DNA, resulting in transient or non-heritable transgene expression.|Non-integrative transgene expression refers to the process where the foreign genetic material is expressed without being permanently incorporated into the host's genome. Instead, the transgene exists in the cell as a separate entity, usually in the form of an episome, plasmid, or mRNA.

LABEL: total desmosterol measurement
IAO_0000115: Quantification of the total amount of desmosterol (sum of free and esterified forms) in a sample. Desmosterol (also known as 24-dehydrocholesterol, CHEBI:17737) is a zoosterol and the immediate precursor to cholesterol in the Bloch pathway of de novo cholesterol biosynthesis, where it is converted to cholesterol by the enzyme DHCR24 (delta-24-sterol reductase).

LABEL: sample ID
hasExactSynonym: sample identifier
IAO_0000115: A string used to identify a sample.

LABEL: myocardial strain
IAO_0000115: Myocardial strain refers to the measurement of heart muscle deformation, or its shortening, thickening, and lengthening, using imaging techniques like echocardiography.

LABEL: biparietal distance
hasExactSynonym: biparietal diameter
IAO_0000115: A measurement of the distance spanning the widest transverse diameter of the fetal skull, between the outer or inner tables of the two parietal bones, typically obtained by ultrasound.

LABEL: amniotic fluid index
hasExactSynonym: amniotic fluid volume index
IAO_0000115: A semi-quantitative prenatal ultrasound measurement of amniotic fluid volume, calculated as the sum of the deepest vertical pocket of amniotic fluid measured in each of the four quadrants of the uterus.

LABEL: fetal heart rate
hasExactSynonym: Heart Rate, Fetal
IAO_0000115: The rate of contraction of the fetal heart, typically expressed as the number of fetal cardiac beats per minute.

LABEL: spatial molecular profiling assay
IAO_0000115: An assay that measures the abundance or distribution of one or more molecular analytes, such as RNA or proteins, while preserving their spatial localization within cells or tissues.

LABEL: DBiT-seq
hasExactSynonym: Deterministic Barcoding in Tissue for Spatial Omics Sequencing
IAO_0000115: A spatial molecular profiling assay that simultaneously maps mRNA transcripts and protein expression within intact tissue sections using microfluidic co-delivery of DNA barcodes. Spatially indexed barcodes are deposited in a deterministic grid pattern onto the tissue, capturing both RNA and antibody-DNA conjugates, which are subsequently sequenced to yield co-registered transcriptomic and proteomic profiles. This approach provides paired spatial gene expression and protein abundance data at near-cellular, pixel resolution.

LABEL: DESI
hasExactSynonym: Desorption Electrospray Ionization
IAO_0000115: A mass spectrometry assay that couples ambient ionization to mass spectrometry (MS) for chemical analysis of samples at atmospheric conditions.

LABEL: Enhanced SRS
IAO_0000115: An imaging assay that selectively amplifies Raman signals from specific molecular bonds (e.g., C?H, C=C) using pulsed laser excitation. Improvements to standard SRS?such as lock-in detection, signal amplification, or optimized laser configurations?increase sensitivity and spatial resolution, enabling detection of low-abundance biomolecules. This technique provides non-destructive, quantitative maps of lipids, proteins, nucleic acids, and other chemical species at subcellular resolution.

LABEL: GeoMx
hasExactSynonym: GeoMx Digital Spatial Profiler
IAO_0000115: A spatial molecular profiling assay that enables non-destructive, multiplexed profiling of RNA and protein from user-selected regions of interest (ROIs) within intact tissue sections. For RNA, tiled in situ hybridization probe sets targeting 1000s of transcripts are conjugated to photocleavable DNA indexing oligonucleotides; for protein, antibodies specific to up to 96 protein targets are similarly conjugated to photocleavable oligo tags. After ROI selection, UV illumination releases the oligo tags from the illuminated areas, which are collected and quantified on the NanoString nCounter system. This approach supports targeted spatial gene expression and protein profiling from defined tissue regions.

LABEL: iCLAP
hasExactSynonym: Individual-nucleotide resolution UV-Crosslinking and Affinity Purification
IAO_0000115: Individual-nucleotide resolution UV-Crosslinking and Affinity Purification (iCLAP) is a high-stringency molecular technique that maps the RNA-binding sites of RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) at single-nucleotide resolution. RNA?protein complexes are covalently crosslinked by UV irradiation, followed by stringent affinity purification of the target RBP and sequencing of the co-purified RNA fragments. The resulting data reveals the positions where an RBP contacts its RNA targets.

LABEL: Illumina Spatial ver0
IAO_0000115: A spatial transcriptomics assay that maps whole-transcriptome gene expression within intact tissue sections at capture-spot resolution, ranging from multi-cellular to near single-cell depending on array configuration. Tissue sections are placed on spatially barcoded capture arrays; RNA transcripts bind to capture probes and are sequenced together with their spatial barcodes to reconstruct a spatially resolved gene expression map. This approach preserves spatial context while enabling unbiased, genome-wide profiling of gene expression across tissue regions.

LABEL: MALDI
IAO_0000115: A mass spectrometry assay in which analytes co-crystallized with a chemical matrix are ionized by a pulsed laser, generating predominantly singly charged ions that are detected by mass-to-charge ratio; when performed as raster-scanned imaging (MALDI-MSI), it generates spatially resolved molecular maps of proteins, peptides, lipids or metabolites directly from tissue sections.

LABEL: MPLEx
hasExactSynonym: Metabolite, Protein, and Lipid Extraction
IAO_0000115: An extraction protocol that partitions a single biological sample into metabolite, protein, and lipid fractions for subsequent multi-omics analyses, typically using mass spectrometry.

LABEL: MS-spatial
hasExactSynonym: mass spectrometry-based spatial molecular profiling assay
IAO_0000115: A spatial molecular profiling assay that uses mass spectrometry to measure the spatial distribution of molecular analytes within cells or tissues.

LABEL: Raman Imaging
IAO_0000115: An imaging assay that maps the molecular composition of biological samples by detecting inelastic (Raman) scattering of light at each spatial pixel. As a laser scans the sample, each pixel generates a Raman spectrum reflecting the unique molecular vibrational fingerprint of that location, enabling detailed mapping of biomolecules such as proteins, lipids, nucleic acids, and water within cells or tissues. The resulting chemical maps provide quantitative, spatially resolved information about tissue composition and molecular organization without the need for staining or fluorescent labels.

LABEL: sc/snATAC + RNA-seq
hasExactSynonym: single-cell/single-nucleus ATAC and RNA sequencing assay
IAO_0000115: A single-cell or single-nucleus sequencing assay that simultaneously measures chromatin accessibility using ATAC sequencing and gene expression using RNA sequencing from the same individual cell or nucleus.

LABEL: sc/snATAC-seq
hasExactSynonym: single-cell/single-nucleus ATAC sequencing assay
IAO_0000115: A single-cell or single-nucleus sequencing assay that profiles chromatin accessibility by sequencing DNA fragments generated through transposase-mediated tagging of accessible chromatin in individual cells or nuclei.

LABEL: sc/snRNA-seq
hasExactSynonym: single-cell/single-nucleus RNA sequencing assay
IAO_0000115: A single-cell or single-nucleus sequencing assay that profiles gene expression by sequencing RNA molecules isolated from individual cells or nuclei.

LABEL: sciATAC-seq
hasExactSynonym: single-cell combinatorial indexing for transposase-accessible chromatin
IAO_0000115: An ATAC sequencing assay that measures genome-wide chromatin accessibility at single-cell resolution. It uniquely uses a split-and-pool "combinatorial indexing" strategy to barcode individual cells, allowing researchers to profile hundreds of thousands of cells without needing to physically isolate them.

LABEL: scRNA-seq + scProteomics
IAO_0000115: A multimodal single-cell assay that simultaneously measures gene expression by RNA sequencing and protein abundance in the same individual cell.

LABEL: Second Harmonic Generation
IAO_0000115: An imaging assay that produces label-free, highly specific contrast from non-centrosymmetric biological structures?most notably fibrillar collagen. When pulsed laser light interacts with ordered molecular assemblies such as collagen fibrils, photons at exactly half the excitation wavelength are coherently emitted, providing structural specificity without the use of exogenous labels or stains. SHG microscopy enables high-resolution, label-free imaging of extracellular matrix architecture and collagen fiber organization in biological tissues.

LABEL: Seq-Scope
IAO_0000115: A spatial transcriptomics assay that uses solid-phase amplification of randomly barcoded single-molecule oligonucleotides on an Illumina sequencing platform to create a dense array of spatially indexed RNA-capture clusters. Tissue sections are placed directly on the sequencing flow cell surface, where RNA molecules are captured by barcoded clusters and sequenced together with their spatial coordinates. With pixels spaced approximately 0.5?0.8 ?m apart, Seq-Scope achieves spatial resolution approaching that of individual cells and subcellular compartments.

LABEL: SIMS
hasExactSynonym: Secondary Ion Mass Spectrometry
IAO_0000115: An assay that characterizes the elemental and molecular composition of solid surfaces and thin films by bombarding the specimen with a focused primary ion beam, causing secondary ions to be sputtered from the surface and detected by a mass spectrometer. By rastering the primary beam across the sample, SIMS generates spatially resolved chemical maps of isotope distributions, elements, and molecular species at high sensitivity and depth resolution. In biological research, SIMS is used for imaging stable isotope tracers, lipid distributions, and subcellular elemental composition within tissue sections.

LABEL: single-cell MS
hasExactSynonym: single-cell mass spectrometry
IAO_0000115: A mass spectrometry assay that measures proteins, metabolites, and lipids in individual cells.

LABEL: Stereo-seq
hasExactSynonym: Spatial Enhanced Resolution Omics Sequencing
IAO_0000115: A spatial transcriptomics assay that captures RNA expression across tissue sections at single-cell to subcellular resolution over a wide field of view. RNA molecules are captured in situ on a patterned chip containing spatially indexed DNA nanoballs (DNBs)?each assigned a unique Coordinate ID (CID)?enabling precise spatial mapping of transcripts from fresh-frozen tissue. The resulting data supports multi-scale analysis of tissue biology, from tissue-level organization to single-cell gene expression and subcellular transcript localization.

LABEL: Xenium
IAO_0000115: A spatial molecular profiling assay that maps the expression of targeted RNA panels within intact tissue sections at single-cell and subcellular resolution. This assay can identify the location of target transcripts within the tissue, providing a single cell resolution map of expression patterns of all genes that are included in the selected probe panel and generating a single-cell-resolution expression map of all profiled genes.

LABEL: HiFi-Slide
hasExactSynonym: High-Fidelity Spatial Transcriptomics Slide sequencing
IAO_0000115: A spatial transcriptomics assay that maps genome-wide RNA expression in fresh-frozen tissue at submicron resolution. RNA molecules are captured in situ on a barcoded slide surface using spatially indexed poly(d)T oligonucleotides spaced ~0.5 ?m apart, then sequenced to reconstruct high-resolution transcriptomic maps. This technology achieves spatial resolution approaching that of a light microscope, enabling near-single-cell or subcellular-level gene expression profiling across intact tissue sections.

LABEL: Pixel-seqV2
IAO_0000115: A spatial transcriptomics and multiomics assay that uses polony gel arrays?micron-scale DNA cluster arrays each carrying unique spatial barcodes?to capture and sequence RNA, proteins, or other molecules directly from tissue sections. Molecules from the overlaid tissue are captured by the barcoded clusters and spatially indexed according to each cluster's coordinates, enabling high-resolution reconstruction of molecular spatial organization after sequencing.

LABEL: Thick Section Multiphoton MxIF
hasExactSynonym: Thick Section Multiphoton Multiplexed Fluorescence Imaging
IAO_0000115: An imaging assay that applies multiplexed fluorescence microscopy to thick tissue sections using multiphoton excitation, enabling simultaneous or sequential visualization of a large number of cellular and histological protein markers in 3D. Multiphoton excitation allows imaging deep into intact thick sections with reduced phototoxicity and superior optical sectioning compared to single-photon methods.

LABEL: Singular Genomics G4X
IAO_0000115: A spatial molecular profiling assay that profiles RNA expression, protein abundance, and tissue morphology (via fluorescence H&E staining) at subcellular resolution directly from FFPE tissue sections.

LABEL: apnea-hypopnea index measurement
hasExactSynonym: apnoea-hypopnoea index
IAO_0000115: A measurement of sleep apnea severity calculated as the total number of apnea and hypopnea events recorded during a sleep study, divided by the total number of hours of sleep.

LABEL: cigarette smoking status measurement
hasExactSynonym: cigarette smoking status
IAO_0000115: A self-reported categorical measurement of an individual's cigarette smoking history, classified as current smoker, former smoker, or never smoker.

LABEL: slide ID
hasExactSynonym: slide identifier
IAO_0000115: A unique identifier for the physical glass slide or cartridge on which a tissue section is mounted and processed.

LABEL: 10x GEM-X Epi Multiome
hasExactSynonym: 10x GEM-X Multiome|GEM-X Multiome
IAO_0000115: The 10x microfluidic assay that simultaneously profiles the transcriptome and epigenome of the same individual cell nucleus, using a redesigned chip architecture to improve cell partitioning and overall performance in sensitivity, throughput, and data quality.

LABEL: 10x Next-GEM Multiome
hasExactSynonym: 10x Next-GEM Single Cell Multiome ATAC + Gene Expression|Chromium Next GEM Multiome
IAO_0000115: The 10x assay that simultaneously profiles the transcriptome and epigenome of the same individual cell nucleus, using the first iteration of the microfluidic chip and reagents.

LABEL: white matter rarefaction
hasExactSynonym: cerebral white matter rarefaction|white matter rarefaction pathology
IAO_0000115: A neuropathologic finding characterised by loss of myelinated axons and associated tissue attenuation in the cerebral white matter, observed on post-mortem histopathologic examination.

LABEL: white matter rarefaction severity measurement
hasExactSynonym: cerebral white matter rarefaction severity
IAO_0000115: Quantification of the severity of rarefaction, comprising loss of myelin, tissue attenuation and reactive astrogliosis, in the cerebral white matter.

LABEL: refractory epilepsy
hasExactSynonym: drug resistant epilepsy|drug-resistant epilepsy|intractable epilepsy
IAO_0000115: An epilepsy characterized by failure of adequate trials of two tolerated, appropriately chosen and used antiepileptic drug schedules, whether as monotherapies or in combination, to achieve sustained seizure freedom.

LABEL: bullous emphysema
hasExactSynonym: bullous lung disease
IAO_0000115: A form of pulmonary emphysema characterized by the presence of one or more bullae, thin-walled air-filled spaces measuring more than 1 cm in diameter formed by destruction of lung parenchyma, which may be complicated by dyspnea, infection, or pneumothorax.

LABEL: anemia in pregnancy
hasExactSynonym: gestational anemia|maternal anemia|prenatal anemia
IAO_0000115: An anemia that occurs during pregnancy, characterized by a reduction in maternal hemoglobin concentration below 11 g/dL in the first trimester or below 10 g/dL in the second and third trimesters, arising from the normal physiologic plasma-volume expansion of pregnancy together with, in most cases, iron or folate deficiency.

LABEL: mitochondrial hepato-encephalopathy
hasExactSynonym: mitochondrial hepatoencephalopathy
IAO_0000115: An inherited mitochondrial disease presenting in infancy or early childhood with combined liver and central nervous system involvement, characterized by progressive liver dysfunction or liver failure together with encephalopathy, and caused by defects in mitochondrial DNA maintenance or in mitochondrial protein synthesis.

LABEL: familial interstitial pneumonia
IAO_0000115: An interstitial lung disease characterized by the occurrence of definite or probable idiopathic interstitial pneumonia in two or more biologically related members of the same family.

LABEL: amyloid-beta plaque measurement
hasExactSynonym: amyloid plaque burden|amyloid plaque measurement|amyloid-beta plaque burden
IAO_0000115: A measurement of the burden of amyloid-beta plaques (extracellular amyloid-beta deposits, including diffuse and neuritic plaques) in brain tissue, assessed by post-mortem neuropathological examination (e.g. immunohistochemistry or silver staining).

LABEL: Braak neurofibrillary tangle stage
hasExactSynonym: Braak NFT stage
IAO_0000115: A neuropathological staging measurement (stages 0 to VI) of Alzheimer-related neurofibrillary tangle pathology, based on the hierarchical topographic distribution of neurofibrillary tangles from the transentorhinal cortex (stages I-II) through limbic (III-IV) to isocortical regions (V-VI), determined post-mortem.

LABEL: limbic-predominant age-related TDP-43 encephalopathy neuropathologic change
hasExactSynonym: LATE neuropathologic change|LATE neuropathological change
IAO_0000115: A TDP-43 proteinopathy of the brain that occurs predominantly in older adults, characterised by TDP-43 inclusions in neurons and glia with a stereotypical, hierarchical anatomical distribution starting in the amygdala and then involving the hippocampus and the middle frontal gyrus, with or without coexisting hippocampal sclerosis. It is the neuropathological substrate of limbic-predominant age-related TDP-43 encephalopathy (LATE) and is assessed by an anatomical staging scheme based on the extent of TDP-43 pathology.

LABEL: TDP-43 proteinopathy measurement
hasExactSynonym: TDP43 proteinopathy measurement
IAO_0000115: A measurement of the burden, extent or severity of TDP-43 proteinopathy (abnormal, phosphorylated TDP-43 inclusions in neurons and glia) in post-mortem brain tissue, typically recorded as an ordinal neuropathologic score.

LABEL: cerebral amyloid angiopathy severity measurement
hasExactSynonym: cerebral amyloid angiopathy severity
IAO_0000115: A measurement of the severity of cerebral amyloid angiopathy, the deposition of amyloid in the walls of cerebral blood vessels, assessed by neuropathological examination of post-mortem brain tissue and graded on an ordinal scale.

LABEL: cerebral atherosclerosis severity measurement
hasExactSynonym: cerebral atherosclerosis severity
IAO_0000115: A measurement of the severity of cerebral atherosclerosis, atherosclerotic disease of the arteries of the brain and circle of Willis, assessed by neuropathological examination of post-mortem tissue and graded on an ordinal scale.

LABEL: cerebral arteriolosclerosis severity measurement
IAO_0000115: A measurement of the severity of arteriolosclerosis in the brain, the thickening and hyalinization of the walls of small arteries and arterioles with narrowing of the lumen, assessed by neuropathological examination of post-mortem brain tissue and graded on an ordinal scale.

LABEL: cerebral arteriolosclerosis
hasExactSynonym: brain arteriolosclerosis
IAO_0000115: A cerebral small vessel disease characterized by arteriolosclerosis of the small arteries and arterioles of the brain, with hyaline or fibrous thickening of the vessel wall and narrowing of the lumen, typically assessed by neuropathological examination of brain tissue.

LABEL: cerebral microinfarcts
hasExactSynonym: brain microinfarcts|cerebral microinfarct|cerebral microscopic infarcts
IAO_0000115: A cerebrovascular disorder consisting of a small, presumed ischaemic lesion of the brain parenchyma that is not visible on gross inspection and is identified by light microscopy as a sharply delimited focus of neuronal loss, gliosis or necrosis, sometimes with cavitation.

LABEL: Zinc deficiency
IAO_0000115: A deficiency of the essential metal Zinc; an essential cofactor for many enzymes. Zinc deficiency is caused by a lack of zinc in the diet, loss of zinc after absorption, for example through loss through burns, inability to absorb Zinc, or increased loss through exercise.

LABEL: anaplastic lung carcinoma
hasExactSynonym: large cell lung carcinoma
IAO_0000115: A poorly differentiated non-small cell lung carcinoma composed of large polygonal cells without evidence of glandular or squamous differentiation

LABEL: postweaning multisystemic wasting syndrome
IAO_0000115: Pig disease caused by porcine circovirus type 2 (PCV2). Most representative symptoms include wasting, unthriftness, paleness of the skin, respiratory distress, diarrhea and sometimes icterus.

LABEL: Adamantinomatous Craniopharyngioma
IAO_0000115: A craniopharyngioma consisting of broad strands, cords and bridges of a multistratified squamous epithelium with peripheral palisading of nuclei. Diagnostic features include nodules of compact 'wet' keratin and dystrophic calcification. (Adapted from WHO)

LABEL: Anaplastic (Malignant) Meningioma
IAO_0000115: A WHO grade III meningioma characterized by the presence of malignant morphologic features, including malignant cytology and a very high mitotic index (20 or more mitoses per ten high power fields).

LABEL: Angiomatous Meningioma
IAO_0000115: A WHO grade I meningioma characterized by the presence of small and medium sized vessels that predominate over the meningioma cells.

LABEL: Appendix Goblet Cell Carcinoid
hasExactSynonym: appendix adenocarcinoid tumor|appendix goblet cell carcinoid|appendix goblet cell carcinoid tumor|appendix mixed carcinoid-adenocarcinoma|goblet cell carcinoid of appendix|goblet cell carcinoid of the appendix|goblet cell carcinoid tumor|mucinous carcinoid tumor
IAO_0000115: An invasive mixed adenoneuroendocrine carcinoma of the appendix characterized by a submucosal growth and the presence of neoplastic signet-ring cells resembling goblet cells of the intestine.

LABEL: Atrophy
IAO_0000115: Any weakening or degeneration, especially through lack of use.

LABEL: Atypical Meningioma
IAO_0000115: A WHO grade II meningioma characterized by the presence of an increased mitotic activity or at least three of the following morphologic features: small cells, high cellularity, prominent nucleoli, lack of architectural pattern, and necrosis.

LABEL: Benign Childhood Cerebral Neoplasm
IAO_0000115: A non-metastasizing neoplasm that arises from the cerebral hemispheres during childhood.

LABEL: Benign Kidney Neoplasm
IAO_0000115: A non-metastasizing neoplasm that arises from the kidney. Representative examples include cystic nephroma, metanephric adenoma, oncocytoma, and urothelial papilloma of the renal pelvis.

LABEL: Benign Ovarian Brenner Tumor
IAO_0000115: A benign transitional cell tumor that arises from the ovary and is composed of a fibrotic stroma and nests of transitional cells without evidence of atypia. There is no evidence of invasion.

LABEL: Benign Ovarian Endometrioid Tumor
IAO_0000115: A non-metastasizing neoplasm that arises from the ovary and is characterized by the presence of glands or cysts lined by benign endometrial-type cells. It includes endometrioid adenofibroma, endometrioid cystadenofibroma, and endometrioid cystadenoma.

LABEL: Benign Ovarian Mixed Epithelial Tumor
IAO_0000115: A non-metastasizing neoplasm that arises from the ovary and is composed of at least two of the following cell types, serous, mucinous, endometrioid, transitional, or clear cell.

LABEL: Benign Ovarian Surface Epithelial-Stromal Tumor
IAO_0000115: A non-metastasizing neoplasm that originates from the surface epithelium of the ovary. It is composed of epithelial cells and stroma. Representative examples include serous cystadenoma, mucinous cystadenoma, clear cell adenofibroma, and benign Brenner tumor.

LABEL: Benign Renal Pelvis Neoplasm
IAO_0000115: A non-metastasizing neoplasm that arises from the renal pelvis. Urothelial papilloma is a representative example.

LABEL: Benign Salivary Gland Myoepithelioma
IAO_0000115: A rare benign tumor composed of sheets and islands of spindle, plasmacytoid, epithelioid, and clear cells that exhibit myoepithelial but not ductal differentiation. The average age of patients has been reported as 44 years. Clinically, these tumors present as asymptomatic masses. Discrimination between myoepithelioma and myoepithelial carcinoma is based primarily on the infiltrative growth of the latter.

LABEL: Benign Skin Appendage Neoplasm
IAO_0000115: A non-metastasizing neoplasm that arises from the hair follicles, sebaceous glands, or sweat glands. Representative examples include cylindroma, hidrocystoma, hidradenoma, and sebaceoma.

LABEL: Bladder Paraganglioma
IAO_0000115: A benign or malignant extra-adrenal sympathetic paraganglioma arising from the urinary bladder. Clinical signs include hypertension and hematuria.

LABEL: Borderline Exocrine Pancreatic Neoplasm
IAO_0000115: A group of epithelial neoplasms that arise from the exocrine pancreatic tissue and have the potential to evolve into invasive malignant neoplasms. This group includes the pancreatic intraepithelial neoplasias, non-invasive pancreatic mucinous-cystic neoplasms, pancreatic intraductal papillary-mucinous neoplasms, and pancreatic intraductal tubulopapillary neoplasms.

LABEL: Borderline Fallopian Tube Serous Neoplasm
IAO_0000115: A neoplasm of low malignant potential arising from the fallopian tube. It is characterized by an atypical proliferation of serous-type epithelial cells without evidence of stromal invasion.

LABEL: Borderline Ovarian Brenner Tumor
IAO_0000115: A neoplasm of low malignant potential arising from the ovary. It is characterized by the presence of neoplastic transitional cells with atypical or malignant features without evidence of stromal invasion.

LABEL: Borderline Ovarian Clear Cell Tumor
IAO_0000115: An epithelial neoplasm with low malignant potential affecting the ovary. It is characterized by the presence of clear or hobnail cells. In some cases, the cells may display nuclear atypia and prominent nucleoli. When such cells are present, they remain confined to the glands. There is no evidence of stromal invasion.

LABEL: Borderline Ovarian Endometrioid Tumor
IAO_0000115: A neoplasm of low malignant potential arising from the ovary. It is characterized by the presence of glandular or cystic spaces which contain atypical glandular epithelial cells resembling endometrial cells. The surrounding ovarian stroma is often fibrotic. There is no evidence of stromal invasion.

LABEL: Borderline Ovarian Mucinous Tumor
IAO_0000115: A low grade mucinous epithelial neoplasm arising from the ovary. It is characterized by an atypical proliferation of mucinous-type epithelial cells without evidence of stromal invasion. The mucinous epithelial cells may be of intestinal or endocervical type.

LABEL: Brain Stem Glioblastoma
IAO_0000115: A malignant, clinically aggressive astrocytic tumor (glioma) localized in the brain stem. -- 2003

LABEL: Cervical Glandular Intraepithelial Neoplasia
IAO_0000115: A neoplastic process that affects the glandular epithelial cells of the cervix. There is no evidence of invasion. It is classified as low or high grade.

LABEL: Chordoid Meningioma
IAO_0000115: A WHO grade II, usually recurring meningioma characterized by the predominance of tissues that are histologically similar to chordoma.

LABEL: Chronic Eosinophilic Leukemia, Not Otherwise Specified
hasExactSynonym: CEL|CEL/hypereosinophilic syndrome|chronic eosinophilic leukemia|chronic eosinophilic leukemia, not otherwise specified|chronic eosinophilic leukemia/hypereosinophilic syndrome|eosinophilic leukemia
IAO_0000115: A rare myeloproliferative neoplasm characterized by a clonal proliferation of eosinophilic precursors resulting in persistently increased numbers of eosinophils in the blood, marrow and peripheral tissues. Since acute eosinophilic leukemia is at best exceedingly rare, the term eosinophilic leukemia is normally used as a synonym for chronic eosinophilic leukemia. In cases in which it is impossible to prove clonality and there is no increase in blast cells, the diagnosis of "idiopathic hypereosinophilic syndrome" is preferred. (WHO, 2001)

LABEL: Clear Cell Meningioma
IAO_0000115: A WHO grade II morphologic variant of meningioma characterized by the presence of clear glycogen-rich polygonal cells.

LABEL: Common Hematopoietic Neoplasm
hasExactSynonym: common hematopoietic tumor
IAO_0000115: URL: https://ncit.nci.nih.gov/ncitbrowser/ConceptReport.jsp?dictionary=NCI_Thesaurus&code=C7588&ns=NCI_Thesaurus

LABEL: Cutaneous Follicular Lymphoma
IAO_0000115: A follicular lymphoma involving the skin. A cutaneous follicular lymphoma may be metastatic to the skin from the lymph nodes or other anatomic sites or primary (cutaneous follicle center lymphoma). --2003

LABEL: Cystic Nephroma
IAO_0000115: A benign encapsulated neoplasm of the kidney, characterized by the presence of cysts separated by septa. There are no solid areas present.
