hasExactSynonym: Capillary hyperpermeability syndrome|Capillary leak syndrome|Clarkson disease|Idiopathic capillary leak syndrome|SCLS
IAO_0000115: Systemic capillary leak syndrome (SCLS) is a severe systemic disease due to increased capillary permeability, characterized by episodes of hypotension, edema and hypovolemia.

LABEL: systemic inflammatory response syndrome
hasExactSynonym: Inflammatory Response Syndrome, Systemic|SIRS|Sepsis Syndrome
IAO_0000115: SIRS is a serious condition related to systemic inflammation, organ dysfunction, and organ failure. It is a subset of cytokine storm, in which there is abnormal regulation of various cytokines. SIRS is also closely related to sepsis, in which patients satisfy criteria for SIRS and have a suspected or proven infection.

LABEL: Tumor Lysis Syndrome
hasExactSynonym: TLS
IAO_0000115: a group of metabolic abnormalities that can occur as a complication during the treatment of cancer, most commonly after the treatment of lymphomas and leukemias.

LABEL: metastatic colorectal cancer
IAO_0000115: colorectal cancer that has already spread to distant sites and is considered stage IV

LABEL: cardiotoxicity
hasExactSynonym: cardiac toxicity
IAO_0000115: Toxicity that impairs or damages the heart. This condition is often caused by the administration of a pharmaceutical agent that initiates a poisonous or toxic response in cardiac tissue.

LABEL: non-obstructive coronary artery disease
hasExactSynonym: non-occlusive coronary artery disease
IAO_0000115: Coronary disease that has not progressed to the point of causing significant occlusion (blockage) of the coronary arteries.

LABEL: secondary biliary cirrhosis
IAO_0000115: Secondary biliary cirrhosis develops due to long-term partial or total obstruction of the large bile ducts outside of the liver. When the ducts are damaged, bile (which is a substance that helps digest fat) builds up in the liver and damages the liver tissue.

LABEL: influenza A (H1N1)
IAO_0000115: Viral infectious disease caused by the H1N1 strain of the influenza type A virus. Symptoms can range from mild to extremely severe.

LABEL: skin and soft tissue Staphylococcus aureus infection
hasExactSynonym: SSTI
IAO_0000115: Staphylococcus aureus infection that occurs specifically in skin or soft tissue and manifests through a specific range of symptoms including but not necesarrily limited to erysipelas, cellulitis, abscesses, mastitis, carbuncle and furuncle, acute lymphadenitis, impetigo, folliculitis and hidradenitis

LABEL: abortion
hasExactSynonym: loss of pregnancy
IAO_0000115: the ending of pregnancy by removing a fetus or embryo before it can survive outside the uterus.

LABEL: atrophic macular degeneration
hasExactSynonym: dry macular degeneration|geographic atrophy
IAO_0000115: Dry AMD is most common type of macular degeneration and affects 90% of the people who have the condition. In the dry form, there is a breakdown or thinning of the layer of retinal pigment epithelial cells (RPE) in the macula. No medical or surgical treatment is available for this condition.

LABEL: cardiac embolism
hasExactSynonym: cardioembolism
IAO_0000115: an embolism that is a result of an obstruction in a cardiac vessel due to a blood clot or other foreign matters

LABEL: psoriasis vulgaris
hasExactSynonym: plaque psoriasis
IAO_0000115: Plaque psoriasis is the most common presentation of psoriasis. It presents as small to large, well demarcated, red, scaly and thickened areas of skin. It most likely to affect elbows, knees, and lower back but may arise on any part of the body.

LABEL: small artery occlusion
IAO_0000115: blockage of blood flow through a small artery, particularly in the brain

LABEL: disseminated atypical mycobacterial infection
IAO_0000115: Atypical mycobacterial infections are infections caused by several types ofmycobacteria similar to the germ that causes tuberculosis. These atypical mycobacterial infections are a frequent complication in patients with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection or AIDS.

LABEL: histiocytic medullary reticulosis
IAO_0000115: rare hereditary disease characterized by histiocytic infiltration of the lungs and lymph nodes. The liver, spleen, and central nervous system can also be affected

LABEL: intellectual disability with language impairment
hasExactSynonym: intellectual disability with language impairment and autistic features|intellectual disability with language impairment and with or without autistic features|intellectual disability with language impairment without autistic features
IAO_0000115: Intellectual disability with language impairment and with or without autistic features is a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by global developmental delay with moderate to severe speech delay that particularly affects expressive speech. Most patients have articulation defects, but frank verbal dyspraxia is not observed. Common dysmorphic features include broad forehead, downslanting palpebral fissures, short nose with broad tip, relative macrocephaly, frontal hair upsweep, and prominent digit pads. Gross motor skills are also delayed. Some patients have autistic features and/or behavioral problems. All reported cases have occurred de novo (review by Le Fevre et al., 2013).

LABEL: type II diabetes mellitus with acanthosis nigricans
hasExactSynonym: Diabetes Mellitus, Insulin-Resistant, with Acanthosis Nigricans, Type A|IRAN, Type A|Insulin Receptor Defect with Insulin-Resistant Diabetes Mellitus and Acanthosis Nigricans|Insulin-resistant diabetes mellitus AND acanthosis nigricans|Type 2 diabetes mellitus with acanthosis nigricans|Type 2 diabetes mellitus with acanthosis nigricans (disorder)|insulin-resistant diabetes mellitus and acanthosis nigricans|type 2 diabetes mellitus with acanthosis nigricans
IAO_0000115: acanthosis nigricans (AN) in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM)

LABEL: small vessel stroke
IAO_0000115: stroke caused by the blockage of blood flow in one of the small blood vessels in the brain

LABEL: cystic liver disease
hasExactSynonym: cystic disease of the liver
IAO_0000115: Cystic disease of the liver is rare and can take several forms. Cysts in the main trunk of the biliary tree are called choledochal cysts. Cysts that occur in the small branches of bile ducts within the liver are referred to as Caroli?s syndrome. The other cysts in the liver that do not occur in the biliary tree are referred to as polycystic liver disease.

LABEL: asparaginase-induced acute pancreatitis
IAO_0000115: acute pancreatits that is the result of treatment with asparaginase, an enzyme used in some cancer treatments

LABEL: liver neoplasm
hasExactSynonym: Cancer of liver|Cancer of the liver|Cancer, hepatic|Cancer, liver|Cancers, hepatic|Cancers, liver|Hepatic Cancer|Hepatic Cancers|Hepatic Neoplasms|LIVER NEOPL|NEOPL LIVER|Neoplasm, hepatic|Neoplasm, liver|liver Cancer|liver Cancers
IAO_0000115: Tumors or cancers of the LIVER.

LABEL: endometrial endometrioid carcinoma
IAO_0000115: endometrioid carcinoma located in the lining of the uterus

LABEL: ovarian endometrioid carcinoma
IAO_0000115: endometrioid carcinoma located in the ovary

LABEL: ovarian serous carcinoma
IAO_0000115: serous carcinoma located in the ovary

LABEL: abdominal abscess
IAO_0000115: An abscess located in the abdominal cavity, i.e., the cavity between the diaphragm above and the pelvis below. (From Dorland, 27th ed)

LABEL: Acrodynia
IAO_0000115: A condition seen primarily in childhood, most often resulting from chronic exposure to MERCURY COMPOUNDS which may result in encephalopathy and POLYNEUROPATHY. Clinical features include pain, swelling and pinkish discoloration of the fingers and toes, weakness in the extremities, extreme irritability, HYPERESTHESIA, and alterations in level of consciousness. (From Menkes, Textbook of Child Neurology, 5th ed, p603)

LABEL: Angiofibroma
IAO_0000115: A benign neoplasm of fibrous tissue in which there are numerous small and large, frequently dilated, vascular channels. (Stedman, 25th ed)

LABEL: autonomic dysreflexia
IAO_0000115: A syndrome associated with damage to the spinal cord above the mid thoracic level (see SPINAL CORD INJURIES) characterized by a marked increase in the sympathetic response to minor stimuli such as bladder or rectal distention. Manifestations include HYPERTENSION; TACHYCARDIA (or reflex bradycardia); FEVER; FLUSHING; and HYPERHIDROSIS. Extreme hypertension may be associated with a STROKE. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, pp538 and 1232; J Spinal Cord Med 1997;20(3):355-60)

LABEL: Birnaviridae Infections
IAO_0000115: Virus diseases caused by the BIRNAVIRIDAE.

LABEL: Bovine mastitis
hasExactSynonym: Mastitis, Bovine
IAO_0000115: INFLAMMATION of the UDDER in cows.

LABEL: brain hypoxia
hasExactSynonym: Hypoxia, Brain|hypoxia of brain
IAO_0000115: A reduction in brain oxygen supply due to ANOXEMIA (a reduced amount of oxygen being carried in the blood by HEMOGLOBIN), or to a restriction of the blood supply to the brain, or both. Severe hypoxia is referred to as anoxia, and is a relatively common cause of injury to the central nervous system. Prolonged brain anoxia may lead to BRAIN DEATH or a PERSISTENT VEGETATIVE STATE. Histologically, this condition is characterized by neuronal loss which is most prominent in the HIPPOCAMPUS; GLOBUS PALLIDUS; CEREBELLUM; and inferior olives.

LABEL: cadmium poisoning
IAO_0000115: Poisoning occurring after exposure to cadmium compounds or fumes. It may cause gastrointestinal syndromes, anemia, or pneumonitis.

LABEL: carcinoid heart disease
IAO_0000115: Cardiac manifestation of gastrointestinal CARCINOID TUMOR that metastasizes to the liver. Substances secreted by the tumor cells, including SEROTONIN, promote fibrous plaque formation in ENDOCARDIUM and its underlying layers. These deposits cause distortion of the TRICUSPID VALVE and the PULMONARY VALVE eventually leading to STENOSIS and valve regurgitation.

LABEL: Carcinoma, Lewis Lung
hasExactSynonym: Lewis lung carcinoma
IAO_0000115: A carcinoma discovered by Dr. Margaret R. Lewis of the Wistar Institute in 1951. This tumor originated spontaneously as a carcinoma of the lung of a C57BL mouse. The tumor does not appear to be grossly hemorrhagic and the majority of the tumor tissue is a semifirm homogeneous mass. (From Cancer Chemother Rep 2 1972 Nov;(3)1:325) It is also called 3LL and LLC and is used as a transplantable malignancy.

LABEL: cardiac edema
hasExactSynonym: Edema, Cardiac
IAO_0000115: Abnormal fluid retention by the body due to impaired cardiac function or heart failure. It is usually characterized by increase in venous and capillary pressure, and swollen legs when standing. It is different from the generalized edema caused by renal dysfunction (NEPHROTIC SYNDROME).

LABEL: Central Cord Syndrome
IAO_0000115: A syndrome associated with traumatic injury to the cervical or upper thoracic regions of the spinal cord characterized by weakness in the arms with relative sparing of the legs and variable sensory loss. This condition is associated with ischemia, hemorrhage, or necrosis involving the central portions of the spinal cord. Corticospinal fibers destined for the legs are spared due to their more external location in the spinal cord. This clinical pattern may emerge during recovery from spinal shock. Deficits may be transient or permanent.

LABEL: Central Nervous System Helminthiasis
IAO_0000115: Infections of the BRAIN; SPINAL CORD; or MENINGES caused by HELMINTHS (parasitic worms).

LABEL: central nervous system venous angioma
hasExactSynonym: thrombophlebitis of central nervous system venous sinuses|venous angioma, central nervous system
IAO_0000115: A vascular anomaly characterized by a radial or wedge-shaped arrangement of dilated VEINS draining into a larger vein in the brain, spinal cord, or the meninges. Veins in a venous angioma are surrounded by normal nervous tissue, unlike a CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM CAVERNOUS HEMANGIOMA that lacks intervening nervous tissue. Drainage of venous angioma is fully integrated with the body's venous system, therefore, in most cases there is no clinical signs and rare bleeding.

LABEL: cerebrospinal fluid otorrhea
IAO_0000115: Discharge of cerebrospinal fluid through the external auditory meatus or through the eustachian tube into the nasopharynx. This is usually associated with CRANIOCEREBRAL TRAUMA (e.g., SKULL FRACTURE involving the TEMPORAL BONE;), NEUROSURGICAL PROCEDURES; or other conditions, but may rarely occur spontaneously. (From Am J Otol 1995 Nov;16(6):765-71)

LABEL: Chilaiditi Syndrome
IAO_0000115: Interposition of a portion of the colon (e.g., SIGMOID COLON) between the liver and the diaphragm. It is associated with abdominal pain, vomiting, constipation, anorexia and volvulus. Chilaiditi anomaly refers to asymptomatic interposition.

LABEL: chloracne
hasExactSynonym: chlorine acne
IAO_0000115: ACNE-like skin eruptions caused by exposure to CHLORINE-containing compounds. Exposure can be by inhalation, ingestion, or through the skin. Chloracne is often seen in people who have occupational contact with chlorinated pesticides, wood preservatives, and sealants.

LABEL: chromosome-defective micronuclei
hasExactSynonym: Micronuclei, Chromosome-Defective
IAO_0000115: Defective nuclei produced during the TELOPHASE of MITOSIS or MEIOSIS by lagging CHROMOSOMES or chromosome fragments derived from spontaneous or experimentally induced chromosomal structural changes.

LABEL: Chylothorax
IAO_0000115: The presence of chyle in the thoracic cavity. (Dorland, 27th ed)

LABEL: Commotio Cordis
IAO_0000115: A sudden CARDIAC ARRHYTHMIA (e.g., VENTRICULAR FIBRILLATION) caused by a blunt, non-penetrating impact to the precordial region of chest wall. Commotio cordis often results in sudden death without prompt cardiopulmonary defibrillation.

LABEL: dental pulp exposure
hasExactSynonym: pulp exposure
IAO_0000115: The result of pathological changes in the hard tissue of a tooth caused by carious lesions, mechanical factors, or trauma, which render the pulp susceptible to bacterial invasion from the external environment.

LABEL: desmoplastic fibroma
hasExactSynonym: Fibroma, Desmoplastic
IAO_0000115: A extremely rare bone tumor characterized by abundant collagen formation and a fibrous stroma, without evidence of mitosis or pleomorphism. It appears on x-rays as an osteolytic lesion with well-defined margins and must be differentiated from primary fibrosarcoma of bone. (DeVita Jr et al., Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 3d ed, p1441)

LABEL: diffuse cutaneous Leishmaniasis
hasExactSynonym: Leishmaniasis, diffuse cutaneous
IAO_0000115: A form of LEISHMANIASIS, CUTANEOUS caused by Leishmania aethiopica in Ethiopia and Kenya, L. pifanoi in Venezuela, L. braziliensis in South America, and L. mexicana in Central America. This disease is characterized by massive dissemination of skin lesions without visceral involvement.

LABEL: diffuse esophageal spasm
hasExactSynonym: Esophageal Spasm, Diffuse|diffuse spasm of esophagus|dyskinesia of esophagus|symptomatic diffuse esophageal spasm
IAO_0000115: A hypermotility disorder of the ESOPHAGUS that is characterized by spastic non-peristaltic responses to SWALLOWING; CHEST PAIN; and DYSPHAGIA.

LABEL: erythroplasia
hasExactSynonym: erythroplakia
IAO_0000115: A condition of the mucous membrane characterized by erythematous papular lesions. (Dorland, 27th ed)

LABEL: experimental arthritis
hasExactSynonym: Arthritis, Experimental
IAO_0000115: ARTHRITIS that is induced in experimental animals. Immunological methods and infectious agents can be used to develop experimental arthritis models. These methods include injections of stimulators of the immune response, such as an adjuvant (ADJUVANTS, IMMUNOLOGIC) or COLLAGEN.

LABEL: Eye Burns
IAO_0000115: Injury to any part of the eye by extreme heat, chemical agents, or ultraviolet radiation.

LABEL: familial apolipoprotein B hypobetalipoproteinemia
hasExactSynonym: Hypobetalipoproteinemia, Familial, Apolipoprotein B
IAO_0000115: An autosomal dominant disorder of lipid metabolism. It is caused by mutations of APOLIPOPROTEINS B, main components of CHYLOMICRONS and BETA-LIPOPROTEINS (low density lipoproteins or LDL). Features include abnormally low LDL, normal triglyceride level, and dietary fat malabsorption.

LABEL: female athlete triad syndrome
hasExactSynonym: female athlete triad|triad syndrome
IAO_0000115: A condition of competitive female athletes in which there are interrelated problems of EATING DISORDERS; AMENORRHEA; and OSTEOPOROSIS.

LABEL: femoral hernia
hasExactSynonym: Hernia, Femoral
IAO_0000115: A groin hernia occurring inferior to the inguinal ligament and medial to the FEMORAL VEIN and FEMORAL ARTERY. The femoral hernia sac has a small neck but may enlarge considerably when it enters the subcutaneous tissue of the thigh. It is caused by defects in the ABDOMINAL WALL.

LABEL: femoral neck fracture
hasExactSynonym: Femoral Neck Fractures|fracture of neck of femur
IAO_0000115: Fractures of the short, constricted portion of the thigh bone between the femur head and the trochanters. It excludes intertrochanteric fractures which are HIP FRACTURES.

LABEL: fetal hypoxia
hasExactSynonym: embryo hypoxia|embryo/fetus hyposia|fetus/embryo hypoxia|intrauterine hypoxia
IAO_0000115: Deficient oxygenation of FETAL BLOOD.

LABEL: fetomaternal transfusion
hasExactSynonym: fetal maternal hemorrhage|fetal-maternal hemorrhage|fetomaternal hemorrhage|fetomaternal placental transfusion syndrome
IAO_0000115: Transplacental passage of fetal blood into the circulation of the maternal organism. (Dorland, 27th ed)

LABEL: Glomus Jugulare Tumor
IAO_0000115: A paraganglioma involving the glomus jugulare, a microscopic collection of chemoreceptor tissue in the adventitia of the bulb of the jugular vein. It may cause paralysis of the vocal cords, attacks of dizziness, blackouts, and nystagmus. It is not resectable but radiation therapy is effective. It regresses slowly, but permanent control is regularly achieved. (From Dorland, 27th ed; Stedman, 25th ed; DeVita Jr et al., Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 3d ed, pp1603-4)

LABEL: Hemoglobin SC Disease
IAO_0000115: One of the sickle cell disorders characterized by the presence of both hemoglobin S and hemoglobin C. It is similar to, but less severe than sickle cell anemia.

LABEL: immunoproliferative small intestinal disease
hasExactSynonym: alpha heavy chain disease
IAO_0000115: A condition that is caused by HYPERPLASIA of LYMPHOCYTES in the small intestine (INTESTINE, SMALL) and the mesenteric LYMPH NODES. These lymphocytes produce an anomalous alpha heavy chain protein. Generally, these IPSID patients have either concurrent LYMPHOMA or develop lymphoma within a few years. The disease was first described in the Mediterranean region and is characterized by malabsorption; WEIGHT LOSS; DIARRHEA; and STEATORRHEA.

LABEL: incomplete abortion
hasExactSynonym: Abortion, Incomplete
IAO_0000115: Premature loss of PREGNANCY in which not all the products of CONCEPTION have been expelled.

LABEL: Intervertebral Disc Displacement
hasExactSynonym: displacement of intervertebral disc
IAO_0000115: An INTERVERTEBRAL DISC in which the nucleus pulposus has protruded through surrounding fibrocartilage. This occurs most frequently in the lower lumbar region.

LABEL: intracranial subdural hematoma
hasExactSynonym: Hematoma, Subdural, Intracranial|intracranial hematoma, subdural|subdural hematoma|subdural intracranial hematoma
IAO_0000115: Accumulation of blood in the SUBDURAL SPACE over the CEREBRAL HEMISPHERE.

LABEL: isolated noncompaction of the ventricular myocardium
hasExactSynonym: Isolated Noncompaction of the Ventricular Myocardium
IAO_0000115: Rare congenital cardiomyopathies characterized by the lack of left ventricular myocardium compaction. The noncompaction results in numerous prominent trabeculations and a loose myocardial meshwork (spongy myocardium) in the LEFT VENTRICLE. Heterogeneous clinical features include diminished systolic function sometimes associated with left ventricular dilation, that presents either neonatally or progressively. Often, the RIGHT VENTRICLE is also affected. CONGESTIVE HEART FAILURE; PULMONARY EMBOLISM; and ventricular ARRHYTHMIA are commonly seen.

LABEL: lingual thyroid
IAO_0000115: A condition characterized by the presence of rudimentary THYROID tissue at the base of the TONGUE. It is due to failed embryonic development and migration of thyroid tissue to its normal location. The lingual thyroid usually cannot maintain adequate hormone production thereby resulting in HYPOTHYROIDISM.

LABEL: Livedo reticularis
IAO_0000115: A condition characterized by a reticular or fishnet pattern on the skin of lower extremities and other parts of the body. This red and blue pattern is due to deoxygenated blood in unstable dermal blood vessels. The condition is intensified by cold exposure and relieved by rewarming.

LABEL: Monteggia's fracture
hasExactSynonym: Monteggia's fracture of ulna
IAO_0000115: Fracture in the proximal half of the shaft of the ulna, with dislocation of the head of the radius.

LABEL: myringosclerosis
IAO_0000115: The formation of dense connective tissue in the TYMPANIC MEMBRANE that does not necessarily cause or lead to loss of hearing.

LABEL: Nasal Septal Perforation
hasExactSynonym: perforation of nasal septum
IAO_0000115: An opening or hole in the NASAL SEPTUM that is caused by TRAUMA, injury, drug use, or pathological process.

LABEL: nephrogenic fibrosing dermopathy
hasExactSynonym: nephrogenic systemic fibrosis
IAO_0000115: A chronic, acquired, idiopathic, progressive eruption of the skin that occurs in the context of RENAL FAILURE. It is sometimes accompanied by systemic fibrosis. The pathogenesis seems to be multifactorial, with postulated involvement of circulating fibrocytes. There is a strong association between this disorder and the use of gadolinium-based contrast agents.

LABEL: nervous system heavy metal poisoning
hasExactSynonym: Heavy Metal Poisoning, Nervous System
IAO_0000115: Conditions associated with damage or dysfunction of the nervous system caused by exposure to heavy metals, which may cause a variety of central, peripheral, or autonomic nervous system injuries.

LABEL: neutropenic enterocolitis
hasExactSynonym: Enterocolitis, Neutropenic
IAO_0000115: A syndrome characterized by inflammation in the ILEUM, the CECUM, and the ASCENDING COLON. It is observed in cancer patients with CHEMOTHERAPY-induced NEUTROPENIA or in other immunocompromised individuals (IMMUNOCOMPROMISED HOST).

LABEL: ocular posterior capsular rupture
hasExactSynonym: Posterior Capsular Rupture, Ocular
IAO_0000115: A breach in the continuity of the posterior chamber of the eyeball.

LABEL: oroficial granulomatosis
hasExactSynonym: Granulomatosis, Orofacial
IAO_0000115: A condition characterized by persistent or recurrent labial enlargement, ORAL ULCER, and other orofacial manifestations in the absence of identifiable CROHN DISEASE; or SARCOIDOSIS. Among experts there is disagreement on whether orofacial granulomatosis is a distinct clinical disorder or an initial presentation of Crohn disease.

LABEL: Periprosthetic Fractures
IAO_0000115: Fractures around joint replacement prosthetics or implants. They can occur intraoperatively or postoperatively.

LABEL: Poroma
IAO_0000115: A benign adnexal neoplasm composed of EPITHELIAL CELLS. They typically manifest as solitary papules and occur only in the skin.

LABEL: post-concussion syndrome
hasExactSynonym: postconcussion syndrome
IAO_0000115: The organic and psychogenic disturbances observed after closed head injuries (HEAD INJURIES, CLOSED). Post-concussion syndrome includes subjective physical complaints (i.e. headache, dizziness), cognitive, emotional, and behavioral changes. These disturbances can be chronic, permanent, or late emerging.

LABEL: post-exercise hypotension
hasExactSynonym: post exercise hypotension
IAO_0000115: Transient reduction in blood pressure levels immediately after exercises that lasts 2-12 hours. The reduction varies but is typically 5-20 mm Hg when compared to pre-exercise levels. It exists both in normotensive and hypertensive individuals and may play a role in excercise related PHYSIOLOGIC ADAPTATION.

LABEL: Posterior Leukoencephalopathy Syndrome
hasExactSynonym: PRES|RPLS|posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome|reversible posterior leukoencephalopathy syndrome
IAO_0000115: A condition that is characterized by HEADACHE; SEIZURES; and visual loss with edema in the posterior aspects of the CEREBRAL HEMISPHERES, such as the BRAIN STEM. Generally, lesions involve the white matter (nerve fibers) but occasionally the grey matter (nerve cell bodies).

LABEL: Psoas abscess
hasExactSynonym: Psoas muscle abscess|iliopsoas abscess
IAO_0000115: Abscess of the PSOAS MUSCLES resulting usually from disease of the lumbar vertebrae, with the pus descending into the muscle sheath. The infection is most commonly tuberculous or staphylococcal.

LABEL: Pubic Symphysis Diastasis
hasExactSynonym: diastasis symphysis pubis
IAO_0000115: Separation of the PUBIC SYMPHYSIS. It is an uncommon complication of CHILDBIRTH causing postpartum PAIN, but it can also arise from other causes.

LABEL: pyogenic liver abscess
hasExactSynonym: Liver Abscess, Pyogenic
IAO_0000115: Single or multiple areas of PUS due to bacterial infection within the hepatic parenchyma. It can be caused by a variety of BACTERIA, local or disseminated from infections elsewhere such as in APPENDICITIS; CHOLECYSTITIS; PERITONITIS; and after LIVER TRANSPLANTATION.

LABEL: rectocele
hasExactSynonym: female rectocele|herniation of rectum into vagina
IAO_0000115: Herniation of the RECTUM into the VAGINA.

LABEL: respiratory aspiration
hasExactSynonym: aspiration into respiratory tract|respiratory tract aspiration
IAO_0000115: Inhaling liquid or solids, such as stomach contents, into the RESPIRATORY TRACT. When this causes severe lung damage, it is called ASPIRATION PNEUMONIA.

LABEL: respiratory paralysis
hasExactSynonym: paralysis, respiratory|respiratory tract paralysis
IAO_0000115: Complete or severe weakness of the muscles of respiration. This condition may be associated with MOTOR NEURON DISEASES; PERIPHERAL NERVE DISEASES; NEUROMUSCULAR JUNCTION DISEASES; SPINAL CORD DISEASES; injury to the PHRENIC NERVE; and other disorders.

LABEL: sebaceous of Jadassohn nevus
hasExactSynonym: Intraepidermal epithelioma of Jadassohn|Nevus, Sebaceous of Jadassohn
IAO_0000115: A syndrome characterized by lesions occurring on the face, scalp, or neck which consist of congenital hypoplastic malformations of cutaneous structures and which over time undergo verrucous hyperplasia. Additionally it is associated with neurological symptoms and skeletal, ophthalmological, urogenital, and cardiovascular abnormalities.

LABEL: sinoatrial nodal reentry tachycardia
hasExactSynonym: AV nodal reentry tachycardia|Tachycardia, Sinoatrial Nodal Reentry|atrioventricular nodal reentry tachycardia
IAO_0000115: Abnormally rapid heartbeats caused by reentry circuit in or around the SINOATRIAL NODE. It is characterized by sudden onset and offset episodes of tachycardia with a HEART RATE of 100-150 beats per minute. The P wave is identical to the sinus P wave but with a longer PR interval.

LABEL: skin mastocytoma
hasExactSynonym: cutaneous solitary mastocytoma|skin solitary mastocytoma|solitary mastocytoma of skin|solitary mastocytoma of the skin
IAO_0000115: A variant of cutaneous mastocytosis which occurs as a single lesion usually in infants. It is found mostly in the wrist and trunk and there is no atypical cytomorphology.

LABEL: spinal cord compression
IAO_0000115: Acute and chronic conditions characterized by external mechanical compression of the SPINAL CORD due to extramedullary neoplasm; EPIDURAL ABSCESS; SPINAL FRACTURES; bony deformities of the vertebral bodies; and other conditions. Clinical manifestations vary with the anatomic site of the lesion and may include localized pain, weakness, sensory loss, incontinence, and impotence.

LABEL: Spinal Osteophytosis
IAO_0000115: Outgrowth of immature bony processes or bone spurs (OSTEOPHYTE) from the VERTEBRAE, reflecting the presence of degenerative disease and calcification. It commonly occurs in cervical and lumbar SPONDYLOSIS.

LABEL: spinal subdural hematoma
hasExactSynonym: Hematoma, Subdural, Spinal
IAO_0000115: Subdural hematoma of the SPINAL CANAL.

LABEL: squamous odontogenic tumor
hasExactSynonym: Odontogenic Tumor, Squamous
IAO_0000115: A well-differentiated, benign, hamartomatous proliferation of odontogenic epithelium, probably arising from the rests of Malassez.

LABEL: stomach diverticulum
hasExactSynonym: Diverticulum, Stomach
IAO_0000115: Saccular, outward protrusion of all or a portion of the wall of the STOMACH.

LABEL: stomach rupture
IAO_0000115: Bursting of the STOMACH.

LABEL: Stomach Volvulus
IAO_0000115: Twisting of the STOMACH that may result in gastric ISCHEMIA and GASTRIC OUTLET OBSTRUCTION. It is often associated with DIAPHRAGMATIC HERNIA.

LABEL: subphrenic abscess
hasExactSynonym: upper abdominal abscess
IAO_0000115: Accumulation of purulent EXUDATES beneath the DIAPHRAGM, also known as upper abdominal abscess. It is usually associated with PERITONITIS or postoperative infections.

LABEL: Superior Vena Cava Syndrome
IAO_0000115: A condition that occurs when the obstruction of the thin-walled SUPERIOR VENA CAVA interrupts blood flow from the head, upper extremities, and thorax to the RIGHT ATRIUM. Obstruction can be caused by NEOPLASMS; THROMBOSIS; ANEURYSM; or external compression. The syndrome is characterized by swelling and/or CYANOSIS of the face, neck, and upper arms.

LABEL: Tarlov Cysts
hasExactSynonym: Tarlov cyst
IAO_0000115: Perineurial cysts commonly found in the SACRAL REGION. They arise from the PERINEURIUM membrane within the SPINAL NERVE ROOTS. The distinctive feature of the cysts is the presence of spinal nerve root fibers within the cyst wall, or the cyst cavity itself.

LABEL: testicular hydrocele
hasExactSynonym: hydrocele testis
IAO_0000115: Accumulation of serous fluid between the layers of membrane (tunica vaginalis) covering the TESTIS in the SCROTUM.

LABEL: thymus hyperplasia
hasExactSynonym: hyperplasia, thymus
IAO_0000115: Enlargement of the thymus. A condition described in the late 1940's and 1950's as pathological thymic hypertrophy was status thymolymphaticus and was treated with radiotherapy. Unnecessary removal of the thymus was also practiced. It later became apparent that the thymus undergoes normal physiological hypertrophy, reaching a maximum at puberty and involuting thereafter. The concept of status thymolymphaticus has been abandoned. Thymus hyperplasia is present in two thirds of all patients with myasthenia gravis. (From Segen, Dictionary of Modern Medicine, 1992; Cecil Textbook of Medicine, 19th ed, p1486)

LABEL: traumatic diaphragmatic hernia
hasExactSynonym: Hernia, Diaphragmatic, Traumatic
IAO_0000115: The type of DIAPHRAGMATIC HERNIA caused by TRAUMA or injury, usually to the ABDOMEN.

LABEL: urinary bladder fistula
hasExactSynonym: bladder fistula
IAO_0000115: An abnormal passage in the URINARY BLADDER or between the bladder and any surrounding organ.

LABEL: Uterine Inertia
hasExactSynonym: uterine atony
IAO_0000115: Failure of the UTERUS to contract with normal strength, duration, and intervals during childbirth (LABOR, OBSTETRIC). It is also called uterine atony.

LABEL: uterine prolapse
IAO_0000115: Downward displacement of the UTERUS. It is classified in various degrees: in the first degree the UTERINE CERVIX is within the vaginal orifice; in the second degree the cervix is outside the orifice; in the third degree the entire uterus is outside the orifice.

LABEL: ventilator-associated pneumonia
hasExactSynonym: Pneumonia, Ventilator-Associated|VAP|ventilator-acquired pneumonia
IAO_0000115: Serious INFLAMMATION of the LUNG in patients who required the use of PULMONARY VENTILATOR. It is usually caused by cross bacterial infections in hospitals (NOSOCOMIAL INFECTIONS).

LABEL: ventral hernia
hasExactSynonym: Hernia, Ventral|hernia of anterior abdominal wall
IAO_0000115: A hernia caused by weakness of the anterior ABDOMINAL WALL due to midline defects, previous incisions, or increased intra-abdominal pressure. Ventral hernias include UMBILICAL HERNIA, incisional, epigastric, and spigelian hernias.

LABEL: Zenker diverticulum
hasExactSynonym: Zenker's diverticulum
IAO_0000115: A DIVERTICULUM at the upper end of the ESOPHAGUS through the cricopharyngeal muscle at the junction of the PHARYNX and the esophagus.

LABEL: late-onset Alzheimers disease
hasExactSynonym: Alzheimer Senile Dementia|Alzheimer Type Senile Dementia|Senile Dementia, Alzheimer Type|late-onset Alzheimer's
IAO_0000115: This is the most common form of the disease, which happens to people age 65 and older. It may or may not run in families. So far, researchers haven?t found a particular gene that causes it. No one knows for sure why some people get it and others don?t.

LABEL: acquired cold urticaria
hasExactSynonym: ACU
IAO_0000115: Acquired cold urticaria (ACU) represents a form of inducible urticaria that is characterized by the development of wheals, angioedema, or both in response to exposure to cold air, solids, or liquids.1 ACU symptoms are usually limited to areas of the skin that have been exposed to cold. However, extensive cold contact may result in generalized symptoms, such as headache, dyspnea, hypotension, and a loss of consciousness.

LABEL: amyloidoma
IAO_0000115: Nodular localized form of amyloidosis with predominantly thoracic localization (pulmonary amyloidosis), considered as secondary protein structure disease in which insoluble protein fibrils accumulate extracellularly. The form of primary amyloid in amyloidoma is characterized by abnormal deposition of light chain proteins composed of monoclonal immunoglobulin. Pulmonary amyloidomas are rare and are often found incidentally as solitary or multiple calcified nodules and masses on chest radiographs in asymptomatic elderly patients. Cavitation is rare, the prognosis is good.

LABEL: anxiety-like behavior
hasExactSynonym: anxiety behavior

LABEL: blood-injection-injury phobia
hasExactSynonym: Blood-injection-injury type phobia|Blood/Injury Phobia|blood phobia|blood-injury phobia
IAO_0000115: According to the DSM-IV classification of mental disorders blood-injection-injury type phobias constitute a subtype of specific phobias. It includes fear of blood (hemophobia), injury phobia and fear of receiving an injection (trypanophobia and some other names) or other invasive medical procedures.

LABEL: chemotherapy-induced gastrointestinal mucositis
hasExactSynonym: chemo-induced gut toxicity|chemotherapy-induced gut toxicity|chemotherapy-induced gut toxicity (CIGT)|chemotherapy-induced mucositis (CIM)
IAO_0000115: inflammation and ulceration of the gastrointestinal mucosa as a result of chemotherapy treatment

LABEL: Dendritic keratitis
hasExactSynonym: Furrow Keratitis
IAO_0000115: a form of herpetic keratitis with dendritic (branching) ulcers

LABEL: dental phobia
hasExactSynonym: dental anxiety|dental fear|dentist phobia|dentophobia|odontophobia
IAO_0000115: Dental fear (also called dental phobia, odontophobia, dentophobia, dentist phobia, and dental anxiety) is the fear of dentistry and of receiving dental care.

LABEL: diffuse alveolar-septal amyloidosis
hasExactSynonym: diffuse parenchymal amyloidosis
IAO_0000115: Diffuse alveolar-septal amyloidosis, also known as diffuse parenchymal amyloidosis, is characterized by the presence of amyloid deposits in the alveolar septa and vessel walls. [PMID:28134587]

LABEL: Endoplasmic Reticulum Stress
hasExactSynonym: ER stress
IAO_0000115: Various physiological or molecular disturbances that impair ENDOPLASMIC RETICULUM function. It triggers many responses, including UNFOLDED PROTEIN RESPONSE, which may lead to APOPTOSIS; and AUTOPHAGY.

LABEL: eye infection
hasExactSynonym: Ocular Infections|eye infections|ocular infection
IAO_0000115: An infectious process affecting any part of the eye. Causes include viruses and bacteria. Symptoms include itching and discomfort in the eye, watery eyes, eye pain and discharge, and blurring vision. Representative examples include pink eye, blepharitis, and trachoma.

LABEL: gastrointestinal mucositis
hasExactSynonym: gastrointestinal mucosa irritation|gastrointestinal mucosal damage|gastrointestinal mucosal injury|gastrointestinal mucosal lesions

LABEL: Hand-foot syndrome
hasExactSynonym: Burgdorf?s reaction|Chemotherapy-Induced Acral Erythema|Chemotherapy-Induced Palmoplantar Erythrodysesthesia|HFS|chemotherapy-induced AE|palmar-plantar erythema|palmar-plantar erythrodysesthesia|peculiar AE|toxic erythema of the palms and soles

LABEL: lateral epicondylitis
hasExactSynonym: archer's elbow|golfer's elbow|hockey elbow|lateral epicondylalgia|lateral humeral epicondylitis|tennis elbow
IAO_0000115: inflammation of the lateral epicondyle.

LABEL: mucositis
IAO_0000115: Mucositis is inflammation and damage of the mucous membranes lining the mouth and other parts of the gastrointestinal (GI) tract.

LABEL: oral mucositis
hasExactSynonym: inflammation of the mouth|oral cavity mucosal damage|oral mucosa irritation|oral mucosal damage|oral mucosal injury|oral mucosal lesions|stomatitis
IAO_0000115: Inflammation of the mucous membranes of any of the structures in the mouth.

LABEL: oxidative stress
IAO_0000115: A disturbance in the prooxidant-antioxidant balance in favor of the former, leading to potential damage. Indicators of oxidative stress include damaged DNA bases, protein oxidation products, and lipid peroxidation products (Sies, Oxidative Stress, 1991, pxv-xvi).

LABEL: panic disorder without agoraphobia
IAO_0000115: A disorder in which an individual experiences recurrent, unexpected panic attacks and persistent concern about having additional panic attacks. Agoraphobia is not a component of this disorder.

LABEL: Plantar Fasciitis
hasExactSynonym: Chronic Plantar Fasciitis|Heel Spur Syndrome|Plantar Heel Spur|Plantar Heel Spurs|Policeman's Heel
IAO_0000115: Inflammation of the plantar fascia (aponeurosis) on the bottom of the foot causing heel pain. The etiology of plantar fasciitis remains controversial but is likely to involve a biomechanical imbalance. Though often presenting along with HEEL SPUR, they do not appear to be causally related.

LABEL: pulmonary amyloidosis
hasExactSynonym: amyloidosis of the lung
IAO_0000115: Amyloidosis is characterized by amyloid extracellular deposition in organs and tissues. Pulmonary involvement is a rare manifestation of the disease and it can be focal or as part of systemic amyloidosis. [PMID:26574992]

LABEL: pulmonary nodular amyloidosis
hasExactSynonym: nodular amyloidoma|nodular parenchymal amyloidosis|nodular pulmonary amyloidosis|single nodular pulmonary Amyloidosis
IAO_0000115: Nodular pulmonary amyloidosis, also known as nodular parenchymal amyloidosis or nodular amyloidoma, is defined as 1 or more tumefactive amyloid deposits involving the lungs. [PMID:28134587]

LABEL: Purpura Fulminans
hasExactSynonym: purpura gangrenosa
IAO_0000115: A severe, rapidly fatal reaction occurring most commonly in children following an infectious illness. It is characterized by large, rapidly spreading skin hemorrhages, fever, or shock.

LABEL: radiation-induced gastrointestinal mucositis
hasExactSynonym: gastrointestinal radiation injury|intestinal radiation-induced injury|ionising radiation-induced duodenal injury|ionising-radiation-induced gastrointestinal syndrome|ionizing-radiation-induced gastrointestinal syndrome|radiation-induced GI syndrome|radiation-induced GI syndrome (RIGS)|radiation-induced acute gastrointestinal syndrome|radiation-induced gastrointestinal damage|radiation-induced gastrointestinal injury|radiation-induced gastrointestinal syndrome|radiation-induced gastrointestinal syndrome (RIGS)|radiation-induced intestinal injury|radiation-mediated gastrointestinal (GI) toxicity|radiotherapy-induced gut toxicity|radiotherapy-induced gut toxicity (RIGT)
IAO_0000115: inflammation and ulceration of the gastrointestinal mucosa as a result of radiation treatment

LABEL: stress-induced anxiety-like behavior
hasExactSynonym: stress induced anxiety behavior|stress-induced anxiety behavior

LABEL: tracheobronchial amyloidosis
IAO_0000115: Tracheobronchial amyloidosis is characterized by amyloid deposition in various segments of the tracheobronchial tree. Most cases represent localized AL amyloidosis and are restricted to the tracheobronchial tree. [PMID:28134587]

LABEL: varicose ulcer
hasExactSynonym: Stasis Ulcer|Venous Hypertension Ulcers|Venous Stasis Ulcers|Venous Ulcer
IAO_0000115: Skin breakdown or ulceration in the drainage area of a VARICOSE VEIN, usually in the leg.

LABEL: pneumococcal bacteremia
IAO_0000115: Presence of pneumococcus bacteria in the blood

LABEL: cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma
IAO_0000115: squameous cell carcinoma of the skin, representing the second most common cutaneous malignancy, behind only basal cell carcinoma in Caucasians

LABEL: idiopathic osteonecrosis of the femoral head
IAO_0000115: Most common form of osteonecrosis, the death of bone tissue following microvascular injury. Osteonecrosis of the femoral head (ONFH) is a complex multifactorial disease that is associated with genetic predisposition and exposure to certain environmental factors. Various etiological factors, including the use of corticosteroids, alcohol abuse, sickle cell anemia, radiation and Gaucher disease, are known to be implicated in the development of secondary osteonecrosis.

LABEL: adult acute megakaryoblastic leukemia
hasExactSynonym: Adult Acute M7 Leukemia|Adult Acute Megakaryocytic Leukemia|Adult Acute Megakaryocytic Leukemia (M7)|M7 Adult Acute Leukemia|M7 Adult Acute Megakaryocytic Leukemia
IAO_0000115: An acute megakaryoblastic leukemia occurring in adults.

LABEL: adult acute myeloid leukemia
hasExactSynonym: Adult Acute Granulocytic Leukemia|Adult Acute Myeloblastic Leukemia|Adult Acute Myelocytic Leukemia|Adult Acute Myelogenous Leukemia|Adult Acute Non-Lymphoblastic Leukemia|Adult Acute Non-Lymphocytic Leukemia
IAO_0000115: An acute myeloid leukemia occurring in adults.

LABEL: bronchioloalveolar carcinoma
hasExactSynonym: Bronchioalveolar Adenocarcinoma of Lung|Bronchioalveolar Lung Carcinoma|Bronchiolo-Alveolar Carcinoma of Lung|Bronchiolo-Alveolar Lung Carcinoma|Bronchioloalveolar Adenocarcinoma of Lung
IAO_0000115: A well or moderately differentiated morphologic variant of lung adenocarcinoma characterized by tumor growth along the alveolar structures without stromal, vascular, or pleural invasion.

LABEL: childhood acute megakaryoblastic leukemia
hasExactSynonym: Childhood AMKL|Childhood Acute M7 Leukemia|Childhood Acute Megakaryocytic Leukemia|M7 Childhood Acute Megakaryocytic Leukemia|M7 Pediatric Acute Megakaryocytic Leukemia|Pediatric Acute Megakaryoblastic Leukemia|Pediatric Acute Megakaryocytic Leukemia
IAO_0000115: An acute megakaryoblastic leukemia occurring in children.

LABEL: childhood acute monocytic leukemia
hasExactSynonym: Childhood Acute Differentiated Monocytic Leukemia (M5b)|Childhood Acute M5b Leukemia|Childhood Acute Monocytic Leukemia with Differentiation|M5b Childhood Acute Differentiated Monocytic Leukemia|M5b Pediatric Acute Differentiated Monocytic Leukemia|Pediatric Acute Differentiated Monocytic Leukemia|Pediatric Acute M5b Leukemia|Pediatric Acute Monocytic Leukemia with Differentiation
IAO_0000115: An acute monocytic leukemia occurring in children.

LABEL: childhood acute myeloid leukemia with maturation
hasExactSynonym: Childhood Acute Granulocytic Leukemia with Maturation|Childhood Acute M2 Leukemia|Childhood Acute Myeloblastic Leukemia with Maturation|Childhood Acute Myeloblastic Leukemia with Maturation (M2)|Childhood Acute Myelocytic Leukemia with Maturation|Childhood Acute Myelogenous Leukemia with Maturation|Childhood Acute Myeloid Leukemia with Maturation
IAO_0000115: An acute myeloid leukemia with maturation occurring in children.

LABEL: endometrial endometrioid adenocarcinoma, variant with squamous differentiation
hasExactSynonym: Adenocanthoma of Endometrium|Endometrial Adenoacanthoma
IAO_0000115: An endometrioid adenocarcinoma of the endometrium showing squamous differentiation.

LABEL: Epstein-Barr virus-related Burkitts lymphoma
hasExactSynonym: EBV-Related Burkitt's Lymphoma
IAO_0000115: Burkitt lymphoma can be classified into three forms which differ in geographic distribution and Epstein?Barr virus (EBV) association: endemic, sporadic and HIV?associated. Endemic Burkitt lymphoma is associated with EBV in over 95% of cases and is predominant in the equatorial belt of Africa and other parts of the world where malaria is hyperendemic.

LABEL: erythroleukemia
IAO_0000115: Acute erythroid leukemia characterised by the presence of at least 50% erythroid precursors and at least 20% myeloblasts in the bone marrow.

LABEL: hereditary thyroid gland medullary carcinoma
hasExactSynonym: Familial Thyroid Gland Medullary Carcinoma|Hereditary Thyroid Gland Medullary Cancer|familial medullary thyroid cancer
IAO_0000115: A medullary thyroid gland carcinoma inherited through an autosomal dominant mode. It is associated with multiple endocrine neoplasia type II (2a) or III (2b).

LABEL: high grade ovarian serous adenocarcinoma
IAO_0000115: A rapidly growing serous adenocarcinoma that arises from the ovary. It is characterized by the presence of high grade cytologic features and frequent mitotic figures.

LABEL: pancreatic somatostatinoma
IAO_0000115: A neuroendocrine tumor arising from the delta cells of the pancreas. It is characterized by inappropriate secretion of somatostatin and associated with diabetes mellitus, hypochlorhydria, gallbladder disease, diarrhea, steatorrhea, anemia, and weight loss.

LABEL: rectosigmoid adenocarcinoma
IAO_0000115: An adenocarcinoma arising from the rectosigmoid area. It is more frequently seen in populations with a Western type diet and in patients with a history of chronic inflammatory bowel disease. Signs and symptoms include intestinal bleeding, anemia, and change in bowel habits. According to the degree of cellular differentiation, rectosigmoid adenocarcinomas are divided into well, moderately, and poorly differentiated. Histologic variants include mucinous adenocarcinoma, signet ring cell carcinoma, medullary carcinoma, serrated adenocarcinoma, cribriform comedo-type adenocarcinoma, and micropapillary adenocarcinoma.

LABEL: thyroid gland sarcoma
hasExactSynonym: Sarcoma of Thyroid|Thyroid Sarcoma
IAO_0000115: A malignant soft tissue neoplasm primarily involving the thyroid gland.

LABEL: ureter urothelial carcinoma
hasExactSynonym: transitional cell carcinoma of the ureter|transitional cell carcinoma of ureter|ureter transitional cell carcinoma|ureter transitional cell carcinoma|ureter urothelial cancer|ureter urothelial carcinoma|ureteral transitional cell carcinoma|ureteral urothelial cell carcinoma|urothelial cell carcinoma of the ureter|urothelial cell carcinoma of ureter
IAO_0000115: A carcinoma that arises from the transitional epithelium of the ureter. It is associated with tobacco use and usually presents with gross or microscopic hematuria.

LABEL: cardioembolic stroke
IAO_0000115: stroke caused by the blockage of blood flow in a brain vessel through a clot or other foreign matters pumped from the heart to the brain

LABEL: cardiac amyloidosis
hasExactSynonym: Amyloid heart disease|Amyloid heart muscle disease|Amyloidosis of heart|Senile cardiac amyloidosis|amyloid cardiomyopathy
IAO_0000115: Cardiac amyloidosis is a condition whereby cardiac tissue is infiltrated by amyloid fibrils. Patients with cardiac amyloidosis commonly develop diastolic and systolic dysfunction, progressive heart failure (HF), arrhythmias, and symptoms of orthostatic hypotension. [PMID:28279425]

LABEL: congenital fibrosis of the extraocular muscles
hasExactSynonym: CFEOM|Congenital fibrosis of extraocular muscles|Congenital ophthalmoplegia|Tukel syndrome|congenital fibrosis of the extraocular muscles

LABEL: Scleroderma Polymyositis Overlap Syndrome
hasExactSynonym: polymyositis in scleroderma|scleroderma/polimyositis overlap|scleromyositis
IAO_0000115: A rare autoimmune disorder in which patients present with overlapping symptoms of systemic scleroderma and polymyositis or dermatomyositis.

LABEL: Sclerodermatomyositis
hasExactSynonym: Scleroderma Polymyositis Overlap Syndrome
IAO_0000115: Sclerodermatomyositis is an overlap syndrome of myositis and scleroderma, with dermatological, muscular and joint involvement, but may also present with ocular manifestations. [ PMID:PMID:27923520 ]

LABEL: core binding factor acute myeloid leukemia
hasExactSynonym: CBF-AML
IAO_0000115: Acute myeloid leukemia characterized by the presence of t(8;21)(q22;q22) or inv(16)(p13q22)/t(16;16)(p13;q22). These cytogenetic abnormalities result in disruption of the transcription factor CBF, which is a regulator of normal hematopoiesis. CBF-AML accounts for 12 to 15 percent of acute myeloid leukemia cases in adults.

LABEL: high altitude pulmonary edema
hasExactSynonym: pulmonary edema of mountaineers
IAO_0000115: a noncardiogenic form of pulmonary edema that develops in unacclimatized healthy individuals at altitudes above 2500?3000 m

IAO_0000115: Macular telangiectasia type 2 is a rare neurovascular degenerative retinal disease. MacTel cases typically present at 40?60 years of age with abnormal right-angled juxtafoveolar capillaries and parafoveal telangiectasias. MacTel is an uncommon disease with a 0.0045?0.1% population prevalence and no obvious sex bias. Retinal lesions typically co- present with MacTel, including retinal transparency, outer retinal and choroidal neovascularization, lamellar holes or foveal cysts, photoreceptor dysfunction, minimal exudation, yellow?white parafoveal crystals, and retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) pigmen- tation abnormalities and atrophy. Central vision impairment and decreased visual acuity are the usual clinical outcomes. MacTel is a bilateral disease, but asymmetry of the eyes for disease severity and presence of lesions is possible. The lesions also occur in 0.06?1.18% of the general population.

The group comprises PSP-Parkinsonism (PSP-P), PSP-Pure akinesia with gait freezing (PSP-PAGF), PSP-corticobasal syndrome (PSP-CBS) and PSP-progressive non fluent aphasia (PSP-PNFA) (see these terms).

LABEL: Non-polyposis Turcot syndrome

LABEL: Autosomal dominant Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2B
hasExactSynonym: CMT2B
IAO_0000115: Autosomal dominant Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2B (CMT2B) is a severe form of axonal Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease, a peripheral sensorimotor neuropathy. CMT2B onset, in the 2nd or 3rd decade, is characterized by ulcerations and infections of feet. Symmetric and distal weakness develops mostly in the legs together with a severe symmetric distal sensory loss, tendon reflexes are only reduced at ankles and foot deformities, including pes cavus or planus and hammer toes, appear in childhood.

LABEL: Autosomal dominant Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2C
hasExactSynonym: CMT2C
IAO_0000115: Autosomal dominant Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2C (CMT2C) is a form of axonal Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease, a peripheral sensorimotor neuropathy, characterized by the association of vocal cord anomalies, impairment of respiratory muscles and sensorineural hearing loss with the distal hands and feet weakness. Onset is between infancy and the 6th decade.

LABEL: Autosomal dominant Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2D
hasExactSynonym: CMT2D
IAO_0000115: Autosomal dominant Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2D (CMT2D) is a form of axonal Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease, a peripheral sensorimotor neuropathy, characterized by distal weakness primarily and predominantly occurring in the upper limbs and tendon reflexes absent or reduced in the arms and decreased in the legs. Progression is slow.

LABEL: Autosomal dominant Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2E
hasExactSynonym: CMT2E
IAO_0000115: Autosomal dominant Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2E (CMT2E) is a form of axonal Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease, a peripheral sensorimotor neuropathy. CMT2E onset is in the first to 6th decade with a gait anomaly and a leg weakness that reaches the arms secondarily. Tendon reflexes are reduced or absent and, after years, all patients have a pes cavus. Other signs may be present, including hearing loss and postural tremor.

LABEL: Autosomal dominant Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2F
hasExactSynonym: CMT2F
IAO_0000115: Autosomal dominant Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2F (CMT2F) is a form of axonal Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease, a peripheral sensorimotor neuropathy. CMT2F is characterized by symmetric weakness primarily occurring in the lower limbs (distal muscles in a majority of cases) and reaching the arms only after 5 to 10 years, occasional and predominantly distal sensory loss and reduced tendon reflexes. CMT2F presents with gait anomaly between the 1st and 6th decade and early onset is generally associated to a more severe phenotype which may include foot drop.

LABEL: Autosomal dominant Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2I
hasExactSynonym: CMT2I
IAO_0000115: Autosomal dominant Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2I (CMT2I) is a form of axonal Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease, a peripheral sensorimotor neuropathy, characterized by a late onset with severe sensory loss (paresthesia and hypoesthesia) associated with distal weakness, mainly of the legs, and absent or reduced deep tendon reflexes.

LABEL: Autosomal dominant Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2J
hasExactSynonym: CMT2J
IAO_0000115: Autosomal dominant Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2J (CMT2J) is a form of axonal Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease, a peripheral sensorimotor neuropathy, characterized by a relatively late onset, papillary abnormalities and deafness, in most patients, associated with distal weakness and muscle atrophy.

LABEL: Autosomal dominant Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2L
hasExactSynonym: CMT2L
IAO_0000115: Autosomal dominant Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2L (CMT2L) is a form of axonal Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease, a peripheral sensorimotor neuropathy. In the single family reported to date, CMT2L onset is between 15 and 33 years. Patients present with a symmetric distal weakness of legs and occasionally of the hands, absent or reduced tendon reflexes, distal legs sensory loss and frequently a pes cavus. Progression is slow.

LABEL: Autosomal dominant Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2A1
hasExactSynonym: CMT2A1
IAO_0000115: Autosomal dominant Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2A1 (CMT2A1) is a form of axonal Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease, a peripheral sensorimotor neuropathy. CMT2A presents with a more prominent muscle weakness in lower than upper limbs and frequent postural tremor.
